title: O for a thousand tongues to sing
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for a thousand tongues to sing
My great Redeemer's praise!
The glories of my God and King,
The triumphs of his grace!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My gracious Master, and my God,
Assist me to proclaim,
To spread through all the earth abroad
The honours of thy Name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus! the Name that charms our feav
That bids our sorrows cease;
Tis music in the sinner's ears,
'Tis life, and health, and peace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He breaks the power of cancell'd sin,
He sets the prisoner free;
His blood can make the foulest clean,
His blood avail'd for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Hear him, ye deaf; his praise, ye dumb,
Your loosen'd tongues employ;
Ye blind, behold your Saviour come,
And leap, ye lame, for joy.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Look unto him, ye nations; own
Your God, ye fallen race;
Look, and be saved through faith alon
Be justified by grace.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
See all your sins on Jesus laid:
The Lamb of God was slain;
His soul was once an offering made
For every soul of man.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Awake from guilty nature's sleep,
And Christ shall give you light;
Cast all your sins into the deep,
And wash the iEthiop white.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
With me, your chief, ye then shall know,
Shall feel your sins forgiven;
Anticipate your heaven below,
And own that love is heaven.

title: Come, sinners, to the gospel feast
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, sinners, to the gospel feast
Let every soul be Jesu's guest;
Ye need not one be left behind,
For God hath bidden all mankind.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sent by my Lord, on you I call;
The invitation is to all:
Come, all the world; come, sinner, thou,
All things' hi Christ are ready now
'6 Come, all ye souls by sin opprest,
Ye restless wanderers after i-est;
Ye poor, and maim'd, and halt, and blind.
In Christ a hearty welcome find=

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, and partake the gospel feast;
Be saved from sin; in Jesus rest:
O taste the goodness of your God,
And eat his flesh, and drink his blood!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
My message as from God receive;
Ye all may come to Christ, and live;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
let his love your hearts constrain,
Nor suffer him to die in vain!

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
See him set forth before your eyes,
That precious, bleeding Sacrifice!
His offered benefits embrace,
And freely now be saved by grace.

sections.label: Verse 9

title: All ye that pass by, To Jesus draw near
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Whoever receives The life-giving word,
In Jesus believes, His God and his Lordj
In him a pure river Of life shall arise;
Shall, in the believer, Spring up to the skies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My God and my Lord! Thy call I obey;
My soul on thy word Of promise I stay:
Thy kind invitation I gladly embrace,
Athirst for salvation, Salvation by grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O hasten the hour, Send down from above
The Spirit of power, Of health, and of love:
Of filial fear, Of knowledge and grace;
Of wisdom and prayer, Of joy and of praise:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Spirit of faith, Of faith in thy blood: [God;
Which saves us from wrath, And brings us to
Removes the huge mountain Of indwelling sin,
And opens a fountain That washes us clean.

title: Ho! every one that thirsts, draw nigh
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
See from the Rock a fountain rise!
For you, in healing streams, it rolls;
Money ye need not bring, nor price, -
Ye labouring, burden'd, sin-sick souls,

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Why seek ye that which is not bread,
Nor can your hungry souls sustain r
On ashes, husks, and air ye feed;
Ye spend your little all in vain.
•0 In search of empty joys below,
Ye toil with unavailing strife:
Whither, ah! Whither would ye go?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
have the words of endless life.
7 Hearken to me with earnest care.
And freely eat substantial food;
The sweetness of my mercy share,
And taste that I alone am good.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
I bid you all my goodness prove:
My promises for all are free:
Come, taste the manna of my love,
And let your souls delight in me.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Your willing ear and heart incline,
My words belie vingly receive;
Quicken'd, your souls, by faith divine,
An everlasting life shall live.

title: Thy faithfulness, Lord, Each moment we
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy faithfulness, Lord, Each moment we
JL find,
So true to thy word, So loving and kind;
Thy mercy so tender To all the lost race,
The vilest offender May turn and find grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The mercy I feel, To others I show,
I set to my seal That Jesus is true:
Ye all may find favour, Who come at his call;
O come to my Saviour, His grace is for all!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To save what was lost, From heaven he came;
Come, shiners, and trust In Jesus's name!
He offers you pardon; He bids you be free:
S]

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O let me commend My Saviour to you,
Tne Publican's Friend, And Advocate too:
For you he is pleading His merits and deatli,
With God interceding For sinners beneath.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let us submit His grace to receive;
Fall down at his feet, And gladly believe:
We all are forgiven For Jesus's sake:
Our title to heaven His merits we take.

title: Sinners, turn, why will ye die
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinners, turn, why will ye die?
God, your Saviour, asks you why:
God, who did your souls retrieve,
Died himself, that ye might live.
Will you let him die in vain?
Crucify your Lord again?
Why, ye ransom'd shiners, why
Will you slight his grace, and die?
S Sinners, turn, why will ye die?
God, the Spirit, asks you why:
He who all your lives hath strove,
Woo'd you to embrace his love:
Will you not his grace receive?
Will you still refuse to live?
Why, ye long-sought sinners, why
"you grieve your God and die?
Why,
Will:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Dead already, dead within,
Spiritually dead in sin:
Dead to God, while here you breathe,
Pant ye after second death?
Will ye still in sin remain,
Greedy of eternal pain?
O, ye dying shiners, why,
Why will you for ever die?

title: Let the beasts their breath resign
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: What could your Eedeemer do
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What could your Eedeemer do,
More than he hath done for you V
To procure your peace with God,
Could he more than shed his blood?
After all his waste of love,
All his drawings from above,
Why will you your Lord deny?
Why will you resolve to die?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Turn, he cries, ye sinners, tui*rt;
By his life your God hath sworn,
He would have you turn and live,
He would all the world receive.
If your death were his delight,
Would he you to life invite?
Would he ask, obtest, and cry,
Why will you resolve to die?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sinners, turn, while God is near:
Dare not think him insincere:
Now, even now, your Saviour stands;
All day long he spreads his hands;
Cries, "Ye will not happy be!
No, ye will not come to me!
Me, who life to none deny:
Why will you resolve to die? "

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Can you doubt if God is love?
If to all his bowels move?
Will you not his Word receive?
Will you not his Oath believe?
See! the suffering God appears!
Jesus weeps; believe his tears!
Mingled with his blood they cry,
"Why will you resolve to die?"

title: Sinners, obey the gospel word
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Ready the Father is to own
And kiss his late-returning son:
Ready your loving Saviour stands,
And spreads for you Iris bleeding hands.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ready the Spirit of his Love,
Just now the stony to remove;
To apply and witness with the blood,
And wash and seal the sons of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ready for you the angels wait,
To triumph in your blest estate:
Tuning their harps, they long to praise
The wonders of redeeming grace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Are ready, with their shining host:
All heaven is ready to resound,
"The dead's alive! the lost is found i "

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Come, then, ye sinners, to your Lord,
In Christ to paradise restored;
His proffer'd benefits embrace,
The plenitude of gospel grace:

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
A pardon written with his blood,
The favour and the peace of God;
The seeing eye, the feeling sense,
The mystic joys of penitence:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
The godly grief, the pleasing smart,
The meltings of a oroken heart;
The tears that tell your sins forgiven,
The sighs that waft your souls to heaven

sections.label: Verse 9
Verse 10
sections.text:
The o'erwhelming power of saving grace,
The sight that veils the seraph's face;
The speechless awe that dares not move,
And all the silent heaven of- love.

title: Ye thirsty for God, To Jesus give ear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye thirsty for God, To Jesus give ear,
And take, through his blood, A power to
draw near;
His kind invitation, Ye sinners, embrace,
Accepting salvation, Salvation by grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sent down from above, Who governs the skies,
In vehement love To sinners he cries,
"Drink into my Spirit, "Who happy would be,
And all things inherit, By coming to me."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Saviour of all, Thy word we believe,
And come at thy call, Thy grace to receive:
The blessing is given Wherever thou art,
The earnest of heaven Is love in the heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To us, at thy feet, The Comforter give,
Who gasp to admit Thy Spirit, and live;
The weakest believers Acknowledge for thine.
And fill us with rivers Of water divine!
G'

title: I, in the stead of Christ, they pray
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I, in the stead of Christ, they pray,
Us, in the stead of God, entreat,
To cast our arms, our sins away,
And find forgiveness at bis feet.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our God in Christ! thine embassy,
And proffer'd mercy, we embrace;
And gladly reconciled to thee,
Thy condescending mercy praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Poor debtors, by our Lord's request,
A full acquittance we receive!
And criminals, with pardon blest,
We, at our Judge's instance, live!

title: Come, ye that love the Lord
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, ye that love the Lord,
And let your joys be known;
Join in a song with sweet accord,
While ye surround his throne:
Let those refuse to sing,
Who never knew our God;
But servants of the Heavenly King
May speak their joys abroad.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The God that rales on high,
That all the earth surveys,
That rides upon the stormy sky,
And calms the roaring seas j
This awful God is ours,
Our Father and our Love;
He will send down his heavenly powers,.
To carry us above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There we shall see his face,
And never, never sin;
There, from the rivers of his grace,
Drink endless pleasures in:
Yea, and before we rise
To that immortal state,
The thoughts of such amazing bliss
Should constant joys create.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The men of grace have found
Glory begun below;
Celestial fruit on earthly ground
From faith and hope may grow:
Then let our songs abound,
And every tear be dry:
We're marching through Jmmanuel's ground,
To fairer worlds on high.

title: Happy soul, that, free from harms
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy soul, that, free from harms.
jLL Bests within his Shepherd's arms
Who his quiet shall molest?
AVho shall violate his rest?
Jesus doth his spirit bear:
Jesus takes his every care:
He who found the wandering sheep,
Jesus, still delights to keep.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Live, till all thy life I know,
Perfect, through my Lord, below:
Gladly then from earth remove,
Gather'd to the fold above:
O that I at last may stand
With the sheep at thy right hand;
Take the crown so freely given,
Enter in by thee to heaven!

title: Happy the man that finds the grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the man that finds the grace,
The blessing of God's chosen race,
The wisdom coming from above,
The faith that sweetly works by love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Happy, beyond description, he
Who knows "the Saviour died for me! "
The gift unspeakable obtains,
And heavenly understanding gains

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wisdom divine! Who tells the price
Of Wisdom's costly merchandise?
Wisdom to silver we prefer,
And gold is dross compared to her.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Her hands are fill'd with length of days,
True riches, and immortal praise;
Riches of Christ, on all hestow'd,
And honour that descends from God.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To purest joys she all invites,
Chaste, holy, spiritual delights;
Her ways are ways of pleasantness,
And all her flowery paths are peace.,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Happy the man who Wisdom gains;
Thrice happy, who his guest retains!
He owns, and shall for ever own,
Wisdom, and Christ, and Heaven are one.

title: Happy the souls to Jesus join'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the souls to Jesus join'd,
And saved hy grace alone:
Walking in all his ways, they find
Their heaven on earth hegun.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The church triumphant in thy love,
Their mighty joys we know;
They sing the Lamb in hymns above,
And we in hymns below.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Happy the souls that first believed
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the souls that first believed,
To Jesus and each other cleaved;
Join'd by the unction from above,
In mystic fellowship of love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Meek, simple followers of the Lamb,
They lived, and spake, and thought the same;
They joyfully conspired to raise
Their ceaseless sacrifice of praise.
S With grace abundantly endued,
A pure, believing multitude,
They all were of one heart and soul,
And only love inspired the whole.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O what an age of golden days!
O what a choice, peculiar race!
Wash'd in the Lamb's all-cleansing blood
Anointed Kings and Priests to God!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where shall I wander now to find
The successors they left behind?
The faithful, whom I seek in vain,
Are 'minish'd from the sons of men.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ye different sects, who all declare,
"Lo, here is Christ,"or, "Christ is there! n
Your stronger proofs divinely give,
And show me where the Christians live.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
The gates of hell cannot prevail;
The church on earth can never fail:
Ah! join me to thy secret ones!
Ah! gather all th)r living stones!

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Scatter'd o'er all the earth they lie,
Till thou collect them with thine eye-
Draw by the music of thy Name,
And charm into a beauteous frame.
i O For this the pleading Spirit groans,
And cries in all thy banish' d ones;
Greatest of gifts, thy love impart,
And make us of one mind and heart.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Join every soul that looks to thee,
In bonds of perfect charity;
Now, Lord, the glorious fulness give,
And all in all for ever live!

title: The few that truly call thee Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The few that truly call thee Lord,
And wait thy sanctifying word,
And thee their utmost Saviour own;
Unite and perfect them in one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O let them all thy mind express,
Stand forth thy chosen witnesses:
Thy power unto salvation show,
And perfect holiness below.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In them let all mankind behold,
How Christians lived in days of old;
Mighty their envious foes to move,
A proverb of reproach —and love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Call them into thy wondrous light,
Worthy to walk with thee in white!
•Make up thy jewels, Lord, and show
The glorious, spotless church below!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
From every sinful wrinkle free,
Redeem' d from all iniquity,
The fellowship of saints make known;
And, O my God, might I be one!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O might my lot be cast with these;
The least of Jesu's witnesses:
O that my Lord would count me meet
To wash his dear disciples' feet '

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
This only thing do I require:
Thou know'st 'tis all my heart's desire,
Freely what I receiye to give,
The servant of thy church to live:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
After my lowly Lord to go,
And wait upon thy saints below;
Enjoy the grace to angels given,
And serve the royal heirs of heaven.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Lord, if I now thy drawings feel,
And ask according to thy will,
Confirm the prayer, the seal impart,
And speak the answer to my heart.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
1 Tell me, or thou shalt never go,
"Thy prayer is heard; it shall be so!"
The word hath pass'd thy lips, and I
Shall with thy people live and die.

title: Bid me in thine image rise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bid me in thine image rise,
A saint, a creature new;
True, and merciful, and wise,
And pure, and happy too:
This thy primitive design,
That I should hi thee he hlest;
Should, within the arms divine,
For ever, ever rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let thy will on me he done;
Fulfil my heart's desire,
Thee to know and love alone,
And rise in raptures higher:
Thee, descending on a cloud,
When with ravish'd eyes I see,
Then shall I he fill'd with God
To all eternity!

title: Eejoice evermore With angels ahove
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eejoice evermore With angels ahove,
In Jesus's power, In Jesus's love:
With glad exultation Your triumph proclaim,
Ascribing salvation To God and the Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
All fulness of peace, All fulness of joy,
And spiritual bliss That never shall cloy;
To us it is given In Jesuu to know
A kingdom of heaven, A heaven below.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
O might they at last, With sorrow return,
The pleasures to taste, For which they weie
born;
Our Jesus receiving, Our happiness prove,
The joy of believing, The heaven of love!

title: Weary souls, that wander wide
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Weary souls, that wander wide
From the central point of bliss,
Turn to Jesus crucified,
Fly to those dear wounds of his; [God.
Sink into the purple flood: Bise into the life of

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Find hi Christ the way of peace,
Peace unspeakable, unknown;
By his pain he gives you ease,
Life by his expiring groan: [in all.
Rise, exalted by his fall: Find in Christ your all

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
This the universal bliss,
Bliss for every soul design'd;
God's original promise this,
God's great gift to all mankind; [eternity!
Blest in Christ this moment be! Blest to &!)

title: Ye simple souls that stray
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye simple souls that stray
Far from the path of peace,
(That lonely, unfrequented way
To life and happiness,)
Why will ye folly love,
And throng the downward road,
And hate the wisdom from above,
And mock the sons of God?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Madness and misery
Ye count our life beneath;
And nothing great or good can see,
Or glorious in our death:
As only born to grieve,
Beneath your feet we lie;
And utterly contemn' d we live
And unlamented die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So wretched and obscure,
The men whom ye despise,
So foolish, impotent, and poor, —
Above your scorn we rise:
We, through the Holy Ghost,
Can witness better things;
For He, whose blood is all our boast.
Hath made us Priests and Kings.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Behold the Saviour of mankind
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold the Saviour of mankind
Nail'd to the shameful tree!
How vast the love that him inclined
To bleed and die for thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis done! the precious ransom's paid;
"Receive my soul,"he cries:
See where he bows his sacred head!
He bows his head and dies!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But soon he'll break death's envious chain,
And in full glory shine:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lamb of God! was ever pain,
Was ever love, like thine?

title: Extended on a cursed tree
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Extended on a cursed tree,
Besmear'd with dust, and sweat, and blood,
See there,, the King of Glory see!
Sinks and expires the Son of God!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who, who, my Saviour, this hath done?
Who could thy sacred body wound?
No guilt thy spotless heart hath known,
No guile hath in thy lips been found.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I, I alone, have done the deed!
'Tis I thy sacred flesh Jiave torn;
My sins have caused thee, Lord, to bleed,
Pointed the nail, and fix'd the thorn.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
In the devouring lion's teeth,
Torn, and forsook of all, I lay
Thou sprang'st into the jaws of death,
From death to save the helpless prey.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
My Saviour, how shall I proclaim,
How pay, the mighty debt I owe?
Let all I have, and all I am,
Ceaseless to all thy glory show.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
The meek, the still, the lowly mind,
O may I learn from thee, my God;
And love, with softest pity join'd,
For those that trample on thy blood!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Still let thy tears, thy groans, thy sighs,
O'erflow my eyes, and heave my breast;
Till loose from flesh and earth I rise,
And ever in thy bosom rest.

title: Ye that pass by, behold the Man
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye that pass by, behold the Man,
The Man of Griefs, condemn' d for yea '
The Lamb of God, for sinners slain,
Weeping to Calvary pursue.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See! how his back the scourges tear,
While to the bloody pillar bound )
The ploughers make long furrows there,
Till all his body is one wound.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nor can he thus their hate assuage;
His innocence, to death pursued,
Must fully glut their utmost rage:
Hark! how they clamour for his blood I

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"To us our own Bar abbas give!
Away with him,"(they loudly cry,)
"Away with him, not fit to live,
The vile seducer crucify! "

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His sacred limbs, they stretch, thev tear,
yith nails they fasten to the wood;
$&s "sacred limbs, —exposed and bare,
Or only cover'd with his blood.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
See there his temples crown' d with thorn,
His bleeding hands extended wide,
His streaming feet transfix'd and torn,
The fountain gushing from his side!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Where is the King of Glory now!
The everlasting Son of God!
The' Immortal hangs his languid brow;
The Almighty faints beneath his load!

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Beneath my load he faints and dies:
Jfill'd his soul with pangs unknown:

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
caused those mortal groans and cries,
Jkill'd the Father's only Son!

title: O thou dear suffering Son of God
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou dear suffering Son of God,
How doth thy heart to sinners move 1
Help me to catch thy precious blood;
Help me to taste thy dying love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give me to feel thy agonies;
One drop of thy sad cup afford:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
fain with thee would sympathize,
And share the sufferings of my Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The earth could to her centre quake,
Convulsed, while her Creator died:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
let mine inmost nature shake,
And die with Jesus crucified!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
At thy lastasp the graves display'd
Their horrors to the upper skies:
O that my soul might burst the shade,
And, quicken'd by thy death, arise!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The rocks could feel thy powerful death,
And tremble, and asunder part:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
rend, with thine expiring breath,
The harder marble of my heart!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
My stony heart thy voice shall rent,
Thou wilt, I trust, the veil remove:
My inmost bowels shall resent
The yearnings of thy dying love.

title: I thirst, thou wounded Lamb of God
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I thirst, thou wounded Lamb of God,
To wash me in thy cleansing blood;
To dwell within thy wounds: then pain
Is sweet, and life or death is gain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Take my poor heart, and let it be
For ever closed to all but thee!
Seal thou my breast, and let me wear
That pledge of love for ever there!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How blest are they who still abide
Close shelter' d in thy bleeding side;
Who life and strength from thence derive,
And by thee move, and in thee live.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
wondrous grace! O boundless love!
5 How can it be thou heavenly King,
That thou should'st us to glory bring?
Make slaves the partners of thy throne,
Deck'd with a never-fading crown?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Hence our hearts melt; our eyes o'erflow;
Our words are lost; nor will we know,
Nor will we think of aught beside,
"My Lord, my Love is crucified."

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Ah, Lord! enlarge our scanty thought,
To know the wonders thou hast wrought;
Unloose our stammering tongues, to tell
Thy love immense, unsearchable.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
First-born of many brethren Thou!
To thee, lo! all our souls we bow:
To thee our hearts and hands we give:
Thine may we die; thine may we live!

title: Was ever grief like thine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Was ever grief like thine?
Thou my pain, my curse hast took,
All my sins were laid on thee:
Help me, Lord; to thee I look;
Draw me, Saviour, after thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
When, O my God, shall I
For thee submit to die?
How the mighty debt repay?
Rival of thy passion prove?
Lead me in thyself, the way;
Melt my hardness into love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To love is all my wish;
1 only live for this:
Grant me, Lord, my heart's desire,
There, by faith, for ever dwell:
This I always will require,
Thee, and only thee, to feel.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy power I pant to prove,
Rooted and fix'd in love;
Strengthen'd by thy Spirit's might,
Wise to fathom things divine,
What the length, and breadth, and height.
What the depth of love like thine.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: O Love divine! what hast thou done
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Love divine! what hast thou done!
The' immortal God hath died for me I
The Father's co-eternal Son
Bore all my sins upon the tree:
The' immortal God for me hath died!
My Lord, my Love is crucified.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Behold him, all ye that pass by,
The bleeding Prince of Life and Peace!
Come, see, ye worms, your Maker die,
And say, was ever grief like his?
Come, feel with me his blood applied:
My Lord, my Love is crucified.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Then let us sit beneath his cross,
And gladly catch the healing stream:
All things for him account but loss,
And give up all our hearts to him:
Of nothing think or speak beside,
"My Lord, my Love is crucified."

title: Come, ye weary sinners, come
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, ye weary sinners, come,
All who groan beneath your load;
Jesus calls his wanderers home:
Hasten to your pardoning God.
Come, ye guilty spirits oppress'd,
Answer to the Saviour's call:
"Come, and I will give you rest:
Come, and I will save you all."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, full of truth and love,
We thy kindest word obey:
Faithful let thy mercies prove;
Take our load of guilt away:
Fain we would on thee rely,
Cast on thee our every care;
To thine arms of mercy fly,
Find our lasting quiet there.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Burden'd with a world of grief,
Burden' d with our sinful load,
Burden'd with this unbelief,
Burden'd with the wrath of God;
Lo! we come to thee for ease,
True and gracious as thou art;
Now our groaning souls release,
Write forgiveness on our heart.

title: how shall I the goodness tell
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
how shall I the goodness tell,
Father, which thou to me hast show d?
That I, a child of wrath arid hell,

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
And shall I slight my Father's love?
Or basely fear his gifts to own?
Unmindful of his favours prove?
Shall I, the hallow'd cross to shun,
Refuse his righteousness to impart,
By hiding it within my heart?

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Outcasts of men, to you I call,
Harlots, and publicans, and thieves!
He spreads his arms to embrace you all
Sinners alone his grace receives:
No need of him the righteous have;
He came the lost to seek and save.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7

title: See, sinners, in the gospel glass
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See, sinners, in the gospel glass,
The Friend and Saviour of mankind!
Not one of all the apostate race
But may in him salvation find!
His thoughts, and words, and actions prove,—
His life and death, —that God is love!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Behold the Lamb of God, who bears
The sins of all the world away!
A servant's form he meekly wears,
He sojourns in a house of clay!
His glory is no longer seen,
But God with God is man with men.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
"Ah! do not of my goodness doubt;
My saving grace for all is free;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
will in nowise cast him out
That comes a sinner unto me;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
can toione myself deny;
Why, sinners, will ye perish, why?"

title: Sinners, believe the gospel word
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
See where the lame, the halt, the blind,
The deaf, the dumb, the sick, the poor,
Flock to the Friend of human kind,
And freely all accept their cure:
To whom did he his help deny?
Whom, in his days of flesh pass by?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Did not his word the fiends expel,
The lepers cleanse, and raise the dead r
Did he not all their sickness heal,
And satisfy their every need?
Did he reject his helpless clay,
Or send them sorrowful away?
i Nay, hut his bowels yeam'd to see
The people hungry, scatter'd, faint;
Nay, but he utter' d over thee,
Jerusalem, a true complaint;
Jerusalem, who shedd'st his blood,
That, with his tears, for thee hath flow'd.

title: Would Jesus have the sinner die
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Would Jesus have the sinner die?
Why hangs he then on yonder tree?
What means that strange expiring cry?
(Sinners, he prays for you and me:)
"Forgive them, Father, O forgive:
They know not that by me they live! "

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Adam descended from above,
Our loss of Eden to retrieve,
Great God of universal love,
If all the world through thee may live,
In us a quick'ning Spirit be,
And witness thou hast died for me!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou loving, all-atoning Lamb,
Thee —by thy painful agony,
Thy bloody sweat, thy grief and shame,
Thy cross, and passion on the tree,
Thy precious death and life —I pray,
Take all, take all my sins away!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O let me kiss thy bleeding feet,
And bathe and wash them with my tears j
The story of thy love repeat
In every drooping shiner's ears;
That all may hear the quick'ning sound,
Since I, even I, have mercy found.
b O let thy love my heart constrain,
Thy love for every sinner free;
That every fallen soul of man
May taste the grace that found out me;
That all mankind with me may prove
Thy sovereign, everlasting love.

title: Let earth and heaven agree
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let earth and heaven agree,
JLi Angels and men be join'd,
To celebrate with me
The Saviour of mankind;
To adore the all-atoning Lamb,
And bless the sound of Jesu's Name.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
His name the sinner hears,
And is from sin set free;
'Tis music in his ears,
'Tis life and victory:
New songs do now his lips employ
And dances his glad heart for joy.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Stung by the scorpion sin,
My poor expiring soul
The balmy sound drinks in,
And is at once made whole:
See there my Lord upon the tree!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
hear, I feel, he died for me.
6 O unexampled love!
O all-redeeming grace L
How swiftly didst thou move
To save a fallen race!
What shall I do to make it known
What thou for all mankind hast done?

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O for a trumpet-voice
On all the world to call!
To bid their heart rejoice
In him who died for all!
For all my Lord was crucified:
For all, for all my Saviour died!

title: Jesus, thou all-redeeming Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thou all-redeeming Lord,
Thy blessing we implore;
Open the door to preach thy word,
The great effectual door.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Gather the outcasts in, and save
From sin and Satan's power;
And let them now acceptance have,
And know their gracious hour.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lover of souls! thou know'st to prize
What thou hast bought so dear:
Come, then, and in thy people's eyes
With all thy wounds appear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Appear, as when of old confest
The suffering Son of God;
And let them see thee in thy vest
But newly dipt in blood.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The hardness from their hearts remove,
Tbou who for all hast died;
Show them the tokens of thy love,
Thy feet, thy hands, thy side.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Thy feet were nail'd to yonder tree,
To trample down their sin:
Thy hands stretch'd out they all may see,
To take thy murderers in.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Thy side an open fountain is,
Where all may freely go,
And drink the living streams of bliss,
And wash them white as snow.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Ready thou art the blood to' apply,
And prove the record true;
And all thy wounds to sinners cry,
"I suffer'd this for you! "

title: Lovers of pleasure more than God
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lovers of pleasure more than God,
For you he suffer'd paki;
Swearers, for you he spilt his blood:
And shall he bleed in vain?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Misers, for you his life was paid;
Your basest crime he bore:
Drunkards, your sins on him were laid,
That you might sin no more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The God of love, to earth he came,
That you might come to heaven;
Believe, believe in Jesu's Name,
And all your sin 's forgiven.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Believe in him that died for thee,
And sure as he hath died,
Thy debt is paid, thy soul is free,
And thou art justified.

title: Jesus, the Name high over all
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, the Name high over all,
In hell, or earth, or sky,
Angels and men before it fall,
And devils fear and fly.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, the Name to sinners dear,
The Name to sinners given;
It scatters all their guilty fear,
It turns their hell to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus the prisoner's fetters breaks,
And bruises Satan's head;
Power into strengthless souls it speaks,
And life into the dead.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that the world might taste and see
The riches of his grace!
The arms of love that compass me.
Would all mankind embrace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His only righteousness I show,
His saving truth proclaim;
'Tis all my business here below
To cry, "Behold the Lamb! "

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Happy, if with my latest breath
I may but gasp his name;
Preach him to all, and cry in death,
"Behold, behold the Lamb! "

title: O God, of good the unfathom'd Sea
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, of good the unfathom'd Sea!
Who would not give his heart to thee?
Who would not love thee with his might,
O Jesu, Lover of mankind?
Who would not his whole soul and mind,
With his whole strength, to thee unite?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
TLou shin'st with everlasting rays:
Before the' insufferable blaze
Angels with both wings veil their eyes;
Yet, free as air thy bounty streams
On all thy works; thy mercy's beams
Diffusive, as thy sun's, arise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Astonish'd at thy frowning brow,
Earth, hell, and heaven's strong pillars bow '
Terrible majesty is thine!
Who then can that vast love express.
Which bows thee down to me, who less
Than nothing am, till thou art mine!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
High throned on heaven's eternal hill,
In number, weight, and measure still
Thou sweetly orderest all that is:
And yet thou deign' st to come to me,
And guide my steps, that I, with thee
Enthroned, may reign in endless bliss.
b Fountain of good, all blessing flows
From thee; no want thy fulness knows:
What but thyself canst thou desire?
Yet, self-sufficient as thou art,
Thou dost desire my worthless heart:
This, only this, dost thou require.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Primeval Beauty! in thy sight,
The first-born fairest sons of light
See all their brightest glories fade:
What then to me thine eyes could turn?
In sin conceived, of woman born,
A worm, a leaf, a blast, a shade!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Hell's armies tremble at thy nod,
And, trembling, own the' Almighty God,
Sovereign of earth, hell, air, and sky:
But who is this that comes from far,
Whose garments roll'd in blood appear?
'Tis God made man, for man to die.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O God, of good the unfatliom'd Sea!
Who would not give his heart to thee?
Who would not love thee with his might,
O Jesu, Lover of mankind?
Who would not his whole soul and mind,
With his whole strength, to thee unite?

title: Father, whose everlasting Love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, whose everlasting Love
Thy only Son for sinners gave;
Whose grace to all did freely move,
And sent him down the world to save:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Help us thy mercy to extol,
Immense, unfathom'd, unconfined;
To praise the Lamb who died for all,
The general Saviour of mankind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy undistinguishing regard
Was cast on Adam's helpless race:
For all thou hast in Christ prepared
Sufficient, sovereign, saving grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The world he suffer'd to redeem:
For all he hath the' atonement made:
For those that will not come to him,
The ransom of his life was paid.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Why then, thou universal Love,
Should any of thy grace despair?
To all, to all, thy bowels move,
But straiten' d in our own we are.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Arise, O God, maintain thy cause!
The fulness of the Gentiles call:
Lift up the standard of thy cross,
And all shall own thou diedst for all

title: Ye neighbours and friends, To Jesus draw
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye neighbours and friends, To Jesus draw
JL near;
His love condescends, By titles so dear,
To call and invite you His triumph to prove,
And freely delight you In Jesus's love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Shepherd who died His sheep to redeem.
On every side Are gather' d to him
The weary and burden'd, The reprobate race;
And wait to be pardon'd Through Jesus's grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
The deaf hear his voice, And comforting word;
It bids them rejoice In Jesus their Lord:
"Thy sins are forgiven, Accepted thou art; "
They listen, and heaven Springs up in their
heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
To us and to them Is publish'd the word:
Then let us proclaim Our life-giving Lord,
Who now is reviving His work in our days,
And mightily striving To save us by grace.

sections.label: Verse 7

title: O God! our help in ages past
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God! our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Under the shadow of thy throne,
Still may we dwell secure;
Sufficient is thine arm alone,
And our defence is sure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting thou art God,
To endless years the same.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A thousand ages, in thy sight,
Are likevan evening gone;
Short as the watch that ends the night,
Before the rising sun.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The busy tribes of flesh and blood,
With all their cares and fears,
Are carried downward by the flood,
AnB lost in following years.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Time, like an ever-rolling stream,
Bears all its sons away;
They fly forgotten, as a dream
Dies at the opening day.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O God! our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come;
Be thou our guard while life shall last,
And our perpetual home.

title: Thee we adore, Eternal Name
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thee we adore, Eternal Name!
And humbly own to thee,
How feeble is our mortal frame,
What dying worms we be!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our wasting lives grow shorter still,
As days and months increase;
And every beating pulse we tell
Leaves but the number less.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The year rolls round, and steals away
The breath that first it gave;
Whate'er we do, where'er we be,
We're travelling to the grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Dangers stand thick through all the ground,
To push us to the tomb;
And fierce diseases wait around,
To hurry mortals home.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Great God! on what a slender thread
Hang everlasting things!
The' eternal states of all the dead,
Upon life's feeble strings!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Infinite joy, or endless woe,
• Attends on every breath;
And yet, how unconcern'd we go
Upon the brink of death!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Waken, O Lord, our drowsy sense,
To walk this dangerous road!
And if our souls be hurried hence,
May they be found with God.

title: And am I born to die
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And am I born to die?
To lay this body down?
And must my trembling spirit fly
Into a world unknown?
—A land of deepest shade,
Unpierced by human thought,
The dreary regions of the dead,
Where all things are forgot.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon as from earth I go,
What will become of me?
Eternal happiness or woe
Must then my portion be:
Waked by the trumpet's sound,

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
How shall I leave my tomb?
With triumph or regret?
A fearful or a joyful doom,
A curse or blessing meet?
Will angel-bands convey
Their brother to the bar?
Or devils drag my soul away,
To meet its sentence there?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Who can resolve the doubt
That tears my anxious breast?
Shall I be with the damn'd cast out,
Or number'd with the blest?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
must from God be driven,
Or with my Saviour dwell;
Must come at his command to heaven,
Or else —depart to hell.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
may with joy appear!
6 Thou art thyself the Way;
Thyself in me reveal:
So shall I spend my life's short day
Obedient to thy will;
So shall I love my God,
Because lie first loved me,
And praise thee in thy bright abode,
To ail eternity.

title: And am I only born to die
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And am I only born to die?
And must I suddenly comply
With nature's stern decree?
What after death for me remains?
Celestial joy, or hellish pains,
To all eternity!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How then ought I on earth to live,
While God prolongs the kind reprieve,
And props the house of clay!
My sole concern, my single care,
To watch, and tremble, and prepare,
Against the fatal day!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No room for mirth or trifling here,
For worldly hope, or worldly fear,
If life so soon is gone:
If now the Judge is at the door,
And all mankind mus.t stand before
The' inexorable throne!
i No matter which my thoughts employ,
A moment's misery, or joy;
But O! when both shall end,
Where shall I find my destin'd place?
Shall I my everlasting days
With fiends or angels spend?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nothing is worth a thought beneath.
But how I may escape the death
That never, never die-»
How make mine own election sure,
And, when I fail on earth, secure
A mansion in the skies!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, vouchsafe a pitying ray:
Be thou my Guide, be thou my Way
To glorious happiness!
Ah, write the pardon on my heart,
And whensoe'er I hence depart,
Let me depart in peace.

title: Shrinking from the cold hand of death
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Shrinking from the cold hand of death,
O I too shall gather up my feet;
Shall soon resign this fleeting breath,
And die, my father's God to meet.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Number'd among thy people, I
Expect with joy thy face to see:
Because thou didst for sinners die,
Jesus, in death, remember me!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O that without a lingering groan
I may the welcome word receive;
My body with my charge lay down,
And cease at once to work and live!

title: The morning flowers display their sweets
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The morning flowers display their sweets,
And gay their silken leaves unfold,
As careless of the noontide heats,
As fearless of the evening cold.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nipt by the wind's unkindly blast,
Parch' d by the sun's directer ray,
The momentary glories waste,
The short-lived beauties die away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So blooms the human face divine,
When youth its pride of beauty shows:
Fairer than spring the colours shine,
And sweeter than the virgin rose.
-i Or worn by slowly rolling years,
Or broke by sickness in a day,
Tbe fading glory disappears,
The short-lived beauties die away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yet these, new rising from the tomb,
With lustre brighter far shall shine;
Revive with ever-during bloom,
Safe from diseases and decline.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Let sickness blast, and death devour,
If heaven must recompense our pains:
Perish the grass, and fade the flower,
If firm the word of God remains.

title: Pass a few swiftly-fleeting years
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Pass a few swiftly-fleeting years,
And all that now in bodies live
Shall quit, like me, the vale of tears,
Their righteous sentence to receive.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But all, before they hence remove,
May mansions for themselves prepare
In that eternal house above;
And, O my God, shall I be there?

title: Ah, lovely appearance of death
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ah, lovely appearance of death!
"What sight upon earth is so fair?
Not all the gay pageants that breathe
Can with a dead body compare:
With solemn delight I survey
The corpse, when the spirit is fled,
In love with the beautiful clay,
And longing to lie in its stead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How blest is our brother, bereft
Of all that could burden his mind!
How easy the soul that has left
This wearisome body behind!
Of evil incapable, thou,
Whose relics with envy I see,
No longer in misery now,
No longer a shiner like me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This earth is affected no more
With sickness, or shaken with pain:
The war in the members is o'er,
And never shall vex him again:
No anger henceforward, or shame,
Shall redden this innocent clay:
Extinct is the animal flame,
And passion is vanish'd away.
£ This languishing head is at rest,
Its thinking and aching are o'er;
This quiet immovable breast
Is heaved by affliction no more:
This heart is no longer the seat
Of trouble and torturing pain;
It ceases to flutter and beat,
It never shall flutter again.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The lids he so seldom could close,
By sorrow forbidden to sleep,
Seal'd up in their mortal repose,
Have strangely forgotten to weep:
The fountains can yield no supplies,
These hollows from water are free;
The tears are all wiped from these eyes,
And evil they never shall see.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To monm and to suffer is mine,
While bound in a prison I breathe,
And still for deliverance pine,
And press to the issues of death;
What now with my tears I bedew,
O might I this moment become!
My spirit created anew,
My flesh be consign' d to the tomb!

title: Rejoice for a brother deceased
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rejoice for a brother deceased,
JLV Our loss is his infinite gain;
A soul out of prison released,
And free from its bodily chain;
With songs let us follow his flight,
And mount with his spirit above,
Escaped to the mansions of light,
And lodged in the Eden of love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our brother the haven hath gain'd,
Out-flying the tempest and wind:
His rest he hath sooner obtain' d,
And left his companions behind,
Still toss'd on a sea of distress,
Hard toiling to make the blest shore,
"Where all is assurance and peace,
And sorrow and sin are no more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There all the ship's company meet,
Who sail'd with the Saviour beneath;
With shouting each other they greet,
And triumph o'er trouble and death:
The voyage of life 's at an end,
The mortal affliction is past;
The age that in heaven they spend,
For ever and ever shall last.

title: Lo! the prisoner is released
author: G  Lesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo! the prisoner is released,
Lighten' d of his fleshly load;
Where the weary are at rest,
He is gather' d in to God!
Lo! the pain of life is past,
All his warfare now is o'er;
Death and hell behind are cast,
Grief and suffering are no mors

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yes, the Christian's course is run,
Ended is the glorious strife;
Fought the fight, the work is done,
Death is swallow'd up of life!
Borne by angels on their wings,
Far from earth the spirit flies,
Finds his God, and sits, and sings,
Triumphing in Paradise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jom we, then, with one accord,
In the new, the joyful song:
Absent from our loving Lord
We shall not continue long:
We shall quit the house of clay,
We a better lot shall share;
We shall see the realms of day,
Meet our happy brother there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let the world bewail their dead,
Fondly of their loss complain *7
Brother, friend, by Jesus freed,
Death to thee, to us, is gain:
Thou art enter'd into joy:
Let the unbelievers mourn;
We in songs our lives employ,
Till we all to God return.

title: Hark! a voice divides the sky
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark! a voice divides the sky,
Happy are the faithful dead!
In the Lord who sweetly die,
They from all their toils are freed
Them the Spirit hath declared
Blest, unutterably blest:
Jesus is their great Reward,
Jesus is their endless Rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Follow'd by their works, they go
Where their Head hath gone before
Reconciled by grace below,
Grace had open'd Mercy's door;
Justified through faith alone,
Here they knew their sins forgiven;
Here they laid their burden down,
Hallow'd, and made meet for heaven
Who can now lament the lot
Of a saint in Christ deceased?
Let the world, who know us not,
Call us hopeless and unbless'd:
When from flesh the spirit freed,
Hastens homeward to return,
Mortals cry, "A man is dead! "
Angels sing, "A child is bom! '
Born into the world above,
They our happy brother greet;
Bear him to the throne of Love,
Place him at the Saviour's feet:
Jesus smiles, and says, "Well done,
Good and faithful servant thou;
Enter, and receive thy crown,
Keign with me triumphant now."
Angels catch the approving sound,
Bow, and bless the just award;
Hail the heir with glory crown'd,
Now rejoicing with his Lord:
Fuller joys ordain'd to know,.
Waiting for the general doom,
When the Archangel's trump shall blow,
"Fuse, ye dead, to judgment come!"

title: Again we lift our voice
author: Vnshjsr J

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Our friend is gone before
To that celestial shore;
He hath left his mates behind,
He hath all the storms outrode!
Found the rest we toil to find,
Landed in the arms of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And shall we mourn to see
Our fellow-prisoner free? —
Free from doubts, and griefs, and fears,
In the haven of the skies?
Can we weep to see the tears
Wiped for ever from his eyes?

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou, in thy youthful prime,
Hast leap'd the bounds of time:
Suddenly from earth released,
Lo! we now rejoice for thee;
Taken to an early rest,
Caught into eternity.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Thither may we repair,
That glorious bliss to share;
We shall see the welcome day,
We shall to the summons bow:
Come, Eedeemer, come away:
Now prepare, and take us now!

title: Give glory to Jesus our Head
author: C    Vesi Ey

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The soul hath o'ertaken her mate,
And caught him again in the sky:
Advanced to her happy estate,
And pleasure that never shall die:
Where glorified spirits by sight,
Converse in their holy abode,
As stars in the firmament bright,
And pure as the angels of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Heaven! what a triumph is there!
Where all in his praises agree;
His.beautiful character bear,
And shine with the glory they sec
The glory of God and the Lamb
(While all in the ecstasy join)
Darts into their spiritual frame,
And gives the enjoyment divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In loud hallelujahs they sing,
And harmony echoes bis nraise
VVTien, lo! the celestial King
Pours out the full light of his face:
The joy neither angel nor saint
Can bear, so ineffably great;
But, lo! the whole company faint,
And heaven is found —at his feet.

title: Hearken to the solemn voice
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hearken to the solemn voice,
The awful midnight cry J
Waiting souls, rejoice, rejoice,
And see the Bridegroom nigh:
Lo! he comes to keep his word,
Light and joy his looks impart:
Go ye forth to meet your Lord,
And meet him in your heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Wait we all in patient hope,
Till Christ, the Judge, shall come j
We shall soon he all caught up
To meet the general doom:
In an hour to us unknown,
As a thief in deepest night,
Christ shall suddenly come down,
With all his saints in light.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Happy he whom Christ shall find
Watching to see him come;
Him the Judge of all mankind
Shall bear triumphant home:
Who can answer to his word?
Which of you dares meet his day?
"Rise, and come to judgment! "—Lord.
We rise, and come away.

title: Thou Judge of quick and dead
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou Judge of quick and dead,
Before whose bar severe,
With holy joy, or guilty dread,
We all shall soon appear;
Our caution' d souls prepare
For that tremendous day;
And fill us now with watchful care,
And stir us up to pray:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To pray and wait the hour,
That awful hour unknown;
When robed in majesty and power,
Thou shalt from heaven come down,
The immortal Son of Man,
To judge the human race,
With all thy Father's dazzling train.
With all thv glorious grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To damp our eartlily joys,
To' increase our gracious fears,
For ever let the Archangel's voice
Be sounding in our ears;
The solemn midnight cry,
"Ye dead, the Judge is come;
Arise, and meet him in the sky,
And meet your instant doom! "

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O may we thus be found
Obedient to his word;
Attentive to the trumpet's sound,
And looking for our Lord!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
may we thus ensure
A lot among the blest;
And watch a moment to secure
An everlasting rest!

title: He comes! he comes! the Judge severe
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He comes! he comes! the Judge severe!
The seventh trumpet speaks him near;
His lightnings flash; his thunders roll:
How welcome to the faithful soul!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Descending on his azure throne,
He claims the kingdoms for his own;
The kingdoms all obey his word,
And hail him their triumphant Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Shout, all the people of the sky!
And all the saints of the Most High;
Our Lord, who now his right obtains,
For ever and for ever reigns.

title: The great Archangel's trump shall sound
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The great Archangel's trump shall sound,
(While twice ten thousand thunders roar,)
Tear up the graves, and cleave the ground,
And make the greedy sea restore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The greedy sea shall yield her dead,
The earth no more her slain conceal;
Sinners shall lift their guilty head,
And shrink to see a yawning hell.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But we, who now our Lord confess,
And faithful to the end endure,
Shall stand in Jesu's righteousness,
Stand, as the Rock of Ages, sure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We, while the stars from heaven shall fall,
And mountains are on mountains hurl'd,
Shall stand unmoved amidst them all,
And smile to see a burning world.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The earth, and all the works therein,
Dissolve, by raging flames destroy'd;
While we survey the awful scene,
And mount above the fiery void.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
By faith we now transcend the skies,
And on that ruin'd world look down:
By love above all height we rise,
And share the everlasting throne.

title: Jesus, faithful to his word
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
First the dead in Christ shall rise,
Then we that yet remain
Shall he caught up to the skies,
And see our Lord again:
We shall meet him in the air,
All rapt up to heaven shall be;
Find, and love, and praise him there.
To all eternity.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who can tell the happiness
This glorious hope affords?
Joy unutter'd we possess
In these reviving words:
Happy while on earth we breathe;
Mightier bliss ordain' d to know;
Trampling down sin, hell, and death,
To the third heaven we go.

title: Thou God of glorious majesty
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Lo! on a narrow neck of land,
'Twixt two unbounded seas I stand,
Secure, insensible;
A point of time, a moment's space,
Removes me to that heavenly place,
Or shuts me up in hell.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O God, mine inmost soul convert!
And deeply on my thoughtful heart
Eternal things imprestt:
Give me to feel their solemn weight,
And tremble on the brink of fate,
And wake to righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Before me place, in dread array,
The pomp of that tremendous clay,
When thou with clouds shalt come,
To judge the nations at thy bar;
And tell me, Lord, shall I be there,
To meet a joyful doom?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Be this my one great business here,
With serious industry and fear
Eternal bliss to' ensure:
Thine utmost counsel to fulfil,
And suffer all thy righteous will,
And to the end endure.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Then, Saviour, then, my soul receive,
Transported from this vale to live
And reign with thee above;
Where faith is sweetly lost in sight,
And hope in full supreme delight,
And everlasting love.

title: Righteous God! whose vengeful phials
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Righteous God! whose vengeful phials
All our fears and thoughts exceed,
Big with woes and fiery trials,
Hanging, bursting o'er our head;
While thou visitest the nations,
Thy selected people spare;
Arm our caution'd souls with patience,
Fill our humbled hearts with prayer,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If thy dreadful controversy
With all flesh is now begun,
In thy wrath remember mercy;
Mercy first and last be sho,wn:
Plead thy cause with sword and fire,
Shake us till the curse remove,
Till thou com'st, the world's desire,
Conquering all with sovereign love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Every fresh alarming token
More confirms the faithful word;
Nature (for its Lord hath spoken)
Must he suddenly restored:
From this national confusion,
From this ruin'd earth and skies,
See the times of restitution,
See the new creation rise!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Vanish, then, this world of shadows
Pass the former things away:
Lord, appear! appear to glad us
With the dawn of endless day!
O conclude this mortal story,
Throw this universe aside!
Come, eternal King of Glory,
Now descend, and take thy bride!

title: Stand the' omnipotent decree
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Stand the' omnipotent decree:
(O Jehovah's will be done!
Nature's end we wait to see,
And hear her final groan:
Let this earth dissolve, and blend
In death the wicked and the just;
Let those ponderous orbs descend,
And grind us into dust.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rests secure the righteous man!
At his Redeemer's beckr
Sure to' emerge, and rise again,
And mount above the wreck;
Lo! the heavenly spirit towers,
Like flame, o'er nature's funeral pyre.
Triumphs in immortal powers,
And claps his wings of fire!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nothing hath the just to lose,
By worlds on worlds destroy'd;
Far beneath his feet he views,
With smiles, the flaming void:
Sees the universe renew'd,
The grand millennial reign begun;
Shouts, with all the sons of God,
Around the eternal throne!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Resting in this glorious hope
To be at last restored,
Yield we now our bodies up
To earthquake, plague, or sword:
Listening for the call divine,
The latest trumpet of the seven,
Soon our soul and dust shall join,
And both fly up to heaven.

title: How happy are the little flock
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy are the little flock,
Who, safe beneath their guardian-rock,
In all commotions rest!
When war's and tumult's waves run high,
Unmoved above the storm they lie,
They lodge in Jesu's breast.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Such happiness, O Lord, have we,
By mercy gather'd into thee,
Before the floods descend:
And while the bursting cloud comes down,
We mark the vengeful day begun,
And calmly wait the eud.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The plague, and dearth, and din of war,
Our Saviour's swift approach declare,
And bid our hearts arise:
Earth's basis shook confirms our hope;
Its cities' fall but lifts us up,
To meet thee in the skies.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Appear with clouds on Sion's hill,
The word and mystery to fulfil,
Thy confessors to' approve,
Thy members on thy throne to place,
And stamp thy name on every face,
In glorious heavenly love!

title: Woe to the men on earth who dwell
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Woe to the men on earth who dwell,
Nor dread the' Almighty's frown;
When God doth all his wrath reveal,
And shower his judgments down!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sinners, expect those heaviest showers:
To meet your God prepare!
For, lo! the seventh angel pours
His phial in the air.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lo! from their seats the mountains leap;
The mountains are not found j
Transported far into the deep,
And in the ocean drown'd.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Who then, shall live, and face the throne,
And face the Judge severe?
When heaven and earth are fled and gone,
O where shall I appear?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Now, only now, against that hour,
We may a place provide;
Beyond the grave, beyond the power
Of hell, our spirits hide:

sections.label: Verse 6

title: By faith we find the place above
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
By faith we find the place above,
The rock that rent in twain;
Beneath the shade of dying love,
And in the clefts remain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, to thy dear wounds we flee,
We smk into thy side;
Assured that all who trust in thee
Shall evermore abide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then let the thund'ring trumpet sound
The latest lightning glare;
The mountains melt; the solid ground
Dissolve as liquid air:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The huge celestial bodies roll,
Amidst that general fire.
And shrivel as a parchment scroll,
And all in smoke expire!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yet still the Lord, the Saviour reign 3
When nature is destroy'd,
And no created thing remains
Throughout the flaming void.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Sublime upon his azure throne,
He speaks the' Almighty word:
His fiat is obey'd! 'tis done;
And Paradise restored.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
So be it! let this system end,
This ruinous earth and skies;
The New Jerusalem descend,
The New Creation rise.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Thy power omnipotent assume;
Thy brightest majesty!
And when thou dost in glory come,
My Lord, remember me!

title: Ye virgin souls, arise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye virgin souls, arise,
With all the dead awake!
Unto salvation wise,
Oil in your vessels take:
Upstarting at the midnight cry,
"Behold the heavenly Bridegroom nigh [ w

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He comes, he comes, to call
The nations to his bar,
And raise to glory all
Who fit for glory are:
Made ready for your full reward,
Go forth with joy to meet your Lord..

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Go, meet him in the sky,
Your everlasting friend;
Your Head to glorify,
With all his saints ascend:
Ye pure in heart, obtain the grace
To see, without a veil, his face!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ye that have here received
The unction from above,
And in his Spirit live,
Obedient to his love,
Jesus shall claim you for his bride:
Rejoice with all the sanctified!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The everlasting doors
Shall soon the saints receive,
Above yon angel powers,
In glorious joy to live;
Far from a world of grief and sin,
With God eternally shut in.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Then let us wait to hear
The trumpet's welcome sound;
To see our Lord appear,
Watching let us be found;
When Jesus doth the heavens bow,
Be found —as Lord, thou find'st us now!
t.olivers, HYMN GQ. p.m. (17,36,33,58)

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
T O! He comes with clouds descending,
I 1 Once for favour'd sinners slain;
Thousand, thousand saints attending,
Swell the triumph of his train:
Hallelujah! God appears on earth to reign.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Every eye shall now behold him
Robed in dreadful majesty;
Those who set at nought and sold him,
Pierced and nail'd him to the tree.
Deeply wailing, shall the true Messiah see.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
The dear tokens of his passion
Still his dazzling body bears;
Cause of endless exultation
To his ransom' d worshippers: [scars!
With what rapture gaze we on those glorious

sections.label: Verse 10

title: How weak the thoughts, and vain
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How weak the thoughts, and vain,
Of self- deluding men;
Men, who, fix'd to earth alone,
Think their houses shall endure,
Fondly call their lands their own,
To their distant hens secure.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How happy then are we,
Who build, O Lord, on thee!
What can our foundation shock!
Though the shatter'd earth removOj
Stands our city on a rock,
On the rock of heavenly Love.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
High on Immanuel's land
We see the fabric stand;
From a tottering world remove
To our steadfast mansion there:
Our inheritance above
Cannot pass from heir to heir.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Those amaranthine bowers
(Unalienably ours)
Bloom, our infinite reward,
Rise, our pennanent abode,
From the founded world prepared;
Purchased by the blood of God.
O might we quickly find
The place for us design' d;
See the long-expected day
Of our full redemption here:
Let the shadows flee away,
Let the new-made world appear.
High on thy great white throne,
O King of saints, come down,
In the New Jerusalem
Now triumphantly descend;
Let the final trump proclaim
Joys begun which ne'er shall end.

title: How happy is the pilgrim's lot
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy is the pilgrim's lot!
How free from every anxious though t
From worldly hope and fear!
Confined to neither court nor cell,
His soul disdains on earth to dwell,
He only sojourns here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This happiness in part is mine,
Already saved from low design,
From every creature-love;
Blest with the scorn of finite good,
My soul is lighten' d of its load,
And seeks the things above.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
neither have nor want.
4 I have no babes to hold me here;
But children more securely dear
For mine I humbly claim,
Better than daughters or than sons.
Temples divine of living stones,
Inscrib'd with Jesu's name.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
Nothing on earth I call my own;
A stranger, to the world unknown,

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
all their goods despise;
I trample on their whole delight,
And seek a country out of sight,
A country hi the skies.

sections.label: Verse 9
Verse 10
sections.text:
I come, —thy servant, Lord, replies;—
I come to meet thee in the skies,
And claim my heavenly rest!
Now let the Pilgrim's journey end:
Now, O my Saviour, Brother, Friend.
Receive me to thy breast I

title: Thou, Lord, on whom I still depend
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou, Lord, on whom I still depend,
Shalt keep me faithful to the end:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
trust thy truth, and love, and power,
Shall save me to the latest hour;
And, when I lay this body down,
Reward with an immortal crown.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, in thy great Name I go
To conquer death, my final foe!
And when I quit this cumbrous clay
And soar on angels' wings away,
My soul the second death defies,
And reigns eternal in the skies

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Eye hath not seen, nor ear hath heard,
What Christ hath for his saints prepared,
Who conquer through their Saviour's might,
Who sink into perfection's height,
And trample death beneath theii feet,
And gladly die their Lord to meet.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Dost thou desire to know and see
What thy mysterious name shall be!
Contending for thy heavenly home,
Thy latest foe hi death o'ercome;
Till then thou searchest out in vain,
What only conquest can explain.

title: I long- to behold him array'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I long- to behold him array'd
With glory and light from above,
The King in liis beauty display'd,
His beauty of holiest love:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
languish and sigh to be there,
Where Jesus hath fix'd his abode:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
when shall we meet in the air,
And fly to the mountain of God!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With him I on Sion shall stand,
(For Jesus hath spoken the word,)
The breadth of Immanuel's land
Survey by the light of my Lord;
But when, on thy bosom reclined,
Thy face I am strengthen'd to see,
My fulness of rapture I find,
My heaven of heavens, in thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
How happy the people that dwell
Secure in the city above!
No pain the inhabitants feel,
No sickness or sorrow shall prove.
Physician of souls, unto me
Forgiveness and holiness give;
And then from the body set free,
And then to the city receive!

title: Leader of faithful souls, and Guide
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Leader of faithful souls, and Guide
JLJ Of all that travel to the sky,
Come, and with us, even us abide,
Who would on thee alone rely;
On thee alone our spirits stay,
While held in life's uneven way.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Strangers and pilgrims here below,
This earth, we know, is not our place;
But hasten through the vale of woe,
And, restless to behold thy face,
Swift to our heavenly country move,
Our everlasting home above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We have no 'biding city here,
But seek a city out of sight;
Thither our steady course we steer,
Aspiring to the plains of light,
Jerusalem, the saints' abode,
Whose founder is the living God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Patient the' appointed race to run,
This weary world we cast behind;
From strength to strength we travel on,
The New Jerusalem to find:
Our labour this, our only aim,
To find the New Jerusalem.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Through thee, who all our sins hast borne,
Freely and graciously forgiven,
With songs to Sion we return,
Contending for our native heaven;
That palace of our glorious King,
We find it nearer while we sing.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Saviour, on me the grace bestow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour, on me the grace bestow,
To trample on my mortal foe;
Conqueror of death with thee to rise,
And claim my station in the skies,
Fix'd as the throne which ne'er can move,
A pillar in thy church above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As beautiful as useful there,
May I that weight of glory bear,
With all who finally o'ercome,
Supporters of the heavenly dome;
Of perfect holiness possess'd,
For ever in thy presence bless'd.
S Write upon me the Name divine,
And let thy Father's nature shine,
His image visibly exprest,
His glory pouring from my breast,
O'er all my bright humanity,
Transform'd into the God I see!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Inscribing with the city's name,
The heavenly New Jerusalem,
To me the victor's title give,
Among thy glorious saints to live,
And all their happiness to know,
A citizen of heaven below.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When thou hadst all thy foes o'ercome,
Returning to thy glorious home,
Thou didst receive the full reward,
That I might share it with my Lord
And thus thy own new name obtain,
And one with thee for ever reign.

title: Away with our sorrow and fear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Away with our sorrow and fear,
We soon shall recover our home,
The city of saints shall appear;
The day of eternity come:
From ear tli we shall quickly remove,
And mount to our native abode;
The house of our Father above,
The palace of angels and God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our mourning is all at an end,
When, raised by the life-giving word,
We see the new city descend,
Adorn'd as a bride for her Lord:
The city so holy and clean,
No sorrow can breath in the air;
No gloom of affliction or sin,
No shadow of evil is there!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By faith we already behold
That lovely Jerusalem here
Her walls are of jasper and gold,
As crystal her buildings are clear:
Immoveably founded in grace,
She stands, as she ever hath stood,
And brightly her Builder displays,
And flames with the glory of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No need of the sun in that day,
Which never is follow'd by night,
Where Jesus's beauties display
A pure and a permanent light:
The Lamb is their Light and their Sur.
And, lo! by reflection they shine,
With Jesus ineffably one,
And bright in effulgence divine!

sections.label: Verse 5

title: We know, by faith we know
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We know, by faith we know,
If this vile house of clay,
This tabernacle, sink below,
In ruinous decay,
We have a house above,
Not made with mortal hands;
And firm as our Bedeemer's love,
That heavenly fabric stands.
It stands securely high,
Indissoluble sure;
Our glorious mansion in the sky
Shall evermore endure:
O were we enter'd there,
To perfect heaven restored!
O were we all caught up to share
The triumph of our Lord!
For this in faith we call,
For this we weep and pray
O might the tabernacle fall;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
might we 'scape away 1
Full of immortal hope,
We urge the restless strife,
And hasten to be swallow'd up
Of everlasting life.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Absent, alas! from God,
We in the body mourn,
And pine to quit this mean abode,
And languish to return.
Jesus, regard our vows,
And change our faith to sight;
And clothe us with our nobler house
Of empyrean light!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
let us put on thee
In perfect holiness,
And rise prepared thy face to see,
Thy bright, unclouded face!
Thy grace with glory crown,
Who hast the earnest given;
And now triumphantly come down,
And take our souls to heaven 1

title: Lift your eyes of faith, and see
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lift your eyes of faith, and see
Saints and angels join'd in one:
What a countless company
Stand before yon dazzling throne!
Each before his Saviour stands;
All in milk-white robes array'd,
Palms they carry in their hands,
Crowns of glory on their head.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Be it so, they all reply,
Him let all our orders praise;
Him that did for shiners die,
Saviour of the favour'd race!
