sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
And when we rise in love rencw'd.
Our souls resemble thee,
An image of the Triune God.,
To all eternity.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The incommunicable right,
Almighty God! receive,
Which angel-choirs, and saints in light,
' And saints embodied, give.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Three Persons, equally divine,
We magnify and love;
And both the choirs, ere long shall join,
To sing thy praise above.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Hail! holy, holy, holy Lord,
(Our heavenly song shall be,)
Supreme, essential One, adored
In co-eternal Three!

title: Holy, holy, holy Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy Lord,
God the Father, and the Word,
God the Comforter, receive
Blessings more than we can give:
Mix'd with those beyond the sky,
banters to the- Lord Most High,
S"e our hearts j*nd voices raise,
Lchoing thy Q+?"nal praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
One inexplicably Three,
One, in simple Unity,
God, incline tay gracious ear,
Us, thy lisping creatures, hear:
Thee while man, the earth-born, sings,
Angels shrink wijin their wings;
Prostrate Seraphh.* above
Breathe unutterable love.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Father, Son, and Holy Ghost
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Jehovah in three Persons, come,
And draw, and sprinkle us, and seal,
Poor, guilty, dying worms, in whom
Thou dost eternal life reveal;
The knowledge of thyself bestow,
And all thy glorious goodness show.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soon as our pardon'd heai believe
That thou art pure essential love,
The proof we in ourselves receive
Of the Three Witnesses; above;
Sure, as the saints arounc hy throne,
That Father, Word, and cirit, are One.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that we now, in lov renew'd,
Might blameless in tuy sight appear s
Wake we in thy similitude,
Stamp'd with the Triune character:
Flesh, spirit, soul, to thee resign;
And live and die entirely thine 1

title: A thousand oracles divine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A thousand oracles divine
Their common beams unite;
That sinners may with angels join
To worship God aright:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To praise a Trinity adored
By all the hosts above;
And one thrice-holy God and Lord
Through endless ages love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Triumphant host! they never cease
To laud and magnify
The Triune God of holiness,
Whose glory fills the sky:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Whose glory to this earth extends,
When God himself imparts,
And the whole Trinity descends
Into our faithful hearts.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
By faith the upper choir we meet,
And challenge them to sing
Jehovah on his shining seat,
Our Maker and our King.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
But God made flesh is wholly ours,
And asks our nobler strain;
The Father of celestial powers,
The Friend of earth-born man!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Ye seraphs, nearest to the throne,
With rapturous amaze
On us, poor ransom' d worms, look down,
For heaven's superior praise.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
The King, whose glorious face ye see,
For us his crown resign' d;
That fulness of the Deity,
He died for all mankind!

title: Father, how wide thy glory shines
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, how wide thy glory shines!
How high thy wonders rise!
Known through the earth by thousand signs,
By thousands through the skies.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Part of thy name divinely stands
On all thy creatures writ;
They show the labour of thy hands.
Or impress of thy feet.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But when we view thy strange design
To save rebellious worms,
Where vengeance and compassion join
In their divinest forms;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here the whole Deity is known,
Nor dares a creature guess
Which of the glories brightest shone,
The justice, or the grace.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Now the full glories of the Lamb
Adorn the heavenly plains;
Bright seraphs learn Immanuel's name,
And try their choicest strains.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O, may I bear some humble part
In that immortal song!
Wonder and joy shall tune my heart,
And love command my tongue 1

title: For this thou hast design'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For this thou hast design'd.
And form'd us man for this,
To know and love thyself, and find
In thee our endless bliss.

title: My we all improve
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My we all improve
The grace already given,
To seize the crown of perfect love.
And scale the mount of heaven )

title: Soldiers of Christ, arise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soldiers of Christ, arise,
lO And put your armour on,
Strong in the strength which God supplies
Through his eternal Son:
Strong in the Lord of Hosts,
And in his mighty power,
Who in the strength of Jesus trusts,
Is more than conqueror.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Stand then m his great might,
With all his strength endued:
But take, to arm you for the fight,
The Panoply of God:
254 fOR bkmeyers iighting.
That having all things done,
And all your conflicts pass'd,
Ye may o'ercome, through Christ alone,
And stand entire at las*.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Stand then against you: toes,
In close and firm array:
Legions of wily fiends oppose
Throughout the evil day:
But meet the sons of night,
But mock their vain design,
Arm'd in the arms of heavenly light,
Of righteousness divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Leave no unguarded place,
No weakness of the soul;
Take every virtue, every grace,
And fortify the whole:
Indissolubly join'd,
To battle all proceed;
But arm yourselves with all the mind
That was in Christ, your Head.

title: But, above all, lay hold
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
But, above all, lay hold
On faith's victorious shield;
Arm'd with that adamant and gold,
Be sure to win the field:
If faith surround your heart,
Satan shall be subdued;
Eepell'd his every fiery dart,
And quench'd with Jesu's blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus hath died for you!
What can his love withstand?
Believe, hold fast your shield, and who
Shall pluck you from his hand?
Believe that Jesus reigns;
All pover to him is given:
Believe, till freed from sin's remains;
Believe yourselves to heaven!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To keep your armour bright,
Attend with constant care,
Still walking in your Captain's sight,
And watching unto prayer,
Beady for all alarms,
Steadfastly set your face,
And always exercise your arms,
And use your every grace.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: In fellowship, alone
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In fellowship, alone,
To God with faith draw near:
Approach his courts, besiege his throne
With all the powers of prayer:
Go to his temple, go,
Nor from his altar move;
Let every house his worship know,
And every heart his love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To God your spirits dart;
Your souls in words declare;
Or groan, to him who reads the heart
The' unutterable prayer:
His mercy now implore,
And now show forth his praise
In shouts, or silent awe, adore
His miracles of grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Pour out your souls to God,
And bow them with your knees;
And spread your heart and hands abroad,
And pray for Sion's peace:
Your guides and brethren bear
For ever on your mind;
Extend the arms of mighty prayer,
In grasping all mankind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From strength to strength go on,
Wrestle, and fight, and pray:
Tread all the powers of darkness down,
And win the well-fought day:
Still let the Spirit cry
In all his soldiers, "Come; "
Till Christ the Lord descend from high,
And take the conquerors home.

title: Surrounded by a host of foes
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Surrounded by a host of foes,
O Storm' d by a host of foes within,
Nor swift to flee, nor strong to' oppose,
Single against hell, earth, and sin,
Single, yet undismay'd, I am;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
dare believe in Jesu's name.
2 "What though a thousand hosts engage,
A thousand worlds, my soul to shake?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
dare believe in Jesu's name.
3 Me to retrieve from Satan's hands.
Me from this evil world to free,
To purge my sins, and loose my bands,
And save from all iniquity,
My Lord and God from heaven he came

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text: dare believe in Jesu's name.

title: Equip me for the war
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O do not let me trust
In any arm but thine!
Humble, O humble to the dust,
This stubborn soul of mine!
A feeble thing of nought,
With lowly shame I own,
The help which upon earth is wrought
Thou dost it alone.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O may I love like thee!
In all thy footsteps tread!
Thou hatest all iniquity,
But nothing thou hast made.
O may I learn the art,
With meekness to reprove;
To hate the sin with all my heart,
But still the sinner love.

title: Almighty God of Love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Almighty God of Love,
Thy holy arm display;
Send me succour from above,
In this my evil day:
Arm my weakness with thy power,
Woman's seed, appear within;
Be my Safeguard and my Tower
Against the face of sin.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Could I of thy strength take hold,
And always feel thee near,
Confident, divinely bold,
My soul would scorn to fear:
Nothing should my firmness shock;
Though the gates of hell assail,
Were I built upon the Kock,
They never could prevail.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Rock of my salvation, haste,
Extend thy ample shade;
Let it over me be cast,
And screen my naked head:
Save me from the trying hour:
Thou my sure protection be;
Shelter me from Satan's power,
Till I am fixed on thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Set upon thyself my feet,
And make me surely stand;
From temptation's rage and heat
Cover me with thy hand:
Let me in the cleft be placed,
Never from my fence remove;
In thine arms of love embraced,
Of everlasting love.

title: Peace, doubting heart; my God's I am 1
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
To him mine eye of faith I turn,
And through the fire pursue my way:
The fire forgets its power to burn,
The lambent flames around me play;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
own his power, accept the sign,
And shout to prove the Saviour mine.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Since thou hast bid me come to thee,
(Good as thou art, and strong to save,)
I'll walk o'er life's tempestuous sea,
Upborne by the unyielding wave,
Dauntless, though rocks of pride be near$
And yawning whirlpools of despair.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
When darkness intercepts the skies,
And sorrow's waves around me roll,
When high the storms of passion rise,
And half o'erwhelm my sinking soul,
My soul a sudden calm shall feel,
And hear a whisper, "Peace, be still!"

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Though in affliction's furnace tried,
Unhurt on snares and death I'll tread;
Though sin assail, and hell, thrown wide,
Pour all its flames upon my head,
Like Moses' hush, I'll mount the higher,
And flourish, unconsumed, in fire.

title: /"omnipotent Lord, My Saviour and King
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
/"omnipotent Lord, My Saviour and King,
Thy succour afford, Thy righteousness
bring:
Thy promises bind thee Compassion to have;
Now, now let me find thee Almighty to save.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rejoicing in hope, And patient in grief,
To thee I look up For certain relief;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
fear no denial, No danger I fear,
Nor start from the trial, While Jesus is near.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
O who can explain This struggle for life!
This travail and pain, This trembling and strife!
Plague, earthquake, and famine, And tumult,
and war,
The wonderful coming Of Jesus declare.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
For every fight Is dreadful and loud!
The warrior's delight Is slaughter and blood,
His foes overturning, Till all shall expire,- -
But this is with burning, And fuel of fire.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Yet God is above Men, devils, and sin;
My Jesus' s love The battle shall win:
So terribly glorious His coming sball be,
His love all-victorious Shall conouer for mo.
"Hiy love the conquest more than gains;
To all I shall proclaim,
"Jesus, the King, the Conqueror reigns j -
Bow down to Jesu's Name."

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
To thee shall earth and hell submit,
And every foe shall fall,
Till death expires beneath thy feet,
And God is all in all.

title: Worship, and thanks, and blessing
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Worship, and thanks, and blessing,
And strength ascribe to Jesus!
Jesus alone Defends his own,
When earth and hell oppress us.
Jesus with joy we witness,
Almighty to deliver;
Our seals set to, That God is true,
And reigns a King for ever.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Omnipotent Redeemer,
Our ransom'd souls adore thee:
Our Saviour thou, We find it now,
And give thee all the glory.
We sing thine arm unshorten'd,
Brought through our sore temptation;
With heart and voice In thee rejoice,
The God of our salvation.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thine arm hath safely brought us
A way no more expected,
Than when thy sheep Pass'd through the deep,
By crystal walls protected.
Thy glory was our rear- ward,
Thine hand our lives did cover,
And we, even we, Have pass'd the sea,
And march'd triumphant over.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The world's and Satan's malice
Thou, Jesus, hast confounded;
And, by thy grace, With songs of praise
Our happy souls resounded.
Accepting our deliv'rance,
We triumph in thy favour,
And for the love Which now we prove,
Shall praise thy name for ever.

title: Jesus, the Conqueror, reigns
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, the Conqueror, reigns,
In glorious strength array'd,
His kingdom over all maintains,
And bids the earth be glad.
Ye sons of men, rejoice
In Jesu's mighty love;
Lift up your heart, lift up your voice,
To him who rules above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Extol his kingly power;
Kiss the exalted Son,
Who died, and lives, to die no more,
High on his Father's throne:
Our Advocate with God,
He undertakes our cause,
And spreads through all the earth abroad
The victory of his cross.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
That bloody banner see,
And in your Captain's sight,
Fight the good fight of faith with me,
My fellow-soldiers fight!
In mighty phalanx join'd,
To battle all proceed;
Arm'd with the' unconquerable mind
Which was in Christ your Head
•4 Urge on your rapid course,
Ye blood-besprinkled bands;
The heavenly kingdom suffers force;
'Tis seized by violent hands:
See there the starry crown
That glitters through the skies!
Satan, the world, and sin tread down,
And take the glorious prize!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Through much distress and pain,
Through many a conflict here,
Through blood, ye must the entrance gain;
Yet, O disdain to fear!
H Courage! "your Captain cries,
Who all your toil foreknew;
'■• Toil ye shall have; yet all despise,

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Who is this gigantic foe
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Who is this gigantic foe
That proudly stalks along,
Overlooks the crowd below,
In brazen armour strong?
Loudly of his strength he boasts,
On his sword and spear relies;
Meets the God of Israel's hosts,
And all their force defies.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tallest of the earth-born race,
They tremble at his power,
Flee before the monster's face,
And own him conqueror. —
Who this mighty champion is,
Nature answers from within;
He is my own wickedness,
My own besetting sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In the strength of Jesu's name,
I with the monster fight;
Feeble and unarm'd I am,
But Jesus is my might:
Mindful of his mercies past,
Still I trust the same to prove
Still my helpless soul I cast,
On his redeeming love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With, my sling and stone I go
To fight the Philistine;
God hath said it shall be so,
And I shall conquer sin:
On his promise I rely,
Trust in an Almighty Lord;
Sure to win the victory,
For he hath spoke the word.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In the strength of God I rise,
I run to meet my foe;
Faith the word of power applies,
And lays the giant low:
Faith in Jesu's conquering name
Slings the sin-destroying ston;?
Points the word's unerring aim,
And brings the monster down,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Rise, ye men of Israel, rise,
Your routed foe pursue;
Sbout His praises to the skies,
Who conquers sin for you:
Jesus doth for you appear,
He his conquering grace affords;
Saves you, not with sword and spear,
The battle is the Lord's.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
that all the earth might know
The power of Jesu's name!

title: Shall I, for fear of feeble man
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Shall I, for fear of feeble man,
O The Spirit's course in me restrain?—
Or, undismay'd in deed and word,
Be a true witness for my Lord!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Awed by a mortal's frown, shall I
Conceal the word of God most high?
How then before thee shall I dare,
To stand, or how thine anger bear?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Shall I, to soothe the' unholy throng,
Soften thy truths, and smooth my tongue,
To gain earth's gilded toys, or flee
The cross endured, my God, by thee!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What then is he whose scorn I dread,
Whose wrath or hate makes me afraid?
A man! an heir of death! a slave
To sin! a bubble on the wave!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yea, let men rage, since thou wilt spread
Thy shadowing wings around my head;
Since in all pain thy tender love
Will still my sure refreshment prove.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Saviour of men, thy searching eye
Doth all mine inmost thoughts descry!
Doth aught on earth my wishes raise,
Or the world's pleasures, or its praise?

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The love of Christ doth me constrain
To seek the wandering souls of men;
With cries, entreaties, tears, to save,
To snatch them from the gaping grave.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
For this let men revile my name,'
No cross I shim, I fear no shame:
All hail, reproach! and welcome, pain!
Only thy terrors, Lord, restrain.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
My life, my blood, I here present,
If for thy truth they may be spent;
Fulfil thy sovereign counsel, Lord!
Thy will be done, thy name adored!

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Give me thy strength, O God of power;
Then let winds blow, or thunders roar,
Thy faithful witness will I be:
'Tis fix'd; I can do all through thee!

title: The Lord is King, and earth submits
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord is King, and earth submits,
Howe'er impatient, to his sway;
Between the Cherubim he sits,
And makes his restless foes obey.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
In vain doth Satan rage his hour,
Beyond his chain he cannot go;
Our Jesus shall stir up his power,
And soon avenge us of our foe.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus shall his great arm reveal;
Jesus the woman's conquering Seed,
(Though now the Serpent bruise his heel,)
Jesus shall bruise the Serpent's head.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The enemy his tares hath sown,
But Christ shall shortly root them up,
Shall cast the dire Accuser down,
And disappoint his children's hope:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Shall still the proud Philistine's noise,
Baffle the sons of unbelief;
Nor long permit them to rejoice,
But turn their triumph into grief.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Come, glorious Lord, the rebels spurn
Scatter thy foes, victorious King:
And Gath and Askelon shall mourn,
And all the sons of God shall sing:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Shall magnify the sovereign grace
Of him that sits upon the throne;
And earth and heaven conspire to praise
Jehovah, and his conquering Son.

title: Are there not in the labourer's day
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Are there not in the labourer's day
Twelve hours, in which he safely may
His calling's work pursue?
Though sin and Satan still are near,
Nor sin nor Satan can I fear,
With Jesus in my view.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not all the powers of hell can frigh1
A soul that walks with Christ in liglrt:
He walks, and cannot fall;
Clearly be sees, and wins his way,
Shining unto the perfect day,
And tno/e than conquers all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Light of the world! thy beams I bless I
On thee, bright Sun of Righteousness,
My faith hath fix'd its eye;
Guided by thee, through all I go,
Nor fear the ruin spread below,
For thou art always nigh.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
urge my way to heaven.
5 Still will I strive, and labour still,
With humble zeal, to do thy will,
And trust in thy defence:
My soul into thy hands I give;
And, if he can obtain thy leave,
Let Satan pluck me thence!

title: And can it be, that I should prove
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And can it be, that I should prove
For ever faithful to thy love,
From sin for ever cease?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
I rest in thine Almighty power;
The name of Jesus is a tower,
That hides my life above:
Thou canst, thou wilt my Helper be j
My confidence is all in thee,
The faithful God of Love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
While still to thee for help I call,
Thou wilt not suffer me to fall,
Thou canst not let me sin;
And thou shalt give me power to pray,
Till all my sins are purged away,
And all thy mind brought in.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Wherefore, in never-ceasing prayer,
My soul to thy continual care

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
faithfully commend!
Assured that thou through life shalt save,
And show thyself beyond the grave
My everlasting Friend.

title: O God, my hope, my heavenly rest
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, my hope, my heavenly rest,
My all of happiness below,
Grant my importunate request,
To me, to me, thy goodness show:
Thy beatific face display,
The brightness of eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before my faith's enlighten'd eyes
Make all thy gracious goodness pass;
Thy goodness is the sight I pi'ize:
O may I see thy smiling face!
Thy nature in my soul proclaim,
Eeveal thy love, thy glorious name!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: To thee, great God of Love! I bow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
The fulness of my vast reward
A blest eternity shall be:
But hast thou not on earth prepared
Some better thing than this for me?
What, —but one drop! —one transient sight I

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
want a sun,—a sea of liflht.
8 Moses thy backward parts might view,
But not a perfect sight obtain;
The Gospel doth thy fulness show
To us, by the commandment slain:
The dead to sin shall find the grace;
The pure in heart shall see thy face.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
More favour'd than the saints of old, —
Who now by faith approach to thee,
Shall all with open face behold
In Christ the glorious Deity;
Shall see and put the Godhead on,
The nature of thy sinless Son!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
This, this is our high calling's prize!
Thine image in thy Son I claim;
And still to higher glories rise,
Till all transform'd I know thy name,
And glide to all my heaven above,
My highest heaven in Jesu's love.

title: Come, Saviour, Jesus, from above
author: Byrom 1

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Saviour, Jesus, from above!
Assist me with thy heavenly grace;
Empty my heart of earthly love,
And for thyself prepare the place.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O let thy sacred presence fill,
And set my longing spirit free,
Which pants to have no other will,
But day and night to feast on thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While in this region here below,
No other good will I pursue;
I'll bid this world of noise and show,
With all its glittering snares, adieu I

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
That path with humhle speed I'll seek,
In which my Saviour's footsteps shine
Nor will I hear, nor will I speak,
Of any other love but thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Henceforth may no profane delight
Divide this consecrated soul;
Possess it thou, who hast the right,
As Lord and Master of the whole.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Wealth, honour, pleasure, and what else
This short-enduring world can give,
Tempt as ye will, my soul repels.
To Christ alone resolved to live.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Thee I can love, and thee alone,
With pure delight and inward bliss:
To know thou tak'st me for thine own,

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
what a happiness is this!
8 Nothing on earth do I desire,
But thy pure love within my breast;
This, only this, will I require,
And freely give up all the rest.

title: Abraham, when severely tried
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Abraham, when severely tried,
jLjL His faith by his obedience show'd:
He with the harsh command complied,
And gave his Isaac back to God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His son the father offer'd up,
Son of his age, his only son,
Object of all his joy and hope,
And less beloved than God alone.
S O for a faith like his, that we
The bright example may pursue;
May gladly give up all to thee,
To whom our more than all is due!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Is there a thing than life more dear?
A thing from which we cannot part?
We can: we now rejoice to tear
The idol from our bleeding heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, accept our sacrifice;
All things for thee we count but loss:
Lo! at thy word our Isaac dies,
Dies on the altar of thy cross.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
For what to thee, O Lord, we give,
A hundred-fold we here obtain;
And soon with thee shall all receive,
And loss shall be eternal gain.

title: Omnipresent God! whose aid
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Omnipresent God! whose aid
No one ever ask'd in vain,
Be this night, about my bed,
Every evil thought restrain:
Lay thy hand upon my soul,
God of my unguarded hours!
All my enemies control,
Hell, and earth, and nature's powers

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Only tell me I am thine,
And thou wilt not quit thy right;
Answer me in dreams divine,
Dreams and visions of the night:
Bid me even in sleep go on,
Restlessly my God desire;
Mourn for God in every groan,
God in every thought require.
Loose me from the chains of sense,
Set me from the body free;
Draw with stronger influence
My unfetter'd soul to thee:
In me, Lord, thyself reveal;
Fill me with a sweet surprise:
Let me thee, when waking, feel,
Let me in thy image rise.

title: O God, thy faithfulness I plead
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, thy faithfulness I plead!
My present help in time of need,
My great Deliverer thou!
Haste to my aid, thine ear incline,
And rescue this poor soul of mine!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
claim the promise now!
2 Where is the way? Ah, show me where,
That I thy mercy may declare,
The power that sets me free:
How can I my destruction shun?
How can I from my nature run?
Answer, O God, for me!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One only way the erring mind
Of man, short-sighted man, can find,
From inbred sin to fly:
Stronger than love, I fondly thought,
Death, only death, can cut the knot,
Which love cannot untie.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But thou, O Lord, art full of grace j
Thy love can find a thousand ways
To foolish man unknown:
My soul upon thy love I cast;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
rest me, till the storm is past,
Upon thy love alone.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Thy faithful, wise, and mighty love
Shall every stumbling-block remove,
And make an open way:
Thy love shall burst the shades of death,
And bear me from the gulf beneath,
To everlasting day.

title: In all my ways thy hand I own
author: Weslet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In all my ways thy hand I own,
Thy ruling Providence I see:
Assist me still my course to run,
And still direct my paths to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oft hath the sea confess'd thy power,
And given me back at thy command j
It could not, Lord, my life devour,
Safe in the hollow of thine hand.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oft from the margin of the grave
Thou, Lord, hast lifted up my head;
Sudden, I found thee near to save;
The fever own'd thy touch, and fled.
• 5 Whither, O whither should I fly,
But to rny loving Saviour's breast?
Secure within thine arms to lie,
And safe beneath thy wings to rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I have no skill the snare to shun,
But thou, O Christ, my Wisdom ar!;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
ever into ruin run,
But thou art greater than my heart.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Foolish, and impotent, and blind,
Lead me a way I have not known;
Bring me, where I my heaven may find,
The heaven of loving thee alone.

sections.label: Verse 7

title: Break not then a bruised reed
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Break not then a bruised reed,
Nor quench the smoking flax in me.
Buried in sin, thy voice I hear,
And burst the barriers of my tomb,
In all the marks of death appear, —
Forth at thy call, though bound, I come.
Give me, O give me, fully, Lord,
Thy resurrection's power to know;
Free me indeed, repeat the word,
And loose my bands, and let me go.
Fain would I go to thee, my God,
Thy mercies and my wants to tell;
To feel my pardon seal'd in blood,
Saviour, thy love I wait to feel.
Freed from the power of cancell'd sin,
When shall my soul triumphant prove?
Why breaks not out the fire within
In flames of joy, and praise, and love?
Jesus, to thee my soul aspires;
' Jesus, to thee I plight my vows;
Keep me from earthly, base desires,
My God, my Saviour, and my Spouse!
Fountain of all-sufficient bliss,
Thou art the good I seek below;
Fulness of joy in thee there is,
Without, —'tis misery all, and woe.

title: Fondly my foolish heart essays
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fondly my foolish heart essays
To' augment the source of perfect bliss,
Love's all-sufficient sea to raise
With drops of creature-happiness.
O Love, thy sovereign aid impart,
And guard the gift thyself hast given:
My portion Thou, my treasure, art,
And life, and happiness, and heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Would ought on earth my wishes share,
Though dear as life the idol be,
The idol from my breast I'd tear,
Resolved to seek my all in thee.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: To the haven of thy breast
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To the haven of thy breast,
O Son of Man, I fly!
Be my refuge and my rest,
For O the storm is high!
Save me from the furious blast;
A covert from the tempest be!
Hide me, Jesus, till o'erpast
The storm of sin I see.
Welcome as the water-spring
To a diy, barren place,
O descend on me, and bring
Thy sweet refreshing graoc;
O'er a parched and weary land
As a great rock extends its shade,
Hide me, Saviour, with thine hand,
And screen my naked head.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In the time of my distress
Thou hast my succour been,
In my utter helplessness
Restraining me from sin:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
how swiftly didst thou move
To save me in the trying hour!
Still protect me with thy love,
And shield me with thy power.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
First and last in me perform
The work thou hast begun;
Be my shelter from the storm,
My shadow from the sun:
Weary, parch'd with thirst, and faint,
Till thou the' abiding Spirit breathe,
Every moment, Lord, I want
The merit of thy death.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Never shall I want it less,
When thou the gift hast given,
Fill'd me with thy righteousness.
And seal'd the heir of heaven:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
shall hang upon my God
Till I thy perfect glory see;
Till the sprinkling of thy blood
Shall speak me up to thee.

title: Jesus, my King, to thee I bow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, my King, to thee I bow,
Enlisted under thy command;
Captain of my salvation, thou
Shalt lead me to the promised land.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou hast a great deliverance wrought,
The staff from off my shoulder broke;
Out of the house of bondage brought,
And freed me from the' Egyptian yoke.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O'er the vast howling wilderness,
To Canaan's bounds thou hast me led;
Thou bidd'st me now the land possess,
And on thy milk and honey feed.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I see an open door of hope;
Legions of sin in vain oppose:
Bold I with thee, my Head, march up,
And triumph o'er a world of foes.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Gigantic lusts come forth to fight
I mark, disdain, and all break through;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
tread them down in Jesu's might,
Through Jesus I can all things do.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Lo! the tall sons of Anak rise!
Who can the sons of Anak meet?
Captain, to thee I lift mine eyes,
And, lo! they fall beneath my feet.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Passion, and appetite, and pride,
(Pride, my old, dreadful, tyrant-foe,)

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
see cast down on every side,
And, conquering, I to conquer go.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
My Lord in my behalf appears;
Captain, thy strength-inspiring eye
Scatters my doubts, dispels my fears,
And makes the hosts of aliens fly.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Who can before my Captain stand?
Who is so great a King as mine?
High over all is thy right hand,
And might and majesty e thins.

title: Jesus, thou sovereign Lord of all
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thou sovereign Lord of all,
The same through one eternal da j,
Attend thy feeblest followers' call,
And O instruct us how to pray!
Pour out the supplicating grace,
And stir us up to seek thy face!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We cannot think a gracious thought,
We cannot feel a good desire,
Till thou, who call'dst a world from nought,
The power into our hearts inspire;
And then we in thy Spirit groan,
And then we give thee back thine own.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, regard the joint complaint
Of all thy tempted followers here!
And now supply the common want,
And send us down the Comforter:
The spirit of ceaseless prayer impart,
And fix thy Agent in our heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To help our soul's infirmity,
To heal thy sin-sick people's care,
To urge our God-commanding plea,
And make our hearts a house of prayer,
The promised Intercessor give,
And let us now thyself receive.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Come in thy pleading Spirit down
To us who for thy coming stay;
Of all thy gifts we ask but one,
We ask the constant power to pray:
Indulge us, Lord, in this request,
Thou can'st not then deny the rest.

title: Come, ye followers of the Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, ye followers of the Lord,
In Jesu's service join:
Jesus gives the sacred word,
The ordinance divine:
Let us his command obey,
And ask and have whate'er we want;
Pray we, every moment, pray,
And never, never faint.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Place no longer let us give
To the old Tempter's will;
Never more our duty leave,
While Satan cries, "Be still: "
Stand we in the ancient way,
And here with God ourselves acquaint;
Pray we, every moment pray,
And never, never faint.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Be it weariness and pain
To slothful flesh and blood,
Yet we will the cross sustain,
And bless the welcome load;
All our griefs to God display,
And humbly pour out our complaint
Pray we, every moment pray,
And never, never faint.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let us patiently endure,
And still our wants declare;
All the promises are sure
To persevering prayer:
Till we see the perfect day,
And each wakes up a sinless saint,
Pray we, every moment pray,
And never, never faint.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Pray we on when all renew'd,
And perfected in love;
Till we see the Saviour God
Descending from above,
All his heavenly charms survey,
Beyond what angel minds can paint,
Pray we, every moment pray,
And never, never faint.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
rtlHE praying Spirit breathe,
JL The watching power impart;
From all entanglements beneath
Call off my anxious heart:
My feeble mind sustain,
By worldly thoughts opprest;
Appear, and bid me turn again
To my eternal rest.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Swift to my rescue come,
Thy own this moment seize;
Gather my wand'ring spirit home,
And keep in perfect peace:
Suffer'd no more to rove
O'er all the earth abroad,
Arrest the prisoner of thy love,
And shut me up in God.
i

title: Shepherd Divine, our wants relieve
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Shepherd Divine, our wants relieve,
O In this our evil day:
To all thy tempted followers give
The power to watch and pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Long as our fiery trials last,
Long as the cross we bear,
O let our souls on thee be cast
In never-ceasing prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Spirit of interceding grace
Give us in faith to claim;
To wrestle till we see thy face,
And know thy hidden name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Till thou thy perfect love impart,
Till thou thyself bestow,
Be this the cry of every heart,
"I will not let thee go.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
"I will not let thee go, unless
Thou tell thy name to me;
With all thy great salvation bless,
And make me all like thee.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
"Then let me on the mountain-top
Behold thy open face;
Where faith in sight is swallow'd up,
And prayer in endless praise."

title: O wondrous power of faithful prayer
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O wondrous power of faithful prayer!
What tongue can tell the' almighty grace?
God's hands or bound or open are,
As Hoses or Elijah prays:
Let Moses in the spirit groan,
And God cries out, "Let me alone!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Let me alone, that all my wrath
May rise the wicked to consume!
While justice hears thy praying faith,
It cannot seal the sinner's doom:
My Son is in my servant's prayer,
And Jesus forces me to spare."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O blessed word of gospel grace!
Which now we for our Israel plead:
A faithless and backsliding race,
Whom thou hast out of Egypt freed:
O do not then in wrath chastise,
Nor let thy whole displeasure rise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Father, we ask in Jesu's name;
In Jesu's power and spirit pray!
Divert thy vengeful thunder's aim!
O turn thy threat'ning wrath away!
Our guilt and punishment remove,
And magnify thy pardoning love.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Jesus, thou hast bid us pray
author: Lesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thou hast bid us pray,
Pray always, and not faint;
With the word a power convey
To utter our complaint:
Quiet shalt thou never know,
Till we from sin are fully freed;
O avenge us of our foe,
And bruise the Serpent's head 1

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We have now begun to cry,
And we will never end,
Till we find salvation nigh,
And grasp the Sinner's Friend;
Day and night we'll speak our woe
With thee importunately plead:
O avenge us of our foe,
And bruise the Seipent's head!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Speak the word, and we shall be
From all our bands released;
Only thou canst set us free,
By Satan long oppress' d:
Now thy power almighty show;
Arise, the Woman's conquering Seed!
O avenge us of our foe,
And braise the Serpent's head!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
avenge us of oxxy foe
And bruise the Serpent's head!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Stronger than the strong man, thou
His fury canst control:
Cast him out, by entering now,
And keep our ransom' d soul;
Satan's kingdom overthrow,
On all the powers of darkness tread,

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
avenge us of our foe,
And bruise the Serpent's head I

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
To the never-ceasing cries
Of thine elect attend;
Send deliverance from the skies,
The mighty Spirit send:
Though to man thou seemest slow,
Our cries thou seemest not to heed;
O avenge us of our foe,
And bruise the Serpent's head!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Come, O come, all-glorious Lord!
No longer now delay;
With thy Spirit's two-edged sword
The crooked Serpent slay!
Bare thine arm, and give the blow,
Root out and kill the hellish seed;
O avenge us of our foe,
And bruise the Serpent's head 1

sections.label: Verse 10

title: Jesus, I fain would find
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, I fain would find
Thy yearning pity for mankind,
Thy burning charity.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In me thy Spirit dwell!
In me thy bowels move!
So shall the fervour of my zeal
Be the pure flame of love.

title: Jesus, my strength, my hope
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, my strength, my hope,
On thee I cast my care,
With humble confidence look up,
And know thou hear'st my prayer.
Give me on thee to wait,
Till I can all things do;
On thee, almighty to create,
Almighty to renew.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I want a sober mind;
A self-renouncing will,
That tramples down and casts behind
The baits of pleasing ill;
A soul inured to pain,
To hardship, grief, and loss,
Bold to take up, firm to sustain.
The consecrated cross.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I want a godly fear
A quick-discerning eye,
That looks to thee when sin is near,
And sees the Tempter fly;
A spirit still prepared,
And arm'd with jealous care,
For ever standing on its guard,
And watching unto prayer.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I want a heart to pray,
To pray and never cease,
Never to murmur at thy stay
Or wish my sufferings less.
This blessing, above all,
Always to pray, I want,
Out of the deep on thee to call,
And never, never faint.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I want a true regard,
A single steady aim,
(Unmoved by threat'ning or reward,)
To thee and thy great name!
A jealous, just concern
For thine immortal praise;
A pure desire that all may learn,
And glorify, thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
I rest upon thy word;
The promise is for me;
My succour and salvation, Lord,
Shall surely come from thee:
But let me still abide,
Nor from my hope remove,
Till thou my patient spirit guide
Into thy perfect love.

title: Lord, that I may learn of thee
author: O    Islet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, that I may learn of thee,
Give me true simplicity;
Wean my soul, and keep it low,
Willing thee alone to know.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let me cast my reeds aside,
All that feeds my knowing pride;
Not to man, but God submit,
Lay my reasonings at thy feet:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Of my boasted wisdom spoil'd,
Docile, helpless as a child;
Only seeing in thy light,
Only walking in thy might

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then infuse the teaching grace,
Spirit of truth and righteousness;
Knowledge, love divine, impart,
Life eternal, to my heart.

title: Ah, when shall I awake
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ah, when shall I awake
.XJl. From sin's soft-soothing power;
The slumber from my spirit shake,
And rise to fall no more!
Awake, no more to sleep,
But stand with constant care,
Looking for God my soul to keep,
And watching unto prayer!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O could I always pray,
And never, never faint,
But simply to my God display
My every care and want!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
know that thou wouldst give
More than I can request;
Thou still art ready to receive
My soul to perfect rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I feel thee willing, Lord,
A sinful world to save:
All may obey thy gracious word,
May peace and pardon have.
Not one of all the race
But may return to thee, —
But at the throne of sovereign grace
May fall and weep, like me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here will I ever lie,
And tell thee all my care,
And Father, Abba, Father, cry,
And pour a ceaseless prayer;
Till thou my sins subdue,
Till thou my sins destroy,
My spirit after God renew,
And fill with peace and joy.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Messiah, Princ of Peace,
Into my soul bring in
The everlasting righteousness,
And make an end of sin.
Into all those that seek
Redemption through thy blood,
The sanctifying Spirit speak,
The plenitude of God.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Let us in patience wait
Till faith shall make us whole;
Till thou shalt all things new create
In each believing soul.
Wbo can resist thy will?
Speak, and it shall be done!
Thou shalt the work of faith fufil,
And perfect us in one.
s-

title: Meeken my soul, thou heavenly Lamb
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Meeken my soul, thou heavenly Lamb,
That I in the new earth may claim
My hundred-fold reward;
My rich inheritance possess,
Co-heir with the great Prince of Peace
Co partner with my Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Me with that restless thirst inspire,
That sacred, infinite desire;
And feast my hungry heart:
Less than thyself cannot suffice:
My soul for all thy fulness cries,
For all thou hast and art.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, the crowning grace impart j
Bless me with purity of heart,
That, now beholding thee,

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
soon may view thy open face,
On all thy glorious beauties gaze,
And God for ever see i

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Not for my fault or folly's sake,
The name, or mode, or form, I take, —
But for true holiness,
Let me be wrong'd, reviled, abhorr'd;
And thee, my sanctifying Lord,
In life and death confess.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Call'd to sustain the hallow' d cross,
And suffer for thy righteous cause,
Pronounce me doubly blest;
And let thy glorious Spirit, Lord,
Assure me of my great leward,
In heaven's eternal feast.

title: Gracious Redeemer, shake
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Gracious Redeemer, shake
This slumber from my soul!
Say to me now, "Awake, awake I
And Christ shall make thee whole "
Lay to thy mighty hand;
Alarm me in this hour;
And make me fully understand
The thunder of thy power 1

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give me on thee to call,
Always to watch and pray,
Lest I into temptation fall,
And cast my shield away.
For each assault prepared
And ready may I be;
For ever standing on my guard,
And looking up to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O do thou always warn
My soul of evil near!
When to the right or J eft I turn,
Thy voice still let me hear:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come back! this is the way;
Come back, and walk herein 1 "
O may I hearken and obey,
And shun the paths of sin J

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou seest my feebleness;
Jesus, be thou my power,
My help and refuge in distress,
My fortress and my tower.
Give me to trust in thee!
Be thou my sure abode;
My hom, and rock, and buckler be,
My Saviour, and my God.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Myself I cannot save,
Myself I cannot keep;
But strength in thee I surely have,
Whose eyelids never sleep:
My soul to thee alone
Now therefore I commend;
Thou, Jesus, love me as thy own,
And love me to the end.

title: Father, to thee I lift mine eyes
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, to thee I lift mine eyes,
My longing eyes, and restless heart:
Before the morning watch I rise,
And wait to taste how good thou art,
To' obtain the grace I humbly claim,
The saving power of Jesu's name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This slumber from my soul, O shake!
Warn by thy Spirit's inward call;
Let me to righteousness awake,
And pray that I no more may fall,
Or give to sin or Satan place,
But walk in all thy righteous ways.
c

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O would'st thou, Lord, thy servant guard,
'Gainst every known or secret foe;
A mind for all assaults prepared,
A sober, vigilant mind bestow,
Ever apprised of danger nigh,
And when to fight, and when to fly

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Attended by the sacred dread,
And wise from evil to depart,
Let me from strength to strength proceed,
And rise to purity of heart;
Through all the paths of duty move,
From humble faith to perfect love.

title: God of all grace and majesty
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of all grace and majesty,
Supremely great and good!
If I have mercy found with thee,
Through the atoning blood;
The guard of all thy mercies give.
And to my pardon join
A fear lest I should ever grieve
The gracious Spirit Divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If mercy is indeed with thee,
lay I obedient prove;
Nor e'er abuse my liberty,
Or sin against thy love:
This choicest fruit of faith bestow
On a poor sojourner;
And let me pass my days below
In humbleness and fear.
Rather I would in darkness mourn
The absence of thy peace,
Than e'er by light irreverence turn
Thy grace to wantonness:
•Rather I would, in painful awe,
Beneath thine anger move,
Than sin against the gospel law
Of liberty and love.
But, O! thou would' st not have me live
In bondage, grief, or pain;
Thou dost not take delight to grieve
The helpless sons of men:
Thy will is my salvation, Lord;
And let it now take place!
And let me tremble at the word
Of reconciling grace.
Still may I walk as in thy sight,
My strict Observer see;
And thou by reverent love unite
My child-like heart to thee:
Still 'let me, till my days are past,
At Jesu's feet abide;
So shall he lift me up at last,
And seat me by his side.

title: I want a principle within
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I want a principle within
Of jealous, godly fear;
A sensibility of sin,
A pain to feel it near.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
want the first approach to feel
Of pride, or fond desire;
To catch the wand'ring of my will,
And quench the kindling fire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
That I from thee no more may part.
No more thy goodness grieve,
The filial awe, the fleshly heart,
The tender conscience, give.
Quick as the apple of an eye,
O God, my conscience make!
Awake my soul, when sin is nigh,
And keep it still awake.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If to the right or left I stray,
That moment, Lord, reprove;
And let me weep my life awy,
For having grieved thy love
O may the least omission pain
My well-instructed soul;
And drive me to the blood again,
Which makes the wounded whole I

title: Help, Lord, to whom for help I fly
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Help, Lord, to whom for help I fly,
And still my tempted soul stand by,
Throughout the evil day:
The sacred watchfulness impart,
And keep the issues of my heart,
And stir me up to pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Whene'er my careless hands hang down,
O let me see thy gathering frown,
And feel thy warning eye;
And starting, cry, from ruin's brink,
Save, Jesus, or I yield, I sink,
O save me, or I die!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If near the pit I rashly stray,
Before I wholly fall away,
The keen conviction dart!
Kecall me by that pitying look,
That kind, upbraiding glance, which broke
Unfaithful Peter's heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In me thine utmost mercy show,
And make me like thyself below,
Unblamable in grace;
Ready prepared, and fitted here,
By perfect holiness, to' appear
Before thy glorious face.

title: Into a world of ruffians sent
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Into a world of ruffians sent,
JL I walk on hostile ground;
While human bears on slaughter bent,
And ravening wolves, surround.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The lion seeks my soul to slay,
In some unguarded hour;
And waits to tear his sleeping prey,
And watches to devour.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But worse than all my foes I find
The enemy within,
The evil heart, the carnal mind,
Mine own insidious sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My nature every moment waits
To render me secure,
And all my paths with ease besets,
To make my ruin sure.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But thou hast given a loud alarm;
And thou shalt still prepare
My soul for all assaults, and arm
With never-ceasing prayer.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O do not suffer me to sleep,
Who on thy love depend;
But still thy faithful servant keep,
And save me to the end!

title: Bid me of men beware
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bid me of men beware,
I) And to my ways take heed;
Discern their every secret snare,
And circumspectly tread.
O may I calmly wait
Thy succours from above;
And stand against their open hate,
And well-dissembled love!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My spirit, Lord, alarm,
When men and devils join;
'Gainst all the powers of Satan arm.
In panoply divine:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
may I set my face
His onsets to repel;
Quench all his fiery darts, and chase
The fiend to his own hell!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But, above all, afraid
Of my own bosom foe,
Still let me seek to thee for aid,
To thee my weakness show;
Hang on thy arm alone,
With self-distrusting care,
And deeply in the Spirit groan
The never-ceasing prayer.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Give me a sober mind,
A quick- discerning eye,
The first approach of sin to find,
And all occasions fly.
Still may I cleave to thee,
And never more depart,
But watch with godly jealousy
Over my evil heart.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Thus may I pass my days
Of sojourning beneath,
And languish to conclude my race,
And render up my breath;
In humble love and fear,
Thine image to regain,
And see thee in the clouds appear,
And rise with thee to reign J

title: Jesu, my Saviour, Brother, Friend
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, my Saviour, Brother, Friend,
On whom I cast my every care,
On whom for all things I depend;
Inspire, and then accept, my prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Still let hhn with my weakness stay,
Nor for a moment's space depart;
Evil and danger turn away,
And keep till he renews my heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When to the right or left I stray,
His voice behind me may I hear:
"Return, and walk in Christ thy way;
Fly back to Christ; for sin is near."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His sacred miction from above
Be still my comforter and guide;
Till all the stony he remove,
And in my loving heart reside.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Jesus, I fain would -walk in thee,
From nature's every path retreat;
Thou art my Way, my Leader be,
And set upon the rock my feet.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Uphold me, Saviour, or I fall;
O reach me out thy gracious hand!
Only on thee for help I call:
Only by faith in thee I stand.

title: Pierce, fill me with an humble fear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Pierce, fill me with an humble fear:
My utter helplessness reveal!
Satan and sin are always near;
Thee may I always nearer feel.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O that to thee my constant mind
Might with an even flame aspire,
Pride in its earliest motions find,
And mark the risings of desire!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O that my tender soul might fly
The first abhorr'd approach of ill;
Quick, as the apple of an eye,
The slightest touch of sin to feel!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Till thou anew my soul create,
Still may I strive, and watch, and pray,
Humbly and confidently wait,
And long to see the perfect day

title: Me, on the mountain-top
author: 0 We8let

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Me, on the mountain-top,
The standard of your God!
In Jesu's name I lift it up,
All stain'd with hallow'd blood.
His standard-bearer, I
To all the nations call:
Let all to Jesu's cross draw nigh!
He bore the cross for all.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Only have faith in God;
In faith your foes assail;
Not wrestling against flesh and blood,
But all the powers of hell:
From thrones of glory driven,
By flaming vengeance hurl'd,
They throng the air, and darken heaven,
And rule the lower world.

title: Angels your march oppose
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Angels your march oppose,
XJL Who still in strength excel,
Your secret, sworn, eternal foes,
Countless, invisible:
With rage that never ends,
Their hellish arts they try,
Legions of dire, malicious fiends,
And spirits enthroned on high.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On earth the' usurpers reign,
Exert their baneful power;
O'er the poor fallen sons of men
They tyrannize their hour:
But shall believers fear?
But shall believers fly?
Or see the bloody cross appear,
And all their powers defy!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesu's tremendous name
Puts all our foes to flight:
Jesus, the meek, the angry Lamb,
A Lion is in fight.
By all hell's host withstood,
We all hell's hosts o'erthrow;
And conquering them, through Jesu's blood,
We still to conquer go.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Eternal Power, whose high abode
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eternal Power, whose high abode
ttl Becomes the grandeur of a God,
Infinite lengths heyond the hounds
Where stars revolve their little rounds!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thee, while the first archangel sings,
He hides his face behind his wings;
And ranks of shining thrones around
Fall worshipping, and spread the ground.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, what shall earth and ashes do?
We would adore our Maker too!
From sin and dust to thee we cry,
The Great, the Holy, and the High.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Earth from afar hath heard thy fame,
And worms have learn'd to lisp thy name;
But, O! the glories of thy mind
Leave all our soaring thoughts behind!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
God is in heaven, and men below:
Be short our tunes, our words be few!
A solemn reverence checks our songs,
And praise sits silent on our tongues.

title: Ah Lord! with trembling I confess
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ah Lord! with trembling I confess,
J. A gracious soul may fall from grace;
The salt may lose its seasoning power,
And never, never find it more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lest this my fearful case should be,
Each moment knit my soul to thee;
And lead me to the mount above,
Through the low vale of humble love.

title: A charge to keep I have
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
may it all my powers engage
To do my Master's will!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Arm me with jealous care,
As in thy sight to live;
And O! thy servant, Lord, prepare
A strict account to give:
Help me to watch and pray,
And on thyself rely;
Assured if I my trust betray,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: shall for ever die.

title: Watch'd by the world's malignant eye
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Watch'd by the world's malignant eye,
Who load us with reproach and shame
As servants of the Lord Most High,
As zealous for his glorious name,
We ought in all his paths to move,
With holy fear and humble love

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That wisdom, Lord, on us bestow,
From every evil to depart;
To stop the mouth of every foe,
While, upright both in life and heart,
The proofs of godly fear we give,
And show them how the Christians live.

title: Be it my only wisdom here
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Be it my only wisdom here,
To serve the Lord with filial fear,
With loving gratitude;
Superior sense may I display,
By shunning every evil way,
And walking in the good.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O may I still from sin depart!
A wise and understanding heart,
Jesus, to me be given;
And let me through thy Spirit know,
To glorify my God below,
And find my way to heaven.

title: Summon'd my labour to renew
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Summon'd my labour to renew,
And glad to act my part,
Lord, in thy name my work I do,
And with a single heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
do it unto thee.
3 Whate'er the Father views as thine,
He views with gracious eyes;
Jesus, this mean oblation join
To thy great Sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Stamp'd with an infinite desert,
My work he then shall own;
Well pleased with me, when mine thou art,
And I his favour' d son.

title: Thy bright example I pursue
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy bright example I pursue,
To thee in all things rise;
And all I think, or speak, or do,
Is one great sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Careless through outward cares I go,
From all distraction free;
My hands are but engaged below,
My heart is still with thee.

title: God of Almighty love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of Almighty love,
vJT By whose sufficient grace

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
lift my heart to things above,
And numbly seek thy face:
Through Jesus Christ the Just,
My faint desires receive;
And let me in thy goodness trust,
And to thy glory live.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Whate'er I say or do,
Thy glory be my aim;
My offerings all be offer'd through
The ever- blessed Name!
Jesus, my single eye
Be fix'd on thee alone:
Thy name be praised on earth, on high j
Thy will by all be done 1

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Spirit of faith inspire,
My consecrated heart:
Fill me with pure, celestial fire,
With all thou hast, and art:
My feeble mind transform,
And, perfectly renew'd,
Into a saint exalt a worm,
A worm exalt to God!

title: Forth in thy name, O Lord, I go
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Forth in thy name, O Lord, I go,
My daily labour to pursue;
Thee, only thee, resolved to know,
In all I think, or speak, or do.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The task thy wisdom hath assigned,
O let me cheerfully fulfil!
In all my works thy presence find,
And prove thy acceptable will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thee may I set at my right hand,
Whose eyes my inmost substance see;
And labour on at thy command,
And offer all my works to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give me to bear thy easy yoke,
And every moment watch and pray;
And still to things eternal look,
And hasten to thy glorious day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
For thee delightfully employ
Whate'er thy bounteous grace hath given j
And run my course with even joy,
And closely walk with thee to heaven.

title: Lo! I come with joy to do
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo! I come with joy to do
The Master's blessed will;
Him in outward works pursue,
And serve his pleasure still.
Faithful to my Lord's commands,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
still would choose the better part
Serve with careful Martha's hands,
And loving Mary's heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Careful without care I am,
Nor feel my happy toil,
Kept in peace by Jesu's name,
Supported by his smile:
Joyful thus my faith to show,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
find his service my reward;
Every work I do below,

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
do it to the Lord.
3 Thou, O Lord, in tender love,
. Dost all my burdens bear!
Lift my heart to things above,
And fix it ever there!
Calm on tumult's wheel I sit,
'Midst busy multitudes alone,
Sweetly waiting at thy feet,
Till all thy will be done

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Thou, O Lord, my portion art,
Before I hence remove!
Now my treasure and my heart
Are all laid up above:
Far above all earthly things,
While yet my hands are here employ'd,
Sees my soul the King of kings,
And freely talks with God.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O that all the art might know
Of living thus to thee!
Find their heaven begun below,
And here thy glory see!
Walk in all the works prepared
By thee to exercise their grace,
Till they gain their full reward,
And see thy glorious face!

title: /captain of Israel's host, and G-uide
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
/captain of Israel's host, and G-uide
Of all who seek the land above,
Beneath thy shadow we abide,
The cloud of thy protecting love:
Our strength, thy grace; our rule, thy word;
Our end, the glory of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: O thou that camest from above
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou that camest from above,
The pure celestial fire to' impart,
Kindle a flame of sacred love,
On the mean altar of my heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There let it for thy glory bum,
With inextinguishable blaze;
4nd trembling to its source return,
In humble prayer and fervent praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, confirm my hearts desire
To work, and speak, and think for thee;
Still let me guard the holy fire,
And still stir up thy gift in me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ready for all thy perfect will,
My acts of faith and love repeat,
Till death thy endless mercies seal,
And make the sacrifice complete.

title: When quiet in my house I sit
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When quiet in my house I sit,
Thy book be my companion still;
My joy thy sayings to repeat,
Talk o'er the records of thy will,
And search the oracles divine,
Till every heart-felt word be mine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O may the gracious words divine
Subject of all my converse be:
So will the Lord his follower join,
And walk and talk himself with me;
So shall my heart his presence prove,
And burn with everlasting love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oft as I lay me down to rest,
O may the reconciling word
Sweetly compose my weary breast!
While, on the bosom of my Lord,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
sink in blissful dreams away,
And visions of eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: O Jesus, full of truth and grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus, full of truth and grace,
Thee, Saviour, we adore;
Thee in affliction's furnace praise,
And magnify thy power.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy power, in human weakness shown,
Shall make us all entire;
We now thy guardian presence own,
And walk unburn' d in fire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thee, Son of Man, by faith we see,
And glory in our guide;
Surrounded and upheld by thee.
The fiery test abide.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The fire our graces shall refine,
Till moulded from above,
We bear the character divine,
The stamp of perfect love.

title: Saviour of all, what hast thou done
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour of all, what hast thou done,
O What hast thou suffer'd on the tree i
Why didst thou groan thy mortal groan,
Obedient unto death for me?
The mystery of thy passion show,
The end of all thy griefs below.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy soul, for sin an offering made,
Hath clear'd this guilty soul of mine
Thou hast for me a ransom paid,
To change my human to divine,
To cleanse from all iniquity,
And make the sinner all like thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Pardon, and grace, and heaven to buy,
My bleeding Sacrifice expired;
But didst thou not my Pattern die,
That by thy glorious Spirit fired,
Faithful to death I might endure,
And make the crown by suffering sui e?

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy every suffering servant, Lord,
Shall as his perfect Master be;
To all thy inward life restored,
And outwardly conform'd to thee,
Out of thy grave the saint shall rise,
And grasp, through death, the glorious prize.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
This is the strait and royal way,
That leads us to the courts above;
Here let me ever, ever stay,
Till, on the wings of perfect love,

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
take my last triumphant flight,
From Calvary's to Sion's height.

title: Thou, Lord, hast blest my going out
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou, Lord, hast blest my going out;
O bless my coming in!
Compass my weakness round about,
And keep me safe from sin.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Still hide me in thy secret place,
Thy Tabernacle spread;
Shelter me with preserving grace,
And screen my naked head.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To thee for refuge may I run,
From sin's alluring snare;
Ready its first approach to shun,
And watching unto prayer.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that I never, never more
Might from thy ways depart!
Here let me give my wanderings o'er,
By giving thee my heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Fix my new heart on things above,
And then from earth release;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
ask not life, but let me love,
And lay me down in peace.

title: Master, I own thy lawful claim
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Pleasure, and wealth, and praise no more
Shall lead my captive soul astray:
My fond pursuits I all give o'er,
Thee, only thee, resolved to' obey;
My own in all things to resign,
And know no other will but thine.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Wherefore to thee I all resign;
Being thou art, and Love, and Power j
Thy only will he done, not mine!
Thee, Lord, let heaven and earth adore!
Flow back the rivers to the sea,
And let our ail be lost in thee!

title: Come on, my partners hi distress
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come on, my partners hi distress,
My comrades through the wilderness,
Who still your bodies feel;
A while forget your griefs and fears,
And look beyond this vale of tears,
To that celestial hill.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beyond the bounds of time and space,
Look forward to that heavenly place,
The saints' secure abode:
On faith's strong eagle-pinions rise,
And force your passage to the skies,
And scale the mount of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who suffer with our Master here,
We shall before his face appear,
And by his side sit down:
To patient faith the prize is sure;
And all that to the end endure
The cross, shall wear the crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thrice blessed, bliss-inspiring hope!
It lifts the fainting spirits up;
It brings to life the dead:
Our conflicts here shall soon be past,
And you and I ascend at last,
Triumphant with our Head.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
That great mysterious Deity
We soon with open face shall see;
The beatific sight
Shall fill heaven's sounding courts with praise,
And wide diffuse the golden blaze
Of everlasting light.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The Father shining on his throne,
The glorious co-eternal Son,
The Spirit, one and seven,
Conspire our rapture to complete;
And, lo! we fall before his feet,
And silence heightens heaven.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
In hope of that ecstatic pause,
Jesus, we now sustain the cross,
And at thy footstool fall;
Till thou our hidden life reveal,
Till thou our ravish'd spirits fill,
And God is All in All!

title: Lord, I adore thy gracious will
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1

title: Cast on the fidelity
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Cast on the fidelity
Of ray redeeming Lord,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
shall his salvation see,
According to his word:
Credence to his word I give;
My Saviour in distresses past
Will not now his servant leave,
But bring me through at last.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Better than my boding fears
To me thou oft hast proved;
Oft observed my silent tears,
And challenged thy beloved:
Mercy to my rescue flew,
And death ungrasp'd his fainting prey;
Para before thy face withdrew,
And sorrow fled away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now as yesterday the same,
In all my troubles nigh,
Jesus, on thy Word and Name

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
To thy blessed will resign'd,
And stay'd on that alone,

sections.label: Verse 7

title: P'ather, in the Name I pray
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
P'ather, in the Name I pray
Of thy Incarnate Love;
Humbly ask, that as my day
My suffering strength may prove:
When my sorrows most increase,
Let thy strongest joys he given:
Jesus, come with my distress,
And agony is heaven!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
For good remember me!
Me, whom thou hast caused to trust
For more than life on thee:
With me in the fire remain,
Till like burnish'd gold I shine,
Meet, through consecrated pain,
To see the Face Divine.

title: Eternal Beam of Light Divine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eternal Beam of Light Divine,
Fountain of unexhausted love,
In whom the Father's glories shine,
Through earth beneath and heaven above:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, the weary wanderer's rest,
Give me thy easy yoke to bear:
With steadfast patience arm my breast,
With spotless love, and lowly fear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thankful I take the cup from thee;
Prepared and mingled by thy skill,
Though bitter to the taste it be,
Powerful tht wounded soul to hea*.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Be thou, O Rock of Ages, nigh!
So shall each murmuring thought he gone;
And grief, and fear, and care, shall fly,
As clouds before the mid-day sun.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Speak to my warring passions, "Peace! "
Say to my trembling heart, "Be still!"
Thy power my strength and fortress is,
For all things serve thy sovereign will.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O death! where is thy sting? Where now
Thy boasted victory, O grave?
Who shall contend with God? or who
Can hurt whom God delights to save?

title: Lamb of God, thou Prince of Peace
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
With fraudless, even, humble mind,
Thy will in all things may I see;
In love be every wish resign'd,
And hallow'd my whole heart to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When pain o'er my weak flesh prevails,
With lamb-like patience arm my breast;
When grief my wounded soul assails,
In lowly meekness may I rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Close by thy side still may I keep,
Howe'er life's various current flow;
With steadfast eye mark every step,
And follow thee where'er thou go.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
may I conquer through thy blood!
6 So, when on Sion, thou shalt stand,
And all heaven's host adore their King,
Shall I be found at thy right hand.
And free from pain thy glories sing.

title: O thou, to whose all-searching sight
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou, to whose all-searching sight
The darkness shineth as the light,
Search, prove my heart; it pants for thee;
O burst these bonds, and set it free!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wash out its stains, refine its dross,
Nail my affections to the cross;
Hallow each thought; let all within
Be clean, as thou, my Lord, art clean!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If in this darksome wild I stray,
Be thou my Light, be thou my Way;
No foes, no violence I fear,
No fraud, while thou, my God, art near.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When rising floods my soul o'erflow,
When sinks my heart in waves of woe,
Jesus, thy timely aid impart,
And raise my head, and cheer my heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Saviour, where'er thy steps I see,
• Dauntless, untired, I follow thee I
O let thy hand support me still,
And lead me to thy holy hill!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
If rough and thorny be the way,
My strength proportion to my day;
Till toil, and grief, and pain shall cease,
Where all is calm, and joy, and peace.

title: The thing my God doth hate
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The thing my God doth hate
That I no more may do,
Thy creature, Lord, again create,
And all my soul renew:
My soul shall then, like thine,
Abhor the thing unclean,
And, sanctified, by love divine,
For ever cease from sin.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That blessed law of thine,
Jesus, to me impart:
The Spirit's law of life divine,
O write it in my heart!
Implant it deep within,
Whence it may ne'er remove;
The law of liberty from sin,
The perfect law of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy nature be my law,
Thy spotless sanctity.
And sweetly every moment draw
My happy soul to thee,
Soul of my soul remain!
Who didst for all fulfil,
In me, O Lord, fulfil again
Thy heavenly Father's will.

title: O Jesus, let thy dying cry
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus, let thy dying cry
Pierce to the bottom of my heart,
Its evils cure, its wants supply,
And bid my unbelief depart.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Let me, according to thy word,
A tender, contrite heart receive,
Which grieves at having grieved its Lord,
And never can itself forgive:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A heart thy joys and griefs to feel,
A heart that cannot faithless prove,
A heart where Christ alone may dwell,
All praise, all meekness, and all love.

title: God of eternal truth and grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of eternal truth and grace,
Thy faithful promise seal!
Thy word, thy oath to Abraham's race,
In us, even us, fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let us, to perfect love restored,
Thy image here retrieve;
And in the presence of our Lord
The life of angels live.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
%hat mighty faith on me bestow,
Which cannot ask in vain;
Which holds, and will not let thee go,
Till I my suit obtain:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Till thou into my soul inspire
The perfect love unknown,
And tell my infinite desire,
