"Whate'er thou wilt, be done."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But is it possible that I
Should live and sin no more?
Lord, if on thee I dare rely,
The faith sball bring the power.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
On me that faith divine bestow,
Which doth the mountain move
And all my spotless life shall show
The omnipotence of love.

title: O for a heart to praise my God
author: 0   Weslet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for a heart to praise my God,
V/ A heart from sin set free!
A heart that always feels thy blood
So freely spilt for me!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A heart resign'd, submissive, meek,
My great Redeemer's throne;
Where only Christ is heard to speak,
Where Jesus reigns alone:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A humble, lowly, contrite heart,
Believing, time, and clean;
Which neither life nor death can part
From him that dwells within:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A heart in every thought renew'd,
And full of love divine;
Perfect, and right, and pure, and good,
A copy, Lord, of thine!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy tender heart is still the same, W
And melts at human woe:
Jesus, for thee distress'd I am,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
want thy love to know.
6 My heart, thou know'st, can never rest,
Till thou create my peace;
Till, of my Eden re-possest,
From every sin I cease.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Fruit of thy gracums lips, on me
Bestow that peace unknown,
The hidden manna, and the tree
Of life, and the white stone.

sections.label: Verse 8

title: Thou hidden love of God, whose height
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou hidden love of God, whose height,
Whose depth unfathom'd, no man knows j

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
see from far thy beauteous light,
Inly I sigh for thy repose:
My heart is pain'd, nor can it he
At rest, till it finds rest in thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
aim at thee, yet from thee stray.
3 'Tis mercy all, that thou hast brought
My mind to seek her peace in thee;
Yet while I seek, but find thee not,
No peace my wandering soul shall see;
O when shall all my wanderings end,
And all my steps to thee- ward tend!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Is there a thing beneath the sun
That strives with thee my heart to share?
Ah, tear it thence, and reign alone,
The Lord of every motion there!
Then shall my heart from earth be free,
When it hath found repose in thee.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O bide this self from me, that I
No more, but Christ in me, may live;
My vile affections crucify,
Nov let one darling lust survive!
In all things nothing may I see,
Nothing desire or seek, hut thee!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O Love, thy sovereign aid impart,
To save me from low-thoughtel care;
Chase this self-will through all my heart,
Through all its latent mazes there:
Make me thy duteous child, that I
Ceaseless may, "Abba Father,"cry!

sections.label: Verse 8
Verse 9
sections.text:
Each moment draw from earth away
My heart, that lowly waits thy call;
Speak to my inmost soul, and say,
"I am thy Love, thy God, thy All!"
To feel thy power, to hear thy voice,
To taste thy love, be all my choice.

title: Ye ransom'd sinners, hear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye ransom'd sinners, hear,
The prisoners of the Lord,
And wait till Christ appear,
According to his word:
Rejoice in hope, rejoice with me,
We shall from all our sins be free.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let others hug their chains,
For sin and Satan plead,
And say from sin's remains
They never can be freed:
Rejoice in hope, rejoice with me,
We shall from all our sins be free.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In God we put our trust;
If we our sins confess,
Faithful he is, and just,
From all unrighteousness
To cleanse us all, both you and me*
We shall from all our sins be free.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Surely in us the hope
Of glory shall appear;
Sinners, your heads lift up,
And see Redemption near:
Again I say, rejoice with me,
We shall from all our sins be free.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Who Jesu's sufferings share,
My fellow-prisoners now,
Ye soon the wreath shall wear
On your triumphant brow:
Rejoice in hope, rejoice with mii,
We shall from all our sins be free

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The word of God is sure,
And never can remove;
We shall in heart be pure,
And perfected in love:
Rejoice in hope, rejoice with me,
We shall from all our sins be tree.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Then let us gladly bring
Our sacrifice of praise;
Let us give thanks, and sing,
And glory in his grace:
Rejoice in hope, rejoice with me
We shall from all our sins be free»

title: For ever here my rest shall be
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For ever here my rest shall be,
Close to thy bleeding side;
This all my hope, and all my plea,
For me the Saviour died

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My dying Saviour, and my God,
Fountain for guilt and sin,
Sprinkle me ever with thy blood.
And cleanse and keep me clean.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wash me, and make me thus thine own j
Wash me, and mine thou art;
Wash me, hut not my feet alone,
My hands, my head, my heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The atonement of thy hlood apply,
Till faith to sight improve;
Till hope in full fruition die,
And all my soul be love.

title: Jesus, my life! thyself apply
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, my life! thyself apply,
Thy Holy Spirit breathe;
My vile affections crucify,
Conform me to thy death.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Conqu'ror of hell, and ea7tl/, and sin,
Still with thy itbel strive;
Enter my soul, aiid work within,
And kill, and make alive!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
More of thy life, and more, I have,
As the old Adam dies:
Bury me, Saviour, in thy grave,
That I with thee may rise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Reign in me, Lord, thy foes control,
Who would not own thy sway;
Diffuse thine image through my sou
Shine to the perfect day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Scatter the last remains of sin,
And seal me thine abode;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
make me glorious all within,
A temple built by God!

title: Heavenly Father, sovereign Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Heavenly Father, sovereign Lord,
Ever faithful to thy word,
Humbly we our seal set to,
Testify that thou art true.
Lo! for us the wilds are glad,
All in cheerful green array'd;
Opening sweets they all disclose,
Bud and blossom as the rose.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
See, these barren souls of ours
Bbom, and put forth fruits and flowers,
Flowers of Eden, fruits of grace,
Peace, and joy, and righteousness.
We behold (the abjects, we!)
Christ, the' incarnate Deity,
Christ, hi whom thy glories shine,
Excellence of strength divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ye that tremble at his frown,
He shall lift your hands cast down f
Christ, who all your weakness sees,
He shall prop your feeble knees.
Ye of fearful hearts, be strong;
Jesus will not tarry long;
Fear not lest his truth should fail:
Jesus is unchangeable.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Faint we were, and parch'd with drought,
Water at thy word gush'd out:
Streams of grace our thirst repress,
Starting from the wilderness.
Still we gasp thy grace to know;
Here for ever let it flow;
Make the thirsty land a pool,
Fix thy Spirit in our soul.

title: Where the ancient Dragon lay
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Where the ancient Dragon lay
Open for thyself a way!
There let holy tempers rise,
All the fruits of Paradise.
Lead us in the way of peace,
In the path of righteousness,
Never by the sinner trod,
Till he feels the cleansing blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, mighty to redeem,
Let our lot be cast with them;
Far from earth our souls remove,
Eansom'd by thy dying love.
Leave us not below to mourn;
Fain we would to thee return,
Crown'd with righteousness, arise
Far above these nether skies.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
TTOLY Lamb, who thee receive,
JlL Who in thee begin to live,
Day and night they cry to thee,
As thou art, so let us be!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Jesu, see my panting breast!
See I pant in thee to rest;
Gladly would I now be clean:
Cleanse me now from every sin.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
Dust and ashes though we be,
Full of sin and misery,
Thine we are, thou Son of God!
Take the purchase of thy blood!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Who in heart on thee believes,
He the' atonement now receives;
He with joy beholds thy face,
Triumphs in thy pardoning grace.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
See, ye sinners! see the flame,
Rising from the slaughter'd Lamb,
Marks the new, the living way,
Leading to eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Jesus, when this light we see,
All our soul's athirst for thee;
When thy quick'ning power we prove.
All our heart dissolves in love.

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
Boundless wisdom, power divine,
Love unspeakable, are thine:
Praise by all to thee be given,
Sons of earth, and hosts of heaven!

title: Come, Holy Ghost, all-quick'ning fire
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Ghost, all-quick'ning fire!
Come, and my hallow'd heart inspire,
Sprinkled with the' atoning blood:
Now to my soul thyself reveal;
Thy mighty working let me feel,
And know that I am bom of God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy witness with my spirit bear,
That God, my God, inhabits there,
Thou, with the Father, and the Son,
Eternal light's co-eval beam: —
Be Christ in me, and I in him,
Till perfect we are made in one.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When wilt thou my whole heart subdue?
Come, Lord, and form my soul anew,
Emptied of pride, and wrath, and hell:
Less than the least of all thy store
Of mercies, I myself abhor:
All, all my vileness may I feel.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
then shall turn my steady face, —
"Want, pain defy, —enjoy disgrace, —
Glory in dissolution near.

sections.label: Verse 8
Verse 9

title: Jesus, thou art our King
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
High on thy Father's throne,
O look with pity down!
Help, O help, attend my call,
Captive lead captivity;
King of glory, Lord of all,
Christ, be Lord, be King t* me!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Triumph and reign in me,
And spread thy victory;
Hell, and death, and sin control,
Pride, and wrath, and every foe,
All subdue; through all my soul
Conquering, and to conquer, go.

title: O jesus, source of calm repose
author: 3   Weslet J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O jesus, source of calm repose,
Thy like nor man nor angel knows;
Fairest among ten thousand fair!
Even those whom death's sad fetters bound,
Whom thickest darkness compass'd round,
Find light and Hie, if thou appear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Effulgence of the Light Divine,
Ere rolling planets knew to shine,
Ere time its ceaseless course began;
Thou, when the' appointed hour was come,
Didst not abhor the virgin's womb,
But, God with God, wast man with man.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord over all, sent to fulfil
Thy gracious Father's sovereign will,
To thy dread sceptre will I bow:
With duteous reverence at thy feet,
Like humble Mary, lo! I sit;
Speak, Lord! thy servant heareth now.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
A patient, a victorious mind,
That life and all things casts behind,
Springs forth obedient to thy call;
A heart that no desire can move,
But still to' adore, believe, and love,
Give me, my Lord, my Life, my AIL'

title: Ever fainting with desire
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
want my God, my All!
Jesus, dear redeeming Lord,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
wait thy coming from above:
Help me, Saviour, speak the word,
And perfect me in love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Wilt thou suffer me to go
Lamenting all my days?
Shall I never, never know
Thy sanctifying grace?
Wilt thou not the light afford,
The darkness from my soul remove?
Help me, Saviour, speak the word,
And perfect me in love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, if I on thee helieve,
The second gift impart;
With the' indwelling Spirit give
A new, a contrite heart:
If with love thy heart is stored,
If now o'er me thy bowels move,
Help me, Saviour, speak the word,
And perfect me in love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Let me gain my calling's hope;
O make the sinner clean!
Dry corruption's fountain up,
Cut off the' entail of sin:
Take me into thee, my Lord,
And I shall then no longer rove:
Help me, Saviour, speak the word,
And perfect me in love.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Thou, my Life, my Treasure be,
My portion here below;
Nothing would I seek but thee,
Thee only would I know,
My exceeding great Reward,
My Heaven on earth, my Heaven above t
Help me, Saviour, speak the word,
And perfect me in love.

sections.label: Verse 8

title: Jesu, shall I never be
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, shall I never be
Firmly grounded upon thee?
Never by thy work abide,
Never in thy wounds reside?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O how wavering is my mind,
Toss'd about with every wind!
O how quickly doth my heart
From the living God depart!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesu, let my nature feel,
Thou art God unchangeable:
Jah, Jehovah, great I AM,
Speak into my soul thy Name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Grant that every moment I
May believe, and feel thee nigh;
Steadfastly behold thy face,
'Stablish'd with abiding grace

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Plant, and root, and fix in me
All the mind that was in thee:
Settled peace I then shall find;
Jesu's is a quiet mind.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Anger I no more shall feel,
Always even, always still,
Meekly on my God reclined;
Jesu's is a qentle mind.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
Verse 9
sections.text:
When I feel it fix'd within,
I shall have no power to sin;
How shall sin an entrance find?
Jesu's is a spotless mind.

sections.label: Verse 10
Verse 11
Verse 12
sections.text:
I shall fully be restored
To the image of my Lord;
Witnessing to all mankind,
Jesu's is a perfect mind.

title: Lord, I believe thy every word
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, I believe thy every word,
JLi Thy every promise, true;
And, lo! I wait on thee, my Lord,
Till I my strength renew.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If in this feeble flesh I may
Awhile show forth thy praise:
Jesu, support the tottering clay,
And lengthen out my days.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If such a worm as I can spread
The common Saviour's name;
Let him who raised thee from the dead
Quicken my mortal frame.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Still let me live thy blood to show,
Which purges every stain;
And gladly linger out below
A few more years in pain.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Spare me till I my strength of soul,
Till I thy love, retrieve;
Till faith shall make my spirit whole,
And perfect soundness give.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Faith to be heal'd thou know'st I have,
From sin to be made clean;
Able thou art from sin to save,
From all indwelling sin.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Surely thou canst, I do not doubt,
Thou wilt, thyself impart;
The hond- woman's base son cast out,
And take up all my heart.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
I shall my ancient strength renew:
The excellence divine
(If thou art good, if thou art true)
Throughout my soul shall shine.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
I shall, a weak and helpless worm,
Through Jesus strengthening me,
Impossibilities perform,
And live from sinning free.

sections.label: Verse 10

title: Jesus, the Life, the Truth, the Way
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, the Life, the Truth, the Way,
In whom I now helieve,
As taught by thee, in faith I pray,
Expecting to receive.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy will hy me on earth be done,
As hy the choirs above,
Who always see thee on thy throne,
And glory in thy love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I ask in confidence the grace,
That I may do thy will,
As angels, who behold thy face.
And all thy words fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Surely I shall, the sinner I
Shall serve thee without fear;
My heart no longer gives the lis
To my deceitful prayer.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When thou the work of faith hast wrought,
I shall he pure within,
Nor sin in deed, or word, or thought;
For angels never sin.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
From thee no more shall I depart,
No more unfaithful prove:
But love thee with a constant heart;
For angels always love.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
I all thy holy will shall prove:
I, a weak, sinful worm,
When thee with all my heart I love,
Shall all thy law perform.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
The graces of my second birth
To me shall all be given;
And I shall do thy will on earth,
As angels do in heaven.

title: Open, Lord, my inward ear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Open, Lord, my inward ear,
And bid my heart rejoice;
Bid my quiet spirit hear
Thy comfortable voice;
Never in the whirlwind found,
Or where earthquakes rock the place,
Still and silent is the sound,
The whisper of thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
wait with humble awe;
Silent am I now and still,
Dare not in thy presence move
To my waiting soul reveal
The secret of thy love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou didst undertake for me,
For me to death wast sold;
"Wisdom in a mystery
Of bleeding love unfold:
Teach the lesson of thy cross,
Let me die with thee to reign;
All things let me count but loss,
So I may thee regain.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Show me, as my soul can bear,
The depth of inbred sin;
All the unbelief declare,
The pride that lurks within:
Take me, whom thyself hast bought;
Bring into captivity
Every high aspiring thought,
That would not stoop to thee.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Lord, my time is in thy hand,
My soul to thee convert;
Thou canst make me understand,
Though I am slow of heart:
Thine in whom I live and move,
Thine the work, the praise is thine;
Thou art Wisdom, Power, and Love,
And all thou art is mine.

title: G od of Israel's faithful Three
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
G od of Israel's faithful Three,
vJT Who braved a tyrant's ire,
Nobly scorn'd to bow the knee,
And walk'd unhurt in fire:
Breathe their faith into my breast;
Arm me in this fiery hour;
Stand, O Son of Man, confest
In all thy saving power I

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Unto thee, my Help, my Hope,
My Safeguard, and my Tower,
Confident I still look up,
And still receive thy power:
All the alien's hosts I chase,
Blast and scatter with mine eyes;
Satan comes; I turn my face,
And, lo! the Tempter flies I

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sin in me, the inbred foe,
Awhile subsists in chains;
But thou all thy power shalt show,
And slay its last remains:
Thou hast conquer'd my desire,
Thou shalt quench it with thy blood,
Fill me with a purer fire.
And make me all like God.

title: Father of Jesus Christ, my Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of Jesus Christ, my Lord,
My Saviour, and my Head,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
trust in thee, whose powerful word
Hath raised him from the dead.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou know'st for my offence he died.
And rose again for me,
Fully and freely justified,
That I might live to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Eternal life to all mankind
Thou hast in Jesus given;
And all who seek, in him shall find
The happiness of heaven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O God! thy record I helieve,
In Abraham's footsteps tread;
And -wait, expecting to receive,
The Christ, the promised Seed.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Faith in thy power thou seest I have,
For thou this faith hast wrought;
Dead souls thou callest from their grave,
And speakest worlds from nought.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Things that are not, as though they were,
Thou callest by their name;
Present with thee the future are,
With thee, the great I AM.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
In hope, against all human hope,
Self-desperate, I helieve:
Thy quick'ning word shall raise me up,
Thou shalt thy Spirit give.

sections.label: Verse 9
Verse 10
sections.text:
Faith, mighty faith, the pi-omise sees,
And looks to that alone;
Laughs at impossibilities,
And cries, "It shall be done!"

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
To thee the glory of thy power
And faithfulness I give;

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
shall in Christ, at that glad hour,
And Christ in me shall live.

sections.label: Verse 13
sections.text:
1 Obedient faith, that waits on thee,
Thou never wilt reprove;
But thou wilt form thy Son in me,
And perfect me in love.

title: My God! I know, I feel thee mine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God! I know, I feel thee mine,
And will not quit my claim,
Till all I have is lost in thine,
And all renew'd I am.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I hold thee with a trembling hand,
But will not let thee go,
Till steadfastly by faith 1 stand,
And all thy goodness know.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When shall I see the welcome houi,
That plants my God in me!
Spirit of health, and life, and power,
And perfect liberty!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, thine all-victorious love
Shed in my heart abroad;
Then shall my feet no longer rove,
Booted and fix'd in God.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Love only can the conquest win,
The strength of sin subdue,
(Mine own unconquerable sin,)
And form my soul anew.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Love can bow down the stubborn neck,
The stone to flesh convert,
Soften, and melt, and pierce, and break,
An adamantine heart.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O that in me the sacred fire
Might now begin to glow!
Burn up the dross of base desire,
And make the mountains flow.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
O that it now from heaven might fall,
And all my sins consume!
Come, Holy Ghost, for thee I call,
Spirit of burning, come!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Refining fire, go through my heart,
Illuminate my soul;
Scatter thy life through every part,
And sanctify the whole.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
No longer then my heart shall mourn,
While, purified by grace,

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
only for his glory burn,
And always see his face.

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
My steadfast soui, from falling free,
Shall then no longer move;
But Christ be all the world to me,
And all my heart be love.

title: Be it according to thy word
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Be it according to thy word,
This moment let it be!
O that I now, my gracious Lord,
Might lose my life for thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, my life appear within,
And bruise the Serpent's head;
Enter my soul, extirpate sin,
Cast out the cursed seed.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Hast thou not made me willing, Lord?
Would I not die this hour?
Then speak the killing, quick'ning word;
Slay, raise me, by thy power.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Slay me, and I hi thee shall trust,
With thy dead men arise;
Awake, and sing out of the dust,
Soon as this nature dies.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
O let it now make haste to die,
The mortal wound receive;
So shall I live; and yet not I,
But Christ in me shall live.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Be it according to thy word!
This moment let it be!
The life I lose for thee, my Lord,

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text: find again in thee.

title: I that! never speak one evil word
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I that! never speak one evil word,
Or rash, or idle, or unkind!
O how shall I, most gracious Lord,
This mark of true perfection find?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Saviour, I long to testify
The fulness of thy saving grace;
O might thy Spirit the blood apply,
Which bought for me the sacred peace!

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Jesus, the gift divine I know
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thee let me drink, and thirst no more
For drops of finite happiness;
Spring up, O Well, in heavenly power,
In streams of pure, perennial peace,
In joy, that none can take away,
In life, which shall for ever stay.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Father, on me the grace hestow,
Unblamable before thy sight,
Whence all the streams of mercy flow;
Mercy, thy own supreme delight,
To me, for Jesu's sake impart,
And plant thy nature in my heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy mind throughout my life be shown,
While list'ning to the wretch's cry,
The widow's and the orphan's groan,
On mercy's wings I swiftly fly,
The poor and helpless to relieve,
My life, my all, for them to give.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: I cannot praise thee as I would
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I cannot praise thee as I would;
But thou art merciful and good;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
know thou never wilt despise
The day of small and feeble things,
But bear me, till on eagles' wings
To all the heights of love I rise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I thank thee for that gracious taste,
(Which pride would not permit to last,)
That touch of love, that pledge of heaven
Surely on me my Father smiled,
And once I knew him reconciled,
And once I felt my sins forgiven.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Vilest of all the sons of men,
When I to folly turn'd again,
And sinn'd against thy light and love,
Grace did much more than sin abound;
Amazed, I still forgiveness found,
And thank'd my Advocate above.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
The boundless love that found out me,
For every soul of man is free;
None of thy mercy need despair:
Patient, and pityful, and kind,
Thee every soul of man may find,
And, freely saved thy grace declare.

sections.label: Verse 8
Verse 9
sections.text:
see an open door of hope;
And wait thy fulness to receive.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
How shall I thank thee for the grace,
The trust I have to see thy face,
When sin shall all be purged away!
The night of doubts and fears is past,
The Morning Star appears at last,
And I shall see the perfect day

title: I soon shall hear thy quick'ning voice
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
find, I find thee strong to save,
And know that Jesus is thy name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By faith I every moment stand,
Strangely upheld by thy right hand;

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Come, then, and loose my stamm'ring tongue,
Teach me the new, the joyful song,
And perfect in a babe thy praise:

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
want a thousand lives to' employ
In publishing the sounds of joy, -
The gospel of thy general grace.

sections.label: Verse 8

title: O come, and dwell in me
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O come, and dwell in me,
Spirit of power within!
And bring the glorious liberty
From sorrow, fear, and sin.
The seed of sin's disease,
Spirit of health, remove,
Spirit of finish'd holiness,
Spirit of perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hasten the joyful day,
Which shall my sins consume,
When old things shall be past away,
And all things new become.
The' original offence
Out of my soul erase,
Enter thyself, and drive it hence,
And take up all the place.
S I want the witness, Lord,
That all I do is right,
According to thy will and word,
Well-pleasing in thy sight.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
ask no higher state;
Indulge me but in this,
And soon or later then translate
To my eternal bliss.

title: Father, see this living clod
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, see this living clod,
I This spark of heavenly fire;
See my soul, the hreath of God,
Doth after God aspire:
Let it still to heaven ascend,
Till I my principle rejoin,
Blended with my glorious end,
And lost in love divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, if thou from me hast broke
The power of outward sin,
Burst this Babylonish yoke,
And make me free within:
Bid my inbred sin depart,
And 1 thy utmost word shall prove,
Upright both in life and heart,
And perfected in love.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
gain that perfect love unknown,
Bright in all thy image shine,
By putting on thy Son.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
In council join again,
To restore thine image lost
By frail, apostate man:
O might I thy form express,
Through faith begotten from above,
Stamp'd with real holiness,
And fill'd with perfect love.

title: O God, most merciful and true
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, most merciful and true!
Thy nature to my soul impart j
'Stablish with me the cov'nant new,
And write perfection on my heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To real holiness restored,
O let me gain my Saviour's mind!
And, in the knowledge of my Lord,
Fulness of life eternal find.
S Remember, Lord, my sins no more,
That them I may no more forget;
But sunk in guiltless shame adore,
In speechless wonder, at thy feet.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O'erwhelm'd with thy stupendous grace,
1 shall not in thy presence move;
But breathe unutterable praise,
And rapturous awe, and silent love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then every murmuring thought and vain
Expires, in sweet confusion lost;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
cannot of my cross complain;
I cannot of my goodness boast.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Pardon'd for all that I have done,
My mouth as in the dust I hide;
And glory give to God alone,
My God for ever pacified!

title: Deepen the wound thy hands have made
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Deepen the wound thy hands have made
JLJ In this weak, helpless soul,
Till mercy, with its balmy aid,
Descends to make me whole.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The sharpness of thy two-edged sword,
Enable me to endure;
Till bold to say, My hallowing Lord,
Hath wrought a perfect cure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I see the' exceeding broad command,
Which all contains in one:
Enlarge my heart to understand
The mystery unknown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that with all thy saints I might
By sweet experience prove,
What is the length, and breadth, and height,
And depth of perfect love!

title: What now is my object and aim
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What now is my object and aim?
What now is my hope and desire?
To follow the heavenly Lamb,
And after his image aspire:
My hope is all centred in thee;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
trust to recover thy love,
On earth thy salvation to see,
And then to enjoy it above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I thirst for a life-giving God,
A God that on Calvary died;
A fountain of water and blood,
Which gush'd from Immanuel's side 1

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
gasp for the stream of thy love,
The Spirit cf rapture unknown:
And then to re-drink it above,
Eternally fresh from the throne.

title: Jesu, thy boundless love to me
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, thy boundless love to me
No thought can reach, no tongue declare,
O knit my thankful heart to thee,
And reign without a rival there:
Thine wholly, thine alone, I am;
Be thou alone my constant flame!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O Love, how cheering is thy ray!
All pain before thy presence flies;
Care, anguish, sorrow, melt away,
Where'er thy healing beams arise:
O Jesu, nothing may I see,
Nothing desire, or seek, but thee!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Unwearied may I this pursue,
Dauntless to the high prize aspire;
Hourly within my soul renew
This holy flame, this heavenly fire j
And day and night be all my care
To guard the 3acred treasure there

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
O that I, as a little child,
May follow thee, and never rest,"
Till sweetly thou hast breathed thy mild
And lowly mind into my breast!
Nor ever may we parted be,
Till I become one spirit with thee.

sections.label: Verse 8
Verse 9

title: Come, Holy Ghost, all-quick'ning fire
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
come and consecrate my breast!
The temple of my soul prepare,
And fix thy sacred presence there!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If now thy influence I feel,
If now in thee begin to live,
Still to my heart thyself reveal;
Give me thyself, for ever give:
A point my good, a drop my store,
Eager I ask, I pant for more.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
My peace, my life, my comfort thou,
My treasure, and my all thou art!
True witness of my sonship, now
Engraving pardon on my heart;
Seal of my sins in Christ forgiven,
Earnest of love, and pledge of heaven.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Saviour from sin, I wait to prove
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour from sin, I wait to prove
That Jesus is thy healing name;
To lose, when perfected in love,
Whate'er I have, or can, or am:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
stay me on thy faithful word,
"The servant shall be as his Lord."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Answer that gracious end in me,
For which thy precious life was given j
Redeem from all iniquity;
Restore, and make me meet for heaven
Unless thou purge my every stain,
Thy suffering and my faith are vain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Didst thou not hi the flesh appear,
Sin to condemn and man to save?
That perfect love might cast out fear?
That I thy mind in me might have?
In holiness show forth thy praise,
And serve thee all my spotless days?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Didst thou not die that I might live
No longer to myself but thee?
Might body, soul, and spirit, give
To him who gave himself to me?
Come then, my Master, and my God,
Take the dear purchase of thy blood.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text: A

title: I want the Spirit of power within
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
When shall I hear the inward voice,
Which only faithful souls can hear?
Pardon, and peace, and heavenly joys,
Attend the promised Comforter;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
come, and righteousness divine,
And Christ, and all with Christ, are mine!
S O that the Comforter would come!
Nor visit as a transient guest,
But fix in me his constant home,
And take possession of my breast,
And fix in me his loved abode,
The temple of indwelling God!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
cannot rest in sins forgiven;
Where is the earnest of my heaven?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
v here the indubitable seal
That ascertains the kingdom mine?
The powerful stamp I long to feel,
The signature of love divine!
O shed it in my heart abroad,
Fulness of love, of heaven, of God!

title: P'ather of everlasting grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
P'ather of everlasting grace,
I Thy goodness and thy truth we praise,
Thy goodness and thy truth we prove:
Thou hastj in honour of thy Son,
The gift unspeakable sent down,
The Spirit of life, and power, and love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Send us the Spirit of thy Son,
To make the depths of Godhead known,
To make us share the life divine:
Send him the sprinkled blood to' apply,
Send him our souls to sanctify,
And show and seal us ever thine.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Till, added to that heavenly choir,
We raise our songs of triumph higher,
And praise thee in a bolder strain;
Out-soar the first-born seraph's flight,
And sing, with all our friends in light,
Thy everlasting love to man.

title: I long to know, and to make known
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I long to know, and to make known,
The heights and depths of love divine,
The kindness thou to me hast shown,
Whose eveiy sin was counted thine!
My God for me resign'd his breath!
He died to save my soul from death!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How shall I thank thee for the grace
On me and all mankind bestow' d?
O that my every breath were praise!
O that my heart were filled with God!
My heart would then with love o'erflow,
And all my life thy glory show.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See me, O Lord, athirst and faint I
Me, weary of forbearing, see!
And let me feel thy love's constraint,
And freely give up all for thee;
True in the fiery trial prove,
And pay thee back thy dying love!

title: O love, I languish at thy stay
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O love, I languish at thy stay!
J I pine for thee with lingering smart,
Weary and faint through long delay:
When wilt thou come into my heart?
From sin and sorrow set me free,
And swallow up my soul in thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, O thou universal Good!
Balm of the wounded conscience, come!
The hungry, dying spirit's food,
The weary, wand'ring pilgrim's home:
Haven to take the shipwreck'd in,
My everlasting rest from sin!
Be thou, O Love, whate'er I want;
Support my feebleness of mind;
Relieve the thirsty soul, the faint
Revive, illuminate the blind;
The mournful cheer, the drooping lead,
And heal the sick, and raise the dead.
Come, O my comfort and delight!
My strength and health, my shield and sunj
My boast, and confidence, and might,
My joy, my glory, and my crown;
My gospel hope, my calling's prize,
My tree of life, my paradise.
The secret of the Lord thou art,
The mystery so long unknown;
Christ in a pure and perfect heart,
The name inscribed in the white stone;
The life divine, the little leaven,
My precious pearl, my present heaven.

title: "prisoners of hope, lift up your heads
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Ye all shall find, whom in his word
Himself hath caused to put your trust,
The Father of our dying Lord
Is ever to his promise just;
Faithful, if we our sins confess,
To cleanse from all unrighteousness.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
ask, the chief of sinners I!
4 O ye of fearful hearts, be strong!
Your downcast eyes and hands lift up!
Ye shall not be forgotten long;
Hope to the end, in Jesus hope!
Tell him, ye wait his grace to prove,
And cannot fail, if God is love!

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Hast thou not died to purge our sin,
And risen, thy death for us to plead?
To write thy law of love within
Our hearts, and make us free indeed?
That we our Eden might regain,
Thou diedst; and could'st not die in vain.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Lord, we believe, and wait the hour
Which all thy great salvation brings;
The Spirit of love, and health, and power,
Shall come, and make us priests and kings
Thou wilt perform thy faithful word,
"The servant shall be as his Lord."

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
The promise stands for ever sure,
And we shall in thine image shine,
Partakers of a nature pure,
Holy, angelical divine;
In spirit join'd to thee the Son,
As thou art with thy Father one.
Faithful and true, we now receive
The promise ratified by thee:
To thee the when and how we leave,
In time and in eternity;
We only hang upon thy word,
"The servant shall be as his Lord."

title: Thou art darkness in my mind
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Not by human might or power
Canst thou be moved from hencs
But thou shalt flow down before
Divine Omnipotence:
My Zerubbabel is near;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
have not believed in vain:
Thou, when Jesus doth appear,
Shalt sink into a plain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Christ the Head, the Corner-Stone
Shall be brought forth in me:
Giory be to Christ alone!
His grace shall set me free:

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Christ hath the foundation laid,
And Christ shall build me up;
Surely I shall soon be made
Partaker of my hope:
Author of my faith he is,
He its Finisher shall be;
Perfect love shall seal me a
To all eternity.

title: Who hath slighted or contemn'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Who hath slighted or contemn'd
The day of feehle things?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
I right early shall awake,
And see the perfect day;
Soon the Lamb of God shall take
My inbred sin away:
When to me my Lord shall come,
Sin for ever shall depart;
Jesus takes up all the room
In a believing heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Son of God, arise, arise,
And to thy temple come!
Look, and with thy flaming eyes
The man of sin consume;
Slay him with thy Spirit, Lord j
Reign thou in my heart alone;
Speak the sanctifying word,
And seal me all thine own.

title: And him lifting up my head
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And him lifting up my head,
He brings salvation near;
5is presence makes me free indeed,
And he will soon appear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He wills that I should holy be;
What can withstand his will?
The counsel of his grace in me
He surely shall fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, I hang upon thy word;
I steadfastly believe
Thou wilt return and claim me, Lord,
And to thyself receive.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Joyful in hope, my spirit soars
To meet thee from above,
Thy goodness thankfully adores;
And sure I taste thy love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy love I soon expect to find,
In all its depth and height;
To comprehend the' Eternal Mind,
And grasp the Infinite.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
When God is mine, and I am his,
Of paradise possest,

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
taste unutterable bliss,
And everlasting rest,

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
The bliss of those that fully dwell,
Fully in thee believe,
'Tis more than angel-tongues can tell,
Or angel-minds conceive.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Thou only know'st, who didst obtain,
And die to make it known;
The great salvation now explain,
And perfect us in one 1

title: Love Divine, all loves excelling
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Finish, then, thy new creation,
Pure and spotless let us be;
Let us see thy great salvation,
Perfectly restored in thee:
Changed from glory into glory,
Till in heaven we take our place.
Till we cast our crowns before thee,
Lost in wonder, love, and praise!

title: Arm of the Lord, awake, awake
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Arm of the Lord, awake, awake!
J.JL Thine own immortal strength put on!
With terror clothed, hell's kingdom shake,
And cast thy foes with fury down!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As in the ancient days appear;
The sacred annals speak thy fame:
Be now omnipotently near,
To endless ages still the same.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
By death and hell pursued in vain,
To thee the ransom'd seed shall come;
Shouting, their heavenly Sion gain,
And pass through death triumphant home

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The pain of life shall there be o'er,
The anguish and distracting care;
There sighing grief shall weep no more,
And sin shall never enter there.
') Where pure essenflal joy is found,
The Lord's redeem'd their heads shall raise,
With everlasting gladness crown'd,
And fill'd with love, and lost in praise.

title: Prisoners of hope, arise
author: R  Weslet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Prisoners of hope, arise,
And see your Lord appear:
Lo! on the wings of love he flies,
He brings redemption near.
Redemption in his blood
He calls you to receive:
"Look unto me, the pardoning God;
Believe,"he cries, "believe! "

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, to thee we look,
Till saved from sin's remains;
Reject the inbred tyrant's yoke,
And cast away his chains.
Our nature shall no more
O'er us dominion have;
By faith we apprehend the power
Which shall for ever save!

title: O that my load of sin were gone
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O that my load of sin were gone!
O that I could at last submit
At Jesu's feet to lay it down,
To lay my soul at Jesu's feet!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When shall mine eyes behold the Lamb!
The God of my salvation see?
Weary, O Lord, thou know'st I am;
Yet still I cannot come to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Rest for my soul I long to find:
Saviour of all, if mine thou art,
Give me thy meek and lowly mind,
And stamp thine image on my heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Break off the yoke of inbred sin,
And fully set my spirit free:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
cannot rest till pure within,
Till I am wholly lost in thee.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Fain would I learn of thee my God;
Thy light and easy burden prove.
The cross all stain'd' with hallow'd blood,
The labour of thy dying love.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
Come, Lord, the drooping sinner cheer,
Nor let thy chariot-wheels delay;
Appear, in my poor heart appear!
My God, my Saviour, come away!

title: O Jesus, at thy feet we wait
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus, at thy feet we wait,
Till thou shalt bid us rise,
. Restored to our unsmiling state,
To love's sweet paradise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Saviour from sin, we thee receive,
From all indwelling sin:
Thy blood, we steadfastly believe,
Shall make us throughly clean.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Since thou would'st have us free from sin,
And pure as those above,
Make haste to bring thy nature in,
And perfect us in love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The counsel of thy love fulfil;
Come quickly, gracious Lord!
Be it according to thy will,
According to thy word!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
According to our faith in thee
Let it to us be done;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
that we all thy face might see,
And know as we are known!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O that the perfect grace were given,
The love diffused abroad!
O that our hearts were all a heaven.
For ever fill'd with God!

title: Since the Son hath made me free
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Abba, Father! hear thy child,
Late in Jesus reconciled;
Hear, and all the graces shower.
All the joy, and peace, and power,
All my Saviour asks above,
All the life and heaven of lovo.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, I will not let thee go,
Till the blessing thou bestow:
Hear my Advocate Divine!
Lo! to his my suit I join;
Join'd to his, it cannot (fail:
Bless me; for I will prevail!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Heavenly Father, Life Divine,
Change my nature into thine!
Move and spread throughout my soul,
Actuate and fill the whole!
Be it I no longer now
Living in the flesh, but Thou.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Holy Ghost, no more delay!
Come, and in thy temple stay!
Now thine inward witness bear,
Strong, and permanent, and clear:
Spring of Life, thyself impart:
Rise eternal in my heart I

title: God of all power, and truth, and grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of all power, and truth, and grace,
Which shall from age to age endure;
Whose word, when heaven and earth shall pass,
Kemains and stands for ever sure:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That I thy mercy may proclaim,
That all mankind thy truth may see,
Hallow thy great and glorious name,
And perfect holiness in me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy sanctifying Spirit pour,
To quench my thirst, and make me clean
Now, Father, let the gracious shower
Descend, and make me pure from sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Give me a new, a perfect heart,
From doubt, and fear, and sorrow free;
The mind which was in Christ impart,
And let my spirit cleave to thee.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O take this heart of stone away!
Thy sway it doth not, cannot own:
In me no longer let it stay;
O take away this heart of stone!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O that I now, from sin released,
Thyword may to the utmost prove,
Enter into the promised rest,
The Canaan of thy perfect love!

title: Father, supply my every need
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The gracious fruits of righteousness,
Thy blessings' unexhausted store,
In me abundantly increase;
Nor ever let me hunger more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let me no more, in deep complaint,
"My leanness, O my leanness! "cry:
Alone consumed with pining want,
Of all my Father's children I.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The painful thirst, the fond desire,
Thy joyous presence shall remove;
But my full soul shall still require
A whole eternity of love.

title: Holy, and true, and righteous Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy, and true, and righteous Lord,
JLjL I wait to prove thy perfect will;
Be mindful of thy gracious word,
And stamp me with thy Spirit's seal.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: O God of our forefathers, hear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God of our forefathers, hear,
And make thy faithful mercies known:
To thee, through Jesus, we draw near,
Thy suffering, well-heloved Son,
In whom thy smiling face we see,
In whom thou art well pleased with me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With solemn faith we offer up,
And spread before thy glorious eyes,
That only ground of all our hope,
That precious, bleeding Sacrifice,
Which brings thy grace on sinners down,
And perfects all our souls in one.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Acceptance through his only name,
Forgiveness in his blood, we have;
But more abundant life we claim
Through him, who died our souls to save,
To sanctify us by his blood,
And fill with all the life of God.
i Father, behold thy dying Son,
And hear the blood that speaks above!
On us let all thy grace be shown:
Peace, Righteousness, and joy, and love, —
Thy kingdom, —come to every heart,
And all thou hast, and all thou art.

title: O God, to whom, in flesh reveal'd
author: Weslet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, to whom, in flesh reveal'd,
The helpless all for succour came,
The sick to be relieved and heal'd,
And found salvation in thy name:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With publicans and harlots, I,
In these thy Spirit's gospel days,
To thee, the sinner's Friend, draw nigh,
And humbly sue for saving grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou seest me helpless and distrest,
Feeble, and faint, and blind, and poor;
Weary, I come to thee for rest,
And sick of sin, implore a cure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My sin's incurable disease
Thou, Jesus, thou alone, canst heal;
Inspire me with thy power and peace,
And pardon on my conscience seal.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
A touch, a word, a look from thee,
Can turn my heart, and make it clean;
Purge the foul, inbred leprosy,
And save me from my bosom-sin.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Lord, if thou wilt, I do believe
Thou canst the saving grace impart;
Thou canst this instant now forgive,
And stamp thine image on my heart.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
My heai't, which now to thee I raise,
I know thou canst this moment cleanse j
The deepest stains of sin efface,
And drive the evil spirit hence.

sections.label: Verse 8

title: Thou, whom once they flock'd to hear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou, whom once they flock'd to hear,
Thy words to hear, thy power to feel;
Suffer the sinners to draw near,
And graciously receive us still.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They that be whole, thyself hast said,
No need of a physician have;
But I am sick, and want thine aid,
And want thine utmost power to save.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy power, and truth, and love divine,
The same from age to age endure;
A word, a gracious word of thine,
The most inveterate plague can cure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Helpless howe'er my spirit lies,
And long hath languish'd at the pool,
A word of thine shall make me rise,
And speak me in a moment whole.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Eighteen, or eight and thirty, years,
Or thousands, are alike to thee:
Soon as thy savmg grace appears,
My plague is gone, my heart is free.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Make this the acceptable hour!
Come, O my soul's Physician, thou!
Display thy sanctifying power,
And show me thy salvation now.
c. weslet.J HYMN* 397. l.m. (1

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
TESU, thy far-extended fame
t) My drooping soul exults to hear;
Thy name, thy all-restoring name,
Is music in a sinner's ear.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Sinners of old thou didst receive,
With comfortable words and kind,
Their sorrows cheer, their wants relieve,
Heal the deceased, and cure the blind,

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
And art thou not the Saviour still,
In every place and age the same?
Hast thou forgot thy gracious skill,
Or lost the virtue of thy name?

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Faith in thy changeless name I have;
The good, the kind Physician, thou
Art able now our souls to save,
Art willing to restore them now.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Though eighteen hundred years are past
Since thou didst in the flesh appear,
Thy tender mercies ever last;
And still thy healing power is here!

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
Wouldst thou the "body's health restore,
And not regard the sin-sick soul?
The sin-sick soul thou lov'st much more,
And surely thou shalt make it whole.

sections.label: Verse 13
sections.text:
All my disease, my every sin,
To thee, O Jesus, I confess;
In pardon, Lord, my cure hegin,
And perfect it in holiness.

sections.label: Verse 14
sections.text:
That token of thine utmost good
Now, Saviour, now on me bestow;
And purge my conscience with thy blood,
And wash my nature white as snow.

title: Jesu, shepherd of the sin-sick soul
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, shepherd of the sin-sick soul,
O Give me faith to make me whole!
Finish thy great work of grace,
Cut it short in righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Nothing less will I require,
Nothing more can I desire:
None but Christ to me be given!
None but Christ in earth or heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that I might now decrease 1
O that all I am might cease S
Let me into nothing fall,
Let my Lord be all in all!

title: Light of Life, seraphic fire
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, in this accepted hour;
Bring thy heavenly kingdom in!
Fill us with the glorious power,
Rooting out the seeds of sin:
Nothing more can we require,
We will covet nothing less;
Be thou all our heart's desire,
All our joy, and all our peace!

title: Jesus comes with all his grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus comes with all his grace,
Comes to save a fallen race;
Object of our glorious hope,
Jesus comes to lift us up!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let the living stones cry out;
Let the sons of Abraham shout:
Praise we all our lowly King,
Give him thanks, rejoice, and sing.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
We are now his lawful right,
Walk as children of the light:
We shall soon obtain the grace,
Pure in heart, to see his face.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We shall gain our calling's prize;
After God we all shall rise,
Fill'd with joy, and love, and peace,
Perfected in holiness.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Let us then rejoice in hope,
Steadily to Christ look up;
Trust to be redeem'd from sin,
Wait till he appear within.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Fools and madmen let us be,
Yet is our sure trust in thee:
Faithful is the promised word,
We shall all be as our Lord.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Hasten, Lord, the perfect day!
Let thy every servant say,
"1 have now obtain'd the power,
Born of God, to sin no more."

title: In, I do believe in thee
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Though earth and hell the word gainsay,
The word of God can never fail;
The Lamb shall take my sins away
'Tis certain, though impossible:
The thing impossible shall be:
All things are possible to me.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy mouth, O Lord, hath spoke, hath sworn,
That I shall serve thee without fear,
Shall find the pearl which others spurn,
Holy, and pure, and perfect here:
The servant as his Lord shall be;
All things are possible to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
All things are possible to God,
To Christ, the power of God in man,
To me when I am all renew'd,
When I in Christ am form'd again,
And witness, from all sin set free,
All things are possible to me.

title: I cut short the work, and make

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
let me sin no more!
3 Fain I would the truth proclaim,
That makes me free indeed,
Glorify my Saviour's Name,
And all its virtues spread:
Jesus all our wants relieves,
Jesus, mighty to redeem,
Saves, and to the utmost saves,
All those that come to him.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
come quickly from ahove!
Empty me of sin, and fill
With all the life of love.
c wesley.] EYMN 403. c. m. (9)

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
T"OED, I believe a rest remains,
I 1 To all thy people known,
A rest where pure enjoyment reigns,
And thou art loved alone:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
A rest, where all our soul's desire
Is fix'd on things above;
Where fear, and sin, and grief expire,
Cast out by perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O that I now the rest might know,
Believe, and enter in!
Now, Saviour, now the power bestow,
And let me cease from sin.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Eemove this hardness from my heart,
This unbelief remove:
To me the rest of faith impart,
The sabbath of thy love.

sections.label: Verse 9
Verse 10
Verse 11
sections.text:
Come, O my Saviour, come away!
Into my soul descend;
No longer from thy creature stay,
My Author, and my End 1

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
Come, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
And seal me thine abode!
Let all I am in thee be lost;
Let all be lost in God.

title: O glorious hope of perfect love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Rejoicing now in earnest hope
I stand, and from the mountain-top
See all the land below:
Rivers of milk and honey rise,
And all the fruits of Paradise
In endless plenty grow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A land of corn, and wine, and oil,
Favour'd with God's peculiar smile,
With every blessing blest;
There dwells the Lord our Righteousness,
And keeps his own in perfect peace,
And everlasting rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that I might at once go up!
No more on this side Jordan stop,
But now the land possess:
This moment end my legal years;
Sorrows, and sins, and doubts, and fears,
A howling wilderness.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Now, O my Joshua, bring me in!
Cast out thy foes; the inbred sin,
The carnal mind, remove;
The purchase of thy death divide!
And O! with all the sanctified
Give me a lot of love!

title: O joyful sound of gospel grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
shall be holy here.
2 This heart shall be his constant home;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
hear his Spirit's cry:
"Surely,"he saith, "I quickly come: "
He saith who cannot lie.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The glorious crown of righteousness
To me reach'd out I view;
Conqu'ror through him, I soon shall seize.
And wear it as my due.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The promised land, from Pisgah's top,
I now exult to see;
My hope is full (0 glorious hope!)
Of immortality.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
With me I know, I feel thou art;
But this cannot suffice,
Unless thou plantest in my heart
A constant paradise.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
My earth thou waterest from on high;
But make it all a pool:
Spring up, O Well, I ever cry,
Spring up within my soul!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Come, O my God, thyself reveal,
Fill all this mighty void;
Thou only canst my Spirit fill:
Come, O my God, my God!

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Fulfil, fulfil my large desires,
Large as infinity;
Give, give me all my soul requires,
All, all that is in thee!

title: What is our calling's glorious hope
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What is our calling's glorious hope,
But inward holiness?
For this to Jesus I look up,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
calmly wait for this.
2 I wait, till he shall touch me clean,
Shall life and power impart,
Give me the faith that casts out sin,
And purifies the heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This is the dear redeeming grace,
For every sinner free;
Surely it shall on me take place,
The chief of sinners me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From all inquity, from all,
He shall my soul redeem;
In Jesus I helieve, and shall
Believe myself to him.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When Jesus makes my heart his home,
My sins shall all depart;
And lo! he saith, "I quickly come,
To fill and rule thy heart! »

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Be it according to thy word!
Redeem me from all sin:
My heart would now receive thee, Lord;
Come in, my Lord, come in!

title: None is like Jeshurun's God
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
None is like Jeshurun's God,
So great, so strong, so high:
Lo! he spreads his wings abroad,
He rides upon the sky:
Israel is his first-horn son:
God, the' Almighty God, is thine;
See him to thy help come down,
The excellence divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thee the great Jehovah deigns
To succour and defend;
Thee the' eternal God sustains,
Thy Maker and thy Friend:
Israel, what hast thou to dread?
Sale from all impending harms,
Round thee and beneath are spread
The everlasting arms.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God is thine; disdain to fear
The enemy within:
God shall in thy flesh appear,
And make an end of sin:
God the man of sin shall slay,
Fill thee with triumphant joy;
God shall thrust him out, and say,
"Destroy them all, destroy! "

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
In a land of corn and wine
His lot shall be below;
Comforts there, and blessings join,
And milk and honey flow:
Jacob's well is in his soul;
Gracious dew his heavens distil,
Fill his soul, already full,
And shall for ever fill.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Blest, O Israel, art thou:
What people is like thee?
Saved from sin, by Jesus, now
Thou art, and still shalt be:
Jesus is thy seven-fold shield;
Jesus is thy flaming sword;
Earth, and hell, and sin shall yield
To God's almighty Word.

title: He wills that I should holy he
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
See, Lord, the travail of thy soul
Accomplish'd in the change of mine;
And plunge me, every whit made whole,
In all the depths of love divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
On thee, O God, my soul is stay'd,
And waits to prove thhie utmost will;
The promise, by thy mercy made,
Thou canst, thou wilt, in me fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No more I stagger at thy power,
Or doubt thy truth, which cannot move
Hasten the long-expected hour,
And bless me with thy perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, thy loving Spirit alone
Can lead me forth, and make me free;
Burst every bond through which I groan,
And set my heart at liberty.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Now let thy Spirit bring me in;
And give thy servant to possess
The land of rest from inbred sin,
The land of perfect holiness.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
Come, Saviour, come, and make me whole
Entirely all my sins remove;
To perfect health restore my soul,
To perfect holiness and love.

title: Jesus, taj Lord, I cry to thee
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, taj Lord, I cry to thee
Against the spirit unclean:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
want a constant liberty
A perfect rest from sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Expel the fiend out of my heart,
By love's almighty power;
Now, now command him to depart,
And never enter more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy killing and thy quick'ning power,
Jesus, in me display;
The life of nature from this hour,
My pride and passion, slay.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then, then, my utmost Saviour, raise
My soul, with saints above,
To serve thy will, and spread thy praise,
And sing thy perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
This moment I thy truth confess;
This moment I receive
The heavenly gift, the dew of grace,
And by thy mercy live.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The next, and every moment, Lord,
On me thy Spirit pour;
And bless me, who believe thy word,
With that last glorious shower.

title: P'ather, I dare believe
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
P'ather, I dare believe
Thee merciful and true:
Thou wilt my guilty soul forgive,
My fallen soul renew.
Come, then, for Jesu's sake,
And bid my heart be clean;
An end of all my troubles make,
An end of all my sin.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I will, through grace, I will,
I do, return to thee;
Take, empty it, O Lord, and fill
My heart with purity!
For power I feebly pray:
Thy kingdom now restore,
To-day, while it is call'd to-day,
And I shall sin no more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I cannot wash my heart,
But by believing thee,
And waiting for thy blood to' impart
The spotless purity:
While at thy cross I lie,
Jesus, thy grace bestow,
Now thy all-cleansing blood apply,
And I am white as snow.

title: Why not now, my God, my God
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why not now, my God, my God!
Ready if thou always art,
Make in me thy mean abode,
Take possession of my heart:
If thou canst so greatly bow,
Friend of sinners, why not now?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God of love, in this my day,
For thyself to thee 1 cry;
Dying, —if thou still delay,
Must I not for ever die?
Enter now thy poorest home,
Now, my utmost Saviour, come!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text: o

title: Kings xviii
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Kings xviii.
God that answerest by fire,

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Bound on the altar of thy cross,
Our old offending nature lies;
Now, for the honour of thy cause,
Come, and consume the sacrifice!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Consume our lusts as rotten wood;
Consume our stony hearts within!
Consume the dust, the serpent's food,
And dry up all the streams of sin.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Its body totally destroy!
Thyself Tlie Lord, The God, approve 1
And fill our hearts with holy joy,
And fervent zeal, and perfect love,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O that the fire from heaven might fall
Our sins its ready victims find,
Seize on our sins, and born up all,
Nor leave the least remains behind!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Then shall our prostrate souls adore,
TJie Lord, lie is the God, confess:
He is the God of saving power!
He is the God of hallowing grace!

title: God, who didst so greatly stoop
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God, who didst so greatly stoop
To a poor virgin's wonib,
Here thy mean abode take up;
To me, my Saviour, come!
Come, and Satan's works destroy,
And let me all thy Godhead prove,
Fill'd with peace and heavenly joy,
And pure eternal love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Then my soul with strange delight,
Shall comprehend and feel
What the length, and breadth, and height
Of love unspeakable;
Then I shall the secret know,
Which angels would search out in vain; —
God was man, and served below,
That man with God might reign!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Spirit, come,
And with thine own abide:
Holy Ghost, to make thee room,
Our hearts we open wide;
Thee, and only thee request,
To every asking sinner given;
Come, our life, and peace, and rest,
Our all in earth and heaven.

title: Now, even now I yield, I yield
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: Jesus hath died that I might live
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus hath died that I might live,
Might live to God alone;
In him eternal life receive,
And be in spirit one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Saviour, I thank thee for the grace,
The gift unspeakable!
And wait with arms of faith to' embrace,
And all thy love to feel.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My soul breaks out in strong desire
The perfect bliss to prove;
My longing heart is all on fire
To be dissolved in love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give me thyself; from every boast,
From every wish set free:
Let all I am in thee be lost;
But give thyself to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy gifts, alas, cannot suffice,
Unless thyself be given;
Thy presence makes my paradise,
And where thou art is heaven!

title: I ask the blood-bought pardon seal'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I ask the blood-bought pardon seal'd,
The liberty from sin,
The grace infused, the love reveal'd,
The kingdom fix'd within.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
My vehement soul cries out opprest,
Impatient to be freed;
Nor can I, Lord, nor will I rest,
Till I am saved indeed.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Art thou not able to convert?
Art thou not willing too?
To change this old rebellious heart,
To conquer and renew?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou canst, thou wilt, I dare believe,
So arm me with thy power,
That I to sin shall never cleave,
Shall never feel it more.

title: Come, O my God, the promise seal
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, O my God, the promise seal,
This mountain, sin, remove:
Now in my gasping soul reveal
The virtue of thy love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I want thy life, thy purity,
Thy righteousness, brought in
J ask, desire, and trust in thee,
To be redeem'd from sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Anger and sloth, desire and pride,
This moment be subdued;
Be cast into the crimson tide
Of my Redeemer's blood.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Saviour, to thee my soul looks upT
My present Saviour thou!
In all the confidence of hope,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
claim the blessing now.
6 'Tis done: thou dost this moment save,
With full salvation bless;
Redemption through thy blood I have,
And spotless love and peace.

title: God, who didst so dearly buy
author: Weslet J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God, who didst so dearly buy
These wretched souls of ours,
Help us thee to glorify
With all our ransom'd powers:
Ours they are not, Lord, but thine:
O let the vessels of thy grace,
Body, soul, and spirit, join
In our Redeemer's praise!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
True and faithful witness, thee,
O Jesus, we receive;
Fulness of the Deity,
In all thy people live!
First-begotten from the dead,
Call forth thy living witnesses;
King of saints, thine empire spread
O'er all the ransom'd race.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Grace, the fountain of all good,
Ye happy saints, receive,
With the streams of peace o'erflow'd.
With all that God can give;
He who is, and was, in peace,
And grace, and plenitude of power,
Comes, your favour'd souls to bless,
And never leave you more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let the Spirit before his throne,
Mysterious One and Seven,
In his various gifts sent down,
Be to the churches given;
Let the pure seraphic joy
From Jesus Christ, the Just, descend;
Holiness without alloy,
And bliss that ne'er shall end.

title: Quicken'd with our immortal Head
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Quicken'd with our immortal Head,
Who daily, Lord, ascend with thee,
Redeem'd from sin, and free indeed,
We taste our glorious liberty.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Saved from the fear of hell and death,
With joy we seek the things above;
And all thy saints the spirit breathe
Of power, sobriety, and love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Power o'er the world, the fiend, and sin,
We through thy gracious Spirit feel;
Full power the victory to win,
And answer all thy righteous will

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Pure love to God thy members find,
Pure love to every soul of man;
And in thy sober, spotless mind,
Saviour, our heaven on earth we gain.

title: Ye faithful souls, who Jesus know
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye faithful souls, who Jesus know,
I If risen indeed with him ye are,
Superior to the joys below,
His resurrection's power declare.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Your faith by holy tempers prove,
By actions show your sins forgiven!
And seek the glorious things above,
And follow Christ, your head, to heaven,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There your exalted Saviour see,
Seated at God's right hand again,
In all his Father's majesty,
In everlasting pomp, to reign,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To him continually aspire,
Contending for your native place
And emulate the angel-choir,
And only live to love and praise.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Your real life, with Christ conceal'd,
Deep in the Father's bosom lies;
And, glorious as your Head reveal''!.
Ye soon shall meet him in the skies.

title: I the good fight have fought,"
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I the good fight have fought,"
O when shall I declare?
The victory hy my Saviour got,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
long with Paul to share.
O may I triumph so,
When all my warfare's past;
And, dying, find my latest foe
Under my feet at last!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This blessed word he mine,
Just as the port is gain'd,
"Kept by the power of grace divine,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
have the faith maintain'd."
The' Apostles of my Lord,
To whom it first was given,
They could not speak a greater word,
Nor all the saints in heaven.

title: Let not the wise his wisdom boast
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
glory in his sprinkled blood.
The Lord my Righteousness I praise;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
triumph in the love divine,
The wisdom, wealth, and strength of grace,
In Christ to endless ages mine.

title: Who can worthily commend
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Who can worthily commend
Thy love unsearchable!
Love that made thee condescend
Our curse and death to feel:
Thou, the great, eternal God,
Who didst thyself our ransom pay,
Hast, with thine own precious blood,
Wash'd all our sins away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By the Spirit of our Head
Anointed priests and kings,
Conquerors of the world, we tread
On all created things;
Sit in heavenly places down,
While yet we in the flesh remain:
Now, partakers of thy throne,
Before thy Father reign.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, let thy kingdom come,
(Inspired by thee we pray,)
Previous to the general doom,
The everlasting day:
Take possession of thine own,
And let us then our Saviour see
Glorious on thy heavenly throne
To all eternity.

title: Us, who climb thy holy hill
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Us, who climb thy holy hill,
vJ A general blessing make:
Let the world our influence feel,
Our gospel grace partake:
Grace, to help in time of need,
Pour out on sinners from above;
All thy Spirit's fulness shed,
In showers of heavenly love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Make our earthly souls a field
Which God delights to bless;
Let us in due season yield
The fruits of righteousness:
Make us trees of paradise,
Which more and more thy praise may show,
Deeper sink, and higher rise,
And to perfection grow.

title: The voice that speaks Jehovah near
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The voice that speaks Jehovah near,
The still small voice I long to hear;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
may it now my Lord proclaim,
And fill my soul with holy shame!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ashamed I must for ever be,
Afraid the God of love to see,
If saints and prophets hide their face,
And angels tremble while they gaze!

title: Lord, in the strength of grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, in the strength of grace,
JLi With a glad heart and free,
Myself, my residue of days,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
consecrate to thee.
2 Thy ransom'd servant, I
Kestore to thee thine own;
And, from this moment, live or die
To serve my God alone.

title: God of all-redeeming grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of all-redeeming grace,
By thy pardoning love compell'd,
Up to thee our souls we raise,
Up to thee our bodies yield:
Thou our sacrifice receive,
Acceptable through thy Son,
While to thee alone we live,
While we die to thee alone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Meet it is, and just, and right,
That we should be wholly thine,
In thy only will delight,
In thy blessed service join:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
that every work and word
Might proclaim how good thou art;
"Holiness unto the Lord "
Still be written on our heart.

title: Let Him to whom we now belong
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let Him to whom we now belong
His sovereign right assert,
And take up every thankful song,
And every loving heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He justly claims us for his own,
Who bought us with a price;
The Christian lives to Christ alone,
To Christ alone he dies!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, thine own at last receive,
Fulfil our hearts' desire,
And let us to thy glory live,
And in thy cause expire.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our souls and bodies we resign;
With joy we render thee
Our all, no longer ours, but thine
To all eternity.
