title: Behold the servant of the Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold the servant of the Lord!
J) I wait thy guiding eye to feel,
To hear and keep thy every word,
To prove and do thy perfect will;
Joyful from my own works to ouase,
Glad to fulfil all righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
My every weak, though good design,
O'er-rule, or change, as seems thee meet
Jesus, let all my work be thine!
Thy work, O Lord, is all complete,
And pleasing in thy Father's sight;
Thou only hast done all things right.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Father, Son, and Holy Ghost
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
One in Three, and Three in One,
As by the celestial host,
Let thy will on earth be done;
Praise by all to thee be given,
Glorious Lord of earth and heaven!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Vilest of the sinful race,
Lo! I answer to thy call;
Meanest vessel of thy grace,
Grace divinely free for all,
Lo! I corne to do thy will,
All thy counsel to fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If so poor a worm as I
May to thy great glory live,
All my actions sanctify,
All my words and thoughts receive;
Claim me for thy service, claim
All I have, and all I am.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Now, O God, thine own I am;
Now I give thee back thine own,
Freedom, friends, and health, and fame
Consecrate to thee alone:
Thine I live, thrice happy
Happier still if thine I die.
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
One in Three, and Three in One,
As by the celestial host,
Let thy will on earth be done
Praise by all to thee be given,
Glorious Lord of earth and heaven!

title: O God, what offering shall I give
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
O never in these veils of shame,
Sad fruits of sin, my glorying be!
Clothe with salvation, through thy name,
My soul, and let me put on thee!
Be living faith my costly dress,
And mv best robe thy righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Send down thy likeness from above,
And let this my adorning be;
Clothe me with wisdom, patience, love,
With lowliness and purity,
Than gold and pearls more precious far,
And brighter than the morning star.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Father, into thy hands alone
author: Eslet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, into thy hands alone
I I have my whole restored;
My all, thy property I own,
The steward of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hereafter, none can take away
My life, or goods, or fame;
Ready at thy demand to lay
Them down I always am.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Confiding in thy only love,
Through Jesus strength'ning me,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
wait thy faithfulness to prove,
And give back all to thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Take when thou wilt into thine hands,
And as thou wilt require;
Resume by the Chaldean bands,
Or the devouring fire.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text: praise thee evermore 1

title: Give me the faith which can remove
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
I want an even, strong desire,
I want a calmly-fervent zeal,
To save poor souls out of the fire,
To snatch them from the verge of hell,
And turn them to a pardoning God,
And quench the brands in Jesu's blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I would the precious time redeem,
And longer live for this alone,
To spend, and to be spent, for them
Who have not yet my Saviour known;
Fully on these my mission prove,
And only breathe, to breathe thy love.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Enlarge, inflame, and fill my heart
With boundless charity divine!
So shall I all my strength exert,
And love them with a zeal like thine 5
And lead them to thy open side,
The sheep for whom their Shepherd died
2o

title: Jesus, all-atoning Lamb
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Fairer than the sons of men,
Do not let me turn again,
Leave the fountain-head of bliss,
Stoop to creature-happiness.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Whom have I on earth below?
Thee, and only Thee I know;
Whom have I in heaven but Thee?
Thou art all in all to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
All my treasure is above;
All my riches is thy love:
Who the worth of love can tell?
Infinite, unsearchable!
o Thou, O love, my portion art:
Lord, thou know'st my simple heart?
Other comforts I despise;
Love be all my paradise.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Father, to thee my soul I lift
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, to thee my soul I lift;
My soul on thee depends,
Convinced that every perfect gift
From thee alone descends.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Mercy and grace are thine alcne,
And power and wisdom too;
Without the Spirit of thy Son,
We nothing good can do.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We cannot speak one useful word,
One holy thought conceive,
Unless, in answer to our Lord,
Thyself the blessing give.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His blood demands the purchased grace:
His blood's availing plea
Obtain'd the help for all out race,
And sends it down to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou all our works in us hast wrought
Our good is all divine;
The praise of every virtuous thought,
And righteous word, is thine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
From thee, through Jesus, we receive
The power on thee to call,
In whom we are, and move, and live;
Our God is all in all I

title: Jesu, my Truth, my Way
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, my Truth, my Way,
My sure, unerring Light,
On thee my feeble steps I stay,
Which thou wilt guide aright.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Wisdom and my Guide,
My Counsellor thou art;
O never let me leave thy side.
O from thy paths depart I

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I lift my eyes to thee,
Thou gracious, bleeding Lamb,
That I may now enlighten'd be,
And never put to shame.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Never will I remove
Out of thy hands my cause
But rest in thy redeeming love,
And hang upon thy cross.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Teach me the happy art
In all things to depend
On thee; O never, Lord, depart,
But love me to the end!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Still stir me up to strive
With thee in strength divine;
And every moment, Lord, revive
This fainting soul of mine.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Persist to save my soul
Throughout the fiery hour.
Till I am every whit made whole,
And show forth all thy power.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Through fire and water bring
Into the wealthy place;
And teach me the new song to sing.
When perfected in grace!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
O make me all like thee,
Before I hence remove!
Settle, confirm, and 'stablish me,
And build me up in love.
SO Let me thy witness live,
When sin is all destroy'd:
And then my spotless soul receive,
And take me home to God.

title: O God, my God, my all thou art
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, my God, my all thou art!
Ere shines the dawn of rising da;,
Thy sovereign light within my heart,
Thy all-enlivening power display.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For thee my thirsty soul doth pant,
While in this desert land I live;
And hungry as I am, and faint,
Thy love alone can comfort give.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In a dry land, "behold I place
My whole desire on thee, O Lord;
And more I joy to gain thy grace,
Than all earth's treasures can afford.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
More dear than life itself, thy Love
My heart and tongue shall still employ;
And to declare thy praise will prove
My peace, my glory, and my joy.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In blessing thee with grateful songs
My happy life shall glide away:
The praise that to thy name belongs
Hourly with lifted hands I'll pay.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Abundant sweetness, while I sing
Thy love, my ravish'd heart o'erflows;
Secure in thee, my God and King,
Of glory that no period knows.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
muse on all thy hands have wrought.
8 In all I do, I feel thine aid;
Therefore thy greatness will I sing,
O God, thou bidd'st my heart be glad,
Beneath the shadow of thy wing I

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
My soul draws nigh and cleaves to thee:
Then let or earth or hell assail,
Thy rnigbty hand shall set me free;
For whom thou sav'st, he ne'er shall fail.

title: O God of peace and pardoning love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
O might our every work and word
Express the tempers of our Lord,
The nature of our Head above:
His Spirit send into our hearts,
Engraving on our inmost parts
The living law of holiest love.
Then shall we do, with pure delight,
Whate'er is pleasing in thy sight,
As vessels of thy richest grace;
And, having thy whole counsel clone,
To thee and thy co-equal Son
Ascribe the everlasting praise.

title: Thy power and saving truth to show
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy power and saving truth to show,
X A warfare at thy charge I go,
Strong in the Lord, and thy great might;
Gladly take up the ballow'd cross;
And, suffering all things for thy cause,
Beneath thy bloody banner fight.
A spectacle to fiends and men,
To all their fierce and cool disdain
With calmest pity I submit:
Determined nought to know, beside
My Jesus and him crucified,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
tread the world beneath my feet.
Superior to their smile or frown,
On all their goods my soul looks down,
Their pleasures, wealth, and power, and state
The man that dares their god despise,
The Christian, —he alone is wise;
The Christian, he alone is great.
O God, let all my life declare
How happy all thy servants are;
How far above these earthly things;
How pure, when wash'd in Jesu's blood;
How intimately one with God,
A heaven-born race of Priests and Kings.
For this alone I live below,
The power of godliness to show,
The wonders wrought by Jesu's name.
O that I might but faithful prove;
Witness to all thy pardoning love,
And point them to the' atoning Lamb!
Let me to every creature cry,
The poor and rich, the low and high,
"Believe, and feel thy sins forgiven J
Damn'd, till by Jesus saved, thou art!
Till Jesu's blood hath wash'd thy heart,
Thou can'st not find the gate of heaven?*

title: Thou, Jesu, thou my breast inspire
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: Let God, who comforts the distrest
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let God, who comforts the distrest,
Let Israel's Consolation hear!
Hear, Holy Ghost, our joint request,
And show thyself the Comforter;
And swell the' unutterable groan,
And breathe our wishes to the throne t
We weep for those that weep below,
And burden' d for the' afflicted, sigh;
The various forms of human woe
Excite our softest sympathy,
Fill every heart with mournful care,
And draw out all our souls in pray or.
We wrestle for the ruin'd race,
By sin eternally undone, —
Unless thou magnify thy grace,
And make thy richest mercy known,
And make thy vanquish'd rebels find
Pardon in Christ for all mankind.
Father of everlasting love,
To every soul thy Son reveal,
Our guilt and sufferings to remove,
Our deep, original wound to heal
And bid the fallen race arise,
And turn our earth to Paradise.

title: Our earth we now lament to see
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our earth we now lament to see
With floods of wickedness o'erflow'd,
With violence, wrong, and cruelty, —
One wide-extended field of blood,
Where men like fiends each other tear,
In all the hellish rage of war.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As 'listed on Abaddon's side,
They mangle their own flesh, and slay:
Tophet is moved, and opens wide
Its mouth for its enormous prey;
And myriads sink beneath the grave,
And plunge into the flaming wave.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Who now against each other rise,
The nations of the earth, constrain
To follow after peace, and prize
The blessings of thy righteous reign,
The joys of unity to prove,
The paradise of perfect love!

title: Sun of unclouded Righteousness
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sun of unclouded Righteousness,
With healing in thy wings arise,
A sad benighted world to bless,
Which now in sin and error lies,
Wrapt in Egyptian night profound;
With chains of hellish darkness bound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The smoke of the infernal cave,
Which half the Christian world o'erspread,
Disperse, thou heavenly Light, and save
The souls by that Impostor led,
That Arab-thief, as Satan bold,
Who quite destroy'd thy Asian fold.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O might the blood of sprinkling cry
For those who spurn the sprinkled blood!
Assert thy glorious Deity,
Stretch out thine arm, thou triune God!
The Unitarian fiend expel,
And chase his doctrine back to hell.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Thou Three in One, and One in Three *
Resume thy own, for ages lost,
Finish the dire apostasy;
Thy universal claim maintain,
And liOrd of the creation reign I

title: Lord over all, if thou hast made
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord over all, if thou hast made,
Hast ransom'd every soul of man,—
Why is the grace so long delay'd?
Why unfulfill'd the saving plan?
The bliss, for Adam's race design'd,
When will it reach to all mankind?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: O come, thou radiant Morning-Star
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O come, thou radiant Morning-Star
Again in human darkness shine I
Arise resplendent from afar!
Assert thy royalty divine!
Thy sway o'er all the earth maintain,
And now begin thy glorious reign.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy kingdom, Lord, we long to see:
Thy sceptre o'er the nations shake!
To' erect that final monarchy,
Edom for thy possession take;
Take (for thou didst their ransom find)
The purchased souls of all mankind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Now let thy chosen ones appear,
And valiantly the truth maintain!
Dispread thy gracious kingdom here;
Fly on the rebel sons of men!
Seize them with faith divinely bold,
And draw the world into thy fold!

title: Jesu, the word of mercy give
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, the word of mercy give,
And let it swiftly run;
And let the priests themselves believe,
And put salvation on.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Clothed with the Spirit of Holiness,
May all thy people prove
The plentitude of gospel grace,
The joy of perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, let all thy lovers shine
Illustrious as the sun;
And, bright with borrow' d rays divine,
Their glorious circuit run:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Beyond the reach of mortals spread
Their light where'er they go;
And heavenly influences shed
On all the world below.
As giants may they run their race,
Exulting in their might;
As burning luminaries, chase
The gloom of hellish night.
As the bright Sun of Righteousness,
Their healing wings display;
And let their lustre still increase
Unto the perfect day.

title: Messiah, Prince of Peace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Messiah, Prince of Peace!
Where men each other tear,
Where war is learn'd they must confess,
Thy kingdom is not there.
Who prompted by thy foe,
Delight in human blood,
Apollyon is their king, we know,
And Satan is their god.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But shall he still devour
The souls redeem' d by thee?
Jesus stir up thy glorious power,
And end the' apostapy!
Come, Saviour, from above,
O'er all our hearts to reign;
And plant the kingdom of thy love
In every heart of man!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then shall we exercise
The hellish art no more,
While thou our long-lost paradise
Dost with thyself restore.
Fightings and wars shall cease,
And in thy Spirit given,
Pure joy and everlasting peace
Shall turn our earth to heaven.

title: Prince of universal peace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
But if thou pronounce the word
That forms our souls again,
Love and harmony restored
Throughout our earth shall reign;
When thy wondrous love they feel,
The human savages are tame;
Ravenous wolves and leopards dwell
And stable with the lamb.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Happy day of union sweet
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy day of union sweet!
O when shall it appear!
When shall all thy people meet
In amity sincere!
Tear each other's flesh no more,
But kindly think and speak the same
All express the meekening power
And spirit of the Lamb!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Visit us, bright Morning Star,
And bring the perfect day!
Urged by faith's incessant prayer,
No longer, Lord, delay:
Now destroy the envious root;
The ground of nature's feuds remove;
Fill the earth with golden fruit,
With ripe, millennial love.

title: Messiah, full of grace
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Messiah, full of grace,
Redeem'd by thee, we plead,
The promise made to Abraham's race,
To souls for ages dead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Their bones, as quite dried up,
Throughout the vale appear:
Cut off and lost their last faint hope
To see thy kingdom here.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Open their graves, and bring
The outcasts forth, to own
Thou art their Lord, their God, their King,
Their true Anointed One.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To save the race forlorn,
Thy glorious arm display!
And show the world a nation born,
A nation in a day!

title: Fatherof faithful Abraham, hear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fatherof faithful Abraham, hear
Our earnest suit for Abraham's seed I
Justly they claim the softest prayer
From us, adopted in their stead,
Who mercy through their fall obtain,
And Christ by their rejection gain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Outcasts from thee, and scatter'd wide
Through every nation under heaven,
Blaspheming whom they crucified,
Unsaved, unpitied, unforgiven;
Branded like Cain, they bear their load,
Abhorr'd of men, and cursed of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But hast thou finally forsook,
For ever cast thy own away?
Wilt thou not bid the murd'rers look
On him they pierced, and weep, and pray?
Yes, gracious Lord, thy word is past;
All Israel shall be saved at last.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, then, thou great Deliverer, come!
The veil from Jacob's heart remove;
Receive thy ancient people home!
That, quicken'd by thy dying love,
The world may their reception find
Life from the dead for all mankind.

title: God of Love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of Love,
Set up the' attracting sign,
And summon whom thou dost approve
For messengers divine:
From favour'd Abraham's seed
The new Apostles choose,
In isles and continents to spread
The dead-reviving news.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Them snatch'd out of the flame,
Through every nation send,
The true Messiah to proclaim,
The universal Friend;
That all the God unknown
May leam of Jews to' adore,
A.nd see thy glory in thy Son,
Till time snail be no more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O that the chosen hand
Might now their brethren bring,
And, gather'd out of every land,
Present to Sion's King 1
Of all the ancient race,
Not one be left behind;
But each, impell'd by secret grace,
His way to Canaan find.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We know it must be done,
For God hath spoke the word;
All Israel shall the Saviour own,
To their first state restored:
Rebuilt by his command,
Jerusalem shall rise;
Her temple on Moriah stand
Again, and touch the skies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Send then thy servants forth,
To call the Hebrews home;
From East, and West, and South, and North,
Let all the wanderers come:
Where'er in lands unknown
The fugitives remain,
Bid every creature help them on,
Thy Holy Mount to gain.
G An offering to their Lord,
There let them all be seen,
Sprinkled with water and with blood,
In soul and body clean.
With Israel's myriads seal'd,
Let all the nations meet,
And show the mystery fulfill'd
Thy family complete!
2e
'S

title: Enter into the Rock

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Enter into the Rock,
Ye trembling slaves of sin,
The Rock of your salvation, struck
And cleft to take you in:
To shelter the distrest,
He did the cross endure;
Enter into the clefts, and rest
In Jesu's wounds secure.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, to thee we fly
From the devouring sword;
Our city of defence is nigh;
Our help is in the Lord.
—Or, if the scourge o'erflow,
And laugh at innocence,
Thine everlasting arms, we know,
Shall be our souls' defence.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We in thy word believe,
And on thy promise stay;
Our life, which still to thee we give,
Shall be to us a prey:
Oar life with thee we hide,
Above the furious blast,
And shelter'd in thy wounds abide,
Till all the storms are past.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Believing against hope,
We hang upon thy grace,
Through every lowering cloud look up,
And wait for happy days;
The days when all shall know
Their sins in Christ forgiven,
And walk awhile with God helow,
And then fly up to heaven.

title: God of unspotted purity
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of unspotted purity,
VJT Us and our works canst thou behold!
Justly we are abhorr'd by thee,
For we are neither hot nor cold.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We call thee Lord, thy faith profess,
But do not from our hearts obey;
In soft Laodicean ease
We sleep our useless lives away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We live in pleasure, and are dead,
In search of fame and wealth we live:
Commanded in thy steps to tread,
We seek sometimes, but never strive.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
How long, great God, have we appear'd
Abominable in thy sight!
Better that we had never heard
Thy word, or seen the gospel light.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Better that we had never known
The way to heaven through saving grace,
Than hasely in our lives disown,
And slight and mock thee to thy face.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Thou rather would'st that we were cold,
Than seem to serve thee without zeal;
Less guilty if, with those of old,
We worshipp'd TJwr and Woden still.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Less grievous will the judgment-day
To /Sodom and Gomorrah prove,
Than us, who cast our faith away,
And trample on thy richer love.

title: O let us our own works forsake
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O let us our own works forsake,
Ourselves, and all we have deny;
Thy condescending counsel take,
And come to thee, pure gold to buy.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O might we, through thy grace, attain
The faith thou never wilt reprove;
The faith that purges every stain,
The faith that always works by love!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O might we see, in this our day,
The things belonging to our peace,
And timely meet thee in thy way
Of judgments, and our sins confess!

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Father, if justly still we claim
author: Dr   H   Moore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, if justly still we claim
To us and ours the promise made,
To us be graciously the same,
And crown with living fire our head.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our claim admit, and from above
Of holiness the Spirit shower,
Of wise descernment, humble love,
And zeal, and unity, and power.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Spirit of convincing speech,
Of power demonstrative, impart;
Such as may every conscience reach,
And sound the unbelieving heart:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The Spirit of refining fire,
Searching the inmost of the mind,
To purge all fierce and foul desire,
And kindle life more pure and kind:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Spirit of faith, in this thy day,
To break the power of cancell'd sin;
Tread down its strength, o'erturn its sway,
And still the conquest more than win.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: On all the earth thy Spirit shower
author: Dr   H   Moore

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Like mighty winds, or torrents fierce,
Let it opposers all overrun;
And every law of sin reverse,
That faith and love may make all one.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yea, let thy Spirit hi every place
Its richer energy declare;
While lovely tempers, fruits of grace,
The kingdom of thy Christ prepare.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Author of faith, we seek thy face
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Author of faith, we seek thy face
For all who feel thy work begun;
Confirm and strengthen them in grace,
And bring thy feeblest children on.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou seest their wants, thou know'st their
names,
Be mindful of thy youngest care;
Be tender of thy new-born lambs,
And gently hi thy bosom bear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The lion roaring for his prey,
With ravening wolves on every side,
Watch over them to tear and slay,
If found one moment from their guide.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Satan his thousand arts essays,
His agents all their powers employ,
To blast the blooming work of grace,
The heavenly offspring to destroy.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Baffle tbe crooked Serpent's skill,
And turn his sharpest dart aside;
Hide from their eyes the devilish ill,
O save them from the demon, Pride!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
In safety lead thy little flock,
From'hell, the' world, and sin secure;
And set their feet upon the Rock,
And make in thee their goings sure.

title: Shepherd of Israel, hear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Shepherd of Israel, hear
Our supplicating cry;
And gather in the souls sincere,
That from their brethren fly.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Scatter' d through devious ways,
Collect thy feeble flock;
And join by thine atoning grace,
And hide them in the Rock.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O would'st thou end the storm,
That keeps us still apart 1
The thing impossible perform,
And make us of one heart,- —

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
One spirit and one mind,
The same that was in thee:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
might we all again be join'd
In perfect harmony!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Jesus, at thy command,
We know it shall be done;
Take the two sticks into thy hand,
The two shall then be one.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
One body and one fold,
We then shall sweetly prove,
And live in thee, like them of old,
The life of spotless love.

title: God of all power and grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of all power and grace,
Set up thy bloody sign;
And gather those that seek thy face,
And by thy Spirit join.
The few remaining sheep,
In Britain's pastures bred,
United to each other keep,
United to their Head.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The soul-transforming word
In us, even us, fulfil;
Join to thyself, our common Lord,
And all thy servants seal.
Confer the grace unknown,
The mystic charity;
As thou art with the Father One,
Unite us all in thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So shall the world believe
Our record, Lord, and thine;
And all with thankful hearts receive
The Messenger divine,
Sent from his throne above,
To Adam's offspring given,
To join and perfect us in love,
And take us up to heaven.

title: Jesus, to thee we humbly cry
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Beguiled, alas! by Satan's art,
We see them now far off removed,
The burden of our bleeding heart,
The souls whom once in thee we loved;
Whom still we love with grief and pain,
And weep for their return in vain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In vain, till thou the power bestow,
The double power of quick'ning grace,
And make the happy sinners know
Their Tempter, with his angel-face,
Who leads them captive at his will,
Captive, but happy sinners still!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O would'st thou break the fatal snare
Of carnal self-security;
And let them feel the wrath they bear,
And let them groan their want of thee.,
Robb'd of their false, pernicious peace,
Stiipp'd of their fancied righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The men of careless lives, who deem
Thy righteousness accounted theirs,
Awake out of the soothing dream;
Alarm their souls with humble fears:
Thou jealous God, stir up thy power,
And let them sleep in sin no more!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Long as the guilt of sin shall last,
Them in its misery detain;
Hold their licentious spirits fast,
Bind them with their own nature's chain,
Nor ever let the wand'rers rest, —
Till lodged again in Jesu's breast.

title: O let the prisoners' mournful cries
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O let the prisoners' mournful cries
As incense in thy sight appear!
Their humble wailings pierce the skies,
If haply they may feel thee near.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The captive exiles make their moans,
From sin impatient to be free:
Call home, call home thy banished ones,
Lead captive their captivity!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Show them the blood that bought their peace,
The anchor of their steadfast hope;
And bid their guilty terrors cease,
And bring the ransom'd prisoners up.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Out of the deep regard their cries,
The fallen raise, the mourners cheer;
O Sun of Eighteousness, arise,
And scatter all their doubt and fear!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Pity the day of feeble things;
O gather every halting soul.'
And drop salvation from thy wings,
And make the contrite sinner whole.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Stand by them in the fiery hour,
Their feebleness of mind defend;
And in their weakness show thy power,
And make them patient to the end.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O satisfy their soul in drought!
Give them thy saving health to see:
And let thy mercy find them out;
And let thy mercy reach to me.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Hast thou the work of grace begun,
And brought them to the birth, in vain?

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
let thy children see the sun!
Let all their souls be born again!

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Relieve the souls whose cross we bear,
For whom thy suff 'ring members mourn:
Answer our faith's effectual prayer;
Bid every struggling child be born!

title: Lamb of God, who bear'st away
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lamb of God, who bear'st away
All the sins of all mankind,
Bow a nation to thy sway; —
While we may acceptance find,
Let us thankfully embrace
The last offers of thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou thy messengers hast sent,
Joyful tidings to proclaim,
Willing we should all repent,
Know salvation in thy name,
Feel our sins by grace forgiven,
Find in thee the way to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: the Spirit of grace o'erflow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
the Spirit of grace o'erflow
Our re- converted land:
Let the least and greatest know
And bow to thy command:
Wisdom, pure religious fear,
Our King's peculiar treasure prove,
Blest with piety sincere,
Inspired with humble love.
c. Wesley.] HYMN 465 cm. (6)
For the King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
SOVEREIGN of all! whose will ordains
O The powers on earth that be,
By whom our rightful Monarch reigns,
Subject to none but thee

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Stir up thy power, appear, appear,
And for thy servant fight;
Support thy great vicegerent here,
And vindicate his right

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lo! in the arms of faith and prayer
We bear him to thy throne;
Receive thy own peculiar care,
The Lord's anointed one.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
With favour look upon his face;
Thy love's pavilion spread,
And watchful troops of angel's place
Around his sacred head.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Guard him from all who dare oppose
Thy delegate and thee;
From open and from secret foes,
From force and perfidy!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Confound whoe'er his ruin seek,
Or into friends convert:
Give him his adversaries' neck;
Give him his people's heart.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Let us, for concience' sake, revere
The man of thy right hand;
Honour and love thine image here,
And bless his mild command.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Thou only didst the blessing give;
The glory, Lord, be thine:
Let all with thankful joy receive
The benefit divine.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
To those, who thee in him obey,
The Spirit of grace impart:
His dear, his sacred burden lay
On every loyal heart.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Still let us pray and never cease,
"Defend him, Lord, defend:
'Stablish his throne in glorious peace,
And save him to the end I "
c. wesley.] HYMN 466 8's&6's. (18)
Job. xxxiv. 29.

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
A NATION God delights to bless,
jLJl. Can all our raging foes distress,
Or hurt whom they surround?
Hid from the general scourge we are,
Nor see the bloody waste of war,
Nor hear the trumpet's sound.

sections.label: Verse 13
sections.text:
O might we, Lord! the grace improve,
By labouring for the rest of love,
The soul-composing power!
Bless us with that internal peace.
And all the fruits of righteousness,
Till time shall be no more.

title: Father of all, by whom we are
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of all, by whom we are,
For whom was made whatever is
Who hast entrusted to our care
A candidate for glorious bliss:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Poor worms of earth, for help we cry,
For grace to guide what grace has given
"We ask for wisdom from on high,
To train our infant up for heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We tremble at the danger near,
And crowds of wretched parents see,
Who, blindly fond, their children rear
In tempers far as hell from thee:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Themselves the slaves of sense and praise.
Their babes who pamper and admire;
And make the helpless infants pass
To murderer Moloch through the fire.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O let us not the demon please;
Our offspring to destruction doom!
Strengthen a sin-sick soul's disease,
Or damn him from his mother's womb!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Eather this hour resume his breath,
From selfishness and pride to save;
By death prevent the second death,
And hide him in the silent grave!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Or, if thou grant a longer date,
With resolute wisdom us endue,
To point him out his lost estate,
His dire apostasy to show:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
To time our every smile or frown,
To mark the bounds of good and ill;
And beat the pride of nature down,
And bend or break his rising will.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Him let us tend, severely kind,
As guardians of his giddy youth
As set to form his tender mind,
By principles of virtuous truth.

sections.label: Verse 10

title: God only wise, almighty, good
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God only wise, almighty, good,
Send forth thy truth and light,
To point us out the narrow road,
And guide our steps aright:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To steer our dangerous course between
The rocks on either hand;
And fix us in the golden mean,
And bring our charge to land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Made apt, by thy sufficient grace,
To teach as taught by thee,
We come to train in all thy ways
Our rising progeny;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Their selfish will in time subdue,
And mortify their pride;
And lend their youth a sacred clew
To find the Crucified.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We would in every step look up;
By thy example taught
To' alarm their fear, excite their hope,
And rectify their thought.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
For this we ask, in faith sincere,
The wisdom from above,
To touch their hearts with filial fear,
And pure, ingenuous love:

sections.label: Verse 8

title: Father of Lights! thy needful aid
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of Lights! thy needful aid
To us that ask impart;
Mistrustful of ourselves, afraid
Of our own treacherous heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O'erwhelm'd with justest fear, again
To thee for help we call:
Where many mightier have been slain,
By thee unsaved, we fall.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Unless restrain'd by grace we are,
In vain the snare we see;
We see, and rush into the snare
Of blind idolatry.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We plunge ourselves in endless woes,
Our helpless infant sell;
Resist the light, and side with those
Who send their babes to hell.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ah! what avails superior light,
Without superior love?
We see the truth, we judge aright,
And wisdom's ways approve:

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
In spite of our resolves, we fear
Our own infirmity;
And tremble at the trial near,
And cry, O God, to thee!
% We soon shall do what we condemn,
And, down the torrent borne,
With shame confess our nature's stream.
Too strong for us to turn.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Our only help in danger's hour,
Our only strength, thou art!
Above the world, and Satan's power,
And greater than our heart!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Us from ourselves thou canst secure,
In nature's slippery ways;
And make our feeble footsteps sure,
By thy sufficient grace.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
If on thy promised grace alone
We faithfully depend,
Thou surely wilt preserve thy own,
And keep them to the end:

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Wilt make us tenderly discreet
To guard what thou hast given;
And bring our child with us to meet
At thy right hand in heaven.

title: After supreme, T look to thee
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
After supreme, T look to thee.
JJJl For grace and wisdom from abovo
Vested with thy authority,
Endue me with thy patient love,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That, taught according to thy will,
To rule my family aright,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
may the' appointed charge fulfil,
With all my heart, and all my might.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Inferiors, as a sacred trust,
I from the Sovereign Lord receive,
That what is suitable and just,
Impartial I to all may give:

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
The servant faithfully discreet,
Gentle to him, and good, and mild,
Him I would tenderly entreat,
And scarce distinguish from a child.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Yet let me not my place forsake,
The' occasion of his stumbling prove;
The servant to my bosom take,
Or mar him by familiar love.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
F
7 Order if some invert, confound,
Their Lord's authority betray, —

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
hearken to the gospel sound,
And trace the providential way.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
As far from abjectness as pride,
With condescending dignity,
Jesus, I make thy word my guide,
And keep the post assign'd by thee.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
O could I emulate the zeal
Thou dost to thy poor servants bear 1
The troubles, griefs, and burdens feel
Of souls entrusted to my care:

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
In daily prayer to God commend
The souls whom Christ expired to save
And think how soon my sway may end,
And all be equal in the grave!

title: How shall I walk my God to please
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How shall I walk my God to please,
JLjL And spread content and happiness
O'er all beneath my care?
A pattern to my household give,
And as a guardian angel live,
As Jesu's messenger?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The opposite extremes I see, —
Remissness and severity, —
And know not how to shun
The precipice on either hand,
While in the narrow path I stand,
And dread to venture on.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Shall I, through indolence supine.
Neglect, betray, my charge divine,
My delegated power?
The souls I from my Lord receive,
Of each I an account must give,
At that tremendous hour!
Lord over all, and God most high!
Jesus, to thee for help I fly,
For constant power and grace;
That, taught by thy good Spirit and led,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
may with confidence proceed,
And all thy footsteps trace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
teach me my first lesson now!
And, while to thy sweet yoke I bow,
Thy easy service prove,
Lowly and meek in heart, I see
The art of governing like thee
Is governing by love.

title: I and my house will serve the Lord
author: 3   Weslet J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I and my house will serve the Lord
But first obedient to his word

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
must myself appear;
By actions, words, and tempers show,
That I my heavenly Master know,
And serve with heart sincere.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Easy to be entreated, mild,
Quickly appeased and reconciled,
A follower of my God.
A saint indeed, I long to be,
And lead my faithful family
In the celestial road.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, if thou didst the wish infuse,
A vessel fitted for thy use
Into thy hands receive!
Work in me both to will and do;
And show them how believers true
And real Christians live.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
A sinner, saved myself from sin,
I come, my family to win,
To preach their sins forgiven,
Children, and wife, and servants seize,
And through the paths of pleasantness
Conduct them all to heaven.

title: Father, Son, and Holy Ghost
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Answer on them the end of all
Our cares, and pains, and studies here;
On them, recover'd from their fall,
Stamp'd with the humble character,
Raised by the nurture of the Lord,
To all their paradise restored.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Unite the pair so long disjoin'd,
Knowledge and vital Piety:
Learning and Holiness combined,
And Truth and Love let all men see,
In those whom up to thee we give,
Thine, wholly thine, to die and live.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Father, accept them through thy Son,
And ever by thy Spirit guide!
Thy wisdom in their lives be shown,
Thy name confess'd and glorified;
Thy power and love diffused abroad,
Till all the earth is fill'd with God.

title: /captain of our salvation, take
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
/captain of our salvation, take
The souls we here present to thee,
And fit for thy great service make
These heirs of immortality;
And let them in thine image rise,
And then transplant to Paradise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Unspotted from the world and pure,
Preserve them for thy glorious cause,
Accustom'd daily to endure
The welcome hurden of thy cross;
Inured to toil and patient pain,
Till all thy perfect mind they gam.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Train up thy hardy soldiers, Lord,
In all their Captain's steps to tread!
Or send them to proclaim thy word,
Thy gospel through the world to spread,
Freely as they receive to give,
And preach the death by which we live!

title: Mountains, alas! on mountains rise
author: Y J

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The things impossible to men
Thou canst for thine own people do:
Thy strength be in our weakness seen*
Thy wisdom in our folly show 1
Prevent, accompany, and bless,
And crown the whole with full success.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Unless the power of heavenly grace,
The wisdom of the Deity,
Direct and govern all our ways,
And all our works be wrought in thee,—
Our blasted works we know shall fail,
And earth and hell at last prevail.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Father, Son, and Holy Ghost
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Honour the means ordain'd by thee
Make good our apostolic boast,
And own thy glorious ministry.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We now thy promised presence claireu
Sent to disciple all mankind,
Sent to baptize into thy name,
We now thy promised presence find.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Father! in these reveal thy Son:
In these for whom ive seek thy face,
The hidden mystery make known,
The inward, pure, baptizing grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesns! with us thou always art:
Effectuate now the sacred sign:
The gift unspeakable impart,
And bless the ordinance divine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Eternal Spirit! descend from high,
Baptizer of our spirits thou!
The sacramental seal apply,
And witness with the water now '.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O that the souls baptized therein
May now thy truth and mercy feel;
May rise and wash away their sin!
Come, Holy Ghost, their pardon seal

title: Father, Son, and Holy Ghost
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
In solemn power come down!
Present with thy heavenly host,
Thine ordinance to crown:
See a sinful worm of earth;
Bless to him the cleansing flood!
Plunge him, by a second birth,
Into the depths of God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let the promised inward grace
Accompany the sign;
On his new-born soul impress
The character divine!
Father, all thy name reveal!
Jesus, all thy name impart!
Holy Ghost, renew and dwell
For ever in his heart!

title: What troubles have we seen
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What troubles have we seen,
What conflicts have we past,
Fightings without, and fears within,
Since we assembled last!
But out of all the Lord
Hath brought us by his love;
And still he doth his help afford,
And hides our life above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Then let us make our boast
Of his redeeming power,
Which saves us to the uttermost,
Till we can sin no more:
Let us take up the cross,
Till we the crown obtain;
And gladly reckon all things loss,
So we may Jesus gain.

title: Peace be on this house bestow'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Peace be on this house bestow'd,
Peace on all that here reside!
Let the unknown peace of God
With the man of peace abide.
Let the Spirit now come down;
Let the blessing now take place!
Son of Peace, receive thy crown,
Fulness of the gospel grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ, my Master and my Lord,
Let me thy forerunner be;

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Let us never, never rest,
Till the promise is fulfill'd;
Till we are of thee possess'd,
Pardon'd, sanctified, and seal'd;
Till we all, in love renew'd,
Find the pearl that Adam lost,
Temples of the living God,
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost!

title: Glory be to God above
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glory be to God above,
God from whom all blessings flow;
Make we mention of his love,
Publish we his praise below:
Call'd together by his grace,
We are met in Jesu's Name;
See with joy each other's face,
Followers of the bleeding Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let us then sweet counsel take,
How to make our calling sure;
Our election how to make
Past the reach of hell sec.ire.
Build we each the other up;
Pray we for our faith's increase,
Solid comfort, settled hope,
Constant joy, and lasting peace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
More and more let love abound:
Let us never, never rest,
Till we are in Jesus found,
Of our paradise possest:
He removes the flaming sword,
Calls us back from Eden driven j,
To his image here restored,
Soon he takes us up to heaven.

title: All thanks to the Lamb, Who gives us to
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All thanks to the Lamb, Who gives us to
J. meet:
His love we proclaim, His praises repeat:
We own him our Jesus, Continually near
To pardon and bless us, And perfect us here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In him we have peace, In him we have power,
Preserved by his grace, Throughout the dark
hour;
In all our temptation, He keeps us to prove
His utmost salvation, His fulness of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
When we would have spurn'd His mero»y and
grace,
To Egypt return'd, And fled from his face,
He hinder'd our flying, (His goodness to show,)
And stopp'd us by crying, "Will ye also go? "

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O what shall we do Our Saviour to love?
To make us anew, Come, Lord, from above!
The fruit of thy passion, Thy holiness, give:
Give us the salvation Of all that believe.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Come, Jesus, and loose The stammerer's
tongue,
And teach even us The spiritual song:
Let us without ceasing Give thanks for thy
grace, [praise.
And glory, and blessing, And honour, and

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Pronounce the glad word, And bid us be free:
Ah! hast thou not, Lord, A blessing for me?
The peace thou hast given This moment
impart,
And open thy heaven, O Love, in my heart.

title: Saviour of sinful men
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour of sinful men,
O Thy goodness we proclaim,
Which brings us here to meet again,
And triumph in thy name:
Thy mighty name hath been
Our safeguard and our tower;
Hath saved us from the world, and sin,
And all the' Accuser's power.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, take all the praise,
That still on earth we live,
Unspotted in so foul a place,
And innocently grieve!
We shall from Sodom flee,
When perfected in love;
And haste to better company,
Who wait for us above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Awhile in flesh disjoin'd,
Our friends that went before
We soon in paradise shall find,
And meet to part no morf*
In yon thrice happy seat,
Waiting for us they are;
And thou shalt there a husband meet!
And I a parent there!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O! what a mighty change
Shall Jesu's suff'rers know,
While o'er the happy plains they range,
Incapable of woe!
No ill-requited love
Shall there our spirits wound;
No base ingratitude above,
No sin in heaven is found.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There all our griefs are spent!
There all our sorrows end!
We cannot there the fall lament
Of a departed friend, —
A brother dead to God,
By sin, alas! undone: —
No father there, in passion loud,
Cries, "O my son, my son! "
No slightest touch of pain,
No sorrow's least alloy,
Can violate our rest, or stain
Our purity of joy:
In that eternal day
No clouds nor tempests rise:
There gushing tears are wiped away
For ever from our eyes.

title: Jesu, to thee our hearts we lift
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, to thee our hearts we lift,
O (May all our hearts with love o'erflow!"
With thanks for thy continued gift-
That still thy precious name we know,
Retain our sense of sin forgiven,
And wait for all our inward heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What mighty troubles hast thou shown
Thy feeble, tempted followers here!
We have through fire aud water gone,
But saw thee on the floods appear,
But felt thee present in the flame,
And shouted our Deliverer's name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When stronger souls their faith forsook,
And, lull'd in worldly, hellish peace,
Leap'd desperate from their Guardian-rock,
And headlong plunged in sin's abyss;
Thy strength was in our weakness shown,
And still it guards and keeps thine own.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou who hast kept us to this hour,
O keep us faithful to the end!
When, robed with majesty and power,
Our Jesus shall from heaven descend,
His friends and confessors to own,
And seat us on his glorious throne.

title: Appointed by thee, We meet in thy
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Appointed by thee, We meet in thy
f name,
And meekly agree To follow the Lamb,
To trace thy example, The world to disdain,
And constantly trample On pleasure and pain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Rejoicing in hope, We humbly go on,
And daily take up The pledge of our crown;
In doing and bearing the will of our Lord,
We still are preparing To meet our reward.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Jesus, appear! No longer delay
To sanctify here, And bear us away:
The end of our meeting On earth let us see,
Triumphantly sitting In glory with thee!

title: Jesu, we look to thee
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, we look to thee,
O Thy promised presence claim!
Thou in the midst of us shalt be,
Assembled in thy name:
Thy name salvation is,
Which here we come to prove;
Thy name is life, and health, and peace,
And everlasting love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not in the name of pride
Or selfishness we meet;
From nature's paths we turn aside,
And worldly thoughts forget.
We meet, the grace to take
Which thou hast freely given;
We meet on earth for thy dear sake,
That we may meet in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Present we know thou art;
But, O, thyself reveal!
Now, Lord, let every bounding heart
The mighty comfort feel!
O may thy quick'ning voice
The death of sin remove;
And bid our inmost souls rejoice
In hope of perfect love!

title: See, Jesus, thy disciples see
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See, Jesus, thy disciples see,
O The promised blessing give!
Met in thy name, we look to thee.
Expecting to receive.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thee we expect, our faithful Lord,
Who in thy name are join'd;
We wait, according to thy word,
Thee in the midst to find.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With us thou art assemhled here;
But, O, thyself reveal!
Son of the living God, appear!
Let us thy presence feel.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Breathe on us, Lord, in this our day,
And these dry bones shall live;
Speak peace into our hearts, and say,
"The Holy Ghost receive! "

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Whom now we seek, O may we meet!
Jesus, the Crucified,
Show ns thy bleeding hands and feet,
Thou who for us hast died.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Cause us the record to receive:
Speak, and the tokens show;
"O be not faithless, but believe
In me, who died for you! "

title: Two are better far than one
author: E  Weslet

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Who of twain hath made us one,
Maintains our unity;
Jesus is the Corner-Stone,
In whom we all agree;
Servants of one common Lord,
Sweetly of one heart and mind,
Who can break a three-fold cord,
Or part whom God hath join'd?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that all with us might prove
The fellowship of saints!
Find supplied in Jesu's love,
What every member wants:
Grasp we our high calling's prize,
Feel our sins on earth forgiven,
Rise, in his whole image rise,
And meet our Head in heaven!

title: How happy are we, Who in Jesus agree
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy are we, Who in Jesus agree
To expect his return from above!
We sit under his vine, And delightfully join
In the praise of his excellent love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How pleasant and sweet, In his name when
we meet,
Is his fruit to our spiritual taste!
We are banqueting here On angelical cheer,
And the joys that eternally last.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Invited by him, We drink of the stream
Ever flowing in bliss from the throne:
Who in Jesus believe, We the Spirit receive
That proceeds from the Father and Son.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The unspeakable grace lie obtain* d for our
race,
And the spirit of faith he impai ts:
Then, then we conceive How in heaven they
live,
By the kingdom of God in our hearts.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
True believers have seen The Saviour of men,
As his head he on Calvary bow'd:
We shall see him again, When, with all his
bright train,
He descends on the luminous cloud.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
We remember the word Of our crucified Lord,
When he went to prepare us a place;
"I will come in that day, And transport yoa
away.
And adoait to a sight of my face."

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
With earnest desire After thee we aspire,
And long thy appearing to see;
Till our souls thou receive In thy presence to
live.
And be perfectly happy in thee.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Come, Lord, from the skies, And command ur
to rise,
Ready made for the mansions above;
With our Head to ascend, And eternity spend
In a rapture of heavenly love.

title: Jesus, thou precious Corner-Stone
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thou precious Corner-Stone,
Preserve inseparably one,
Whom thou didst by thy Spirit join:
Still let us in thy Spirit live,
And to thy church the pattern give
Of unanimity divine!
Still let us to each other cleave,
And from thy plentitude receive
Constant supplies of hallowing grace;
Till to a perfect man we rise,
O'ertake our kindred in the skies,
And find prepared our heavenly place.

title: Behold how good a thing
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold how good a thing
It is to dwell in peace;
How pleasing to our King,
This fruit of righteousness:
When brethren all in one agree,
Who knows the joys of unity!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Where unity takes place,
The joys of heaven we prove;
This is the gospel grace,
The unction from above,
The Spirit on all believers shed,
Descending swift from Christ our 11 tad

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where unity is found,
The sweet anointing grace
Extends to all around,
And consecrates the place;
To every waiting soul it comes,
And fills it with divine perfumes.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, our great High-Priest,
For us the gift received;
For us and all the rest,
Who have in him believed:
Forth from our Head the blessing goos,
And all his seamless coat o'erfiows.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
On all his chosen ones
The precious oil comes down:
It runs, and as it runs,
It ever will run on;
Even to his skirts (the meanest name
That longs to love the bleeding Lamb.)

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
From Aaron's beard it rolls,
(Those nearest to his face.)
The humble, trembling souls
Who feebly sue for grace:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
know the grace for all is free,
For, lo! it reaches now to me.

sections.label: Verse 9
Verse 10
sections.text:
Even now our Lord doth pour
The blessing from above,
A kindly gracious shower
Of heart reviving love;
The former and the latter ram,
The love of God and love of mar*

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
In him, when brethren join,
And follow after peace,
The fellowship divine
He promises to bless;
His choicest graces to bestow,
Where two or three are met below.

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
1 The riches of his grace
In fellowship are given
To Sion's chosen race,
The citizens of heaven:
He fills them with the choicest store,
He gives them life for evermore.

title: Come away to the skies, My beloved, arise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come away to the skies, My beloved, arise,
And rejoice in the day thou wast born;
On this festival day, Come exulting away,
And with singing to Sion return.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We have laid up our love And treasure above,
Though our bodies continue below;
The redeem'd of the Lord, We remember his
word,
And with singing to Paradise go.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With singing we praise The original grace,
By our heavenly Father bestow'd;
Our being receive From his bounty, and live
To the honour and glory of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For thy glory we are, Created to share
Both the nature and kingdom divine;
Ci eated again, That our souls may remain
In time and eternitv thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
With thanks we approve The design of thy love
Which hath join'd us in Jesus's name;
So united in heart, That we never can part,
Till we meet at the feast of the Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
There, there at his feet We shall suddenly meet,
And he parted in body no more!
We shall sing to our lyres, With the heavenly
choirs,
And our Saviour in glory adore.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Hallelujah we sing, To our Father and King,
And his rapturous praises repeat:
To the Lamb that was slain, Hallelujah again,
Sing all heaven, and fall at his feet!

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
In assurance of hope, We to Jesus look up,
Till his banner unfurl'd in the air
From our graves we shall see, And cry out,
"It is he!"
And fly up to acknowledge him there.

title: What shall we offer our good Lord
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What shall we offer our good Lord,
Poor nothings, for his boundless grace?
Fain would we his great name record,
And worthily set forth his praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Great Object of our growing love,
To whom our more than all we owe,
Open the fountain from above,
And let it our full souls o'erflow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So shall our lives thy power proclaim,
Thy grace for every sinner free;
Till all mankind shall learn thy name,
Shall all stretch out their hands to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Open a door which earth and hell
May strive to shut, but strive in vain;
Let thy word richly in us dwell,
And let our gracious fruit remain.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O multiply the sower's seed!
And fruit we every hour shall bear,
Throughout the world thy gospel spread,
Thy everlasting truth declare.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
We all, in perfect love renew'd,
Shall know the greatness of thy power;
Stand in the temple of our God
As pillars, and go out no more.

title: The people that in darkness lay
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The people that in darkness lay,
The confines of eternal night,
We, we have seen a gospel day,
The glorious beams of heavenly light;
His Spirit in our hearts hath shone,
And show'd the Father in the Son.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Father of eveidasting grace,
Thou hast in us thy arm reveal' d,
Hast multiplied the faithful race,
Who, conscious of their pardon seal'd,
Of joy unspeakable possest,
Anticipate their heavenly rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In tears who sow'd, in joy we reap,
And praise thy goodness all day long
Him in our eye of faith we keep,
Who gives us our triumphal song,
And doth his spoils to all divide,
A lot among the sanctified.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou hast our bonds in sunder broke,
Took all our load of guilt away;
From sin, the world, and Satan's yoke,
(Like Israel saved in Midiaivs day,)
Redeem'd us by our conquering Lord,
Our Gideon, and his Soirit's sword.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: I And own how dreadful is this place
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I And own how dreadful is this place!
Let all within us feel his power,
And silent bow before his face;
Who know his power, his grace who prove,
Serve him with awe, with reverence love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Gladly the toys of earth we leave,
Wealth, pleasure, fame, for thee alone:
To thee our will, soul, flesh, we give;
O take, O seal them for thine own!
Thou art the God, thou art the Lord:
Be thou by all thy works adored:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Being of beings! may our praise
Thy courts with grateful fragrance fill;
Still may we stand before thy fact.
Still hear and do thy sovereign will:
To thee may all our thoughts arise.
Ceaseless, accepted sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In thee we move: —all things of thee
Are full, thou Source and Life of all;
Thou vast unfathomable Sea!
(Fall prostrate, lost in wonder, fall,
Ye sons of men, for God is man!)
All mav wc lose, so thee we gain.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
As flowers their op'ning leaves display,
And glad drink in the solar fire,
So may we catch thy every ray,
So may thy influence us inspire;
Thou Beam of the eternal Beam,
Thou purging Fire, thou quick'ning Flame.

title: Come, let us arise, And press to the skies
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The Master of all For our service doth call,
And deigns to approve,
With smiles of acceptance, our labour of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His burden who bear, We alone can declare
How easy his yoke,
While to love and good works we each other
provoke; —

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By word and by deed, The bodies in need,
The souls to relieve,
And freely as Jesus hath given to give.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let us attend Our heavenly Friend,
In his members clistrest,
By want, or affliction, or sickness opprest:

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
Thus while we bestow Our moments below,
Ourselves we forsake,
And refuge in Jesus's righteousness take:

sections.label: Verse 8

title: The earth is the Lord's, And all it contains
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
To him our request We now have made known,
Who sees what is best For each of his own:
Our heathenish care, We cast it aside;
He heareth the prayer, And he will provide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The modest and meek The earth shall possess
The kingdom who seek Of Jesus's grace,
The power of his Spirit Shall joyfully own,
And all things inherit, In virtue of one.

title: Come, all whoe'er have set
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, all whoe'er have set
Your faces Sion-ward,
In Jesus let us meet,
And praise our common Lord;
In Jesus let us still go on,
Till all appear before his throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nearer, and nearer still,
We to our country come:
To that celestial hill,
The weary pilgrim's home.
The New Jerusalem above,
The seat of everlasting love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The ransom'd sons of God,
All earthly things we scorn;
And to our high abode
With songs of praise return:
From strength to strength we still proceed.
With crowns of joy upon our head.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The peace and joy of faith
Each moment may Ave feel:
Redeem'd from sin and wrath,
From earth, and death, and hell,
We to our Father's house repair,
To meet our elder brother there.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Come, let us anew Our journey pursue
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us anew Our journey pursue,
With vigour arise,
And press to our permanent place in the skies.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
A country of joy, Without any alloy,
We thither repair:
Our hearts and our treasure already are there.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
We march hand in hand To Immanuel's land
No matter what cheer
We meet with on earth; for eternity's near

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
The fiercer the blast, The sooner 'tis past:
The troubles that come
Shall come to our rescue, and hasten us home.

title: Come, let us ascend, My companion and
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us ascend, My companion and
J friend,
To a taste of the banquet above;
If thy heart be as mine, If for Jesus it pine,
Come up into the chariot of love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who in Jesus confide, We are bold to outride
The storms of affliction beneath;
With the prophet we soar To the heavenly
shore,
And outfly all the arrows of death.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By faith we are come To our permanent home
By hope we the rapture improve:
By love we still rise, And look down on the
skies,
For the heaven of heavens is love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Who on earth can conceive How happy we live,
In the palace of God, the great King?
What a concert of praise, When our Jesu's
gi-ace
The whole heavenly company sing!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
What a rapturous song, When the glorified
throng
In the spirit of harmony join:
Join all the glad choirs, Hearts, voices, and]
lyres,
And the burden is, "Mercy divine!"

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Hallelujah, they cry, To the King of the sky,
To the great everlasting I AM;
To the Lamb that was slain, And liveth again.
Hallelujah to God and the Lamb!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The Lamb on the throne, Lo! he dwells with
his own,
And to rivers of pleasure he leads!
With his mercy's full blaze, With the sight of
his face,
Our beatified spirits he feeds.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Our foreheads proclaim His ineffable name;
Our bodies his glory display:
A day without night, We feast in his sight,
And eternity seems as a day!

title: All praise to our redeeming Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All praise to our redeeming Lord,
Who joins us by his grace,
And bids us, each to 'each restored
Together seek his face.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He bids us build each other up,
And gather'd into one,
To our high calling's glorious hope
We hand in hand go on.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The gift which he on one bestows,
We all delight to prove:
The grace through every vessel flows
In purest streams of love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ev'n now we think and speak the same,
And cordially agree;
Concentred all, through Jesu's name,
In perfect harmony,

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We all partake the joy of one,
The common peace we feel;
A peace to sensual minds unknown,
A joy unspeakable.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
And if our fellowship below
In Jesus be so sweet.
What heights of rapture shall we know,
When round his throne we meet!

title: Jesu, Shepherd of the shsep
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
He comes, of hellish malice full,
To scatter, tear, and slay;
He seizes every straggling soul,
As his own lawful prey.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Us into thy protection take,
And gather with thy arm;
Unless the fold we first forsake,
The wolf can never harm.
i We laugh to scorn his cruel power,
While by our Shepherd's side:
The sheep he never can devour,
Unless he first divide.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
do not suffer him to part
The souls that here agree;
But make us of one mind and heart,
And keep us one in thee!
Together let us sweetly live,
Together let us die;
And each a starry crown receive,
And reign above the sky.

title: Come, thou omniscient Son of Man
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou omniscient Son of Man,
Display thy sifting power;
Come with thy Spirit's winnowing fan,
And throughly purge thy floor,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The chaff of sin, the' accursed thing,
Far from our souls be driven!
The wheat into thy garner bring,
And lay us up for heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Look through us with thy eyes of flame
The clouds and darkness chase;
And tell me what by sin I am,
And what I am by grace

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Whate'er 'offends thy glorious eyes,
Far from our hearts remove;
As dust before the whirlwind flies,
Disperse it by thy love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let us all thy fulness know,
From every sin set free;
jSaved, to the utmost —saved below,
And perfectly like thee.

title: Eternal source Of every sinful heart
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eternal source Of every sinful heart:
Whate'er of sin in us is found,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
bid it all depart!
2 When to the right or left we stray,
Leave us not comfortless;
But guide our feet into the way
Of everlasting peace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Help us to help each other, Lord,
Each other's cross to bear;
Let each bis friendly aid afford,
And feel his brother's care.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Help us to build each other up,
Our little stock improve;
Increase our faith, confirm our hope,
And perfect us in love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Up into thee, our living Head,
Let us in all things grow,
Till thou hast made us free indeed,
And spotless here below.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Then, when the mighty work is wrought,
Receive thy ready bride:
Give us in heaven a happy lot
With all the sanctified.

title: Jesus, united by thy grace
author: A  Weseey

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, united by thy grace,
And each to each endear'd,
With confidence we seek thy face,
And know our praver is heard-

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Still let us own our common Lord,
And bear thine easy yoke;
A band of love, a threefold cord,
Which never can be broke.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Touch'd by the loadstone of thy love,
Let all our hearts agree;
And ever tow'rds each other move,
And ever move tow'rds thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To thee inseparably join'd,
Let all our spirits cleave;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
may we all the loving mind
That was in thee receive!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
This is the bond of perfectness,
Thy spotless charity;

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
let us (still we pray) possess
The mind that was in thee!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Grant this, and then from all below
Insensibly remove;
Our souls their change shall scarcely know
Made perfect first in love!

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
With ease our souls through death shall glide
Into their paradise;
And thence, on wings of angels, ride
Triumphant through the skies.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Yet when the fullest joy is given,
The same delight, we prove;
In earth, in paradise, in heaven,
Our all in all is lovo.

title: Unchangeable, almighty Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Unchangeable, almighty Lord,
Our souls upon thy truth we stay;
Accomplish now thy faithful word,
And give, O give us all one way!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O let us all join hand in hand,
Who seek redemption in thy blood;
Fast in one mind and spirit stand,
And build the temple of our God!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou only canst our wills control,
Our wild unruly passions bind;
Tame the old Adam in our soul,
And make us of one heart and mind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Speak but the reconciling word,
The winds shall cease, the waves subside
We all shall praise our common Lord,
Our Jesus, and him crucified.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Giver of peace and unity,
Send down thy mild, pacific Dove:
We all shall then in one agree,
And breathe the spirit of thy love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
We all shall think and speak the same
Delightful lesson of thy grace;
One undivided Christ proclaim,
And jointly glory in thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O let us take a softer mold,
Blended and gather'd into thee;
Under one Shepherd make one fold,
Where all is love and harmony!

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Regard thine own eternal prayer,
And send a peaceful answer down;
To us thy Father's name declare;
Unite and perfect us in on? I
So shall the world beiieve and know,
That God hath sent thee from above,
When thou art seen in us below,
And every soul displays thy love.

title: Father of our dying Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of our dying Lord,
Remember us for good;
O fulfil his faithful word,
And hear his speaking blood!
Give us that for which he prays:
Father, glorify thy Son!
Show his truth, and power, and grace,
And send the Promise down.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
True and faithful Witness, thou,
O Christ, thy Spirit give!
Hast thou not received him now,
That we might now receive?
Art thou not our living Head?
Life to all thy limbs impart:
Shed thy love, thy Spirit shed
In every waiting heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Holy Ghost, the Comforter,
The gift of Jesus, come;
Glows our heart to find thee near.
And swells to make thee room:
Present with us thee we feel,
Come, O come, and in us be!
With us, in us, live and dwell,
To all eternity.

title: Saviour of all, to thee we bow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour of all, to thee we bow,
And own thee faithful to thy word;
We hear thy voice, and open now
Our hearts to entertain our Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come in, come in, thou heavenly Guest,
Delight in what thyself hast given;
On thine own gifts and graces feast,
And make the contrite heart thy heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Smell the sweet odour of our prayers,
Our sacrifice of praise approve;
And treasure up our gracious tears,
Who rest in thy redeeming love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Beneath thy shadow let us sit,
Call us thy friends, and love, and bride;
And bid us freely drink and eat
Thy dainties, and be satisfied.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O let us on thy fulness feed;
And eat thy flesh, and drink thy blood!
Jesus, thy blood is drink indeed.
Jesus, thy flesh is angels' food.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The heavenly manna faith imparts;
Faith makes thy fulness all our own,
We feed upon thee in our hearts.
And find that heaven and thou are one.

title: Almighty god of love, that hear'st the prayer
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Almighty god of love, that hear'st the prayer,
VJT Kindly for thy people care,
Who on thee alone depend:
Love us, save us to the end.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Save us, in the prosperous hour,
From the flatt'ring Tempter's powe:
From his unsuspected wiles,
From the world's pernicious smiles.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Cut off our dependence vain
On the help of feeble man:
Every arm of flesh remove;
Stay us on thy only love!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Men of worldly, low design,
Let not these thy people join,
Poison our simplicity,
Drag us from our trust in thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Save us from the great and wise,
Till they sink in their own eyes,
Tamely to thy yoke submit,
Lay their honours at thy feet.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Never let the world break in
Fix a mighty gulf between:
Keep us little and unknown,
Prized and loved by God alone.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Let us still to thee look up,
Thee, thy Israel's Strength and Hope;
Nothing know, or seek, beside
Jesus, and him crucified.
