sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Far above all earthly things,
Look we down on earthly kings '
Taste our glorious liberty;
Find our happy all in thee!

title: Jesu, we look to thee
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, we look to thee,
Let us in thy name agree:
Show thyself the Prince of Peace;
Bid our jars for pver cease.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By thy reconciling love,
Every stumbling-block remove;
Each to each unite, endear:
Come, and spread thy banner here!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Make us of one heart and mind,
Courteous, pitiful, and kind,
Lowly, meek, in thought and word,
Altogether like our Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let us for each other care,
Each the other's burden bear,
To thy church the pattern give,
Show how true believers live.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Free from anger and from pride,
Let us thus in God abide;
All the depths of love express,
All the heights of holiness!

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Thou God of truth and love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou God of truth and love,
We seek thy perfect way,
Ready thy choice to' approve,
Thy providence to' obey;
Enter into thy wise design,
And sweetly lose our will in thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Why hast thou cast our lot
In the same age and place?
And why together brought
To see each other's face?
To join with softest sympathy,
And mix our friendly souls in thee?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Didst thou not make us one,
That we might one remain,
Together travel on,
And bear each other's pain;
Till all thy utmost goodness prove,
And rise renew'd in perfect love?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Surely thou didst unite
Our kindred spirits here,
That all hereafter might
Before thy throne appear;
Meet at the marriage of the Lamb,
And all thy glorious love proclaim.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let us ever bear
The blessed end in view,
And join, with mutual care,
To fight our passage through;
And kindly help each other on,
Till all receive the starry crown

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O may thy Spirit seal
Our souls unto that day,
With all thy fulness fill,
And then transport away!
Away to our eternal rest,
Away to our Redeemer's breast!

title: Forgive us, for thy mercy's sake
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Forgive us, for thy mercy's sake,
Our multitude of sins forgive!
And for thy own possession take,
And bid us to thy glory live;
Live in thy sight, and gladly prove
Our faith, by our obedient love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The cov'nant of forgiveness seal,
And all thy mighty wonders show!
Our inbred enemies expel;
And conquering them to conquer go,
Till all oi pride and wrath be slain,
And not one evil thought remain!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Put it in our inward parts,
The living law of perfect love!
Write the new precept in our hearts:
We shall not then from thee remove.
Who in thy glorious image shine,
Thy people, and for ever thine

title: Centre of our hopes thou art
author: C   Wesi Ey

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
All our works in thee he wrought,
Levell'd at one common aim;
Every word, and every thought,
Purge in the refining flame:
Lead us, through the paths of peace,
On to perfect holiness.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Jesus, with kindest pity see
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, with kindest pity see
The souls that would be one in thee,
If now accepted in thy sight,
Thou dost our upright hearts unite,
Allow us even on earth to prove
The noblest joys of heavenly love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
A drop of that unbounded sea,
O Lord, resorb it into thee!
While all our souls, with restless strife,
Spring up into eternal life,
And, lost in endless raptures, prove
Thy whole immensity of lovel

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A spark of that ethereal fire,
Still let it to its source aspire.
To thee in every wish return,
Intensely for thy glory burn;
While all our souls fly up to thee,
And blaze through all eternity.

title: Father, at thy footstool see
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, at thy footstool see,
Those who now are one in thee:
Draw us by thy grace alone;
Give, O give us to thy Son!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Heavenly, all-alluring Dove,
Shed thy over-shadowing love;
Love, the sealing grace, impart,
Dwell within our single heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Be to us what Adam lost:
Let us in thine image rise;
Give us back our paradise.

title: Father, Son, and Spirit, hear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Build us in one hody up,
Call'd in one high calling's hope
One the Spirit whom we claim;
One the pure baptismal flame;
One the faith, and common Lord
One the Father lives adored,
Over, through, and in us all,
God incomprehensible.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One with God, the source of bliss,
Ground of our communion this:
Life of all that live below,
Let thine emanations flow;
Rise eternal in our heart:
Thou our long-sought Eden art;
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Be to us what Adam lost.

title: Other ground can no man lay
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Other ground can no man lay
Jesus takes our sins away;
Jesus the foundation is,
This shall stand, and only this:
Fitly framed in him we are,
All the building rises fair;
Let it to a temple rise,
Worthy him who fills the skies.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Husband of thy church below,
Christ, if thee our Lord we knoAV,
Unto thee, betrothed in love,
Always let us faithful prove;
Never rob thee of our heart,
Never give the creature part:
Only thou possess the whole $
Take our body, spirit, soul.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: /christ, our Head, pone up on high
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
/christ, our Head, pone up on high,
Be thou in thy Spirit nigh:
Advocate with God, give ear
To thine own effectual prayer!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Still, O Lord, (for thine we are,)
Still to us his name dechire:
Thy revealing Spirit give,
Whom the world cannot receive.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fill us with the Father's love;
Never from our souls remove:
Dwell in us, and we shall be
Thine through all eternity.

title: Join us, in one spirit join
author: C Wesi Ey J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Join us, in one spirit join,
Let us still receive of thine:
Still for more on thee we call,
Thou who fillest all in all!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Closer knit to thee, our Head;
Nourish us, O Christ, and feed j
Let us daily growth receive,
More and more in Jesus live.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Never from our office move,
Needful to each other prove;
Use the grace on each bestow' d,
Temper' d by the art of God,

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
Wounded by the grief of one,
Now let all the members groan;
Honour'd if one member is,
All partake the common bliss.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Many are we now and one,
We who Jesus have put on:
There is neither bond nor free,
Male nor female, Lord, in thee!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Love, like death, hath all destroy'
Render'd all distinctions void;
Names, and sects, and parties tali:
Thou, O Christ, art all in all 1

title: Come, and let us sweetly join
author: Wesi Ey J

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Strive we, in affection strive;
Let the purer flame revive,
Such as in the martyrs glow'd,
Dying champions for their God:
We, like them, may live and love;
Call'd we are their joys to prove,
Saved with them from future wrath,
Partners of like precious faith.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sing we then in Jesu's name,
Now as yesterday the same;
One in every time and place,
Full for all of truth and grace:
We for Christ, our Master, stand,
Lights in a benighted land:
We our dying Lord confess,
We are Jesu's witnesses.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Come, thou high and lofty Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou high and lofty Lord!
Lowly, meek, incarnate Word!
Humbly stoop to earth again;
Come and visit abject man!
Jesus, dear expected guest,
Thou art bidden to the feast;
For thyself our hearts prepare:
Come, and sit, and banquet there!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Make us all in thee complete,
Make us all for glory meet,
Meet to' appear before thy sight,
Partners with the saints in light.
Call, O call us each, by name,
To the marriage of the Lamb!
Let us lean upon thy breast;
Love be there our endless feast!

title: Let us join, ('tis God commands,)
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Let us then as brethren love,
Faithfully his gifts improve,
Carry on the earnest strife,
Walk in holiness of life;
Still forget the things behind.
Follow Christ in heart and mind.
Tow'rd the mark unwearied press,
Seize the crown of righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Plead we thus for faith alone,
Faith which by our works is shown:
God it is who justifies;
Only faith the grace applies; —
Active faith that lives within,
Conquers earth, and hell, and sin,
Sanctifies, and makes us whole,
Forms the Saviour in the soul.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let us for this faith contend;
Sure salvation is its end:
Heaven already is begun,
Everlasting life is won.
Only let us persevere,
Till we see our Lord appear;
Never from the Rock remove,
Saved by faith which works by lova.

title: O thou, our Husband, Brother, Friend
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou, our Husband, Brother, Friend,
v/ Behold a cloud of incense rise!
The prayers of saints to heaven ascend,
Grateful, accepted sacrifice!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Before thy sheep, great Shepherd, go,
And guide into thy perfect will,
Cause us thy hallow'd name to know,
The work of faith in us fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Help us to make our calling sure;
O let us all be samts indeed,
And pure as thou thyself art pure,
Conform'd in all things to our Head.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Take the dear purchase of thy blood:
Thy blood shall wash us white as snov,
Present us sanctified to God,
And perfected in love below.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
That blood which cleanses from all sin,
That efficacious blood apply;
And wash, and make us wholly clean.
And change, and throughly sanctify.

sections.label: Verse 7

title: Whate'er thou dost on one bestow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Witnesses of the' all-cleansing blood,
Long may we work the works of God,
And do thy will like those above:
Together spread the gospel sound,
And scatter peace on all around,
And joy, and happiness, and love.
True yoke-fellows, by love compell'd,
To labour in the gospel field,
Our all let us delight to spend,
In gathering in thy lambs and sheep;
Assured that thou our souls wilt keep,
Wilt keep us faithful to the end.

title: Jesus, thou great redeeming Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Give all thy saints to find in thee
The fulness of the Deity;
His nature, life, and mind to prove,
In perfect holiness and love:
Fountain of Grace! thyself make known,
With God and man for ever one.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Except the Lord conduct the plan
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Except the Lord conduct the plan,
The best concerted schemes are vain,
And never can succeed;
We spend our wretched strength for nought 1
But if our works in thee be wrought,
They shall be blest indeed.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, if thou didst thyself inspire
Our souls with this intense desire
Thy goodness to proclaim, —
Thy glory if we now intend, —
O let our deed begin and end
Complete in Jesu's name I

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
One only thing resolved to know,
And square our useful lives below,
By reason and by grace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Not in the tombs we pine to dwell,
Not in the dark monastic cell,
By vows and grates confined;
Freely to all ourselves we give,
Constrain'd by Jesu's love to live
The servants of mankind.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Now, Jesus, now thy love impart,
To govern each devoted heait,
And fit us for thy will:
Deep founded in the truth of grace,
Build up thy rising Church, and place
The city on the hill.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O let our faith and love abound!
O let our lives to all around
With purest lustre shine;
That all around our works may see,
And give the glory, Lord, to thee,
The heavenly Light Divine.

title: Come, "Wisdom, Power, and Grace Divine 5
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, "Wisdom, Power, and Grace Divine 5
Come, Jesus, in thy name to join
A happy, chosen band;
Who fain would prove thine utmost will,
And all thy righteous laws fulfil,
In love's benign command.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If pure, essential Love thou art,
Thy nature into every heart,
Thy loving self, inspire:
Bid all our simple souls be one,
United in a bond unknown,
Baptized with heavenly fire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Still may we to our centre tend, —
To spread thy praise our common end.
To help each other on:
Companions through the wilderness,
To share a moment's pain, and seize
An everlasting crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, our tender'd souls prepare!
Infuse the softest social care,
Tltc warmest charity,
The howels of our bleeding Lamb,
The virtues of thy wondrous name,
The heart that was in thee.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: O saviour, cast a gracious smile
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O saviour, cast a gracious smile!
Our gloomy guilt, and selfish guile,
And shy distrust remove:
The true simplicity impart,
To fashion every passive heart,
And mould it into love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our naked hearts to thee we raise;
Whate'er obstructs thy work of grace,
For ever drive it hence:
Exert thy all-subduing power,
And each regenerate soul restore
To child-like innocence.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soon as in thee we gain a part,
Our spirit purged from nature's art
Appears, by grace forgiven;
We then pursue our sole design,
To lose our melting will in thine,
And want no other heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that we now the power might feel,
To do on earth thy Messed will,
As angels do above!
In thee, the Life, the Truth, the Way,
To walk, and perfectly to' obey
Thy sweet constraining love!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, fulfil our one desire,
And spread the spark of living fire
Through every hallow'd breast;
Bless with divine conformity,
And give us now to find in thee
Our everlasting rest.

title: Holy Lamb, who thee confess
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy Lamb, who thee confess,
JLX Followers of thy holiness,
Thee they ever keep in view,
Ever ask, "What shall we do? »
Govem'd by thy only will,
All thy words we would fulfil,
Would in all thy footsteps go,
Walk as Jesus walk'd below.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
While thou didst on earth appear,
Servant to thy servants here,
Mindful of thy place above,
All thy life was prayer and love.
Such our whole employment be,
Works of faith and charity;
Works of love on man bestow'd,
Secret intercourse with God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Early in the temple meet,
Let us still our Saviour greet;
Nightly to the mount repair,
Join our praying Pattern there.
There by wrestling faith obtain
Power to work for God again;
Power his image to retrieve,
Power, like thee, our Lord, to live.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Vessels, instruments of grace,
Pass we thus our happy days
'Twixt the mount and multitude,
Doing or receiving good;
Glad to pray and labour on,
Till our earthly course is run,
Till we, on the sacred tree,
Bow tbe head and die like thee.

title: Come, thou all-inspiring Spirit
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou all-inspiring Spirit,
Into every longing heart!
Bought for us by Jesu's merit,
Now thy blissful self impart:
Sign our uncontested pardon;
Wash us in the' atoning blood!
Make our hearts a water'd garden;
Fill our spotless souls with God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If thou gav'st the' enlarged desire
Which for thee we ever feel,
Now our panting souls inspire,
Now our cancell'd sin reveal:
Claim us for thy habitation;
Dwell within our hallow'd breast;
Seal us heirs of full salvation,
Fitted for our heavenly rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Give as quietly to tarry,
Till for all thy glory meet,
Waiting, like cittentive Maiy,
Happy at the Saviour's feet;
Keep us from the world unspotted,
From all earthly passions free,
Wholly to thyself devoted,
Fix'd to live and die for thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Wrestling on in mighty prayer,
Lord, we will not let thee go,
Till thou all thy mind declare,
All thy grace on us bestow;
Peace, the seal of sin forgiven,
Joy, and perfect love, impart,
Present, everlasting heaven,
All thou hast, and all thou art!

title: Christ, whose glory fills the skies
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christ, whose glory fills the skies,
That famous Plant thou art:
Tree of Life eternal, rise
In every longing heart!
Bid us find the food in thee,
For which our deathless spirits pine,
Fed with immortality,
And fill'd with love divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Long we have our burden borne
Our own unfaithfulness,
Object of the Heathens' scorn,
Who mock'd our scanty grace:
Jesus, our reproach remove;
Let sin no more thy people shame!
Fhow us rooted in thy love,
In life and death the same.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In thy spotless people show
Thy power and constancy;
Give us thus to feel and know
Our fellowship with thee:
Give us all thy mind to' express,
And blameless in our Lord to' abide,
Transcripts of thy holiness,
Thy fair unspotted bride.

title: Come, let us use the grace divine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us use the grace divine,
And all, with one accord,
In a perpetual Covenant join
Ourselves to Christ the Lord:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give up ourselves, through Jesu's power,
His name to glorify;
And promise, in this sacred hour,
For God to live and die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Covenant we this moment make,
Be ever kept in mind: —
We will no more our God forsake,
Or cast his words behind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We never will throw off his fear,
Who hears our solemn vow: —
And if thou art well-pleased to hear,
Come down and meet us now!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thee, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Let all our hearts l'eceive;
Present with the celestial host,
The peaceful answer give!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
To each the covenant blood apply,
Which takes our sins away;
And register our names on high,
And keep us to that day

title: I And in thy pleasure rest
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I And in thy pleasure rest;
We, only we, can say,
"Whatever is, is best; "
Joyful to meet, willing to part,
Convinced we still are one in heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hereby we sweetly know
Our love proceeds from thee, —
We let each other go,
From every creature free,
And cry, in answer to thy call,
"Thou art, O Christ, our all in all! "

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our Husband, Brother, Friend,
Our Counsellor Divine!
Thy chosen ones depend
On no support but thine:
Our everlasting Comforter!
We cannot want, if thou art here.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Blest be the dear uniting love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest be the dear uniting love,
That will not let us part:
Our bodies may far off remove, —
We still are one in heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Join'd in one spirit to our Head,
Where he appoints we go;
And still in Jesu's footsteps tread,
And show his praise below.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O may we ever walk in him,
And nothing know beside;
Nothing desire, nothing esteem,
But Jesus Crucified.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Closer and closer let us cleave
To his beloved embrace;
Expect his fulness to receive,
And grace to answer grace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Partakers of the Saviour's grace,
The same in mind and heart,
Nor joy, nor grief, nor time, nor place,
Nor life, nor death can part.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
But let us hasten to the day,
Which shall our flesh restore,
When death shall all be done away,
And bodies part no more!

title: And let our bodies part
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And let our bodies part,
To different climes repair, —
Inseparably join'd in heart
The friends of Jesus are.
Jesus, the Corner-stone,
Did first our hearts unite,
And still he keeps our spirits one,
Who walk with him in wliite.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O let us still proceed
In Jesu's work below;
And, following our triumphant Head,
To farther conquests go!
The vineyard of the Lord
Before his labourers lies;
And, lo! we see the vast reward
Which waits us in the skies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
let our heart and mind
Continually ascend,
That haven of repose to find
Where all our labours end;
Where all our toils are o'er,
Our suffering and our pain: —
Who meet on that eternal shore
Shall never part again.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
happy, happy place,
Where saints and angels meet!
There we shall see each other's face,
And all our brethren greet.
The Church of the first-born,
We shall with them be blest,
And, crown' d with endless joy, returr.
To our eternal rest.
With joy we shall behold,
In yonder blest abode,
The patriarchs and prophets old,
And all the saints of God.
Abraham and Isaac there,
And Jacob shall receive
The followers of their faith and prayer.
Who now in bodies live.
We shall our time beneath
Live out in cheerful hope,
And feai-less pass the vale of death,
And gain the mountain-top-
To gather home his own
God shall his angels send.
And bid our bliss, on earth begun,
In deathless triumph end.

title: Jesus accept the praise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus accept the praise
That to thy Name belongs;
Matter of all our lays,
Subject of all our songs:
Through thee we now together came,
And part exulting in thy Name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In flesh we part awhile,
But still in spirit join'd,
To' embrace the happy toil,
Thou hast to each assign'd;
And while we do thy blessed will,
We bear our heaven about us still.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O let us thus go on
In all thy pleasant ways,
And, arm'd with patience, ran
With joy the' appointed race:
Keep us, and every seeking soul,
Till all attain the heavenly goal.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There we shall meet again,
When all our toils are o'er,
And death, and grief, and pain,
And parting are no more:
We shall with all our brethren rise,
And grasp thee in the flaming skies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O happy, happy day,
That calls thy exiles home!
The heavens shall pass away,
The earth receive its doom:
Earth we shall view, and heaven destroy' I
And shout above thu iiery void.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
These eyes shall see them fall,
Mountains, and stars, and skies
These eyes shall see them all -.
Out of their ashes rise!
These lips his praises shall rehearse,
Whose nod restores the universe.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
According to his word,
His oath to sinners given,
We look to see restored
The ruin'd earth and heaven;
In a new world his truth to prove,
A world of righteousness and love.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Then let us wait the sound,
That shall our souls release;
And labour to be found
Of him in spotless peace,
In perfect holiness renew'd,
Adom'd with Christ, and meet for God.

title: God of all consolation, take
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of all consolation, take
The glory of thy grace!
Thy gifts to thee we render back
In ceaseless songs of praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Subsists as in us all one soul,
No power can make us twain;
And mountains rise, and oceans roll,
To sever us in vain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Present we still in spirit are,
And intimately nigh,
While on the wings of faith and prayer
We each to other fly.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In Jesus Christ together we
In heavenly places sit;
Clothed with the sun, we smile to sea
The moon beneath our feet.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Our life is hid with Christ in God;
Our Life shall soon appear,
And shed his glory all abroad
In all his members here.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The heavenly treasure now we have
In a vile house of clay;
But he shall to the utmost save.
And keep it to that day.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Our souls are in his mighty hand,
And he shall keep them still;
And you and I shall surely stand
With him on Sion's hill!

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Him eye to eye we there shall see;
Our face like his shall shine:
O what a glorious company,
When saints and angels join!

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
1 O what a joyful meeting there!
In robes of white array'd,
Palms in our hands we all shall bear..
And crowns upon our head.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Then let us lawfully contend,
And fight our passage through;
Bear in our faithful minds the end,
And keep the prize in view.

sections.label: Verse 12
Verse 13
sections.text: Jesus, quickly come!

title: Jesus, soft harmonious Name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, soft harmonious Name,
Every faithful heart's desire;
See thy followers, O Lamb!
All at once to thee aspire:
Drawn by thy uniting grace,
After thee we swiftly run;
Hand in hand we seek thy face:
Come, and perfect us in one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Mollify our harsher will;
Each to each our tempers suit,
By thy modulating skill,
Heart to heart, as lute to lute:
Sweetly on our spirits move;
Gently touch the trembling strings
Make the harmony of love,
Music for the King of kings!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See the souls that hang on thee!
Sever'd though in flesh we are,
Join'd in spirit all agree;
All thy only love declare;
Spread thy love to all around:
Hai-k! we now our voices raise!—
Joyful consentaneous sound,
Sweetest symphony of praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesu's praise be all our song;
While we Jesu's praise repeat,
Glide our happy hours along,
Glide with down upon their feet 1
Far from sorrow, sin, and fear,
Till we take our seats above,
Live we all as angels here,
Only sing, and praise, and love.

title: Lift up your hearts to things above
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lift up your hearts to things above,
JLj Ye followers of the Lamb,
And join with us to praise his love,
And glorify his name:
To Jesu's Name give thanks and sing,
Whose mercies never end:
Rejoice! rejoice! the Lord is King;
The King is now our Friend!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We, for his sake, count all things loss
On earthly good look down;
And joyfully sustain the cross,
Till we receive the crown.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
let us stir each other up,
Our faith by works to' approve,
By holy, purifying hope,
And the sweet task of love!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Love us, though far in flesh disjoin'd,
Ye lovers of the Lamb;
And ever bear us on your mind,
Who think and speak the same:
You on our mmds we ever bear,
Whoe'er to Jesus bow;
Stretch out the arms of faith and prayer,
And, lo! we reach you now.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The blessings all on you be shed,
Which God in Christ imparts;
We pray the Spirit of our Head
Into your faithful hearts.
5k
Mercy and peace your portion be,
To carnal minds unknown,
The hidden manna, and the tree
Of life, and the white stone.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Let all who for the Promise wait,
The Holy Ghost receive;
And, raised to our unsinning state,
With God in Eden live!
Live till the Lord in glory come,
And wait his heaven to share:
He now is fitting up your home;
Go on; —we'll meet you there.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
"T OED! dismiss us with thy blessing,
JlJ Fill our hearts with joy and peace
Let us all, thy love possessing,
Triumph in redeeming grace:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
refresh us,
Travelling through this wilderness.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Thanks we give, and adoration,
For thy gospel 's joyful sound;
Let the fruits of thy salvation
In our hearts and lives abound,
Ever faithful
To the truth may we be found.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
So whene'er the signal's given,
Us from earth to call away,
Bome on angels' wings to heaven,
Glad the summons to obey,
May we ever —
Reign with Christ in endless day
Not in the Editions published during the Life of
Me. Wesley.
On Divine Worship.

title: His sovereign power, without our aid
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
His sovereign power, without our aid,
Made us of clay, and form'd us men;
And when like wandering sheep we stray 'd,
He brought us to his fold again.
J We'll crowd thy gates with thankful songs.
High as the heavens our voices raise,
And earth, with her ten thousand tongues.
Shall fill thy courts with sounding praise.
Wide as the world is thy command;
Vast as eternity thy love;
Firm as a rock thy truth shall stand,
When rolling years shall cease to move.

title: Ye humble souls that pray
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye humble souls that pray
Where God delights to hear!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
happy men that pay
Their constant service there!
They praise thee still; And happy they
Who love the way To Zion's hill!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
They go from strength to strength,
Through this dark vale of tears,
Till each o'ercomes at length,
Till each in heaven appears:
O glorious seat! Thou God, our King,
Shalt thither hring Our willing feet,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
God is our sun and shield,
Our light and our defence!
With gifts his hands are fill'd,
We draw our blessings thence:
He shall bestow Upon our race
His saving grace, And glory too.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Lord his people loves;
His hand no good withholds
From those his heart approves,
From holy, humble souls:
Thrice happy he, O Lord of Hosts,
Whose spirit trusts Alone in thee!

title: Lord and God of heavenly powers
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord and God of heavenly powers!
Theirs,—yet, O! benignly ours;
Glorious King! let earth proclaim,
Worms attempt to chant thy name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thee to laud in songs divine
Angels and archangels join:
We with them our voices raise,
Echoing thine eternal praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy Lord,
Live by heaven and earth adored!
Full of thee, they ever cry,
"Glory be to God Most High 1"

title: Being of Beings, God of Love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Being of Beings, God of Love!
To thee our hearts we raise;
Thy all-sustaining power we prove,
And gladly sing thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Heavenward our every wish aspires;
For all thy mercies' store,
The sole return thy love requires
Is, that we ask for more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For more we ask; we open then
Our hearts to' embrace thy will;
Turn, and beget us, Lord, again,
With all thy fulness fill.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Come, Holy Ghost, the Saviour's love
Shed in our hearts abroad!
So shall we ever live, and move,
And be with Christ in God.

title: The Lord of Sabbath let us praise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord of Sabbath let us praise,
In concert with the blest,
Who, joyful, in harmonious lays
Employ an endless rest.
Thus, Lord, while we remember Thee,
We blest and pious grow;
By hymns of praise we learn to be
Triumphant here below.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On this glad day a brighter scene
Of glory was display'd,
By God, the' eternal Word, than when
This universe was made.
He rises, who mankind has bought
With grief and pain extreme:
'Twas great to speak a world from nought;
'Twas greater to redeem!

title: O thou eternal Victim, slain
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou eternal Victim, slain
J A sacrifice for guilty man,
By the eternal Spirit made
An offering in the sinner's stead;
Our everlasting Priest art thou,
And plead' st thy death for sinners now.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O that our faith may never move,
But stand unshaken as thy love!
Sure evidence of things unseen,
Now let it pass the years between,
And view thee bleeding on the tree,
My God, who dies for me, for me!

title: Let all who truly bear
author: Eslev

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let all who truly bear
The Name of Christ your Lord.
His last mysterious supper share.
And keep his kindest word.
Hereby your faith approve
In Jesus crucified:
"In memory of my dying love,
Do this,"—he said, —and di«d.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The badge and token this,
The sure confirming seal,
That he is ours, and we are his,
The servants of his will;
His dear peculiar ones,
The purchase of his blood;
His blood which once for all atones,
And brings us now to God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then let us still profess
Our Master's honour'd name;
Stand forth his faithful witnesses,
True followers of the Lamb.
In proof that such we are,
His saying we receive,
And thus to all mankind declare
We do in Christ believe.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Part of his church below,
We thus our right maintain;
Our living membership we show,
And in the fold remian, —
The sheep of Israel's fold,
In England's pastures fed:
And fellowship with all we hold,
Who hold it with our Head.

title: Come, thou everlasting Spirit
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou everlasting Spirit,
Bring to every thankful mind
All the Saviour's dying merit,
All his sufferings for mankind!
True Recorder of his passion,
Now the living faith impart;
Now reveal his great salvation;
Preach his gospel to our heart.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Lamb of God, whose bleeding love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Never will we hence depart,
Till thou our wants relieve,
Write forgiveness on our heart,
And all thine image give!
Still our souls shall cry to thee,
Till perfected in holiness;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
remember Calvary,
And bid us go in peace!

title: Jesu, at whose supreme command
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, at whose supreme command,
We now approach to God,
Before us in thy vesture stand,
Thy vesture dipp'd in blood!
Obedient to thy gracious word,
We break the hallow'd bread,
Commem'rate thee, our dying Lord,
And trust on thee to feed.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now, Saviour, now thyself reveal,
And make thy nature known;
Affix thy blessed Spirit's seal,
And stamp us for thine own,
The tokens of thy dying love

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
The cup of blessing, bless'd by thee,
Let it thy blood impart;
The bread thy mystic body be,
And cheer each languid heart.
The grace which sure salvation brings
Let us herewith receive;
Satiate the hungry with good things,
The hidden manna give.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The living bread, sent down from heaven,
In us vouchsafe to he:
Thy flesh for all the world is given,
And all may live by thee.
Now, Lord, on us thy flesh bestow,
And let us drink thy blood,
Till all our souls are fill'd below
With all the life of God.

title: Come, Holy Ghost, thine influence shed
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Ghost, thine influence shed,
And realize the sign;
Thy life infuse into the bread,
Thy power into the wine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Effectual let the tokens prove,
And made, by heavenly art,
Fit channels to convey thy love
To every faithful heart.

title: Victim Divine, thy grace we claim
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Victim Divine, thy grace we claim,
While thus thy precious death we show;
Once offer'd up, a spotless Lamb,
In thy great temple here below,
Thou didst for all mankind atone,
And standest now before the throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou standest in the holy place,
As now for guilty sinners slain;
The blood of sprinkling speaks, and prays,
All prevalent for helpless man;
Thy blood is still our ransom found,
And speaks salvation all around
The smoke of thy atonement here
Darken'd the sun, and rent the veil,
Made the new way to heaven appear,
And show'd the great Invisible:
Well-pleased in thee, our God look'd down,
And calls his rebels to a ciwvn.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Jesus drinks the bitter cup
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Dies the glorious cause of all!
The true eternal Pan
Falls, to raise us from our fall,
To ransom sinful man!
Well may Sol withdraw his light,
With the Sufferer sympathize,
Leave the world in sudden night,
While the Creator dies!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Well may heaven be clothed in black.
And solemn sackcloth wear,
Jesu's agonies partake,
The hour of darkness share:
Mourn the' astonish'd hosts above;
Silence saddens all the skies;
Kindler of seraphic love,
The God of Angels dies!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O my God, he dies for me,
I feel the mortal smart!
See him hanging on the tree, —
A sight that breaks my heart!
O that all to thee might turn!
Sinners, ye may love him too;
Look on him ye pierced, and mourn
For one who bled for you!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Weep o'er your desire and hope,
With tears of humblest love:
Sing, for Jesus is gone up,
And reigns enthroned above:
Lives our Head, to die no more;
Power is all to Jesus given, —
Worshipp'd, as he was before,
The' Immortal King of Heaven,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Lord, we bless thee for thy grace
And truth, which never fail:
Hastening to behold thy face,
Without a dimming veil,
We shall see our heavenly King,
All thy glorious love proclaim 5
Help the angel-choirs to sing
The dear triumphant Lamb.

title: He dies! the Friend of sinners dies
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He dies! the Friend of sinners dies!
Salem's daughters weep around!
A solemn darkness veils the skies;
A sudden trembling shakes the ground:
Come, saints, and drop a tear or two
On the dear bosom of your God:
He shed a thousand drops for you,
A thousand drops of richer blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here's love and grief beyond degree;
The Lord of glory dies for man!
But, lo! what sudden joys I see!
Jesus, the dead, revives again!
The rising God forsakes the tomb;
The tomb in vain forbids his rise!
Cherubic legions guard him home,
And shout him welcome to the skies!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Break off your tears, ye saints, and tell
How high your great Deliverer reigns;
Sing how he spoil'd the hosts of hell,
And led the monster death in chains.
Say, "Live for ever, wondrous King!
Bom to redeem, and strong to save! "
Then ask the monster, "Where's thy sting? "
And, "Where's thy victory, boasting grave?"

title: Our Lord is risen from the dead
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Loose all your bars of massy light,
And wide unfold the' ethereal scene:
He claims these mansions as his right;
Receive the King of Glory in!
Who is the King of Glory? Who?
The Lord that all our foes o'ercame;
The world, sin, death, and hell o'erthrew
And Jesus is the Conqueror's name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lo! his triumphal chariot waits,
And angels chant the solemn lay:
Lift up your heads, ye heavenly gates;
Ye everlasting doors give way!
Who is the King of Glory? Who?
The Lord, of glorious power possess'd;
The King of saints, and angels too,
God over all, for ever bless'd!

title: Come, Desire of nations, come
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Desire of nations, come!
Hasten, Lord, the general doom!
Hear the Spirit and the Bride;
Come, and take us to thy side.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Mindful of thy chosen race,
Shorten these vindictive days;
Who for full redemption groan,
Hear us now, and save thine own.
i Now destroy the man of sin;
Now thine ancient flock bring in!
Fill'd with righteousness divine,
Claim a ransom'd world for thine.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: To the hills I lift mine eyes
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To the hills I lift mine eyes,
The everlasting hills;
Streaming thence, in fresh supplies,
My soul the Spirit feels:
Will he not his help afford?
Help, while yet I ask, is given;
God comes down; the God and Lord
That made both earth and heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Christ shall bless thy going out,
Shall bless thy coming in;
Kindly compass thee about,
Till thou art saved from sin:
Like thy spotless Master, thou,
Fill'd with wisdom, love, and power,
Holy, pure, and perfect, —now,
Henceforth and evermore.

title: Ye servants of God, Your Master proclaim
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The waves of the sea Have lift up their voice,
Sore troubled that we In Jesus rejoice;
The floods they are roaring, But Jesus is here
While we are adoring, He always is near.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
"Salvation to God Who sits on the throne,"
Let all cry aloud, And honour the Son;
Our Jesus' s praises The angels proclaim,
Fall down on their faces, And worship the Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let us adore, And give him his right,
All glory and power, All wisdom and might,
All honour and blessing, With angels above,
And thanks never ceasing, And infinite love.
C Come, Lord, and display Thy sign in the sky,
And bear us away To mansions on high;
The kingdom be given, The purchase divine,
And crown us in heaven Eternally thine.

title: Come, Lord, from above, the mountains
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Lord, from above, the mountains
J remove; [love.
Overturn all that hinders the course of thy
My bosom inspire, Inkindle the fire,
And wrap my whole soul in the flames of desire.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I languish and pine For the comfort divine;
O when shall I say, My Beloved is mine!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
have chos'n the good part; My portion thou art,
O Love; let me find thee, O God, in my heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For this my heart sighs: Nothing else can
suffice; [price?
How, Lord, can I purchase the pearl of great
It cannot be bought, And thou know'st I have
nought,
Not an action, a word, or a truly good thought.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But I hear a voice say, "Without money ye may
Receive it, whoever have nothing to pay:
Who on Jesus relies, Without money or price,
The pearl of forgiveness and holiness buys:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The blessing is free;"—So, Lord, let it be;
1 yield that thy love should be given to me.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
freely receive What thou freely dost give,
And consent in thy love, in thy Eden, to live.

sections.label: Verse 8

title: God moves in a mysterious way
author: William Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God moves in a mysterious way,
VJT His wonders to perform;
He plants his footsteps in the sea,
And rides upon the storm.
Deep in unfathomable mines
Of never-failing skill,
He treasures up his bright designs,
And works his sovereign will.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ye fearful saints fresh courage take!
The clouds ye so much dread
Are big with mercy, and shall break
In blessings on your head.
Judge not the Lord by feeble sense,
But trust him for his grace:
Behind a frowning providence
He hides a smiling face.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His purposes will ripen fast,
Unfolding every hour;
The bud may have a bitter taste,
But sweet will be the flower.
Blind unbelief is sure to err,
And scan his work in vain:
God is his own Interpreter,
And he will make it plain.
ORD, dismiss us with thy blessing!
Bid us now depart in peace;
Still on heavenly manna feeding,
Let our faith and love increase:
Fill each breast with consolation;
Up to thee our hearts we raise:
When we reach yon blissful station,
Then wedl.give thee nobler praise1
Halleluiah 1

title: Hail to the Lord's Anointed
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail to the Lord's Anointed!
JLJL Great Davids greater Son!
Hail! in the time appointed,
His reign on earth begun!
He comes to break oppression,
To set the captive free;
To take away transgression,
And rule in equity.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He shall come down like showers
Upon the fruitful earth,
And joy and hope, like flowers,
Spring in his path to birth.
Before him, on the mountains,
Shall Peace, the herald, go;
And righteousness, in fountains,
From hill to valley flow.
? Arabia's desert-ranger
To him shall bow the knee;
The Ethiopian stranger
His glory come to see:
With offerings of devotion,
Ships from the isles shall meet,
To pour the wealth of ocean
In tribute at his feet.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Kings shall fall down before him.
And gold and incense bring;
All nations shall adore him,
His praise all people sing
For he shall have dominion
O'er river, sea, and shore,
Far as the eagle's pinion
Or dove's light wing can soar.
For him shall prayer unceasing
And daily vows ascend:
His kingdom still increasing, —
A kingdom without end.
The mountain dew shall nourish
A seed in weakness sown,
Whose fruit shall spread and flourish,
And shake like Lebanon.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O'er every foe victorious,
He on his throne shall rest;
From age to age more glorious,
All blessing and all blest.
The tide of time shall never
His covenant remove:
His name shall stand for ever;
His great, best name of love.

title: All hail the power of Jesus name
author: Msrbonett

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All hail the power of Jesus name!
Let angels prostrate fall;
Bring forth the royal diadem,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Crown him, ye martyrs of our God,
Who from his altar call;
Extol the Stem of Jesse's roi,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye chosen seed of Israel's race,
A remnant weak and small,
Hail him who saves you by his grace,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ye Gentile sinners ne'er forget
The wormwood and the gall;
Go spread your trophies at his feet,
And crown him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Let every kindred, every tribe,
On this terrestrial ball,
To him all majesty ascribe,
And crown him Lord of all

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O that with yonder sacred throng,
We at his feet may fall;
There join the everlasting song,
And crown him Lord of all!

title: Where are the Dead? —In heaven or
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Where are the Dead? —In heaven or
VV hell
Their disembodied spirits dwell;
Their lifeless forms, in bonds of clay,
Reserv'd until the judgment-day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who were the Dead? —The sons of time
In every age, and state, and clime;
Eenown'd, dishonour'd, or forgot,
The place that knew them, knows them not.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Where are the Living? —On the ground,
Where prayer is heard, and mercy found: —
There, in the compass of a span,
The mortal makes the' immortal man.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Who are the Living? —They, whose breath
Draws every moment nigh to death: —
Of endless bliss or woe the heirs;
O what an awful lot is theirs!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then, timely warn'd, let us begin
To follow Christ and flee from sin,
Daily grow up in Him our head;
Lord of the Living and the Dead.

title: When shall these eyes thy heaven-built walls
author: Non

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When shall these eyes thy heaven-built walls
And pearly gates behold?
Thy bulwarks, with salvation strong,
And streets of shining gold?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, when, thou city of my God,
Shall I thy courts ascend,
Where congregations ne'er break up,
And Sabbaths have no end.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Why should 1 shrink at pain or woe?
Or feel at death dismay?
I've Canaan's goodly land in view,
And realms of endless day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Apostles, martyrs, prophets there,
Around my Saviour stand;
And soon my friends in Christ below
Will join the glorious band.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jerusalem! my happy home!
My soul still pants for thee;
Then shall my labours have an end,
When I thy joys shall see.

title: Sweet is the scene when Virtue dies
author: R   Bernard

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet is the scene when Virtue dies,
When sinks a righteous soul to rest;
How mildly beam the closing eyes!
How gently heaves th' expiring breast!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Triumphant smiles the victor-bi*ow,
Fann'd by some angel's purple wing
O Grave! where is thy victory now?
Invidious death! where is thy sting?
A holy quiet reigns around;
A calm, which nothing can destroy;
Nought can disturb that peace profound
Which their unfetter'd souls enjoy.
Farewell! conflicting hopes and fears,
Whose lights and shades, alternate, dwell!
How bright th' unchanging morn appears!
Farewell! inconstant world! Farewell!
Its duty done, as sinks the clay,
Light from its load the spirit flies;
While heaven and earth combine to say,
Sweet is the scene when Virtue dies.

title: Hail, Father, whose creating call
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail, Father, whose creating call
JUL Unnumber'd worlds attend;
Jehovah, comprehending all,
Whom none can comprehend!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In light unsearchable enthroned,
Whom angels dimly see;
The fountain of the Godhead own'd,
And foremost of the Three.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
From whom, through an eternal now,
The Son, thine offspring, flow'd;
An everlasting Father, thou,
An everlasting God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nor quite display'd to worlds above,
Nor quite on earth conceal 'd;
By wondrous, unexhausted love,
To mortal man reveal'd.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Supreme and all-sufficient God,
When nature shall expire:
When worlds created by thy nod
Shall perish by thy fire.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Thy name, Jehovah, be adored
By creatures without end;
Whom none but thy essential Word
And Spirit comprehend.

title: In steadfast faith on thee I call
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In steadfast faith on thee I call,
Saviour, and Sovereign Lord of all,
My Brother, and my Friend;
Lead me my few remaining days,
And finish thy great work of grace,
And love me to the end.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Till I from all my sins am freed,
O may I lean my languid head,
On thy dear, loving breast:
Thou, Jesu, catch my parting breath,
And let me smoothly glide through death,
To my eternal rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Saviour, bring near the joyful hour,
The fulness of thy Spirit pour,
And while I here remain,
Christ let it be that lives, not I:
Or now, permit me now to die;
To die is greatest gain.
4. Come, then, my health, my hope, my home,
My love, my life eternal, come,
Me to thyself receive;
Soul, flesh, and spirit sanctify,
And bid me live in thee to die,
And die in thee to live.

title: Great is our Redeeming Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great is our Redeeming Lord.
In power, and truth, and grace;
Him, by highest heaven adored,
His church on earth doth praise;
In the city of our God,
In his holy mount below,
Publish, spread his name abroad,
And all his greatness show.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For thy loving-kindness, Lord,
We in thy temple stay;
Here thy faithful love record.
Thy saving power display:
With thy name thy praise is known,
Glorious thy perfections shine;
Earth's remotest bounds shall own
Thy works are all divine.
,.? See the gospel church secure,
And founded on a rock:
W Her bulwarks who can shock?
Count her every precious shrine;
Tell, to after-ages tell,
Fortified by power divine,
The church can never fail.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sion's God is all our own,
Who on his love rely;
We his pardoning love have known,
And live to Christ, and die:
To the New Jerusalem
He our faithful guide shall be;
Him we claim, and rest in him,
Through all eternity.

title: Great God, to Thee we raise
author: J Dryden J

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Messiah, joy of every heart
author: Dbyden J

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Bent to redeem a sinful race,
Thou, Lord, with unexampled grace,
Into our lower world didst come,
And stoop to a poor virgin's womh;
Whom all the heavens cannot contain,
Our God appeared a child of man!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When thou hadst render'd up thy breath,
And dying drawn the sting of death,
Thou didst from earth triumphant rise,
And ope the portals of the skies,
That all who trust in thee alone
Might follow and partake thy throne.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Wherefore we now for mercy pray,
O Saviour, take our sins away!
Before thou as our Judge appear,
In dreadful majesty severe,
Appear our Advocate with God,
And save the purchase of thy blood.
f) Hallow, and make thy servants meet,
And with thy saints in glory seat
Sustain and bless us by thy sway,
And keep to that tremendous day,
When all thy church shall chant above
The new eternal song of love.

title: Saviour, we now rejoice in hope
author: Dryden

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Still let us, Lord, with grace be blest,
Who in thy guardian mercy rest:
Extend thy mercy's arms to me,
The weakest soul that trusts in thee;
And never let me lose thy love,
Till I, ev'n I, am crown'd above.

title: The spacious firmament on high
author: T   Addison

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The spacious firmament on high,
I With all the blue ethereal sky,
And spangled heavens, a shining frame,
Their great Original proclaim.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The' unwearied sun, from day to day,
Does his Creator's power display;
And publishes to every land
The work of an almighty hand.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soon as the evening shades prevail,
The moon takes up the wondrous tale;
And nightly to the list'ning earth
Kepeats the story of her birth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Whilst all the stars that round her burn,
And all the planets in their turn,
Confirm the tidings as they roll,
And spread the truth from pole to pole.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
In reason's ear they all rejoice,
And utter forth a glorious voice;
For ever singing as they shine,
"The hand that made us is divine."
dr. watts.] HYMN"573. l. m. (38)

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
/ OD is a name my soul adores,
VJT The' almighty Three, the' eternal One;
Nature and grace, with all their powers,
Confess the Infinite unknown.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Thy voice produced the sea and spheres,
Bade the waves roar and planets shine:
But nothing like Thyself appears
Through all these spacious works of thine.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Still restless nature dies and grows,
From change to change the creatures run
Thy Being no succession knows,
And all thy vast designs are one.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
A glance of thine runs through the globes,
Kules the bright worlds, and moves their
frame;
Broad sheets of light compose thy robes,
Thy guards are formed of living flame.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
How shall polluted mortals dare
To sing thy glory or thy grace?
Beneath thy feet we lie so £ir,
And see but shadows of thy face.

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
Who can behold the blazing light?
Who can approach consuming flame?
None but thy Wisdom knows thy might,
None but thy Word can speak thy name.

title: The Lord Jehovah reigns
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord Jehovah reigns,
His throne is built on high;
The garments he assumes
Are light and majesty:
His glories shine with beams so bright,
No mortal eye can bear the sight.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
And can this sovereign King
Of glory condescend?
And will he write his name,
My Father and my Friend?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
love his name, I love his word:
Join all my powers and Draise the Lord.

title: High in the heavens, eternal God
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
High in the heavens, eternal God,
Thy goodness in full glory shines;
Thy truth shall break through every cloud
That veils and darkens thy designs.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy providence is kind and large,
Both man and beast thy bounty share;
The whole creation is thy charge,
But saints are thy peculiar care.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My God, how excellent thy grace,
Whence all our hope and comfort springs!
The sons of Adam in distress
Fly to the shadow of thy wings.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Life, like a fountain rich and free,
Springs from the presence of the Lord;
And in thy light our souls shall see
The glories promised in thy word.

title: With glory clad, with strength array'd
author: Tate  And  Brady

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With glory clad, with strength array'd,
The Lord that o'er all nature reigns,
The world's foundations strongly laid,
And the vast fabric still sustains.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How sure established is thy throne,
Which shall no change or period see!
For thou, O Lord, and thou alone,
Art King from all eternity.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The floods, O Lord, lift up their voice,
And toss their troubled waves on high:
But God above can still their noise,
And make the angry sea comply.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy promise, Lord, is ever sure:
And they that in thy house would dwell,
That happy station to secure,
Must still in holiness excel.

title: The earth and all her fulness owns
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The earth and all her fulness owns
Jehovah for her sovereign Lord;
The countless myriads of her sons
Eose into being at his word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His word did out of nothing call
The world, and founded all that is:
Launch 'd on the floods this solid ball,
And fix'd it in the floating seas.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But who shall quit this low abode,
Who shall ascend the heavenly place,
And stand upon the mount of God,
And see his Maker face to face?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The man whose hands and heart are cler.ii
That blessed portion shall receive;
Who here by grace is saved from sin,
Hereafter shall in glory live.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He shall obtain the starry crown;
And, number'd with the saints above,
The God of his salvation own,
The God of his salvation love.

title: Come, sound his praise abroad
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, sound his praise abroad,
And hymns of glory sing;
Jehovah is the sovereign God,
The universal King.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
To-day attend his voice,
Nor dare provoke his rod;
Come, as the people of his choice,
And own your gracious God.

title: How lovely are thy tents, O Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How lovely are thy tents, O Lord!
JZL Where'er thou choosest to record
Thy name, or place thy house of prayer,
My soul outflies the angel-choir,
And faints, o'erpower'd with strong desire,
To meet thy special presence there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Happy the men to whom 'tis given,
To dwell within that gate of heaven,
And in thy house record thy praise;
Whose strength and confidence thou art,
Who feel thee, Saviour, in their heart,
'J 'he Way, the Truth, the Life of grace:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
m
3 Who, passing through the mournful vale,
Drink comfort from the living well,
That flows replenish' d from ahove;
From strength to strength advancing here,
Till all hefore their God appear,
And each receives the crown of love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Better a day thy courts within,
Than thousands in the tents of sin;
How base the noblest pleasures there!
How great the weakest child of thine!
His meanest task is all divine,
And kings and priests thy servants are.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
T OED God, the Holy Ghost!
1 J In this accepted hour,
As on the day of Pentecost,
Descend in all thy power;
We meet with one accord,
In this thy holy place,
And wait the promise of our Lord,
The Spirit of all grace.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Like mighty rushing wind
Upon the waves beneath,
Move with one impulse every mind,
One soul, one feeling breathe: —
The young, the old inspire,
With wisdom from above;
And give us hearts and tongues of fug
To pray, and praise, and love

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Spirit of Light! explore.
And chase our gloom away,
With lustre shining more and more
Unto the perfect day:
Spirit of Truth! he Thou
In life and death our guide;
O Spirit of adoption! Now
May we be sanctified.

title: My soul, inspired with sawed love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Long as my God shall lend me breath,
My every pulse shall beat for him,
And when my voice is lost in death,
My spirit shall resume the theme;
The gracious theme, for ever new,
Through all eternity pursue.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
True to his everlasting word,
He loves the injured to redress;
Poor helpless souis the bounteous Lord
Eelieves, and fills with plenteousness:
He sets the mournful prisoners free,
He bids the blind their Saviour see.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Lord thy God, O Sion, reigns,
Supreme in mercy as in power,
The endless theme of heavenly strains,
When time and death shall be no more:
And all eternity shall prove
Too short to utter all his love.

title: Great God, attend, while Sion sings
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God, attend, while Sion sings
VJT The joy that from thy presence springs
To spend one day with thee on earth
Exceeds a thousand days of mirth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Might I enjoy the meanest place
Within thine house, O God of grace;
Not tents of ease, nor thrones of power,
Should tempt my feet to leave thy door.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
All needful grace will God bestow,
And crown that grace with glory too:
He gives us all things, and withholds
No real good from upright souls.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O God our King, whose sovereign sway
The glorious hosts of heaven obey,
And devils at thy presence flee,
Blest is the man that trusts in thee.

title: Sweet is the work, my God, my King
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet is the work, my God, my King,
To praise thy name, give thanks, and sing;
To show thy love by morning light,
And talk of all thy truth at night.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet is the day of sacred rest,
No mortal cares distract my breast;
O may my heart in tune be found,
Like David's harp of solemn sound.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My heart shall triumph in the Lord,
And bless his works, and bless his word:
Thy works of grace, how bright they shine!
How deep thy counsels, how divine!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
But I shall share a glorious part,
When grace hath well refined my heart;
And fresh supplies of joy are shed,
Like holy oil, to cheer my head.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Then shall I see, and hear, and know
All I desired and wish'd below;
And every power find sweet employ
In that eternal world of joy.

title: Great is the Lord our God
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great is the Lord our God,
And let his praise be great;
He makes his churches his abode,
His most delightful seat.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
These temples of his grace,
How beautiful they stand!
The honours of our native place,
And bulwarks of our land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In Sion God is known
A refuge in distress;
How bright has his salvation shone
Through all her palaces!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In every new distress
We '11 to his house repair;
We'll think upon his wondrous grace,
And seek deliverance there.

title: Great God, this hallow'd day of thine
author: Miss  A   Steel

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God, this hallow'd day of thine
Demands our souls' collected powers;
May we employ in works divine
These solemn and devoted hours:
O may our souls adoring own
The grace which calls us to thy throne!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hence, ye vain cares and trifles, fly!
Where God resides, appear no more:
Omniscient Lord, thy piercing eye
Doth every secret thought explore:
O may thy grace our thoughts refine,
And fix our hearts on things divine!

title: Welcome, sweet day of rest
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Welcome, sweet day of rest,
That saw the Lord ai-ise;
Welcome to this reviving breast,
And these rejoicing eyes!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The King himself comes near,
And feasts his saints to-day;
Here we may sit, and see him here,
And love, and praise, and pray.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One day amidst the place
Where thou, my Lord, hast been,
Is sweeter than ten thousand days
Of pleasurable sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My willing soul would stay
In such a frame as this,
And sit and sing herself away
To everlasting bliss.

title: Lord of the Sabbath, hear our vows
author: 1 R   Doddbidge J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of the Sabbath, hear our vows,
JLi On this thy day, in this thy house;
And own, as grateful sacrifice,
The songs which from the desert rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
No more fatigue, no more distress,
Nor sin, nor hell shall reach the place;
No groans to mingle with the songs
Which warble from immortal tongues.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
O long expected day, begin;
Dawn on these realms of woe and sin:
Fain would we leave this weary road,
And sleep in death, to rest with God.

title: Again our weekly labours end
author: J   Stennett J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Again our weekly labours end,
JLjL And we the Sabbath's call attend;
Improve, our souls, the sacred rest,
And seek to be for ever blest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This day let our devotions rise
To heaven, a grateful sacrifice;
And God that peace divine bestow,
Which none but they who feel it know.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This holy calm within the breast
Prepares for that eternal rest,
Which for the sons of God remains;
The end of cares, the end of pains.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In holy duties, let the day,
In holy pleasures, pass away:
How sweet the Sabbath thus to spend,
In hope of that which ne 'er shall end!

title: O render thanks to God above
author: Tate  And  Brady J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O render thanks to God above,
The fountam of eternal love,
Whose mercy firm through ages past
Hath stood, and shall for ever last.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who can his mighty deeds express,
Not only vast but numberless?
What mortal eloquence can raise
His tribute of immortal praise?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Extend to me that favour, Lord,
Thou to thy chosen dost afford:
When thou return 'st to set them free,
Let thy salvation visit me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O may I worthy prove to see
Thy saints in full prosperity;
That I the joyful choir may join,
And count thy people's triumph mine.
D Let Israel's God he ever bless'd,
His name eternally confess'd;
Let all his saints with full accord
In solemn hymns proclaim their Lord.

title: Far as creation's bounds extend
author: J   Merrick  J

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The splendours of thy kingdom tell,
Delighted on thy wonders dwell;
And bid the world's wide realms admire
The glories of the' Almighty Sire,
Whose throne shall nature's wreck survive,
Whose power through endless ages live.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
From thee, great God, while every eye
Expectant waits the wish'd supply,
Their bread proportion' d to the day
Thy opening hands to each convey;
In every sorrow of the heart,
Eternal mercy bears a part.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Paternal depth of love divine
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Paternal depth of love divine,
In Jesus, God with us, display'd;
How bright thy beaming glories shine!
How wide thy healing streams are spread I

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With whom dost thou delight to dwell?
Sinners, a vile and thankless race;
O God, what tongue aright can tell
How vast thy love, how great thy grace!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The dictates of thy sovereign will
With joy our grateful hearts receive:
All thy delight in us fulfil;
Lo! all we are to thee we give.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To thy sure love, thy tender care,
Our flesh, soul, spirit, we resign;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
fix thy sacred presence there,
And seal the' abode for ever thine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O King of glory, thy rich grace
Our short desire surpasses far;
Yea, even our crimes, though numberless,
Less numerous than thy mercies are.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Still, Lord, thy saving health display,
And arm our souls with heavenly zeal;
So fearless shall we urge our way
Through all the powers of earth and hell.

title: Let every tongue thy goodness speak
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let every tongue thy goodness speak,
Thou sovereign Lord of all;
Thy strengthening hands uphold the weak,
And raise the poor that fall.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When sorrows bow the spirit down,
Or virtue lies distress'*!
Beneath the proud oppressor's frown,
Thou giv'st the mourner rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Lord supports our infant days,
And guides our giddy youth;
Holy and just are all thy ways,
And all thy words are truth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou know'st the pains thy servants feel,
Thou hear'st thy children cry;
And their best wishes to fulfil,
Thy grace is ever nigh.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy mercy never shall remove
From men of heart sincere;
Thou sav'st the souls whose humble love
Is join'd with holy fear.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
My lips shall dwell upon thy praise,
And spread thy fame abroad:
Let all the sons of Adam raise
The honours of their God!

title: God is the God we adore
author: J   Hart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God is the God we adore,
I Our faithful, unchangeable Friend;
Whose love is as great as his power,
And neither knows measure nor end.
' Tis Jesus, the First and the Last,
Whose Spirit shall guide us safe home
We'll praise him for all that is past,
And trust him for all that's to come.

title: Sweet is the memory of thy grace
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet is the memory of thy grace,
O My God, my heavenly King;
Let age to age thy righteousness
In sounds of glory sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God reigns on high, but not confines
His goodness to the skies:
Through the whole earth his bounty shines,
And every want supplies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With longing eyes the creatures wait
On thee, for daily food;
Thy liberal hand provides them meat,
And fills their mouths with good.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How kind are thy compassions, Lord!
How slow thine anger moAres!
But soon he sends his pard'ning word,
To cheer the soul he loves.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Creatures, with all their endless race,
Thy power and praise proclaim;
But we, who taste thy richer grace,
Delight to bless thy name.

title: In all my vast concerns with thee
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In all my vast concerns with thee,
In vain my soul would try
To shun thy presence, Lord, or flee
The notice of thine eye.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy all-surrounding sight surveys
My rising and my rest,
My public walks, my private ways,
The secrets of my breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My thoughts lie open to thee, Lord,
Before they're form'd within;
And, ere my lips pronounce the word,
Thou know'st the sense I mean.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O wondrous knowledge, deep and high 1
Where can a creature hide?
Within thy circling arms I lie,
Beset on every side.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
So let thy grace surround me still,
And like a bulwark prove,
To guard my soul from every ill,
Secured by sovereign love.

title: Guide me, O thou great Jehovah
author: T   Olivers

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Guide me, O thou great Jehovah,
Pilgrim through this barren land:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
am weak, but thou art mighty,
Hold me with thy powerful hand:
Bread of heaven,
Feed me till I want no more.
? Open thou the crystal fountain,
Whence the healing streams do flow j
Let the fiery cloudy pillar
Lead me all my journey through;
Strong deliverer,
Be thou still my help and shield.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text: will ever give to thee.

title: When all thy mercies, O my God
author: Iddison

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When all thy mercies, O my God,
My rising soul surveys,
Transported with the view, I'm lost
In wonder, love, and praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy Providence my life sustain'd,
And all my wants redress'd,
While in the silent womb I lay,
And hung upon the breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To all my weak complaints and cries
Thy mercy lent an ear,
Ere yet my feeble thoughts had learn'd
To form themselves in prayer.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Unnumber'd comforts on my soul
Thy tender care bestow'd,
Before my infant heart conceived
From whom those comforts flow'd.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When in the slippery paths of youth
With heedless steps I ran,
Thine arm, unseen, convey'd me safe,
And led me up to man.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Through hidden dangers, toils, and der
It gently clear'd my way;
And through the pleasing snares of vice,
More to be fear'd than they.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Through every period of my life
Thy goodness I'll pursue;
And after death, in distant worlds,
The pleasing theme renew.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Through all eternity, to thee
A grateful song I'll raise;
But O eternity's too short
To utter all thy praise!

title: The Lord, how wondrous are his ways
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord, how wondrous are his ways!
How firm his word, how large his grace!
Goodness and Truth surround his throne,
And thence he makes his mercy known.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
High as his mighty arm hath spread
The starry heavens ahove our head,
His bounteous love exceeds our praise,-
Exceeds the highest hopes we raise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nor half so far hath nature placed
The rising morning from the west,
As his forgiving grace removes
The daily guilt of those he loves.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How slowly doth his wrath arise!
On swifter wings salvation flies;
And if he bids his anger burn,
How soon his frowns to pity turn!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The mighty God, the wise and just,
Knows that our frame is feeble dust
And will no load on us impose
Beyond the strength that he bestows.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
For his eternal love is sure
To all the saints, and shall endure:
From age to age his truth shall reign,
Nor children's children hope in vain.

title: Father of earth and sky
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of earth and sky,
Thy name we magnify:
O that earth and heaven might join.
Thy perfections to proclaim;
Praise the attributes divine,
Fear and love thy awful name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When shall thy Spirit reign
In every heart of man?
Father, bring the kingdom near,
Honour thy triumphant Son;
God of heaven, on earth appear,
Fix with us thy glorious throne.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy good and holy will,
Let all on earth fulfil
Men with minds angelic vie,
Saints below with saints above,
Thee to praise and glorify,
Thee to serve with perfect love.
This day with this day's bread
Thy hungry children feed;
Fountain of ail blessings, grant
Now the manna from above;
Now supply our bodies' want,
Now sustain our souls with love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our trespasses forgive:
And when absolved we live,
Thou our life of grace maintain;
Lest we from our God depart,
Lose thy pardoning grace again,
Grant us a forgiving heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6

title: With pitying eyes, the Prince of Peace
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With pitying eyes, the Prince of Peace
Beheld our helpless grief;
He saw, and —O amazing love!
He ran to our relief.
«-$ Down from the shining seats above
With joyful haste he fled;
Enter' d the grave in mortal flesh,
And dwelt among the dead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O for this love let rocks and hills
Their lasting silence break,
And all harmonious human tongues
The Saviour's praises speak!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Angels, assist our mighty joys,
Strike all your harps of gold;
But when you raise your highest notes,
His love can ne'er be told.

title: Who can describe the joys that rise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Who can describe the joys that rise
Through all the courts of Paradise,
To see a prodigal return,
To see an heir of glory bom!
