sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With joy the Father doth approve
The fruit of his eternal love;
The Son with joy looks down, and sees
The purchase of his agonies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Spirit takes delight to view
The contrite soul he for.ins anew;
And saints and angels join to sing
The growing empire of their King,

title: Great God, indulge my humble claim
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God, indulge my humble claim;
Be thou my hope, my joy, my rest:
The glories that compose thy name
Stand all engaged to make me bless'd.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou great and good, thou just and wise,
Thou art my Father and my God;
And I am thine, by sacred ties,
Thy son, thy servant bought with blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With heart, and eyes, and lifted hands,
For thee I long, to thee I look;
As travellers in thirsty lands
Pan! for the cooling water-brook.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Should I from thee, my God, remove,
Life could no lasting joy afford:
My peace, the sense of pard'ning love;
My guard, the presence of my Lord.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I'll lift my hands, I'll raise my voice,
While I have breath to pray or praise;
This work shall make mv heart rejoice,
And fill the remnant of my days.

title: My heart is fix'd, O God, my heart
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My heart is fix'd, O God, my heart
Is fix'd to triumph in thy grace:
(Aw nice, my lute, and bear a part:)
My glory is to sing thy praise,
Till of thy nature I partake,
And bright in all thine image wake.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: All of his wondrous faithfulness
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All of his wondrous faithfulness,
And sound his power abroad;
Sing the sweet promise of his grace,
And the performing God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Proclaim salvation from the Lord,
For wretched, dying men:
His hand hath writ the sacred word
With an immortal pen.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Engraved as in eternal brass,
The mighty promise shines;
Nor can the powers of darkness rase
Those everlasting lines.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His every word of grace is strong,
As that which built the skies;
The voice that rolls the stars along
Speaks all the promises.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
How would my fainting heart rejoic
To know thy favour sure:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
trust the all- creating voice,
And faith desires no more.

title: Come, thou everlasting King
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou everlasting King,
Accept the tribute which we bring j
Accept thy well-deserved renown,
And wear our praises as thy crown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let every act of worship be
Like our espousals, Lord, to thee;
Like that blest hour when from above
We first received the pledge of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The gladness of that happy day,
O may it ever, ever stay!
Nor let our faith forsake its hold,
Our hope decline, our love grow cold.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Each following moment as it flies,
Increase thy praise, improve our joys,
Till we are raised to sing thy name,
At the great supper of the Lamb.

title: Hail, God the Son, in glory crown'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail, God the Son, in glory crown'd,
Ere time began to be;
Throned with thy Sire, through half the round
Of vast eternity.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let heaven and earth's stupendous frame
Display their Author's power;
And each exalted seraph-flame,
Creator, thee adore.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy wondrous grace the Godhead show'd
In love's redeeming plan,
The co-eternal Son of God,
The mortal son of man-

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To save us from our lost estate,
Behold his life-blood stream:
Hail, Lord, almighty to create,
Almighty to redeem!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Mediator's God-like sway
His church on earth sustains;
Till nature shall her Judge survey,
The King Messiah reigns.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Hail, with essential glory crown'd,
When time shall cease to be;
Throned with thy Father through the round
Of whole eternity.

title: Hark, the herald-angels sing
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark, the herald-angels sing
Glory to the new-born King,
"Peace on earth, and mercy mild,
God and sinners reconciled."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ, by highest heaven adored,
Christ, the everlasting Lord,
Late in time behold him come,
Offspring of a virgin's womb,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Veil'd in flesh the Godhead see;
Hail the' incarnate Deity!
Pleased as man with men to' appear,
Jesus our Immanuel here.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hail the heaven-born Prince of Peace,
Hail the Sun of Righteousness!
Light and life to all he brings,
Risen with healing in his wings.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Mild he lays his glory by,
Born that man no more may die;
Born to raise the sons of earth,
Born to give them second birth.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Come, Desire of Nations, come,
Fix in us thy humble home;
Eise, the woman's conquering Seed,
Bruise in us the Serpent's head.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Adam's likeness now efface,
Stamp thine image in its place:
Second Adam from above,
Ee-instate us in thy love.

title: Hark, the glad sound! the Saviour comes
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark, the glad sound! the Saviour comes!
The Saviour promis'd long!
Let every heart prepare a throne,
And every voice a song.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On him the Spirit, largely pour'd,
Exerts his sacred fire;
Wisdom and might, and zeal and love,
His holy breast inspire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He comes the prisoners to release,
In Satan's bondage held;
The gates of brass before bun burst,
The iron fetters yield.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He comes, from thickest films of vice
To clear the mental ray,
And on the eyes opprest with night,
To pour celestial day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He comes the broken heart to bind,
The bleeding soul to cure,
And with the treasures of his grace
To' enrich the humble poor.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Our glad hosannas, Prince of Peace,
Thy welcome shall proclaim;
And heaven's eternal arches ring
With thy beloved name.

title: Bright and joyful is the morn
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bright and joyful is the morn,
For unto us a Child is born;
From the highest realms of heaven,
Unto us a Son is given.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On his shoulders He shall bear
Power and majesty; —andwear
On his vesture, and his thigh,
Names most awful, names most high.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wonderful in counsel He;
The Incarnate Deity,
Sire of ages ne'er to cease,
King of Kings, and Prince, of Peace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come and worship at his feet,
Yield to Christ the homage meet,
From his manger to his throne,
Homage due to God alone.

title: Mortals awake, with angels join
author: Ascribed  To  Medley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Mortals awake, with angels join,
And chant the solemn lay;
Joy, love, and gratitude combine
To hail the ' auspicious day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hark! the cherubic armies shout,
And glory leads the song;
Good will and peace are heard throughout
Th' harmonious, heavenly throng.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With joy the chorus we repeat,
"Glory to God on high! "
Good will and peace are now complete,
Jesus was born to die.
Hail! Prince of Life! for ever hail!
Eedeemer, Brother, Friend!
Though earth, and time, and life shall fan
Thy praise shall never end.

title: Light of those whose dreary dwelling
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Light of those whose dreary dwelling
JLj Borders on the shades of death,
Come, and by thy love revealing,
Dissipate the clouds beneath:
The new heaven and earth's Creator,
In our deepest darkness rise,
Scattering all the night of nature,
Pouring eye-sight on our eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
thou mild, pacific Prince;
Give the knowledge of salvation,
Give the pardon of our sins:
By thy all -restoring merit,
Every burden 'd soul release;
Every weary, wandering spirit
Guide into thy perfect peace.

title: Glory be to God on high
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glory be to God on high,
And peace on earth descend;
God comes down, he bows the sky,
And shows himself our Friend:
God, the' Invisible appears!
God, the blest, the great I AM,
Sojourns in this vale of tears,
And Jesus is his Name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Him the angels all adored,
Their Maker and their King;
Tidings of their humble Lord
They now to mortals bring.
Emptied of his majesty,
Of his dazzling glories shorn.
Being's Source begins to be,
And God himself is born.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See the' eternal Son of God
A mortal Son of man
Dwelling in an earthly clod,
Whom heaven cannot contain!
Stand amazed, ye heavens, at this;
See the Lord of earth and skies;
Humbled to the dust he is,
And in a manger lies.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"We, the sons of men, rejoice,
The Prince of Peace proclaim;
With heaven's host lift up our voice,
And shout Immanuel's name:
Knees and hearts to him we bow
Of our flesh and of our bone,
Jesus is our Brother now,
And God is all our own

title: Sweet the moments, rich in blessing
author: Robinson  Or  Batty

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet the moments, rich in blessing,
Which before the cross I spend;
Life, and health, and peace possessing,
From the sinner's dying Friend:
Here I '11 sit, for ever viewing
Mercy's streams, in streams of blood;
Precious drops, my soul bedewing,
Plead and claim my peace with God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Truly blessed is this station,
Low before the cross to lie;
While I see divine compassion
Floating in his languid eye:
Here it is I find my heaven,
While upon the Lamb I gaze:
Love I much? I've much forgiven,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'm a miracle of grace!
3 Love and grief my heart dividing,
With my tears his feet I '11 bathe;
Constant, still, in faith abiding,
Life deriving from his death.
May I still enjoy this feeling,
In all need to Jesus go;
Prove his wounds each day more healing,
And himself more deeply know.

title: Angels from the realms of glory
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Angels from the realms of glory,
JJL Wing your flight o'er all the earth
Ye, who sang creation's story,
Now proclaim Messiah's birth:
Come and worship,
Worship Christ, the new-born King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shepherds, in the field abiding,
Watching o'er your flocks by night,
God with man is now residing;
Yonder shines the infant light:
Come and worship,
"Worship Christ, the new-born King.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sages, leave your contemplations,
Brighter visions beam afar,
Seek the great Desire of Nations,
Ye have seen his natal star;
Come and worship,
Worship Christ, the new-born King.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Saints, before the altar bending,
Waiting long with hope and fear,
Suddenly the Lord descending,
In his temple shall appear:
Come and worship,
Worship Christ, the new-born King.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sinners, wrung with true repentance,
Doom'd for guilt to endless pain,
Justice now repeals the sentence,
Mercy calls you, —break your chains:
Come and worship,
Worship Christ, the new-born King.

title: O God of gods, in whom combine
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
All things in earth, and air, and sea.
Exist, and live, and move in thee:
All nature tremhles at thy voice:
With awe even we thy children prove
Thy power: O let us taste thy love!
So evermore shall we rejoice.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O powerful Love! to thee we bow;
Object of all our wishes thou,
Our hearts are naked to thine eye:
For thee, who from the' eternal throne
Cam'st emptied of thy glory down,
For us to groan, to bleed, to die.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
O Love! our stubborn wills subdue,
Create our ruin'd frame anew,
Dispel our darkness by thy light;
Into all truth our spirit guide,
And from our eyes for ever hide
All things displeasing in thy sight.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: There is a fountain fill'd with blood
author: William Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a fountain fill'd with blood
Drawn from Emmanuel's veins;
And sinners plunged beneath that flood,
Lose all their guilty stains.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The dying thief rejoiced to see
That fountain in his day;
And there have I, as vile as he,
Wash'd all my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Dear dying Lamb, thy precious blood
Shall never lose its power,
Till all the ransom' d church of God
Be saved to sin no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
E'er since, by faith, I saw the stream
Thy flowing wounds supply,
Redeeming love bas been my theme.
And shall be till I die.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then, in a nobler, sweeter song,
I'll sing thy power to save;
When this poor lisping, stammering tongue,
Lies silent in the grave.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Lord I believe thou hast prepared
(Unworthy though I be)
For me a blood-bought free reward,
A golden harp for me!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
' Tis Strang, and tuned, tor endless years,
And form 'd by power divine;
To sound in God the Father's ears
No other Name but thine.

title: Fain would we love the God we fear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fain would we love the God we fear,
The Lord of earth and heaven,
And feel the grace of which we hear,
And know our sins forgiven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our sins, though great and numberless,
We now at last believe,
O Son of Man, O Prince of Peace,
Thou canst on earth forgive.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, then, the saving grace impart,
Remove the mountain-load,
Inspeak thy peace into our heart
Which pants to feel thy blood.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy Spirit let us now receive,
And Abba, Father, cry,
And happy in thy service live,
And in thy service die.

title: From whence these dire portents around
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From whence these dire portents around,
That heaven and earth amaze?
Wherefore do earthquakes cleave the ground?
Why hides the sun his rays?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not thus did Sinai's trembling head
With sacred horror nod,
Beneath the dark pavilion spread
Of legislative God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou Earth, thy lowest centre shake,
With Jesus sympathize!
Thou Sun, as hell's deep gloom be black,
' Tis thy Creator dies!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
See, streaming from the' accursed tree,
His all-atoning blood!
Is this the Infinite? —' Tis he!
My Saviour and my God!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
For me these pangs his soul assail,
For me the death is borne;
My sins gave sharpness to the nail,
And pointed every thorn.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: 'Tis finish'd! The Messiah dies
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Tis finish'd! The Messiah dies,
Cut off for sms, hut not his own;
Accomplish'd is the sacrifice,
The great redeeming work is done.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Saved from the legal curse I am,
My Saviour hangs on yonder tree:
See there the meek, expiring Lamb!
'Tis finish 'd! He expires for me.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Accepted in the Well-beloved,
And clothed in righteousness divine

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
see the bar to heaven removed;
And all thy merits, Lord, are mine.

sections.label: Verse 9

title: But Christ, the heavenly Lamb
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
But Christ, the heavenly Lamb,
Takes all our sins away;
A Sacrifice of nobler name,
And richer blood than they.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Believing, we rejoice
To feel the curse remove;
We bless the Lamb, with cheerful voice,
And sing his bleeding love.
A]

title: For what you have done
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For what you have done.
His blood must atone:
The Father hath punish;d for you his dear Son.
The Lord, in the day
Of his anger, did lay
Your sins on the Lamb; and he bore them away,

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
He dies to atone
For sins not his own;
Your debt he hath paid, and your work he hath
done.
Ye all may receive
The peace he did leave,
Who made intercession, "My Father, forgive I"

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For you and for me
He pray 'd on the tree:
The prayer is accepted, the sinner is free.
That sinner am I,
Who on Jesus rely,
And come for the pardon God cannot deny.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My pardon I claim,
For a sinner I am:
A sinner believing in Jesus 's name.
He purchased the grace
Which now I embrace:
Q Father, thou know'st he hath died in my place

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
His death is my plea;
My Advocate see,
A.nd hear the blood speak that hath answer 'd
for me:
Acquitted I was
When he bled on the cross:
A.nd by losing his life he hath carried my cause.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text: o

title: Thou very Paschal Lamb
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou very Paschal Lamb,
I Whose blood for tis was shed,
Through whom we out of Egypt came,
Thy ransom 'd people lead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Angel of gospel grace,
Fulfil thy character:
To guard and feed the chosen race,
In Israel's camp appear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Throughout the desert way,
Conduct us by thy light;
Be thou a cooling cloud by day,
A cheering fire by night.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our fainting souls sustain
With blessings from above:
And ever on thy people rain
The manna of thy love.

title: This, this is He that came
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
This, this is He that came
I By water and by blood I
Jesus is our atoning Lamb,
Our sanctifying God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See from his wounded side
The mingled current flow!
The water and the blood applied
Shall wash us white as snow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The water cannot cleanse,
Before the blood we feel,
To purge the guilt of all our sin-j
And our forgiveness seal.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But both in Jesus join,
Who speaks our sins forgiven,
And gives the purity divine
That makes us meet for heaven.

title: O thou, whose offering on the tree
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou, whose offering on the tree
The legal offerings all foreshow 'd,
Borrow 'd their whole effect from thee,
And drew their virtue from thy blood:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The blood of goats, and bullocks slain,
Could never for one sin atone:
To purge the guilty offerer's stain,
Thine was the work and thine alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Tain in themselves their duties were,
Their services could never please,
Till join'd with thine, and made to share
The merit of thy righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Forward they cast a faithful look,
On tby approaching sacrifice;
And thence their pleasing savour took,
And rose accepted in the skies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Those feeble types, and shadows old,
Are all in thee, the Truth, fulfill 'd;
And in thy dying love behold
The substance of those rites reveal 'd.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
By faith we see thy sufferings past
In this mysterious rite brought back:
And on thy grand oblation cast,
Its saving benefits partake.

title: Behold the sure foundation-stone
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold the sure foundation-stone
Which God in Sion lays,
To bnild our heavenly hopes upon,
And his eternal praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Chosen of God, to sinners dear,
The saints adore thy name;
They trust their whole salvation here,
Nor can they suffer shame.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The foolish builders, scribe and priest,
Reject it with disdain;
Yet on this Rock the church shall rest,
And envy rage in vain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What though the gates of hell withstood,
Yet must this building rise:
' Tis thine own work, almighty God,
And wondrous hi our eyes.

title: Jesus, thy Sovereign Name I bless
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thy Sovereign Name I bless!
Sorrow is joy, and pain is ease
To those that trust in thee:
All things together work for good,
To me, the purchase of thy blood,
The much-loved sinner me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As sure as now thy cross I bear,
I shall the heavenly kingdom share,
And take my seat above;
Celestial joy is in this pain,
It tells me I with thee shall reign,
In everlasting love.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
So be it then, if thou ordain.
Crowd all my happy life with pain,
And let me daily die:

sections.label: Verse 5

title: When I can read my title clear
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I can read my title clear
To mansions in the skies,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
bid farewell to every fear,
And wipe my weeping eyes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Should earth against my soul engage,
And hellish darts be hurl'd,
Then I can smile at Satan's rage,
And face a frowning world.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let cares like a wild deluge come,
And storms of sorrow fall,
May I but safely reach my home,
My God, my heaven, my all.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There shall I bathe my weary soul
In seas of heavenly rest,
And not a wave of trouble roll
Across my peaceful breast.

title: When I survey the wondrous cross
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I survey the wondrous cross,
On which the Prince of glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the death of Christ, my God:
All the vain things that charm me most,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
sacrifice them to his blood.
3 See, from his head, his hands, his feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down:
Did e'er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so amazing, so divine,
Demands my soul, my life, my all.

title: Rock of Ages, cleft for me
author: Augustus Toplady

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Jlj Let me hide myself in thee;
Let the water and the hlood,
From thy wounded side which flow'd,
Be of sin the double cure,
Save from wrath and make me pure.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Could my tears for ever flow,
Could my zeal no languor know,
These for sin could not atone;
Thou must save, and thou alone:
In my hand no price I bring,
Simply to thy cross I cling.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While I draw this fleeting breath,
When my eyelids close in death,
When I rise to worlds unknown,
And behold thee on thy throne, —
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in thee.

title: Angels rejoice in Jesu's grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Or, 'stablish'd and confirai'd by him
Who did our fallen world redeem,
Secure they hold their blest estate,
Firm on an everlasting seat;
Or, raised above themselves aspire,
In bliss improved, in glory higher.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Him they beheld our conquering God,
Keturn'd with garments roll'd in blood!
They saw, and kindled at the sight,
And fill'd with shouts the realms of light;
With loudest hallelujahs met,
And fell, and kiss'd his bleeding feet.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Jesus, to thee we fly
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, to thee we fly,
On thee for help rely:
Thou our only refuge art,
Thou dost all our fears control,
Eest of every trouhled heart,
Life of every dying soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We lift our joyful eyes,
And see the dazzling prize,
See the purchase of thy hlood,
Freely now to sinners given;
Thou the living way hast show'd,
Thou to us hast open'd heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We now, divinely hold,
Of thy reward lay hold:
All thy glorious joy is ours,
All the treasures of thy love;
Now we taste the heavenly powers,
Now we reign with thee above.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
By faith already there,
In thee our Head, we are;
With our great Forerunner we
Now in heavenly places sit,
Banquet with the Deity,
See the world beneath our feet.
Thou art our flesh and bone,
Thou art to heaven gone;
Gone, that we might all pursue,
Closely in thy footsteps tread;
Gone, that we might follow too,
Eeign triumphant with our Head.

title: Enter' d the holy place above
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Enter' d the holy place above,
Jul Cover'd with meritorious scars,
The tokens of his dying love,
Our great High Priest in glory bears;
He pleads his passion on the tree,
He shows himself to God for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
This instant now I may receive
The answer of his powerful prayer:
This instant now by him I live,
His prevalence with God declare;
And soon my spirit, in his hands,
Shall stand where my Forerunner stands.

title: Ye humble souls that seek the Lord
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye humble souls that seek the Lord,
Chase all your fears away;
And bow with pleasure down to see
The place where Jesus lay. ]

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thus low the Lord of Life was brought;
Such wonders love can do:
Thus cold in d»ath that bosom lay,
Which throbb'd and bled for you.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then raise your eyes, and tune your songs,
The Saviour lives again:
Not all the bolts and bars of death
The Conqueror could detain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
High o'er the' angelic bands he rears
His once dishonour 'd head;
And he through endless ages reigns,
Who dwelt among the dead.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
With joy like his shall every saint
His vacant tomb survey;
Then rise with his ascending Lord
To realms of endless day.

title: /christ, the Lord, is risen to-day,"
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
/christ, the Lord, is risen to-day,"
Sons of men and angels say!
Raise your joys and triumphs high;
Sing, ye heavens; thou earth reply.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Vain the stone, the watch, the seal,
Christ hath burst the gates of hell:
Death in vain forbids his rise;
Christ hath open'd Paradise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lives again our glorious King!
Where, O death, is now thy sting?
Dying once, he all doth save;
Where's thy victory, boasting grave?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Soar we now, where Christ hath led,
Following our exalted Head;
Made like him, like him we rise,
Ours the cross —the grave —the skies.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
King of glory! Soul of hliss!
Everlasting life is this;
Thee to know, thy power to prove,
Thus to sing, and thus to love.

title: Hail the day that sees Him rise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail the day that sees Him rise
Ravish'd from our wishful eyes!
Christ, awhile to mortals given,
Re-ascends his native heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Circled round with angel powers,
Their triumphant Lord, and ours,
Conqueror over death and sin;
Take the King of glory in!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Him though highest heaven receives,
Still he loves the earth he leaves:
Though returning to his throne,
Still he calls mankind his own.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
See, he lifts his hands ahove!
See, he shows the prints of love!
Hark, his gracious lips bestow
Blessings on his church below!

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
Master, (will we ever say,)
Taken from our bead to-day;
See thy faithful servants, see,
Ever gazing up to thee.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Grant, though parted from our sight,
High above yon azure height,
Grant our hearts may thither rise,
Following thee beyond the skies.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Ever upward let us move,
Wafted on the wings of love;
Looking when our Lord shall come,
Longing, gasping after home.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
There we shall with thee remain,
Partners of thy endless reign;
There thy face unclouded see,
Fmd our heaven of heavens in thee.

title: Sons of God, triumphant, rise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sons of God, triumphant, rise,
Shout the accomplish'd sacrifice!
Shout your sins in Christ forgiven,
Sons of God, and heirs of heaven!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ye that round our altars throng,
Listening angels, join the song;
Sing with us, ye heavenly powers,
Pardon, grace, and glory ours!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Him by faith we taste below,
Mightier joys ordain'd to know,
Him, when fully ours we prove,
Ours tin heaven of oerfect love.

title: Father, God, we glorify
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, God, we glorify
Thy love to Adam's seed;
Love that gave thy Son to die,
And raised him from the dead:
Him for our offences slain,
That we all might pardon find,
Thou hast brought to life again,
The Saviour of mankind.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By thy own right hand of power
Thou hast exalted him,
Sent the mighty Conqueror
Thy people to redeem:
King of saints, and Prince of Peace,
Him thou hast for sinners given,
Sinners from their sins to bless,
And lift them up to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Father, God, to us impart
The gift unspeakable;
Now in every waiting heart
Thy glorious Son reveal:
Quicken' d with our living Lord
Let us in thy Spirit rise,
Rise to all thy life restored,
And praise thee in the skies.
c. wesley. J HYMN 638 8's. & 7's. (49,58 J
Isa. liii. 6.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
TTAIL, thou once despised Jesus!
XI Hail thou Galilean King!
Who didst suffer to release us;
Who didst free salvation bring.
Hail thou universal Saviour
Bearer of our sin and shame!
By thy merits -we find favour;
Life is given through thy nama

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Paschal Lamb, by God appointed,
All our sins on thee were laid;
By almighty Love anointed,
Thou hast full atonement made:
Every sin may be forgiven,
Through the virtue of thy blood;
Open'd is the gate of heaven,
Peace is made 'twixt man and God.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Jesus, hail! enthroned in glory,
There for ever to abide:
All the heavenly host adore thee,
Seated at thy Father's side:
There for sinners thou art pleading,
Spare them yet another year;
Thou for saints art interceding,
Till in glory they appear.

sections.label: Verse 7

title: What equal honours shall we bring
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What equal honours shall we bring
To thee, O Lord our God, the Lamb?
When all the notes that angels sing
Are far inferior to thv Name
S Worthy is He that once was slain,
The "Prince of Peace, that groan'd and died;
Worthy to rise, and live, and reign
At his almighty Father's side.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Power and dominion are His due
Who stood condemn'd at Pilate's bar;
Wisdom belongs to Jesus too,
Though he was charged with madness here.
Honour immortal must be paid,
Instead of scandal and of scorn;
While glory shines around his head,
And a bright crown without a thorn.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blessing for ever to the Lamb,
Who bore our sin, and curse, and pain;
Let angels sound his sacred Name,
And every creature say, Amen.

title: God in the flesh below
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God in the flesh below,
For us he reigns above:
Let all the nations know
Our Jesu's conquering love!
Join all on earth, rejoice and sing
Glory ascribe to glory's King.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Till all the earth, renew'd
In righteousness divine,
With all the hosts of God
In one great chorus join, —
Join all on earth, rejoice and sing;
Glory ascribe to glory's King.

title: Great God, whose universal sway
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God, whose universal sway
The known and unknown worlds obey,
Now give the kingdom to thy Son;
Extend his power, exalt his throne,

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
With power he vindicates the just,
And treads the' oppressor in the dust:
His worship and his fear shall last
Till the full round of time is past.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
As rain on meadows newly mown,
So shall he send his influence down:
His grace on fainting souls distils,
Like heavenly dew on thirsty hills.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The heathen lands that lie beneath
The shades of overspreading death,
Revive at his first dawning light;
And deserts blossom at the sight.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The saints shall flourish in his days,
Array 'd in robes of joy and praise;
Peace, like a river, from his throne
Shall flow to nations yet unknown.

title: My heart and voice I raise
author: Benj   Rhodes

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
A servant's form he wore,
And in his body bore
Our dreadful curse on Calvary:
He like a victim stood,
And pour'd his sacred blood,
To set the guilty captives free.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But soon the Victor rose
Triumphant o'er his foes,
And led the vanquish'd host in chains:
He threw their empire down,
His foes compell'd to own,
O'er all the great Messiah reigns.
2r

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With mercy's mildest grace,
He governs all our race
In wisdom, righteousness, and love:
Who to Messiah fly
Shall find redemption nigh,
And all his great salvation prove.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Hail, Saviour, Prince of Peace!
Thy kingdom shall increase,
Till all the world thy glory see;
And righteousness abound,
As the great deep profound,
And fill the earth with purity!

title: Jerusalem divine
author: Bknj   Rhodes

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jerusalem divine,
When shall I call thee mine?
And to thy holy hill attain,
Where weary pilgrims rest,
And in thy glories blest,
With God Messiah ever reign?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There saints and angels join
In fellowship divine,
And rapture swells the solemn lay:
While all with one accord
Adore their glorious Lord,
And shout his praise in endless day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
May I but find the grace
To fill an humble place
In that inheritance above;
My tuneful voice I'll raise
In songs of loudest praise,
To r.pxead thy fame, Redeeming Love i
4t Mysterious Deity,
Who ne'er began to be,
To sound thy endless praise be mine!
Reign, true Messiah reign!
Thy kingdom shall remain,
When stars amd sun no more shall shine.

title: My heart is full of Christ, and longs
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My heart is full of Christ, and longs
Its glorious matter to declare!
Of him I make my loftier songs,

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Fairer than all the earth-born race,
Perfect in comeliness thou art;
Eeplenish'd are thy lips with grace,
And full of love thy tender heart:
God ever blest! we bow the knee,
And own all fulness dwells in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Come, and maintain thy righteous caus'r,
And let thy glorious toil succeed j
Dispread the victory of thy cross,
Eide on, and prosper in thy deed;
Through earth triumphantly ride on,
And reign in every heart alone.

title: let us join our cheerful songs
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
let us join our cheerful songs
With angels round the throne;
Ten thousand thousand are their tongues,
But all their joys are one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Worthy the Lamh that died,"they cry,
"To be exalted thus! "
"Worthy the Lamh! "our hearts reply;
"For he was slain for us."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus is worthy to receive
Honour and power divine;
And blessings, more than we can give,
Be, Lord, for ever thine!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The whole creation join in one,
To bless the sacred name
Of Him that sits upon the throne,
And to adore the Lamb.

title: Join all the glorious names
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Join all the glorious names
That ever mortals knew,
That angels ever bore;
All are too mean to speak his worth,
Too mean to set our Saviour forth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But O, what gentle means,
What condescending ways,
Doth our Redeemer use,
To teach his heavenly grace!
My eyes, with joy and wonder see
What forms of love he bears for ras I

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Cloth'd with our mortal flesh
The Cov'nant -Angel stands,
Holds, with the promises,
Our pardon in Lis hands;
Commissioned from his Father's throne
To make his grace to mortals known.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Great Prophet of my God,
My lips shall bless thy name:
By thee the joyful news
Of our salvation came;
The joyful news of sins forgiven,
Of hell subdued, and peace with Heaven

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Be thou my Counsellor,
My Pattern, Lord, and Guide;
And through this desert land
Still keep me near thy side:
O let me never run astray,
Nor follow the forbidden way

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
I love my Shepherd's voice;
His watchful eye shall keep
My wand'ring foul amoag
The thousands of his sheep:
He feeds his flock, he calls their names,
Bears in his arms the tender lambs.

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
O thou almighty Lord,
My Saviour and my King,
Thy sceptre and thy sword,
Thy glorious reign, I sing;
Thine is the power; and here, I Bit
In willing bonds before thy feet.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Now would my soul arise,
And tread the spoiler down:
My Captain leads me on
To conquest and a crown:
March on, nor fear to win the day,
Though death and hell obstruct the way

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Should all the hosts of hell,
And powers of death unknown,
Put all their dreadful forms
Of rage and malice on,

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
shall be safe; for Christ displays
Transcendant power, and saving grace.

title: God of my salvation, hear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
fall to rise no more.
2 Thou hast oft my refuge been,
And thou art still the same;
Snatch me from the jaws of sin,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
quench the violent flame;
Bring thy great salvation nigh,
Stir up thine interposing power
Save me, save me, or I die,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
fall to rise no more.
3 Help on Thee, thou Mighty One,
For all mankind is laid;
Let it now on me be shewn
Be thou my present aid,
MISCELLANEOUS HYMNS. fififl
O come quickly, and stand by
My soul throughout the trying hour;
Save me, save me, or I die,

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
fall to rise no more.
4 Help me now, hut let me still,
My want of help confess,
Hang upon thy arm, and feel
My utter helplessness;
Only this be all my cry,
Till thou my ruin'd soul restore;
Save me, save me, or I die,

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text: fall to rise no more.

title: Come, o thou Prophet of the Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, o thou Prophet of the Lord,
Thou great Interpreter divine,
Explain thine own transmitted word;
To teach and to inspire is thine:
Thou only canst thyself reveal,
Open the book, and loose the seal.
2- Now, Jesus, now the veil remove,
The folly of our darken'd heart;
Unfold the wonders of thy love,
The knowledge of thyself impart;
Our ear, our inmost soul we bow:
Speak, Lord, thy servants hearken now.

title: Coming through our great High Priest
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Coming through our great High Priest,
"We find a pard'ning God:
Jesu's Spirit in our breast
Bears witness with the blood.
Speaks our Father pacified
Toward every soul that Christ receives;
Tells us, once our Surety died,
And now for ever lives.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ for ever lives to pray
For all that trust in him;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
my soul on Jesus stay,
Almighty to redeem:
He shall purify my heart,
Who in his blood forgiveness have,
All his hallowing power exert,
And to the utmost save.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Basis of our steadfast hope,
Saviour, thy ceaseless prayer
Sanctifies and lifts us up
To meet thee in the air:
Yes, thine interceding grace
Preserves us every moment thiny,
Till we rise to see thy face, *
And share the throne divine.

title: Blow ye the trumpet, blow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blow ye the trumpet, blow
The gladly solemn sound:
Let all the nations know,
To earth's remotest bound,
The year of Jubilee is come;
Return, ye ransom'd sinners, home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, our great High Priest,
Hath full atonement made:
Ye weary spirits, rest;
Ye mournful souls, be glad,
The year, &a

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Extol the Lamb of God,
The all-atoning Lamb;
Redemption in his blood
Throughout the world proclaim:
The year, &c.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ye slaves of s'.n and hell,
Your liberty receive;
And safe in Jesus dwell,
And- blest in Jesus live:
The year, &c.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ye who have sold for nought
Your heritage above,
Shall have it back unbought,
The gift of Jesu's love:
The year, &c.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The gospel trumpet hear,
The news of heavenly grace;
And, saved from earth, appear
Before your Saviour's face:
The year, &c.

title: With joy we meditate the grace
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With joy we meditate the grace
Of our High-Priest above;
His heart is made of tenderness,
His bowels yearn with love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Touch'd with a sympathy within,
He knows our feeble frame;
He knows what sore temptations mean.
For he hath felt the same.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He in the days of feeble flesh
Pour'd out his cries and tears;
And in his measure, feels afresh
What everv member bears.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He'll never quench the smoking fla:
But raise it to a flame;
The bruised reed he never breaks,
Nor scorns the meanest name.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let our humble faith address
His mercy and his power:
We shall obtain delivering grace
In the distressing hour.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
/ SUN of Righteousness, arise,
/ With healing in thy wing!
To my diseased, my fainting soul,
Life and salvation bring.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
These clouds of pride and sin dispel,
By thy all-piercing beam;
Lighten* my eyes with faith, my hehrt
With holy hope inflame.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
My mind, by thy all-quick'ning power,
From low desires set free;
Unite my scattered thoughts, and fix
My love entire on thee.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Father, thy long-lost son receive;
Saviour, thy purchase own:
Blest Comforter, with peace and joy
Thy new-made creature crown.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Eternal, undivided Lord,
Co-equal One and Three,
On Thee, all faith, all hope be placed;
All love be paid to Thee!
• First appeared in the Wesleyan Collections iu 175L

title: Let everlasting glories crown
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let everlasting glories crown
Thy head, my Saviour and my Lord;
Thy hands have brought salvation down,
And writ the blessing in thy word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In vain the trembling conscience seeks
Some solid ground to rest upon;
With long despair our spirit breaks,
Till we apply to Christ alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How well thy blessed truths agree!
How wise and holy thy commands!
Thy promises, how firm they be!
How firm our hope and comfort stands!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Should all the forms that men devise
Assault my faith with treacherous art,
I'd call them vanity and lies,
And bind thy Gospel to my heart.

title: Come, Holy Ghost, Jehovah, Third
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Ghost, Jehovah, Third
JOL In order of the Three;
Sprung from the Father and the Word
From all eternity!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy Godhead brooding o'er the' abyss
Of formless waters lay;
Spoke into order all that is,
And darkness into day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In deepest hell, or heaven's height,
Thy presence who can fly?
Known is the Father to thy sight,
The' abyss of Deity.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy power through Jesu's life display'd,
Quite from the virgin's womb,
Dying, his soul an offering made,
And raised him from the tomb.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
God's image, which our sins destroy,
Thy grace restores below;
And truth, and holiness, and joy,
From thee their Fountain flow.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Hail, Holy Ghost, Jehovah, Third
In order of the Three;
Thron'd with the Father and the Word
From all eternity!

title: Branch of Jesse's stem, arise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Branch of Jesse's stem, arise,
And in our nature grow,
Turn our earth to Paradise,
By flourishing below:
Bless us with the Spirit of Grace
Immeasurably shed on thee;
Pour on all the faithful race
The streaming Deity.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let the Spirit of our Head
On all the members rest;
From thyself to us pi*oceed,
And dwell in every breast:
Teach to judge and act aright,
Inspire with wisdom from above.
Holy faith, and heavenly might.
And reverential love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, of thee we fain would learn
Thy heavenly Father's will;
Give us quickness to discern,
And boldness to fulfil:
All his mind to us explain,
All his name on us impress;
Then our souls in thee obtain
The perfect righteousness.

title: My Father God!"how sweet the sound
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Father God!"how sweet the sound,
How tender and how dear!
Not all the harmony of heaven
Could so delight the ear.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: In vain we tune our formal song.*
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In vain we tune our formal song.*.,
In vain we strive to rise;
Hosannas languish on our tongueb,
And our devotion dies.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And shall we thus for ever live
At this poor dying rate?
Our love so faint, so cold to Thee,
And thine to us so great!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, heavenly Dove,
With all thy quick'ning powers;
Come, shed abroad the Saviour's love-,
And that shall kindle ours.

title: Come, Holy Spirit, raise our songs
author: R   C   Brackenbury

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, raise our songs,
To reach the wonders of the day,
When with thy fiery cloven tongues
Thou didst these glorious scenes display.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O 'twas a most auspicious hour,
Season of grace and sweet delight,
When thou didst come with mighty power,
And light of truth divinely bright.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By this the blest disciples knew
Their risen Head had enter'd heaven;
Had now obtain'd the promise due,
Fully by God the Father given.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, we believe to us and ours
The apostolic promise given;
We wait the Pentecostal powers,
The Holy Ghost sent down from heaven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ah! leave us not to mourn below,
Or long for thy return to pine;
Now, Lord, the Comforter bestow,
And fix in us the Guest divine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Assembled here with one accord,' w
Calmly we wait the promised grace,
The purchase of our dying Lord:
Come, Holy Ghost, and fill the place.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
If every one that asks may find,
If still thou dost on sinners fall,
Come, as a mighty rushing wind;
Great grace he now upon us all.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Behold, to thee our souls aspire,
And languish thy descent to meet;
Kindle in each the living fire,
And fix in every heart thy seat.

title: Creator, Spirit, by whose aid
author: J   Dryden J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Creator, Spirit, by whose aid
The world's foundations first were laid,
Come visit every waiting mind,
Come pour thy joys on human kind;
From sin and sorrow set us free,
And make thy temples worthy thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Source of uncreated heat,
The Father's promised Paraclete!
Thrice holy Fount, immortal Fire,
Our hearts with heavenly love inspire:
Come, and thy sacred unction bring,
To sanctify us while we sing.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Plenteous of gs&ce, descend from high,
Rich in thy sevenfold energy!
Thou strength of His almighty hand,
Whose power does heaven and earth commwi.
Refine and purge our earthly parts,
And stamp thine image on our hearts.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Immoi'tal honours, endless fame,
Attend the' Almighty Father's name;
The Saviour Son he glorified,
Who for lost man's redemption died;
And equal adoration he,
Eternal Comforter, to Thee!
c. weslet.] HYMN G60. l. m. (12)

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
TESUS, we on the words depend,
t) Spoken by thee while present here, —
"The Father in my name shall send
The Holy Ghost, the Comforter."

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
That promise made to Adam's race,
Now, Lord, in us, even us, fulfil;
And give the Spirit of thy grace,
To teach us all thy perfect will.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
That heavenly Teacher of mankind,
That Guide infallible impart,
To bring thy sayings to our mind,
And write them on our faithful heart.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
He only can the words apply,
Through which we endless life possess;
And deal. to each his legacy,
Our Lord's unutterable peace.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
That peace of God, that peace of thine,
Oh might he now to us bring in,
And fill our souls with power divine,
And make an end of fear and sin.

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
The length and breadth of love reveal,
The height and depth of Deity;
And all the sons of glory seal,
And change and make us all like thee,

title: Why should the children of a King
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why should the children of a King
Go mourning all their days V
Great Comforter, descend and bring
The tokens of thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Dost thou not dwell in all the saints,
And seal the heirs of heaven?
When wilt thou banish my complaints,
And show my sins forgiven?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Assure my conscience of its part,
In the Redeemer's blood;
And bear thy Avitness with my heart,
That I am born of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou art the earnest of his love,
The pledge of joys to come:
May thy blest wings, celestial Dove,
Convey me safely home.

title: Eternal Spirit, come
author: O Weslet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eternal Spirit, come
Into thy meanest home;
From thy high and holy place,
Where thou dost in glory reign,
Stoop, in condescending grace,
Stoop to the poor heart of man

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For thee our hearts we lift,
And wait the heavenly gift:
Giver, Lord of life divine,
To our dying souls appear,
Grant the grace for which we pine,
Give thyself, the Comforter.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our ruin'd souls repair,
And fix thy mansion there:
Claim us for "thy constant shrine,
All thy glorious self reveal;
life, and power, and love divine,
God in us for ever dwell.

title: Father, glorify thy Son
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, glorify thy Son;
Answer his prevailing prayer.
Send that Intercessor down,
Send that other Comforter,
Whom helievingly we claim,
Whom we ask in Jesu's name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Then hy faith we know and feel
Him, the Spirit of truth and grace
With us he vouchsafes to dwell,
With us while unseen he stays:
All our help and good, we own,
Freely flows from him alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wilt thou not the promise seal,
True and gracious as thou art,
Send the Comforter to dwell
Every moment in our heart?
Yes, thou must the grace bestow:
Jesus saith it shall be so.

title: O thou that hear'st when sinners cry
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou that hear'st when sinners cry,
Though all my crimes before thee lie,
Behold me not with angry look,
But blot their memory from thy book.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Create my nature pure within,
And form my soul averse from sin;
Let thy good Spirit ne'er depart,
Nor hide thy presence from my heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I cannot live without thy light,
Cast out and banish'd from thy sight:
Thy holy joys, O Lord, restore,
And guard me that I fall no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though I have grieved thy Spirit, Lord,
His help and comfort still afford;
And let a wretch come near thy throne,
To plead the merits of thy Son.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My soul lies humbled in the dust.
And owns thy dreadful sentence just:
Look down, O Lord, with pitying eye,
And save the soul condernn'd to die.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
O may thy love inspire my tongue!
Salvation shall be all my song;
And all my powers shall join to bless
The Lord my strength and righteousness.

title: How sad our state by nature is
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sad our state by nature is!
Our sin, ho"W deep its stains!
And Satan binds our captive minds
Fast in his slavish chains.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But there's a voice of sovereign grace
Sounds from the sacred word:
"Ho, ye despairing sinners, come,
And trust upon the Lord! "

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My soul obeys the' Almighty's call,
And runs to this relief:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
would believe thy promise, Lord;
O help my unbelief!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To the blest fountain of thy blood.
Incarnate God, I fly:
Here let me wash my spotted soul
From sins of deepest dye.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
A guilty, weak, and helpless worm,
Upon thy arm I fall;
Be thou my strength and righteousness,
My Saviour, and my all.
c. wesley.J HYMN 66G. 8's & 6's.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
f THOU who hast redeem'd of old,
S And bidd'st me of thy strength lay
And be at peace with thee;
Help me thy benefits to own,
And hear me tell what thou hast done.
O dying Lamb, for me!

sections.label: Verse 8
Verse 9
sections.text:
Canst thon deny that love to me 'i
Say, thou Incarnate Deity,
Thou Man of Sorrows, say;
Thy glory why didst thou enshrine
In such a clod of earth as mine,
And wrap thee in my clay?

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
Ancient of Days, why didst thou come,
And stoop to a poor virgin's womb,
Who wert ere time began?
Flesh of our flesh why wast thou made,
And humbly in a manger laid,
The new-bom Son of Man?

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
Love, only love thy heart inclined,
And brought thee, Saviour of mankind,
Down from thy throne above;
Love made my God a Man of grief,
Distress' d thee sore for my relief:
O mystery of Love!
S Because thou loVdst, and diedst for me,
Cause me, my Saviour, to love thee,
And gladly to resign
Whate'er I have, whate'er I am;
My life be all with thine the same,
And all thy death be mine.

title: Regardless now of things below
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Regardless now of things below,
Jesus, to thee my heart aspires,
Determined thee alone to know,
Author and end of my desires:
Fill me with righteousness divine:
To end, as to begin, is thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What is a worthless worm to thee?
What is in man thy grace to move?
That still thou seekest those who flee
The arms of thy pursuing love?
That still thine inmost bowels cry,
"Why, shiner, wilt thou perish, why? "

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ah, show me, Lord, my depth of sin!
Ah, Lord, thy depth of mercy show!
End, Jesus, end this war within!
No rest my spirit e'er shall know,
Till thou thy quick'ning influence give:
Breathe, Lord, and these dry bones shall live.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There, there before the throne thou art,
The Lamb ere earth's foundation slain!
Take thou, O take this guilty heart!
Thy blood will wash out every stain:
No cross, no sufferings I decline;
Only let all my heart be thine.

title: Hath the sins that made thee mourn
author: W   Cowrer J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hath the sins that made thee mourn,
That drove thee from my breast.
The dearest idol I have known,
Whate'er that idol be,
Help me to tear it from thy throne,
And worship only thee.
So shall my walk be close with God,
Calm and serene my frame;
So purer light shall mark the road
That leads me to the Lamb.

title: With steady course the shining sun
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With steady course the shining sun
Keeps his appointed way;
And all the hours obedient run
The circle of the day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But, ah! how wide my spirit flies,
And wanders from her God!
My soul forgets the heavenly prize,
And treads the downward road.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The raging fire and stormy sea
Perform thy awful will;
And every beast and every tree
Thy great designs fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Shall creatures of a meaner frame
Pay all their dues to thee?
Creatures that never knew thy name,
Nor ere were loved like me?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Great God! create my soul anew,
Conform my heart to thine;
Melt down my will, and let it flow,
And take the mould divine.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
Then shall my feet no more depart,
Nor my affections rove;
Devotion shall be all my heart,
And all my passions, love.

title: Long have I sat beneath the sound
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Long have I sat beneath the sound
Of thy salvation, Lord;
But still how weak my faith is found,
And knowledge of thy word!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My glorious Saviour and my God,
How little art thou known
By all the judgments of thy rod,
The blessings of thy throne!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How cold and feeble is my love!
How negligent my fear!
How low my hope of joys above!
How few affections there 1
[ Great God! thy sovereign power impart,
To give thy word success;
Write thy salvation on my heart,
And make me learn thy grace.
Show my forgetful feet the way
That leads to joys on high,
Where knowledge grows without decay,
And love shall never die.

title: Father, I stretch my hands to thee
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, I stretch my hands to thee,
No other help I know;
If thou withdraw thyself from me,
Ah! whither shall I go?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What did thy only Son endure
Before I drew my breath;
What pain, what labour, to secuie
My soul from endless death!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Jesus, could I this believe,
I now should feel thy power;
My wants thou would' st at once relieve
In this accepted hour.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Author of faith, to thee I lift
My weary, longing eyes:
O let me now receive that gift!
My soul without it dies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Surely thou canst not let me die;
O speak, and I shall live!
For here I will unwearied lie,
Till thou thy Spirit give.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
How would my anxious soul rejoice,
Could I but see thy face!
O, let me hear thy quick' ning voice,
And taste thy pardoning grace.

title: Come to Calvary's holy mountain
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come to Calvary's holy mountain,
Sinners ruin'd by tKe fall;
Here a pure and healing fountain
Flows to you, to me, to all,
In a full perpetual tide, —
Open'd when the Saviour died.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, in poverty and meanness,
Come, denied without, within;
From infection, from uncleanness,
From the leprosy of sin,
Wash your robes and make them white; —
Ye shall walk with God in light.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, in sorrow and contrition,
Wounded, impotent, and blind,
Here the guilty free remission,
Here the troubled peace may find;
Health this fountain will restore,
He that drinks shall thirst no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He that drinks shall live for ever;
'Tis a soul-renewing flood:
God is faithful; —God will never
Break his covenant in blood:
Sign'd when our Redeemer died,
Seal'd when He was glorified.

title: Come, thou long expected Jesus
author: Non J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou long expected Jesus,
Born to set thy people free;
From our sins and fears release os,
Let us find our rest in thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Israel's strength and consolation,
Hope of all the earth Thou art;
The desire of every nation,
Joy of every contrite heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, thy children to deliver,
Born a child, and yet a king;
Come, to reign in us for ever,
Now thy gracious kingdom bring.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By thine own Eternal Spirit,
Rule in all our hearts alone;
By thine all-sufficient merit,
'Raise us to thy glorious throne.

title: The God of Abraham praise
author: T Olivers

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The God of Abraham praise,
Who reigns enthroned above,
Ancient of everlasting days,
And God of Love:
Jehovah, Great I AM,
By earth and heaven confest;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
bow and bless the sacred Name,
For ever blest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The God of Abraham praise,
At whose supreme command,
From earth I rise, and seek the joys
At his rigbt hand:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
all on earth forsake,
Its wisdom, fame, and power;
And him my only portion make.
My shield and tower.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The God of zVbraham praise,
Whose all-sufficient grace,
Shall guide me all my happy days,
In all his ways.
He calls a worm his friend,
He calls himself my God:
And he shall save me to the end,
Through Jesu's blood.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
He by himself hath sworn,
I on his oatli depend;

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
shall on eagles' wings upborne,
To heaven ascend:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
shall behold his face,
I shall his power adore,
And sing the wonders of his grace
For evermore.

title: Though nature's strength decay
author: F Olivers J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Though nature's strength decay,
And earth and hell withstand,"
To Canaan's bounds I urge my way,
At his command.
The watery deep I pass,
With Jesus in my view;
And through the howling wilderness
My way pursue.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
There dwells the Lord our King,
The Lord our Righteousness,
Triumphant o'er the world and sin.
The Prince of Peace;
On Sion's sacred height,
His kingdom still maintains;
And glorious with his saints in light
For ever reigns.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He keeps his own secure,
He guards them by his side,
Arrays in garments white and pure
His spotless bride:
With streams of sacred bliss,
With groves of living joys,
With all the fruits of Paradise,
He still supplies.

title: Before the great Three-One
author: T Olivers

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Before the great Three-One
They all exulting stand,
And tell the wonders he hath done,
Through all their land:
The listening spheres attend,
And swell the growing fame;
And sing, in songs which never end,
The wondrous Name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The God who reigns on high
The great archangels sing;
And "Holy, holy, holy,"cry,
"Almighty King!
Who was and is the same,
And evermore shall be;
Jehovah, Father, Great I AM,
We worship Thee."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Before the Saviour's face.
The ransom'd nations bow;
O'erwhelm'd at his almighty grace,
For ever new:
He shows his prints of love,—
They kindle to a flame!
And sound through all the worlds above,
The slaughter' d Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The whole triumphant host
Give thanks to God on high;
"Hail, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,"
They ever cry:
Hail, Abraham's God, and mine i
(I join the heavenly lays,)
All might and majesty are thine,
And endless praise.

title: True 'tis a strait and thorny road
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
True 'tis a strait and thorny road,
And mortal spirits tire and faint;
But they forget the mighty God,
That feeds the strength of every saint,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thee, mighty God, whose matchless pov. oi-
ls ever new and ever young;
And firm endures, while endless years
Their everlasting circles run.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
From Thee, the ever-flowing Spring.
Our souls shall drink a fresh supply;
While such as trust their native strength
Shall melt away, and sink, and dio.
Swift as the eagle cuts the air,
We'll mount aloft to thine ahode;
On wings of love our souls shall fly,
Nor tire, while on the heavenly road.

title: /commit thou all thy griefs
author: John Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
/commit thou all thy griefs
And ways into his hands,
To His sure truth and tender care,
Who earth and heaven commands.
Who points the clouds their course,
Whom winds and seas ohey;
He shall direct thy wandering feet,
He shall prepare thy way.
Thou on the Lord rely,
So safe shalt thou go on;
Fix on His work thy steadfast eye,
So shall thy work be done.
No profit canst thou gain,
By self-consuming care;
To him commend thy cause, His ear
Attends the softest prayer.
Thy everlasting truth,
Father, thy ceaseless love,
Sees all thy children's wants, and knows
What best for each will prove.
Thou everywhere hast sway,
And all things serve thy might;
Thy every act pure blessing is,
Thy patn unsullied light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When thou ai-isest, Lord,
"What shall thy work withstand?
Whate'er thy children want, thou giv'st;
Who, who shall stay thy hand?

title: Away, my needless fears
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Away, my needless fears,
And doubts no longer mine
A ray of heavenly light appears,
A messenger divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thrice comfortable hope,
That calms my stormy breast;
My Father's hand prepares the cup,
And what He wills is best.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
know it shall be mine.
4 Still let then? counsel take
To frustrate his decree,
They cannot keep a blessing back.
By Heaven design' d for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here then I doubt no more,
But hi his pleasure rest,
Whose wisdom, love, and truth, and power
Engage to make me blest.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
To' accomplish his design
The creatures all agree;
And all the attributes diving
Are now at work for me.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text: x.

title: Bless'd are the humble souls that see
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bless'd are the humble souls that see
Their emptiness and poverty:
Treasures of grace to them are given,
And crowns of joy laid up in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Bless'd are the men of broken heart,
Who mourn for sin with inward smart;
The blood of Christ divinely flows,
A healing balm for all their woes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Bless'd are the souls that pant for grace,
Hunger and thirst for righteousness:
They shall be well supplied and fed,
With living streams, and living bread.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Bless'd are the pure, whose hearts are clean
From the defiling power of sin:
With endless pleasure they shall see
The God of spotless purity.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Bless'd are the sufferers, who partake
Of pain and shamo for Jesu's sake:
Their souls shall triumph in the Lord;
Glory and joy are their reward.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
These are the men, the pious race,
Who seek the God of Jacob's face;
These shall enjoy the blissful sight,
And dwell in everlasting light.

title: Who in the Lord confide
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Who in the Lord confide,
And feel his sprinkled blood,
In storms and hurricanes abide,
Firm as the mount of God:
Steadfast, and fix'd, and snre,
His Sion cannot move;
His faithful people stand secure
In Jesu's guardian love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As round Jerusalem
The hilly bulwarks rise,
So God protects and covers them
From all their enemies.
On every side he stands,
And for his Israel cares;
And safe in his almighty hands
Their souls for ever bears.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But let them still abide
In thee, all- gracious Lord,
Till every soul is sanctified,
And perfectly restored:
The men of heart sincere
Continue to defend;
And do them good, and save them her-c,
And love them to the end.

title: God is the refuge of his saints
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God is the refuge of his saints,
When storms of sharp distress invade;
Ere we can offer our complaints,
Behold him present with his aid!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let mountains from their seats be hurl'c
Down to the deep, and buried there, —
Convulsions shake the solid world, —
Our faith shall never yield to fear.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
There is a stream, whose gentle flow
Supplies the city of our God;
Life, love, and joy still gliding through,
And watering our divine abode.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This sacred stream, thy living word,
Thus all our raging fear controls:
Sweet peace thy promises afford,
And give new strength to fainting souls.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Sion enjoys her Monarch's love,
Secure against the threat'ning hour;
Nor can her firm foundation move,
Built on His truthfulness and power.

title: Happy the heart where graces reign
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the heart where graces reign,
JUL Where love inspires the breast;
Love is the brightest of the train,
And perfects all the rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Knowledge, alas! 'tis all in vain,
And all in vain our fear:
Our stubborn sins will fight and reign,
If love be absent there.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis love that makes our cheerful feet
In swift obedience move:
The devils know, and tremble too;
But Satan cannot love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This is the grace that lives and sings,
When faith and hope shall cease;
'Tis this shall strike our joyful strings
In the sweet realms of bliss.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Before we quite forsake our clay,
Or leave this dark abode,
The wings of love bear us away
To see our gracious God.

title: Vain delusive world, adieu
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Vain delusive world, adieu,
With all of creature- good!
Only Jesus I pursue,
Who bought me with his blood:
All thy pleasures I forego,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
trample on thy wealth and pride:
Only Jesus will I know,
And Jesus crucified.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Other knowledge I disdain,
'Tis all but vanity;
Christ, the Lamb of God, was slain.
He tasted death for me.
Me to save from endless woe,
The sin-atoning Victim died:
Only Jesus will I know,
And Jesus crucified.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Turning to my rest again,
The Saviour I adore;
He relieves my grief and pain,
And bids me weep no more.
Rivers of salvation flow
From out his head, his hands, his side:
Only Jesus will I know,
And Jesus crucified.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here will I set up my rest,
My fluctuating heart
From the haven of his breast
Shall never more depart.
Whither should a sinner go!
His wounds for me stand open wide:
Only Jesus will I know,*
And Jesus crucified.

title: Wait to see thy glorious face
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Wait to see thy glorious face,
I seek redemption through thy blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now in thy strength I strive with thee,
My Friend and Advocate with God;
Give me the glorious liberty,
Grant me the purchase of thy blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou art the anchor of my hope,
The faithful promise I receive;
Surely thy death shall raise me up,
For thou hast died that I might live.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Satan, with all his ai-ts, no more
Me from the gospel hope can move;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
shall receive the gracious power,
And find the pearl of perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Though nature gives my God the lie,
I all his truth and grace shall know;

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
shall, the helpless creature T,
Shall perfect holiness below.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
My flesh, which cries, "It cannot be,"
Shall silence keep before the Lord;
And earth, and hell, and sin shall flee
At Jesu's everlasting word.

title: Author of faith, appear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Author of faith, appear;
Be thou its finisher!
Upward still for this we gaze,
Till we feel the stamp divine,
Thee behold with open face,
Bright in all thy glory shine.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O that our life might be
One looking up to thee!
Ever hast'ning to the day,
When our eyes shall see thee near;
Come, Redeemer, come away,
Glorious in thy saints appear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesu, the heavens bow,
We long to meet thee now!
Now in Majesty come down,
Pity thine elect and come:
Hear us in thy Spirit groan,
Tiike the weary exiles homo.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
Thee I seiwe, my Lord, my God;
In me thy power display:
Save me, save me, and defraud
The lion of his prey.
Angel of the Covenant,
Jesus mighty to retrieve,
of 1782.
Let him to my help be sent:
In Jesus I believe.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Save me for thine own great name,
That all the world may know,
Daniel's God is still the same,
And reigns supreme below:
Him let all mankind adore,
Spread his glorious name abroad
Tremble all, and bow before
The great, the living God.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Absolute, unchangeable,
O'er all his works he reigns;
His dominion cannot fail,
But un disturb' d remains:
His dominion standeth fast,
Is when time no more shall be;
Still shall his dominion last
Through all eternity.

title: To God, the only wise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To God, the only wise,
Our Saviour and our King,
Let all the saints below the skies
Their humble praises bring.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis his almighty love,
His counsel and his care,
Preserves us safe from sin and death,
And every hurtful snare.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He will present our souls
Unblemish'd and complete,
Before the glory of his face,
With joys divinely great.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then all the chosen seed
Shall meet around the throne,
Shall bless the conduct of his grace,
And make his wonders known.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To our Redeemer God
Wisdom and power belongs,
Immortal crowns of majesty,
And everlasting songs.

title: Wait a few sorrowful years
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Wait a few sorrowful years,
And then I no longer shall mourn,
But flee from the valley of tears
A way I shall never return:
From earth I shall quickly remove
To sure everlasting abodes,
And sing with the spirits above,
And triumph with angels and God.
My days when extinguish'd and gone,
And time as a shadow is fled,
Then, then I will lay myself down
To rest with the peaceable dead:
The dead ever-living attend,
Whose dust is all safe in the tomb,
Where many a glorified friend
Is ready to welcome me home.

title: Father, to me the faith impart
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, to me the faith impart
Which makes the blessing mine,
Thy Son discover to my heart
In majesty divine;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That knowing him, my soul may prove
The sense of sin forgiven,
And through the bliss of perfect love
Pass to the bliss of heaven.

title: Whate'er my heavenly Father wills
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Whate'er my heavenly Father wills
Through faith in Christ I still receive,
His blood my every promise seals,
And quicken'd by his blood I live.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His blood shall wash me white as snow;
It now hath brought me near to God,
And all my gifts and blessings flow
Through the dear channel of his blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To buy and make me free indeed,
The ransom of his blood was given,
For me his blood on earth was shed,
And now it intercedes in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It speaks to God, my God, for me,
For me obtains whate'er is best;
And lo! the bleeding Lamb I see,
And in his wounds for ever rest.

title: Jesu, my God and King
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesu, my God and King,
Thy regal state I sing:
Thou, and only thou, art great,
High thine everlasting throne;
Thou the sovereign Potentate,
Bless'd, immortal, thou alone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Essay your choicest strains,
The King Messiah reigns!
Tune your harps, celestial choir,
Joyful all your voices raise;
Christ, than earth-horn monarchs higher,
Sons of men and angels praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hail your dread Lord and ours,
Dominions, thrones, and powers I
Source of power, He rules alone:
Veil your eyes, and prostrate fall,
Cast your crowns hefore his throne,
Hail the Cause, the Lord of all!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Worthy, O Lord, art thou,
That every knee should bow,
Every tongue to thee confess;
Universal nature join,
Strong and mighty, thee to bless,
Gracious, merciful benign.
Wisdom is due to thee,
