And might, and majesty;
Thee in mercy rich we prove;
Glory, honour, praise receive;
Worthy thou of all our love,
More than all we pant to give.
Justice and truth maintain
Thine everlasting reign:
One with thine almighty Sire,
Partner of an equal throne,
King of saints, let all conspire
Gratefully thy sway to own.

title: our Lord is King
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
our Lord is King!
Sons of men, his praises sing;
Sing ye in triumphant strains,
Jesus our Messiah reigns!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Power is all to Jesus given,
Lord of hell, and earth, and heaven!
Every knee to him shall bow;
Satan, hear, and tremble now!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Angels and archangels join,
All triumphantly combine;
All in Jesu's praise agree,
Carrying on his victory.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though the sons of night blasphemy
More there are with us than them:
God with us, we cannot fear;
Fear, ye fiends, for Christ is here!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lo! to faith's enlighten'd sight,
All the mountain flames with light
Hell is nigh, but God is nigher,
Circling us with hosts of fire.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Our Messias is come down,
Points us to the victor's crown,
Bids us take our seats above,
More than conquerors through his love.

title: Come, thou conqueror of the nations
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, thou conqueror of the nations,
On thy great white horse appear;
Earthquakes, deaths, and desolations
Signify thy kingdom near:
True and faithful!
'Stablish thy dominion here.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Thee let all mankind admire,
Object of our joy and dread!
Flame thine eyes with heavenly fire,
Many crowns upon thy head";
But thine essence
None, except thyself, can read.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yet we know our Mediator,
By the Father's grace bestow'd.
Meanly clothed in human nature,'
Thee we call the Word of God':
Flesh thy vesture,
Dipp'd in thy own sacred blood.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Captain, God of our salvation,
Thou who hast the wine-press trod,
Borne the' Almighty's indignation,
Quenched the fiercest wrath of God:
Take the kingdom,
Claim the purchase of thy blood.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
On thy thigh and vesture written,
Show the world thy heavenly name,
That with love and wonder smitten,
All may glorify the Lamb;
All adore thee,
All the Lord of Hosts proclaim.

sections.label: Verse 7

title: Father of boundless grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of boundless grace,
A- Thou hast in part fulfill'd
The promise made to Adam's race,
In God incarnate seal'd.
A few from every land
At first to Salem came,
And saw the wonders of thy hand,
And saw the tongues of flame.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yet still we wait the end,
The coming of our Lord;
The full accomplishment attend
Of thy prophetic word.
Thy promise deeper lies
In unexhausted grace,
And new-discover'd worlds arise
To sing their Saviour's praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Beloved for Jesu's sake,
By him redeem'd of old,
All nations must come in, and make
One undivided fold;
While gather'd in by thee,
And perfected in one,
They all at once thy glory see,
In thine eternal Son.

title: Head of thy Church, whose spirit fills
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Head of thy Church, whose spirit fills,
XjL And flows through every faithful soul,
Unites in mystic love, and seals
Them one, and purifies the whole:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Come Lord,"thy glorious Spirit cries,
And souls beneath the altar groan;
"Come Lord,"the Bride on earth replies,
"And perfect all our souls in one."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Pour out the promised gift on all,
Answer the universal, "Come!"
The fulness of the Gentiles call,
And take thine ancient people home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To thee let all the nations flow,
Let all obey the gospel word;
Let all their bleeding Saviour know,
Fill'd with the glory of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O for thy truth and mercy's sake,
The purchase of thy passion claim;
Thine heritage the Gentiles take,
And cause the vorld to know thy name*

title: "[eternal Lord of earth and skies
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"[eternal Lord of earth and skies,
We wait thy Spirit's latest call:
Bid all our fallen race arise,
Thou who hast purchased life for all;
Whose only name to sinners given,
Snatches from hell, and lifts to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The word thy sacred lips has past,
The sure irrevocable word,
That every soul shall how at last,
And yield allegiance to its Lord;
The kingdoms of the earth shall be
For ever subjected to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, for this we still attend,
Thy kingdom in the isles to prov-3;
The law of sin and death to end,
We wait for all the power of love,
The law of perfect liberty,
The law of life which is in thee.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Let Sion in her King rejoice
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let Sion in her King rejoice,
Though Satan rage, and kingdoms rise
He utters his almighty voice,
The nations melt, the tumult dies.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
s
2 The Lord of old for Jacob fought;
And Jacob's God is still our aid:
Behold the works his hand hath wrought
What desolations he hath made!
S From sea to sea, through all their shores.,
He makes the noise of battle cease;
When from on high his thunder roars,
He awes the trembling world to peace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He breaks the bow, he cuts the spear;
Chariots he burns with heavenly flame
Keep silence, all the earth, and hear
The sound and glory of his name!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Be still, and learn that I am God
Exalted over all the lands;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
will be known and fear'd abroad;
For still my throne in Sion stands."

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O Lord of hosts, almighty King!
While we so near thy presence dwell,
Our faith shall rest secure, and sing
Defiance to the gates of hell.

title: Arm of the Lord, awake, awake
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Then the whole earth again shall rest,
And see its paradise restored;
Then every soul, in Jesus blest,
Shall bear the image of its Lord,
In finish'd holiness renew'd,
Immeasurably fill'd with God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O wouldst thou bring the final scene,
Accomplish the redeeming plan,
Thy great millennial reign begin;
That every ransom'd child of man,
That every soul, may bow the knee,
And rise to reign with God in thee!

title: Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
Doth his successive journeys run;
His kingdom stretch from shore to shore,
Till suns shall rise and set no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For him shall endless prayer be made,
And praises throng to crown his head;
His name like sweet perfume shall rise
With every morning sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
People and realms of every tongue
Dwell on his love with sweetest song,
And infant-voices shall proclaim
Hosannas to his sacred name.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Where he displays his healing power,
Death and the curse are known no more '
Tn him the tribes of Adam boast
More blessings than their father lost.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Let every creature rise, and bring
Its grateful honours to our King;
Angels descend with song's again,
And earth repeat the joyful strain.

title: The heavens declare thy glory, Lord
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The heavens declare thy glory, Lord,
In every star thy wisdom shines;
But when our eyes behold thy word,
We read thy name in fairer lines.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The rolling sun, the changing light,
And nights and days, thy power confess;
But the blest volume thou hast writ
Reveals thy justice and thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sun, moon, and stars convey thy praise
Round the whole earth, and never stand
So when thy truth began its race,
It touch'd and glanced on every land.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nor shall thy spreading gospel rest,
Till through the world thy truth has run
Till Christ has all the nations blest,
That see the light or feel the sun.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Great Sun of Righteousness, arise,
Bless the dark world with heavenly light:
Thy gospel makes the simple wise;
Thy laws are pure, thy judgments right.

title: From all that dwell below the skies
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From all that dwell below the skies,
I Let the Creator's praise arise:
Let the Redeemer's name be sung,
Through every land, by every tongue.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Eternal are thy mercies, Lord;
Eternal truth attends thy word:
Thy praise shall sound from shore to shore,
Till suns shall rise and set no more.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Thy needy servaDts cry
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Convert, and send forth more
Into thy church abroad;
And let them speak thv word of power,
As workers with their God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give the pure gospel word,
The word of general grace;
Thee let them preach, the common Lord,
The Saviour of our race.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O Let them spread thy name,
Their mission fully prove;
Thy universal grace proclaim,
Thy all-redeeming love!
G On all mankind, forgiven,
Empower them still to call;
And tell each creature under heaven,
That thou hast died for all.

title: How beauteous are their feet
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
How rapt'rous is their voice, —
So sweet the tidings are!
"Sion, behold thy Sciviour King;
He reigns and triumphs here."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How favour'd are our ears.
That hear the joyful sound,
Which kings and prophets waited for,
And sought, but never found!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How blessed are our eyes,
That see this heavenly light!
Prophets and kings desired long,
But died without the sight

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The watchmen join their voice,
And tuneful notes employ;
Jerusalem breaks forth in songs,
And deserts learn the joy.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The Lord makes bare his arm
Through all the earth abroad:
Let all the nations now behold
Their Saviour and their God.

title: Salvation! O the joyful sound
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Salvation! O the joyful sound!
What pleasure to our ears!
A sovereign balm for every wound,
A cordial for our fears.
Glory, honour, praise, and power.
Be unto the Lamb for ever:
Jesus Christ is our Redeemer,
Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah,
Praise the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Salvation! let the echo fly
The spacious earth around;
While all the armies of the sky
Conspire to raise the sound!
Glory, honour, praise, and power, &c.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Salvation! O thou bleeding Lamb!
To thee the praise belongs:
Salvation shall inspire our hearts,
And dwell upon our tongues:
Glory, honour, praise, and power, &c-

title: According to thy gracious word
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
According to thy gracious word,
jljL In meek humilty,
This will I do, my dying Lord,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
will remember Thee.
2 Thy body broken for my sake,
My bread from heaven shall be j
Thy testamental cup I take,
And thus remember Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Gethsemane can I forget?
Or there thy conflict see,
Thine agony and bloody sweat,
And not remember Thee?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When to the cross I turn my eyes
And rest on Calvary,

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lamb of God, my sacrifice!
I must remember Thee: —

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Eemember thee, and all thy pains,
And all thy love to me;
Yea, while a breath, a pulse remains,
Will I remember Thee.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
And when these failing lips grow dumb,
And mind and memory flee,
When Thou shalt in thy kingdom come,
Jesus, remember me.

title: For a song of ardent praise
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For a song of ardent praise,
To bear our souls above!
What should allay our lively hope,
Or damp our flaming love. '

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Draw us, O Lord, with quickening grace.
And bring us yet more near;
Here may we see thy glories shine,
And taste thy mercies here.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O may that love which spread thy board
Dispose us for the feast;
May faith behold a smiling God,
Through Jesu's bleeding breast.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fir'd with the view, our souls shall rise,
In such a scene as this,
And view the happy moment near,
That shall complete our bliss.

title: This is the feast of heavenly wine
author: William Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
This is the feast of heavenly wine,
And God invites to sup;
The juices of the living vine
Were press'd to fill the cup.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O bless the Saviour, ye that eat,
With royal dainties fed!
Not heaven affords a costlier treat,
For Jesus is the bread.
S Approach ye poor, nor dare refuse
The banquet spread for you;
Dear Saviour, this is welcome news,
Then I may venture too!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If guilt and sin afford a plea
And may obtain a place,
Surely the Lord will welcome me,
And I shall see his face.

title: As many as in Adam died
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As many as in Adam died,
In Christ may be restored,
And freely sav'd in Christ confide,
And love their bleeding Lord:
To purge the universal sin,
The bloody fountain flow'd,
To make our life and nature clean,
And bring us all to God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Father, I ask in Jesu's name,
My hungry spirit feed,
With humble confidence I claim
The true immortal bread:
As by his promise bound thou art,
Thy Son bestow on me.
And fill with Christ my longing heart,
With all that is hi thee.
John vi. 54-56.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
XYTHO now his flesh and blood partake,
V V Partakers of the life divine,
We soon shall see our Lord come back,
His members all in him to join;
And feeding on this living bread,
This earnest of our glorious bliss,
We too shall riee to meet our Head,
We too shall see him as he is.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Saviour, thy flesh is meat indeed!
Thy nature to thy Church made known
Doth every saint with manna feed,
Till every saint with thee is one,
Till blended with its heavenly food
The soul thy gracious fulness feels,
And all transform'd we dwell in God,
And God in us for ever dwells.

title: A ATHEIl we still the fragments up
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
I cannot doubt thy love for me:
Thy love for me doth now constrain
My heart to seek a power from thee
To love my gracious Lord again:
Thou wilt, for thine own mercy sake,
To me the power of faith impart,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
then the just return shall make,
And give thee all my loving heart.

title: The Lord of earth and sky
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
When justice bared the sword,
To cut the fig-tree down,
The pity of our Lord
Cried, "Let it still alone; "
The Father rnild inclines his ear,
And spares us yet another year.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, thy speaking blood
From God obtain'd the grace,
Who therefore hath bestow'd
On us a longer space;
Thou didst in our behalf appear,
And, lo, we see another year!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then dig about our root,
Break up the fallow ground,
And let our gracious fruit
To thy great praise abound:
O let us all thy praise declare,
And fruit unto perfection bear!

title: Who are these that come from far
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Who are these that come from far,
Swifter than a flying cloud!
Thick as flocking doves they are,
Eager in pursuit
Trembling1 as the storm draws nigh,
Hastening to their place of rest,
See them to the windows fly,
To the Ark of Jesu's bi'east.
Who are these but sinners poor,
Conscious of their lost estate,
Sin-sick souls, who for their cure
On the good Physician wait;
Fallen who bewail their fall,
Proferr'd mercy who embrace,
jJst'ning to the gospel-call,
Longing to be saved by grace.
For his mate the turtle moans,
For his God the sinner sighs;
Hark! the music of their groans,
Humble groans that pierce the skies!
Surely God their sorrows hears,
Every accent, eveiy look,
Treasures up their gracious tears,
Notes their sufferings in his book.
He who hath their cure begun,
Will he now despise their pain?
Gan he leave his work undone,
Bring them to the birth in vain?
No; we all who seek shall find,
We who ask shall all receive,
Be to Christ in spirit join'd,
Free from sin for ever live.

title: Eternal Source of every joy
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Eternal Source of every joy,
Well may thy praise our iips employ,
While in thy temple we appear,
Whose goodness crowns the circling year.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The flowery spring, at thy command*
Embalms the air, and paints the land
The summer rays with vigour shine,
To raise the corn, and cheer the vine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy hand in autumn richly pours
Through all our coasts redundant stores;
And winters, soften'd by thy care,
No more a face of horror wear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Seasons, and months, and weeks, and days,
Demand successive songs of praise:
Still be the cheerful homage paid
With opening light, and evening shade.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here in thy house shall incense rise,
As circling Sabbaths bless our eyes;
Still will we make thy mercies known
Around thy board, and round our own.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O may our more harmonious tongues
In worlds unknown pursue the songs;
And in those brighter courts adore,
Where days and years revolve no more.

title: Come, sinners, to the Great Jehovah's praise
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, sinners, to the Great Jehovah's praise!
O All praise to him belongs:
Who kindly lengthens out our days,
Demands our choicest songs.
, His providence hath brought us through
Another varied year:
We ail with vows and anthems new,
Before our God appear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Father, thy mercies past we own,
Tliy still continued care;
To thee presenting, through thy Son,
Whate'er we have or are
Our lips and lives shall gladly show
The wonders of thy love,
While on in Jesu's steps we go
To see thy face above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our residue of days or hours
Thine, wholly thine, shall be;
And all our consecrated powers
A sacrifice to thee:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Till Jesus in the clouds appear
To saints on earth forgiven,
And bring the grand sabbatic year,
The Jubilee of heaven.

title: Wisdom ascribe, and might, and praise
author: Wf Sley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Wisdom ascribe, and might, and praise,
To God, who lengthens out our days;
Who spares us yet another year,
And lets us se*. his goodness here:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
may we all our time redeem,
And henceforth live or die to Him!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How often, when his arm was bared,
Hath he our sinful Israel spared!
"Let me alone,"his mercy cried,
And turn'd the vengeful bolt aside;
Indulged another kind reprieve,
And strangely suffer'd us to live.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Still in the doubtful balance weigh 'd
We trembled, while the remnant pray'fl:
The Father heard his Spirit groan,
And answer'd mild, "It is my Son! "
He let the prayer of faith prevail,
And Mercy turu'd the doubtful scale.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Merciful God, how shall we raise
Our hearts to pay thee all thy praise
Our hearts shall beat for thee alone;
Our lives shall make thy goodness known
Our souls and bodies shall be thine,
A living sacrifice divine.

title: God of my life, through all my days
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of my life, through all my days,
vJT My grateful powers shall sound thy praise;
My song shall wake with opening light,
And cheer the dark and silent night.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When anxious cares would br&ak my rest,
And griefs would tear my throbbing breast,
Thy tuneful praises, raised on high,
Shall check the murmur and the sigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When death o'er nature shall prevail,
And all the powers of language fail,
Joy through my swimming eyes shall break.
And mean the thanks I cannot speak.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But O when that last conflict's o'er,
And I am chain'd to earth no more,
With what glad accents shall I rise
To join the music of the skies!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Soon shall I learn the' exalted strains
Which echo through the heavenly plains;
And emulate, with joy unknown,
The glowing seraphs round the throne.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The cheerful tribute will I give,
Long as a deathless soul shall live:
A work so sweet, a theme so high,
Demands and crowns eternity.

title: Jesus, was ever love like thine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, was ever love like thine?
Thy life a scene of wonders is;
Thy death itself is all divine,
While, pleased thy spirit to dismiss,
Thou dost out of the flesh retire,
And like the Prince of Life expire.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O let thy death's mysterious power,
With all its sacred weight, descend,
To consecrate my final hour,
To bless me with thy peaceful end:
And breathed into the hands divine,
My spirit be received with thine!

title: Hear what the voice from heaven proclaims
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hear what the voice from heaven proclaims
For all the pious dead!
Sweet is the savour of their names,
And soft their dying bed.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They die in Jesus, and are blest:
How calm their slumbers are!
From sufferings and from tears released.
And freed from every snare:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Till that illustrious morning come,
When all thy saints shall rise,
And, deck'd in full immortal bloom,
Attend thee to the skies.
2t

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Their tongues, great Prince of Life, shall join
With their recover'd hreath,
And all the' immortal host ascribe
Their victory to thy death.

title: Why should our tears in sorrow flow
author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why should our tears in sorrow flow,
When God recalls his own;
And bids them leave a world of woe
For an immortal crown?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Say, is not death a gain to those
Whose life to God was given?
Gladly on earth their eyes they close,
To open them in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Their toils are past; their work is done;
And they are fully blest:
They fought the fight, the victory won,
And enter'd into rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then let our sorrows cease to flow!
God has recall'd his own!
But let our hearts, in every woe,
Still say, "Thy will be done."

title: I call the world's Redeemer mine
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Then the last judgment-day shall come $
And though the worms this skin devour,
The Judge shall call me from the tomb,
Shall hid the greedy grave restore,
And raise this individual me,
God in the flesh, my God, to see.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In this identic body I,
With eyes of flesh refined, restored,
Shall see that self same Saviour nigh,
See for myself my smiling Lord,
See with ineffable delight;
Nor faint to bear the glorious sight.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O the transporting, rapturous scene
author: Btennett J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O the transporting, rapturous scene
That rises to my sight!
Sweet fields, array'd in living green,
And rivers of delight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There generous fruits that never fail,
On trees immortal grow;
There rocks and hills, and brooks and vale4.
With milk and honey flow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All o'er those wide extended plains
Shines one eternal day;
There God, the sun, for ever reigns,
And scatters night away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No chilling wind, or poisonous breath,
Can reach that healthful shore;
Sickness and sorrow, pain and death,
Are felt and fear'd no more.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When shall I reach that happy place,
And be for ever blest?
When shall I see my Father's face,
And in his bosom rest?

title: Why do we mourn departing friends
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why do we mourn departing friends,
Or shake at death's alarms?
'Tis but the voice that Jesus sends,
To call them to his arms.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The graves of all his saints he bless'd,
And soften' d every bed:
Where should the dying members rest.
But with their dying Head?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thence he arose, ascending high,
And show'd our feet the way:
Up to the Lord our flesh shall fly,
At the great rising-day

sections.label: Verse 4

title: And must this body die
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And must this body die?
XjL This well- wrought frame decay?
And must these active limbs of urine
Lie mouldering in the clay?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Corruption, earth, and worms
Shall but refine this flesh;
Till my triumphant spirit comes
To put it on afresh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God, my Kedeemer, lives,
And ever from the skies
Looks down, and watches all my dust,
Till he shall bid it rise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Array 'd in glorious grace
Shall these vile bodies shine;
And every shape and every face
Be heavenly and divine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
These lively hopes we owe,
Lord, to thy dying love:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
may we bless thy grace below,
And sing thy power above!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Saviour, accept the praise
Of these our humble songs,
Till tunes of nobler sound we raise
With our immortal tongues.

title: Almighty Maker of my frame
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Almighty Maker of my frame,
Teach me the measure of my days,
Teach me to know how frail I am,
And spend the remnant to thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My days are shorter than a span;
A little point my life appears:
How frail, at best, is dying man!
How vain are all his hopes and fears!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Y&in his ambition, noise, and show;
Vain are the cares which rack his mind:
He heaps up treasures mix'd with woe,
And dies, and leaves them all behind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O be a nobler portion mine!
My God, I bow before thy throne:
Earth's fleeting treasures I resign,
And fix my hope on thee alone.

title: Happy who in Jesus live
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Yet, if so thy will ordain,
For our companions' good,
Let us in the flesh remain,
And meekly bear the load:
When we have our grief fill'd up,
When we all our work have done,
Late partakers of our hope,
And sharers of thy throne.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To thy wise and gracious will,
We quietly submit,
Waiting for redemption still,
But waiting at thy feet;
When thou wilt the blessing giva,
Call us up thy face to see
Only let thy servants live,
And let us die, to Thee.

title: Hosanna to God
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hosanna to God
In his highest abode;
All heaven be join'd,
To extol the Redeemer and Friend of mankind!
He claims all our praise,
Who in infinite grace
Again hath stoop' d down,
And caught up a worm to inherit a crown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our friend is restored
To the joy of his Lord,
With triumph departs,
But speaks by his death to our echoing hearts.
"Follow after,"he cries,
As he mounts to the skies,
"Follow after your friend, [end."
To the blissful enjoyments that never shall

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through Jesus' s name,
Our comrade o'ercame;
And Jesus is ours,
And arms us with all his invincible powers:
He looks from the skies,
He shows us the prize,
And gives us a sign
That we shall o'ercorne by the mercy divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For us is prepared
The angelical guard;
The convoy attends,
A minist'ring host of invisible friends:
Ready wing'd for the flight
To the regions of light,
The horses are come,
The chariots of Israel to carry us home.

title: Happy soul, thy days are ended
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy soul, thy days are ended,
All thy mourning days below:
Go, by angel guards attended,
To the sight of Jesus go!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Waiting to receive thy spirit,
Lo! the Saviour stands above;
Shows the purchase of his merit,
Eeaches out the crown of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Struggle through thy latest passion
To thy dear Redeemer's breast,
To his uttermost salvation,
To his everlasting rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Forthe joy he sets before thee,
Bear a momentary pain;
Die, to live the life of glory,
Suffer, with thy Lord to reign.

title: I know that my Redeemer lives
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I know that my Redeemer lives
He lives, and on the earth shall stand;
And though to worms my flesh he gives,
My dust lies number'd in his hand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In this re-animated clay
I surely shall behold him near;
Shall see him in the latter day
In all his majesty appear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I feel what then shall raise me up,
The 'eternal Spirit lives in me;
This is my confidence of hope,
That God I face to face shall see.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Mine own and not another's eyes
The King shall in his beauty view;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
shall from him receive the prize,
The crown of life, —the victor's due.

title: O when shall we sweetly remove
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O when shall we sweetly remove,
O when shall we enter our rest,
Return to the Sion above,
The mother of spirits distrest!
That city of God the great King,
Where sorrow and death are no more;
But saints our Immanuel sing,
And cherub and seraph adore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not all the archangels can tell
The joys of that holiest place,
Where Jesus is pleased to reveal
The light of his heavenly face;
When caught in the rapturous flame,
The sight beatific they prove,
And walk in the light of the Lamb,
Enjoying the beams of his love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou know'st, in the spirit of prayer,
We hope thy appearing to see,
Resign' d to the burden we bear,
But longing to triumph with thee:
'Tis good at thy word to be here,
'Tis better in thee to be gone,
And see thee in glory appear,
And rise to a share in thy throne.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To mourn for thy coming is sweet,
To weep at thy longer delay;
But thou, whom we hasten to meet,
Shalt chase all our sorrows away.
The tears shall he wiped from our eyes,
When thee we behold in the cloud,
And echo the joys of the skies,
And shout to the trumpet of God.

title: There is a land of pure delight
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a land of pure delight,
Where saints immortal reign;
Infinite day excludes the night,
And pleasure's banish pain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There everlasting spring abides,
And never-withering flowers:
Death, like a narrow sea, divides
This heavenly land from ours.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sweet fields beyond the swelling flood
Stand dress'd in living green:
So to the Jews old Canaan stood,
While Jordan roll'd between.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But timorous mortals start and shrink
To cross this narrow sea;
And linger, shivering on the brink,
And fear to launch away.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O could we make our doubts remove,
Those gloomy thoughts that rise,
And see the Canaan that we love,
With unbeclouded eyes!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Could we but climb where Moses stood,
And view the landscape o'er.
Not Jordan's stream, nor death's cold flood,
Should fright us from the shore.

title: Lift your heads, ye friends of Jesus
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lift your heads, ye friends of Jesus,
Partners in his patience here;
Christ, to all "believers precious,
Lord of lords, shall soon appear:
Mark the tokens
Of his heavenly kingdom near!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oose hehind the trihulation
Of the last tremendous days,
See the flaming revelation,
See the universal blaze!
Earth and heaven
Melt before the Judge's face!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sun and moon are both confounded,
Darken'd into endless night,
When, with angel-hosts surrounded,
In his Father's glory bright,
Beams the Saviour,
Shines the everlasting Light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
See the stars from heaven falling,
Hark on earth the doleful cry,
Men on rocks and mountains calling,
While the frowning Judge draws nigh,
"Hide us, hide us,
Rocks and mountains, from his eye! "

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
With what different exclamation
Shall the saints his banner see!
By the tokens of his passion,
By the marks received for me,
All discern him,
All with shouts cry out "'Tis he! "

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Give me the wings of faith to rise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Give me the wings of faith to rise
Within the veil, and see
The saints above, how great their joys,
How bright their glories be.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Once they were mourning here below,
And wet their couch with tears:
They wrestled hard, as we do now,
With sins, and doubts, and fears.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I ask them whence their victory came:
They, with united breath,
Ascribe their conquest to the Lamb,
Their triumph to his death.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
They mark'd the footsteps that he trod,
His zeal inspired their breast;
And following their incarnate God,
Possess the promised rest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Our glorious Leader claims our praise
For his own pattern given;
While the long cloud of witnesses.
Show the same path to heaven.

title: When they once are enter' d there
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When they once are enter' d there,
Their mourning days are o'er;
Pain, and sin, and want, and care.
And sighing is no more;
Subject then to no decay,
Heavenly bodies they put on,
Swifter than tbe lightning's ray,
And brighter than the sun.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But their greatest happiness,
Their highest joy, shall be,
God their Saviour to possess,
To know, and love, and see:
With that beatific sight
Glorious ecstasy is given;
This is their supreme delight,
And makes a heaven of heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Him beholding face to face,
To him they glory give,
Bless his name and sing his praise,
As long as God shall live.
While eternal ages roll,
Thus employ'd in heaven they are
Lord, receive my happy soul
With all thy servants there!

title: To trusting in their Lord depart
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To trusting in their Lord depart,
Cleansed from all sin, and pure in heart,
The hliss unmix'd, the glorious prize,
They find with Christ in paradise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Close follow'd hy their works they go,
Their Master's purchased joy to know;
Their works enhance the bliss prepared,
And each hath its distinct reward.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet glorified by grace alone,
They cast their crowns before the throne;
And fill the echoing courts above
With praises of redeeming love.

title: How happy every child of grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy every child of grace,
Who knows his sins forgiven!
This earth, he cries, is not my place,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
seek my place in heaven;
A country far from mortal sight; —
Yet, O! by faith I see
The land of rest, the saints' delight,
The heaven prepared for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A stranger in the world below,
I calmly sojourn here;
Nor can its happiness or woe
Provoke my hope or fear:
Its evils in a moment end,
Its joys as soon are past;
But, O! the bliss to which I tend
Eternally shall last.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To that Jerusalem above
With singing I repair
While in the flesh, my hope and love,
My heart and soul are there:
There my exalted Saviour stands,
My merciful High Priest,
And still extends his wounded hands
To take me to his breast.
i What is there here to court my stay,
Or hold me back from home,
While angels beckon me away,
And Jesus bids me come?
Shall I regret my parted friends,
Still in the vale confined?
Nay, but whene'er my soul ascends,
They will not stay behind.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The race we all are running now;
And if I first attain,
They too their willing head shall bow,
They too the prize shall gain.
Now on the brink of death we stand;
And if I pass before,
They all shall soon escape to land,
And hail me on the shore.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O what a blessed hope is ours!
While here on earth we stay,
We more than taste the heavenly power*.
And antedate that day:
We feel the resurrection near,
Our life in Christ conceal'd,
And with his glorious presence here
Our earthen vessels fill'd.
O would he more of heaven bestow,
And let the vessel break,
And let our ransom'd spfrits go
To grasp the God we seek:
In rapturous awe on him we gaze,
Who bought the sight for me;
And shout, and wonder at his grace,
Through all eternity!

title: And let this feeble body fail
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And let this feeble body fail,
And let it droop and die;
My soul shall quit the mournful vale,
And soar to worlds on high;
Shall join the disembodied saints,
And find its long-sought rest,
That only bliss for which it pants,
In my Eedeemer's breast.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I bow me to my God's decree,
I own the sentence just,
(The sentence of mortality)
And dust return to dust:
Yet quicken' d by the trumpet's sound,
This dust again shall rise,
Beyond the old creation bound,
And shine above the skies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In hope of that immortal crown,
I now the cross sustain,
And gladly wander up and down,
And smile at toil and pain:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
suffer on my three- score years.
Till my Deliverer come,
And wipe away his servant's tears,
And take his exile home.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O what hath Jesus bought for me
Before my ravish' d eyes
Rivers of life divine I see,
And trees of paradise:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
see a world of spirits bright.
Who taste the pleasures there;
They all are robed in purest white,
And conquering palms they bear.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O what are all rny sufferings here,
If, Lord, thou count me meet
With that enraptured host to' appear,
And worship at thy feet!
Give joy or grief, give ease or pain,
Take life or friends away:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
come, to find them all again
In that eternal day:

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
That day, when death's last triumph ends,
His conquest o'er the just;
When from the grave each saint ascends,
No more a child of dust.
And, lo! I see the scattering shades!
The dawn of heaven appears!
The rich, immortal morning, spreads
Its blushes round the spheres.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
I see the Lord of glory come,
And flaming guards around!
The skies divide to make him room,
The trumpet shakes the ground!

sections.label: Verse 11
sections.text:
hear the voice, —"Ye dead arise "—
And, lo! the graves obey,
And waking saints, with joyful eyes,
Salute the' expected day!

sections.label: Verse 12
sections.text:
They leave the dust, and on the wing
Rise to the middle air,
In shining garments meet their King,
And low adore him there.
O, may my humble spirit stand
Among them, cloth'd in white!
The meanest place at his right hand
Is infinite delight!
2u

title: let us join our friends above
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
let us join our friends above,
That have obtain'd the prize,
And on the eagle wings of love
To joys celestial rise:
Let all the saints terrestrial sing,
With those to glory gone;
For all the servants of our King,
In earth and heaven, are one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
One family we dwell in him,
One church above, beneath,
Though now divided by the stream,
The narrow stream of death:
One armv of the living God,
To his command we bow;
Part of his host have cross'd the flood,
A ad part are crossing now.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ten thousand to tbeir endless home
This solemn moment fly;
And we are to the margin come,
And we expect to die:
His militant embodied host,
With wishful looks we stand,
And long to see that happy coast,
And reach the heavenly land.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our old companions in distress
We haste again to see,
And eager long for our release
And full felicity:
Even now by faith we join our hands
With those that went before;
And greet the blood-besprinkled bands
On the eternal shore.
Our spirits too shall quickly join,
Like theirs with glory crown' d,
And shout to see our Captain's sign,
To hear his trumpet sound.
O that we now might grasp our Guide!
O that the word were given!
Come, Lord of hosts, the waves divide,
And land us all in heaven

title: Great God, thy watchful care we bless
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God, thy watchful care we bless,
Which guards these sacred courts in peace;
Nor dare tumultuous foes invade,
To fill thy worshippers with dread,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And will the great eternal God
On earth establish his abode?
And will he from his radiant throne
Avow our temples for his own?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We bring the tribute of our praise,
And sing that condescending grace,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Which to our notes will lend an ear,
And call such sinful mortals near.
, 4 These walls we to thy honour raise,
Long may they echo to thy praise!
And thou, descending, fill the place
With choicest tokens of thy grace.
Here let the great Redeemer reign,
With all the virtues of his train;
While power divine his word attends
To conojier foes, and cheer his friends J

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And in the great decisive day,
When God the nations shall survey,
May it before the world appear,
That crowds were born to glory here.

title: This stone to thee in faith we lay
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
This stone to thee in faith we lay,
We build the temple, Lord, to thee;
Thine eye be open night and day
To guard this house and sanctuary.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here, when thy people seek thy face,
And dying sinners pray to live,
Hear, thou, in heaven, thy dwelling-place,
And when thou hearest, O forgive!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here, when thy messengers proclaim
The blessed Gospel of thy Son,
Still by the power of his great name,
Be mighty signs and wonders done.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hosannah! to their heavenly King,
When children's voices raise that song;
Hosannah! let their angels sing,
And heaven with earth the strain prolong

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But will indeed Jehovah deign,
Here to abide, no transient guest?
Here will the world's Redeemer reign,
And here the Holy Spirit rest?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
That glory never hence depart!
Yet choose not, Lord, this house alone;
Thy kingdom come to every heart,
In every bosom fix thy throne.

title: How pleasant, how divinely fair
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How pleasant, how divinely fair,
O Lord of Hosts, thy dwellings are!
With stroag desire my spirit faints
To meet the; assemblies of thy saints.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blest are the saints that sit on high,
Around the throne of majesty;
Thy brightest glories shine above,
And all their work is praise and love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest are the souls that find a place
Within the temple of thy grace;
There they behold thy gentle rays,
And seek thy face, and learn thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest are the men whose hearts are set
To find the way to Sion's gate;
God is their strength, and through the road
They lean upon their helper God.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Cheerful they walk with growing strength,
Till all shall meet in heaven at length;
Till all before thy face appear,
And join in nobler worship there.

title: Father of all, thy care we bless
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of all, thy care we bless,
Which crowns our families with peace:
From thee they spring; and by thy hand
They are, and shall be e'er sustained.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To God, most worthy to be praised,
Be our domestic altars raised;
Who, Lord of heaven, scorns not to dwell
And sanctify the humblest cell.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To thee may each united house
Morning and night present its vows:
Our servants there, and rising race.
Be taught thy precepts, and thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And may each future age proclaim
The honours of thy glorious name;
And each succeeding tribe remove
And join the family above.

title: God of eternal truth and love
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of eternal truth and love,
Vouchsafe the promised aid we claim,
Thine own great ordinance approve,
The child baptized into thy name
Partaker of thy nature make,
And give him all thine image back.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Father, if such thy sovereign will,
If Jesus did the rite enjoin,
Annex thy hallowing Spirit's seal,
And let the grace attend the sign;
The seed of endless life impart,
Take for thine own this infant's heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Answer on him thy wisdom's end,
In present and eternal good;
Whate'er thou didst for man intend,
Whate'er thou hast on man bestow'd,
Now to this favour'd babe be given,
Pardon, and holiness, and heaven
Thyself we faithfully require;
Come Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
By blood, by water, and by fire,
And fill up all thy human shrine.
And seal our souls for ever thine

title: How large the promise, how divine
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How large the promise, how divine,
To Abr'am and his seed!
. "I am a God to thee and thine,
Supplying all their need."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The words of his extensive love
From age to age endure;
The Angel of the Covenant proves
And seals the blessing sure.
o Jesus the ancient faith confirms
To our great father given;
He takes the children to his arms,
And calls them heirs of heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Faithful, O God, are all thy ways!
Thy love endures the same;
Nor from the promise of thy grace
Blots out the children's name.

title: Jesus, kind inviting Lord
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, kind inviting Lord,
We with joy obey thy word.
In their earliest infancy,
Bring our little ones to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Born they are, like us, in sin,
Touch th' unconscious lepers clear*;
Purchase of thy blood they are,
►Save them by thy dying prayer.

title: See Israel's gentle Shepherd stand
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See Israel's gentle Shepherd stand
O With all-engaging charms:
Hark how he calls the tender lambs,
And folds them in his arms!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Permit them to approach,'' he cries,
"Nor scorn their humble name:
For 'twas to bless such souls as these,
The Lord of angels came."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We bring them Lord, in thankful hands,
And yield them up to thee;
Joyful that we ourselves are thine,
Thine let our offspring be.

title: Hence sprung the' Apostles' honour'd name
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hence sprung the' Apostles' honour'd name
Sacred beyond heroic fame:
In lowlier forms before our eyes,
Pastors from hence, and teachers rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From Christ their varied gifts derive,
And fed by Christ their graces live:
While shielded by his mighty hand,
'Midst all the rage of hell they stand..

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So shall the bright succession run
Through the last courses of the sun;
While unborn churches, by their care,
Shall rise and nourish large and fair.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, now teach our hearts to know
The spring whence all these blessings flow;
Pastors and people shout thy praise
Through the long round of endless days.

title: Father, live, by all things fear'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Three in person, one in power,
Thee we worship evermore:
Praise by all to thee be given,
Endless theme of earth and heaven.

title: Father of mercies, in thy word
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of mercies, in thy word
What endless glory shines I
For ever be thy name adored
For these celestial lines.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here may the wretched sons of want
Exhaustless riches find;
Riches above what earth can grant,
And lasting as the mind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here the fair Tree of knowledge grows,
And yields a free repast;
Sublimer sweets than nature knows,
Invite the longing taste.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here the Redeemer's welcome voice
Spreads heavenly pea?e around;
And life and everlasting joys
Attend the blissful sound.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Divine Instructer, gracious Lord,
Be thou for ever near!
Teach me to love thy sacred word,
And view my Saviour there.

title: O would'st thou now thy Spirit breathe
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O would'st thou now thy Spirit breathe,
And bid my unbelief depart,
The peace thou didst to me bequeath,
The pardon speak into my heart,
And let me now my Father see,
The image of my God in thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sufficient is that sight alone
To answer all my wishes here;
Come then, and make thy Godhead known,
As crucified for me appear,
Be thou set forth before mine eyes,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
ask no other paradise.
3 With me, I find, thou still dost dwell,
For unconsum'd on earth I live,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
am not with the lost in hell,
But wait thy Spirit to receive,
Who makes thy heavenly Father known,
And shows that God and* thou art One

title: Saviour, cast a pitying eye
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour, cast a pitying eye,
V/ A sinner at thy feet I lie,
And will not thence depart,
Till thou regard my ceaseless moan,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
speak, and take away the stone,
The unbelieving heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Till thou the mountain load remove,
1 groan beneath my want of love,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
hear my bitter cry:
Without thy love I cannot live,
Give, Jesus, friend of sinners, give
Me love, or else I die.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Dost thou not all my sufferings know,
Dost thou not see my eyes o'erflow,
My lab'ring bosom move?
Why do I all this burthen bear?
Need I to thee the cause declare?
Thou knowst I cannot love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
This is my sin and misery,
I always find thy love to me,
Seal'd by thy precious blood;
And yet I make thee no return,

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
only for my baseness mourn,
1 cannot love my God.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Now, then, O God, thine hand lay to,
And let me all the means look through.
And trust to thee alone;
To thee alone for all things trust,
And say, (let me be saved or lost,)
Thine only will be done.

title: O how shall a sinner perform
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O how shall a sinner perform
The vows he hath vow'd to the Lord!
How can I be true to my word!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
tremble at what I have done:
But look for thy help from above;
The power that I never have known,
The virtue of Jesu's love!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My solemn engagements are vain,
My promises empty as air;
My vows, I shall break them again.
And plunge in eternal despair;
Unless my omnipotent God
The sense of his goodness impart,
And shed by his Spirit abroad
The love of himself in my heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O Lover of sinners, extend
To me thy compassionate grace;
Appear my affliction to end,
Afford me a glimpse of thy face!
That sight shall enkindle in me
A flame of reciprocal love,
And then I shall cleave unto thee,
And then I shall never remove.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O come to a mourner in pain,
Thy peace in my conscience reveal!
And then I shall love thee again,
And sing of the goodness I feel:
Constraint by the grace of my Lord,
My soul shall in all things obey,
And wait to be fully restored,
And long to be summon'd away.

title: O happy day that fix'd my choice
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O happy day that fix'd my choice
On thee, my Saviour and my God I
Well may this glowing heart rejoice,
And tell its raptures all abroad.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O happy bond, that seals my vows
To Him who merits all my love!
Let cheerful anthems fill his house.
While to that sacred shrine I move.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis done, the great transaction's done,
I am my Lord's, and he is mme;
He drew me, and I foilow'd on,
Charm'd to confess the voice divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
High heaven that heard the solemn vow,
That vow renew'd shall daily hear,
Till in life's latest hour I bow,
And bless, in death, a bond so dear.

title: The promise of my Father's love
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The promise of my Father's love
Shall stand for ever good,"
He said; and gave his soul to death,
And seal'd the grace with blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To this sure covenant of thy word
I set my worthless name;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
seal the' engagement to my Lord,
And make my humble claiuu

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy light, and strength, and pardoning grace,
And glory shall be mine;
My life and soul, my heart and flesh,
And all my powers are thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I call that legacy my own,
Which Jesus did bequeath;
'Twas purchased with a dying groan,
And ratified in death.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Sweet is the memory of his name,
Who blest us in his Will,
And to his Testament of love
Made his own life the seal.

title: Through Jesus, our divine High-Priest
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Through Jesus, our divine High-Priest,
Who pleads the sinners cause in heaven,
Father, presenting our request,
We humbly sue to be forgiven;
Mercy we ask in Jesu's name,
Who died for all our sins to' atone,
Who rose our purchas'd peace to claim,
And now appears before thy throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There, at thy throne of grace we meet,
United to th' incarnate God,
Boldly approach the mercy-seat,
Which Jesus sprinkled with his blood
He paid the price on Calvary
For every sinful child of man,
And trusting in his death for me,
My pardon seal'd I now obtain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Father, I still his passion plead,
Which bought thy love for all mankind
And pardon'd in this time of need

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
come, confirming grace to find,
Importunate in faithful prayer,
Thy promis'd succour I implore,
Power to withstand, and strength to bear,
'Till sin destroy'd can tempt no more!

title: Let all who truly bear
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let all who truly bear
The bleeding Saviour's name,
Their faithful hearts with us prepare,
And eat the Paschal Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This eucharistic feast
Our every want supplies;
And still we by his death are bless'd,
And share his sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who thus our faith employ,
His sufferings to record,
Even now we mournfully enjoy
Communion with our Lord,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We too with him are dead,
And shall with him arise;
The cross on which he bows his head,
Shall lift us to the skies.

title: Wellpleasing to our God above
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Wellpleasing to our God above,
His sacrifice of life arid love

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
plead before the gracious throne:
Father, a prodigal receive,
And bid a pardon'd rebel live,
The purchase of thy bleeding Son.

title: Lord of heaven and earth and ocean
author: J   Crosse

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of heaven and earth and ocean,
Hear us from thy bright abode,
While our hearts with deep devotion,
Own their great and gracious God:
Now, with joy we come before thee,
Seek thy face —thy mercies sing;
Lord of life, and light, and glory,
Guard thy church, and guide our kii ig.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Health and every needful blessing
Are thy bounteous gift alone;
Comforts undeserv'd possessing,
Here we bend before thy throne;
Whilst the babe, the youth, the hoary,
Their united tribute bring,
Lord of life, and light, and glory,
Shield our isle, and save our king.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thee with humble adoration,
Lord, we praise for mercies past;
Still, to this most favour'd nation,
May those mercies ever last:
Britons, then through future story,
Songs of ceaseless praise shall sing s
Lord of life, and light, and glory 5
Bless thy people, —bless our king.

title: Brother in Christ, and well-beloved
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Brother in Christ, and well-beloved,
To Jesus and his servants dear,
Enter, and show thyself approved;
Enter, and find that God is here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Welcome from earth: lo, the right hand
Of fellowship to thee we give!
With open hearts and hands we stand,
And thee in Jesu's name receive.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Say, is thy heart resolved as ours?
Then let it burn with sacred love;
Then let it taste the heavenly powers,
Partaker of the joys above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesu, attend, thyself reveal!
Are we not met in thy great name?
Thee in the midst we wait to feel,
We wait to catch the spreading flame.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou God that answerest by fire,
The Spirit of burning now impart;
And let the flames of pure desire
Rise from the altar of the heart.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Truly our fellowship below
With thee and with the Father is:
in thee eternal life we know,
And heaven's unutterable bliss.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
In part we only know thee here,
But wait thy coming from above;
And we shall then behold thee near,
And we shall all be lost iu love.
?x

title: Thy precious time misspent —redeem
author: Bishop  Kenn

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
In all thy converse he sincere,
In conscience as the noon-tide clear;
Think, how the' all-seeing God surveys
Thy secret thoughts, thy words and ways,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wake, and lift up thyself, my heart.
And with the angels take thy part;
Who all night long unwearied sing
High glory to the' eternal King.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Loi d, I my vows to thee renew;
Scatter my sins as morning dew!
Guard my first springs of thought and will,
And with thyself my spirit fill.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Direct, control, suggest, this day,
All I design, or do, or say;
That all my powers, with all their might.
In thy sole glory may unite.

title: Glory to thee, my God, this night
author: Bishop  Kenn

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glory to thee, my God, this night,
VJT For all the blessings of the light;
Keep me, O keep me, King of kings,
Beneath thine own almighty wings!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Forgive me, Lord, for thy dear Son,
The ills that I this day have done;
That, with the world, myself, and thee
I, ere I sleep, at peace may he.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O let my soul on thee repose!
And with sweet sleep mine eyelids close;
Sleep that shall me more vigorous make,
To serve my God when I awake.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Teach me to live, that I may dread
The grave as little as my bed;
Teach me to die, that so I may
With joy behold the judgment day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
If through the night, I sleepless lie,
With heavenly thoughts my soul supply;
Let no ill dreams disturb my rest,
No powers of darkness me molest.

title: O thou that hangedst on the tree
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou that hangedst on the tree,
Our curse and sufferings to remove,
Pity the souls that look to thee,
And save us by thy dying love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Save us by grace, through faith alone,
A faith thou must thyself impart;
A faith that would by works be shown,
A faith that purifies the heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A faith that doth the mountains move,
A faith that shows our sins forgiven,
A faith that sweetly works by love,
And ascertains our claim to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This is the faith we humbly seek,
The faith in thy all-cleansing blood;
That blood which doth for sinners speak,
O let it speak us up to God!

title: Canst thou reject our dying prayer
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Canst thou reject our dying prayer,
Or cast us out who come to thee?
Our sins, ah! wherefore didst thou bear?
Jesus, remember Calvary!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Number'd with the transgressors thou,
Between the felons crucified,
Speak to our hearts, and tell us now,
Wherefore hast thou for sinners died?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For us wast thou not lifted up?
For us a bleeding victim made?
That we, the abjects we, might hope,
Thou hast for all a ransom paid.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O might we, with our anxious eyes,
Thee in thy bloody vesture see;
And cast us on thy sacrifice!
Jesus, my Lord, remember me!

title: Lord of the wide, extended main
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of the wide, extended main,
JLi Whose power the winds and seas controls,
Whose hand doth earth and heaven sustain,
Whose Spirit leads believing souls:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For thee we leave our native shore,
(We whom thy love delights to keep,")
In other lands thy works explore,
And see thy wonders in the deep.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis here thine unknown paths we trace,
Which dark to human eyes appear;
While through the mighty waves we pass,
Faith only sees that God is here.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Throughout the deep thy footsteps shine,
We own thy way is in the sea,
O'erawed by majesty divine,
And lost in thy immensity.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy wisdom here we learn to' adore,
Thine everlasting truth we prove;
Amazing heights of boundless power,
Unfathomable depths of love.

title: Infinite God, thy greatness spann'd
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Infinite God, thy greatness spann'd
These heavens, and meted out the skies;
Lo! in the hollow of thy hand
The measured waters sink and rise!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thee to perfection who can tell!
Earth and her sons beneath thee lie,
Lighter than dust within thy scale,
And less than nothing in thine eye.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet, in thy Son, divinely great,
We claim thy providential care;
Boldly we stand before thy seat,
Our Advocate hath placed us there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With him we are gone up on high,
Since he is ours, and we are his;
With him we reign above the sky,
And walk upon the subject seas.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We boast of our recover'd powers,
Lords are we of the lands and floods;
And earth, and heaven, and all is ours,
And we are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

title: Jesus, where'er thy people meet
author: William Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, where'er thy people meet
Where'er they seek thee, thou art found,
And every place is hallow'd ground.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For thou, within no walls confined,
Inhabitest the humble mind;
Such ever bring thee where they come,
And going, take thee to their home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Dear Shepherd of thy chosen few!
Thy former mercies here renew;
Here to our waiting hearts proclaim
The sweetness of thy saving name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here may we prove the power of prayei,
To strengthen faith, and sweeten care;
To teach our faint desires to rise,
And bring all heaven before our eyes.

title: In tenderest pity to thine own
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In tenderest pity to thine own,
Thou dost thy wrath forbear;
Thine every servant is a son
Whom thou delight'st to spare:
And while our hearts are bowed to thee,
Thine easy yoke we prove,
And own it perfect liberty
To serve the God we love.
According to thy faithful word
It then shall surely he,
Thou wilt remember us, O Lord,
Who now remember thee;
To seek, and challenge us for thine,
Thou wilt from heaven come down,
And we around thy head shall shine,
As jewels of thy crown.

title: How are thy servants blest, O Lord
author: J   Addison

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How are thy servants blest, O Lord!
JlL How sure is their defence!
Eternal Wisdom is their guide,
Their help Omnipotence.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In foreign realms, and lands remote,
Supported by thy care,
Through burning climes they pass unhurt,
And breathe in tainted air.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When by the dreadful tempest borne,
High on the broken wave,
They know thou art not slow to hear,
Nor impotent to save.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The storm is laid, the winds retire,
Obedient to thy will;
The sea, that roars at thy command,
At thy command is still.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In midst of dangers, fears, and deaths,
Thy goodness we'll adore;
We'll praise thee for thy mercies past,
And humbly hope for more.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Our life, while thou preserv'st that life,
Thy sacrifice shall be;
And death, when death shall be our lot,
Shall join our souls to thee.

title: How many spend the guilty night
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How many spend the guilty night
XX In re veilings and frantic mirth!
The creature is their sole delight,
Their happiness the things of earth:
For us suffice the season past;
We choose the better part at last.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We will not close our wakeful eyes,
We will not let our eyelids sleep,
But humbly lift them to the skies,
And all a solemn vigil keep:
So many years on sin bestow'd,
Can we not watch one night for God V

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We can, O Saviour, for thy sake,
Devote our every hour to thee:
Speak but the word, our souls shall wake,
And sing with cheerful melody:
Thy praise shall our glad tongues employ,
And every heart shall dance for joy.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Shout in the midst of us, O King
Of saints, and make our joys abound:
Let us exult, give thanks, and sing,
And triumph in redemption found:
We ask for every waiting soul,
O let our glorious joy be full!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O may we all triumphant rise,
With joy upon our heads return,
And far above those nether skies,
By thee on eagles' wings upborne.
Through all yon radiant circles move,
And gain the highest heaven of love.

title: Join, all ye ransom'd sons of grace
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Join, all ye ransom'd sons of grace.
The holy joy prolong,
And shout to the Redeemer's praise
A solemn midnight song.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blessing, and thanks, and love, and might,
Be to our Jesus given,
Who turns our darkness into light,
Who turns our hell to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thither our faithful souls he leads,
Thither he bids us rise,
With crowns of joy upon our heads,
To meet him in the skies.

title: Out of the depth of self-despair
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Out of the depth of self-despair,
To thee, O Lord, I cry;
My misery mark, attend my prayer,
And bring salvation nigh.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If thou art rigorously severe,
Who may the test abide?
Where shall the man of sin appear,
Or how be justified?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But, O, forgiveness is with thee,
That sinners may adore!
With filial fear thy goodness see.;
And never grieve thee mora.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My soul, while still to Him it flies,
Prevents the morning ray:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
that his mercy's beams would rise,
And bring the gospel day.'

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Ye faithful souls, confide in God,
Mercy with Him remains;
Plenteous redemption through his bloodj
To wash out all your stains.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
His Israel himself shall clear,
From all their sins redeem;
The Lord our Righteousness is near,
And we are just in Him.

title: The God of nature and of grace
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The God of nature and of grace
In all his works appears;
His goodness through the earth we trace,
His grandeur in the spheres.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Behold this fair and fertile globe,
By him in wisdom plann'd;
Twas he who girded, like a robe,
The ocean round the land.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
He bows the heavens, —the mountains stand
A highway for their God:
He walks amid'st the desert-land,
'Tis Eden where he trod.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The forests in his strength rejoice;
Hark! on the evening breeze,
As once of old, the Lord God's voice
Is heard among the trees.

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
—Mount with the lark, and hear our song
Up to the gates of light;
Or, with the nightingale, prolong
Our numbers through the night.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
In every stream his bounty flows,
Diffusing joy and wealth;
In every breeze his Spirit blows,
—The breath of life and health.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
His blessings fall ha plenteous showers
Upon the lap of earth,
That teems with foliage, fruit, and flowers,
And rings with infant mirth.

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
If God hath made this world so fair,
Where Sin and Death abound;
How beautiful beyond compare
Will Paradise be found!

title: O God, who dost the motives know
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, who dost the motives know
From which our various actions flow.
And what we now intend;
Our purposes, if thee they please,
Prevent, accompany, and bless,
With an auspicious end.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Unmoved by vanity or pride,
Things honest, Lord, we would provide.
According to thy will;
And (while thy hand points out our way)
Thy providential call obey,
And thy designs fulfil.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By thy paternal love decreed,
To labour for our daily bread,
Our business we pursue;
In every step look up to thee,
And ask, till we thy counsel see,
What would' st thou have us do?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Who dost from man his purpose hide,-—
If from thy paths we turn aside,
Our wandering feet repress:
Stop us, impatient to proceed,
Nor let us snatch with eager speed
At dangerous success.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Deceived by each appearance fair,
The tempting bait, the pleasing snare,
Alas! we Cannot shun,
Unless we thy direction find,
Who promisest to bring the blind
A way they have not known.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Safe through the world's insidious arts,
The labyrinth of human hearts,
Thou wilt thy children lead;
Thou wilt (if we of men beware,
And cast on thee our every care)
Supply our every need.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Thee, then, we joyfully confess,
In all our works, in all our ways,
Disposer of thine own;
And, satisfied with God, our Friend,
Soul, body, and estate, commend
Into thy hands alone.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Who in thy Providence confide,
Thou wilt in all our actions guide,
And all our paths attend;
Give of every gift and grace,
Till, happily, our earthly race,
In life eternal end.

title: Our souls to thee we lift
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our souls to thee we lift,
Father of earth and heaven,
Convinced that every useful gift,
Is by thy goodness given;
That every well-meant deed,
(Which thou vouchsaf'st to bless
When offer'd up through Christ our Head)
Is crown'd with full success.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our thoughts, thou know'st, are vain,
Our wisdom nought avails,
Our best-contrived and order'd plan,
Without tbv blessing fails:
But with my gracious nod,
Whate'er in faith is done,
Must work together for our good,
And for thy praise alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The hearts of feeble men
Thou only dost incline
To act by secret springs unseen.
And answer thy design;
While still our farthest end
Is, God to glorify,
To serve and please our heavenly Friend.
And thine to live and die.

title: Father, thou Know'st whate'er we need
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, thou Know'st whate'er we need,
Before our wants we own,
Nor wilt refuse thy children bread,
Or mock us with a stone;
If nature's gifts thou dost bestow,
They speak the Giver kind.
Not hurtful presents of a foe,
But for our good design'd.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The talents to my offspring lent,
I thankfully confess:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
may they answer thy intent,
And use them for thy praise!
What to put on, and drink, and eat,
Hard toiling to procure, —
But more laborious for the meat,
Which always shall endure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou seest my fears, lest thou, their God,
They should forget and slight,
Follow the unregenerate crowd,
And in the world delight;
To evil with the many run,
Fantastic man to please,
By lawful things, alas, undone,
And through their own success.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The thing, whose consequence unknown,
I tremble to foresee,
Or let it in thy name be done,
Or let it never be:
To thee the matter I resign,
And in thy pleasure rest,
For order'd by the will divine,
Whatever is is best.

title: Jesus, from whom, all blessings Sow
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, from whom, all blessings Sow,
Ord'rer of all events below,
With gracious smiles thy children see,
Who hope success from none but thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Prosper, for our Redeemer's sake,
What, in his name, we undertake,
Who our appointed task fulfil,
And serve thy providential will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The gift thou hast on us bestow'd,
Productive of our needful food,
As a sure token of thy grace.
We use it to the Giver's praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And if we lawfully pursue
What thou commandest us to do,
Let it thy approbation meet;
Or else our surest hopes defeat.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
A thousand ways thou canst prevent
The deed that hath not thy consent:
And, O, forbid it to be done,
If ours, O Lord, is ours alone.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
But if thou favour our design,
Though men and fiends against us join,
They cannot thy decree repeal,
They cannot contradict thy will.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The counsel of the Lord shall stand,
(For all bow down to thy command,)
It must be done, whate'er it be;
And, lo, we wait our wish to see:

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Thou wilt not let us hence remove,
Without the convoy of thy love;
And if thy love our steps attend,
Our toil on earth m heaven shall end.

title: A God upon the action shine
author: Weslet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A God upon the action shine,
And stamp it with the stamp divine,
And graciously vouchsafe to bless,
His blessing ascertains success.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Then all th.' opposing mountains flow,
And God's intent we plainly know,
And thankful at his feet approve
The fiat of Almighty Love.

title: Man, sinful man, to labour born
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Man, sinful man, to labour born,
jj/JL And urged by the divine command,
Till, dust he doth to dust return,
Idle on earth should never stand,
But still his six day's work pursue,
And do what God appoints to do.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With readiness and lowly fear
We come, O God, to serve thy will,
Sentenc'd to toil incessant here,'
And then to rest on Sion's hill;
But while thy Justice we obey,
O let thy Love point out our way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our way by reason's glimmering light,
Unable clearly to perceive,
Teach us to think and act aright,
A more distinct direction give,
And let thy Providence declare
The work it doth for us prepare.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The work, the time, the manner show,
And if we now our path mistake,
No further surfer us to go,
But warn, and stop, and turn us hick,
(Who would on thee alone confide,)
And into all thy counsel guide.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Infinite are thy means and ways,
The wants of nature to supply;
Thou canst maintain the chosen race,
By making windows in the sky, —
Canst in the barren desert feed,
Or hid the ravens bring us bread.

sections.label: Verse 6
