sections.text:
O might we seek the kingdom first —
Th' unutterable joy and peace,
For God, the living Fountain, thirst,
And hunger after righteousness;
We then should by thy promise prove,
The all-sufficient power of love.

title: Glory to thee, my God, I wait
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glory to thee, my God, I wait,
And on thy word rely,
Blind, inexorable Fate,
And Fortune I defy;
Not by Destiny compell'd,
Not by Chance at random driven,
In the hand Almighty held,
And kept by watchful heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Him who for his servant cares,
In all things I respect,
Him who numbers all my hairs,
And doth my paths direct:
2y
He demands my utmost love:
And loving Him with all my heart,
Neither men nor fiends can move,
Nor life, nor death can part.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, shelter'd in thy Name,
My adamantine tower,
Thee I joyfully proclaim,
Supreme in love and power;
Power that earth and hell controls,
Love which none can e'er explain,
Love that reigns in faithful souls,
And shall for ever reign!

title: When the chief Shepherd shall appear
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When the chief Shepherd shall appear,
And small and great before him stand,
O may the flock assembled here,
Be found as sheep at his right hand!

title: Great God to thee my voice I raise
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God to thee my voice I raise,
To thee my youngest hours belong:
J would begin my life with praise,
Till growing years improve the song.
' Tis to thy sovereign grace I owe
That I was born on British ground;
Where, streams of heavenly mercy flow,
And words of sweet salvation sound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
would not change my native land
For rich Peru with all her gold:
A nobler prize * lies in my hand,
Than East or Western Indies hold.
How do I pity those who dwell
Where ignorance and darkness reign!
They know no heav'n, they fear no hell,
Those endless joys, that endless pain.
Thy praise shall still employ my breath,
Since thou hast mark'd my way to heaven:
Nor will I run the road to death,
And waste the blessings thou hast given.

title: The eagle fond her charge awakes
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
' Twas thus in nature's sleep I lay,
When Christ his Spirit shed:
His Spirit stirr'd me up to pray,
And hover' d o'er my head,
Infusing the first gracious hope
He spread his wings abroad.
And train'd his infant pupil up
To seek the face of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The object of his kindest care
He never yet forsook,
But did himself my weakness bear,
And all my burthen took;
He bore me up, from earth he bore
On wings of heavenly love,
And taught my unfledg'd soul to soar
To those bright realms above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The Spirit of redeeming grace
Hath been my sure defence,
And through the pathless wilderness
Lead on my innocence:
When simple as a little child
All idols I abhorr'd,
And saw, as my Eedeemer smil'd,
My Paradise restored.

title: O hear me, Lord! on Thee I call
author: Merrick

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O hear me, Lord! on Thee I call,
And prostrate at thy footstool fall;
Propitious to my cause appear,
And bow to my request thine ear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Seek ye my face with duteous care,
"And frequent to my throne repair: "
Thus to my heart I hear thee speak;
"Thy face,"my heart replies, "I seek."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O let me on thy aid reclin'd,
Thee still my great salvation find!
Nor leave me helpless and forlorn,
The absence of thy grace to mourn.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When doom'd the orphan's lot to bear,
No father's kind concern I share,
Nor o'er me wakes a mother's eye,
My wants attentive to supply; —

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Adopted by thy care, in Thee
The parent and the friend I see,
And nourish'd by thy fost'ring hand,
Within thy courts secure I stand.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Instruct me, Lord, thy path to know,
And while, with secret art, the foe
My doubting steps would turn aside;
Be Thou my guardian and my guide.

title: Mine, to chide me when I rove
author: Bubton J

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Mine, to comfort in distress,
If the Holy Spirit bless;
Mine, to shew, by living faith,
Man can triumph over death!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Mine to tell of joys to come,
Shew the rebel-sinner's doom; —
O thou blessed book divine!
Precious treasure! thou art mine.

title: Now let our hearts conspire to raise
author: D   Bkaderbery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now let our hearts conspire to raise
JLl A cheerful anthem to his praise
Who reigns enthron'd above:
Let music, sweet as incense, rise
With grateful odoui'S to the skies,
The work of joy and love.
Children.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Teach us to bow before thy face;
Nor let our hearts forget thy grace,
Or slight tby providence;
When lost in ignorance we lay,
To vice and death an easy prey,
Thy goodness snatch'd us thence
Congregation*

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O what a numerous race we see,
In ignorance and misery,
Unprincipled, untaught!
Shall they continue still to lie
In ignorance and misery?
We cannot bear the thought.
Children,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Give, Lord, each liberal soul to prove
The joys of thine exhaustless love;
And while thy praise we sing,
May we the sacred scriptures know,
And like the blessed Jesus grow,
That earth and heaven may ring.
Congregation.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Youth is the morning of our days
author: Burton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Youth is the morning of our days,
When reason's dawn appears:
If spent in sacred wisdom's ways,
' Twill crown our future years.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Be it our object, to employ
The blooming moments given,
The Lord our God to glorify,
And thus prepare for heaven,

title: A broken heart he'll not despise
author: Ja Ne  Taylor

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A broken heart he'll not despise,
For 'tis his chief delight:
This is a humble sacrifice,
Well pleasing in his sight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though treasures brought before his throne
Would no acceptance find,
He kindly condescends to own
A meek and lowly mind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This is an off'ring we may bring,
However mean our store:
The poorest child, the greatest king.
Can give him nothing more.

title: Ye hearts with youthful vigour warm
author: Philip Doddridge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye hearts with youthful vigour warm,
In smiling crowds draw near,
And turn from every mortal charm,
A Saviour's voice to hear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He, Lord of all the worlds on high,
Stoops to converse with you,
And lays his radiant glories by,
Your friendship to pursue.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"The soul that longs to see my face,
Is sure my love to gain;
And those that early seek my grace,
Shall never seek in vain."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What object, Lord, my soul should move,
If once compar'd with thee?
What beauty should command my love,
Like what in Christ I see?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Away, ye false delusive toys,
Vain tempters of the mind!
» Tis here I fix my lasting choice,
And here true bliss I find.

title: From yon delusive scene
author: G   Clayton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From yon delusive scene,
Where death and ruin smile,
Beneath a treacherous mien,
The sinner to beguile,
The Saviour calls, O hear his voice,
And make his love your only choice

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Down from the realms of light,
To this dark -world of woe,
He came with speedy flight,
Eedemption to hestow:
The Saviour calls, O hear his voice,
And make his love your early choice.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With pardon in his hands,
And purity and joy,
How sweet are his commands!
His bliss without alloy!
The Saviour calls, O hear his voice,
And make his love your only choice.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Through life your guard and guide,
In death your strength and stay,
He'll keep you near his side,
Nor ever turn away:
The Saviour calls, O hear his voice,
And make his love your only choice.

title: How happy is the youth who hears
author: Logan

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy is the youth who hears
JlL Instruction's warning voice;
And who celestial wisdom makes,
His early, only choice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For she has treasures greater far,
Than East or West unfold;
And her rewards more precious are
Than all their stores of gold.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In her right hand she holds to view
A length of happy days;
Riches with splendid honours join'd,
Are what her left displays.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
According as her labours rise,
So her rewards increase:
Her ways are ways of pleasantness,
And all her paths are peace.

title: Religion like a sun appears
author: Vr   B   Collyer J

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Religion like a sun appears,
And shines upon our dawning years
We follow still the guiding ray,
That kindles into perfect day;
Conducted safe along the road,
That leads to peace —that leads to God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With active feet, with ardent eyes,
We seek our home above the skies;
Subdued by love, and taught of God,
Rejoicing in redeeming blood,
We press to find that happy shore,
Where sin and sorrow reign no more.

title: Hark! 'tis your heavenly Father's call
author: Heginbotham

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark! 'tis your heavenly Father's call,
How soft the charming accents fall;
"Ask, and receive, my son,"he cries,
With loving heart and melting eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, I accept thine offer'd grace,
I come to seek a Father's face:
Nor will he turn his ear away
Who taught my heart and lips to pray.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One thing I ask, and wilt thou hear,
And grant my soul a gift so dear?
Wisdom descending from above,
The sweetest token of thy love:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Wisdom, betimes to know the Lord,
To fear his name, and keep his word,
To lead my feet in paths of truth,
And guide and guard my wandering youth.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then, should'st thou grant a length of days,
My life shall still proclaim thy praise;
Or early death my soul convey
To realms of everlasting: day.
oowper.] HYMN 796- o. m. (30)
Prayer for Young Persons.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
"OESTOW, dear Lord, upon our youth
D The gift of saving grace;
And let the seed of sacred truth,
Fall in a fruitful place.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Grace is a plant, where'er it grows,
Of pure and heavenly root:
But fairest in the youngest shews,
And yields the sweetest fruit.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Ye careless ones, O hear betimes,
The voice of sovereign love!
Your youth is stain'd with many crimes,
But mercy reigns above.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
For you the public prayer is made,
Oh! join that public prayer!
For you the secret tear is shed,
O shed yourselves a tear!

sections.label: Verse 10
sections.text:
We pray that you may early prove
The Spirit's power to teach;
You cannot be too young to love
That Jesus, whom we preach.

title: Gracious Lord, our children see
author: William Cowper

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
When the angel of the Lord,
Drawing forth his dreadful sword,
Slew with an avenging hand,
All the first -horn of the land;
Then thy people's doors he pass'd,
Where the bloody sign was plac'd;
Hear us, now, upon our knees,
Plead the blood of Christ for these!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, we tremble, for we know
That the fierce, malicious foe,
Wheeling round his watchful flight,
Keeps them ever in his sight:
Spread thy pinions King of kings,
Hide them safe beneath thy wings
Lest the ravenous bird of prey,
Stoop, and bear the brood away.

title: Almighty God, in humble prayer
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Almighty God, in humble prayer,
To thee our souls we lift
Do thou our waiting minds prepare
For thy most needful gift.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We ask not golden streams of wealth,
Along our path to flow;
We ask not undecaying health,
Nor length of years below.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We ask not honours, which an hour
May bring and take away;
We ask not pleasure, pomp, and power,
Lest we should go astray.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We ask for wisdom: —Lord, impart
The knowledge how to live;
A wise and understanding heart,
To all before thee give.

title: /children once were heard to sing
author: Kelly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
/children once were heard to sing,
When so many silent were;
Glad they welcom'd Israel's King,
And hosannah's fill'd the air.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
David's Son, and David's Lord,
Heard their praises and approved:
Be our Saviour's grace adored,
Be our Saviour's name beloved.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Count us not, O Lord, too hold,
If we try our song to raise;
Children we, like those of old,
Taught, like them, to lisp thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: When blooming youth is snatch'd away
author: Anne Steele

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When blooming youth is snatch'd away
By death's resistless hand,
Our hearts the mournful tribute pay,
Which pity must demand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
While pity prompts the rising sigh,
O may this truth, imprest
With awful power —I too must die —
Sink deep in every breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
The voice of this alarming scene
Let every heart obey;
Nor be the heavenly warning vain
Which calls to watch and pray.

title: There is a happy land
author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Come to this happy land,
Come, come away;
Why will ye doubting stand,
Why still delay?
O, we shall happy be,
When from sin and sorrow free;
Lord, we shall live with thee-
Blest, blest for aye.

title: Around the throne of God in heaven
author: Anonymous

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Around the throne of God in heaven
Thousand's of children stand;
Children, whose sins are all forgiven,
A holy, happy band.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What brought them to that world tbovy,
That heaven so bright and fair,
Where all is peace, and joy, and love?
How came those children there?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Because the Saviour shed his blood,
To wash away their sin;
Bathed in that pure and precious flood,
Behold them white and clean.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
On earth they sought the Saviour's grace,
On earth they loved his name;
So now they see his blessed face,
And stand before the Lamb.

title: A God! I thank thee that the night
author: Pierpont

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A God! I thank thee that the night
In peace and rest hath past away,
And that I see in this fair light
My Father's smile, that makes it day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Be thou my guide, and let me live
As under thine all-seeing eye;
Supply my wants, my sins forgive,
And make me happy when I die.

title: Another day its course hath ran
author: Pierpont

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Another day its course hath ran,
And still, O God, thy child is blest;
For thou hast been by day my sun,
And thou wilt be by night my rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet sleep descends my eyes to close;
And now, while all the world is still,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
give my body to repose,
My spirit to my Father's will.
